description: Found by the oculist-nq1x.13 implementer 2026-09-23. github.com/ya8282/oculist.git (the code repo, not the outer workspace repo that oculist-296.8 covered) has annotated tag v1.7.0 'Oculist v1.7.0', created 2026-09-02 16:24:45, peeling to 9490187 (Merge branch 'docs/store-submission'), an ancestor of the goal branch. oculist-296 says 'Only v1.5.0 is tagged' and STORE.md section 7 tags only after store approval; v1.5.0's tag subject says 'published to the Chrome Web Store', v1.7.0's does not. title: available_effects_malformed_packs.test.js races against background.js seedHalloweenPack() and intermittently fails
description:
Measured 2026-09-22 while proving oculist-vr2p (npm test concurrency/timeout flake).
Intermittent failure, unrelated to that bead's contention cause:

test at test/available_effects_malformed_packs.test.js:204:5
'settings.enabledPacks as a plain object degrades to core-only effects, without throwing'
AssertionError: expected the CORE_KEYS list, got that list plus 'boneassembly'.
Fails fast (~7ms for the assertion, ~522ms for the whole file) -- not a timeout, so
unrelated to any poll-budget/contention mechanism. Passes 5/5 in isolation
(`node --test test/available_effects_malformed_packs.test.js`), so it is a race that
only surfaces alongside the rest of the suite.

CAUSE: extension/background.js's seedHalloweenPack() (added in 9bba8bf,
oculist-nq1x.5) runs on every chrome.runtime.onInstalled -- i.e. on every fresh
--load-extension the test suite does, since each test launches its own persistent
context/profile. It does an async chrome.storage.sync round trip that pushes
'halloween' into settings.enabledPacks and writes it back. extension/content.js
picks that up via its storage.onChanged listener and overwrites its module-private
`settings.enabledPacks`.

test/available_effects_malformed_packs.test.js's own fixture calls
window.__ocTest.setEnabledPacksRaw(malformedValue) then immediately reads
availableEffects() back through window.__ocTest.getAvailableEffectKeys(), with no
guard against the seed's async write landing in between. When the seed write's
onChanged fallout beats the test's readback, settings.enabledPacks is
['halloween'] instead of the malformed test value, so availableEffects() correctly
(and unhelpfully, for this test) includes the halloween-packed 'boneassembly' entry,
and the test's hardcoded CORE_KEYS list (which rightly excludes it) mismatches.

The 9bba8bf commit message says "Adapt two existing tests to the first real pack
effect and to the async Halloween seeding" (effect_pack_settings_control.test.js,
settings_panel_effect_list_overflow.test.js) -- this third file, which also reads
settings.enabledPacks through the same seeded background script, was missed.

FIX SHAPE (not investigated further -- out of scope for oculist-vr2p): either set
settings.seededHalloweenPack = true (or push 'halloween' pre-seeded) before this
test's malformed-value assertions the way the two adapted tests do, or otherwise wait
for the seed write to settle before overriding enabledPacks.

Evidence: 1 failure in test/../scratchpad/rr2-adjacent runs.tsv row 3 (this session,
run3.log) out of 5 concurrency=2/SCALE=2 runs; 0/2 further occurrences at
concurrency=2/SCALE=3 in the same session, but sample size is too small to rule it out
-- it is a genuine race, not fixed by either lever.
close_reason: Added test/helpers/halloween_seed.js waitForHalloweenSeedSettled (storage flag landed, then content.js applied it); malformed_packs and effect_list_overflow wait on it before writing fixture packs. Forced race red on HEAD's test, green on new; both helper steps shown load-bearing by mutation. Sweep: no other test exposed. Low, not fixed: misleading timeout message if the seed was skipped; hard-coded 'boneassembly' probe; low-core onboarding performanceMode write could re-send enabledPacks.

title: Jack-o'-Lantern: occlusion sweep reports 33/96 grid scenarios dirty at the t=120ms entrance flicker
description:
Found 2026-09-21 while checking whether repo-c3's uncommitted v2 round could merge.
First time fxJackOLantern has been through the general occlusion sweep: neither
oculist-xl8f nor oculist-9r5k ran it; they gated on jackolantern-check.js and
jackolantern-strict-check.js, which both pass.

RESULT, from `node occlusion-sweep.js jackolantern` on the playground as committed
in the per-effect v2 commit:
- grid: 63/96 clean, 33 DIRTY, maxPixels=2262. 32 of the 33 peak at atTime=120ms,
  one at 80ms -- the entrance flicker. Dirty rows appear at every desktop viewport
  (6 each at 1280x600, 1280x900, 1440x800, 700x1000, 900x700) and 3 at 320x900.
- forced-landing 4/4 clean, edge 12/12 clean.

THE QUESTION, answer it before fixing anything: is this a real defect or a contract
mismatch? Jack's mouth-framing placement deliberately centres the match inside the
pumpkin's transparent mouth cavity, which no other effect does, and the sweep may be
counting pixels the design is allowed to change (for example the warm face-light
visible through the cavity around the glyphs). If so, the fix is in the harness:
register jackolantern the way horseman is registered (NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT)
with its own strict check as the gate, and say why. If the flicker is actually
painting onto or tinting the match glyphs or the protected mouth rectangle, it is a
real defect, and oculist-4rso's acceptance criterion ("No effect paint enters the
protected mouth rectangle") would fail on promotion.

Measure it: capture the dirty frame at t=120ms for one 1280x900 scenario, diff it
against the no-effect frame, and show where the changed pixels are relative to the
match rect and the mouth cavity. Say which case it is, with the image as evidence.

Blocks oculist-4rso.
notes:
DIAGNOSED 2026-09-21, no code changed. Baseline reproduced exactly (grid 63/96, maxPixels 2262; forced 4/4, edge 12/12). Cause: the static mouth-panel rect (x26 y67 128x40, #E86F1C, fill-opacity 0.18, playground ~:10019) sits in the .fx wrap (fixed, positive z-index) ABOVE #match and tints it: 396 glyph-ink px + 1866 highlight px in 1280x900/24px. Constant from t=120 to 2150ms, so it is the whole hold, not the flicker; flicker states contribute nothing. Evidence: artifacts/outputs/jackolantern-nq1x15/ (diagnosis.json, *-diff.png, *-match-crop.png).
DESIGN CONFLICT, needs the human: xl8f's spec says zero glyph-pixel changes, but jackolantern-check.js:76 locks the 0.18 panel and :134 plus jackolantern-strict-check.js:119 REQUIRE the match crop to change in mouth mode. Sweep maxPixels=0 and those checks cannot both hold. Options: (A) the tint is a defect, so move the panel behind the match or cut a hole for the match rect, and flip the two check assertions to require no change; (B) the tint is intended, so register jackolantern in NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT with the strict check as gate, and amend xl8f's zero-glyph rule for mouth mode.
RUN STOPPED 2026-09-21, second review FAIL (the /goal stop condition). NOT closed, NOT committed. Uncommitted in the outer repo on goal/bone-assembly-detail: occlusion-sweep.js (jackolantern exempted whole-key, comment rewritten), jackolantern-check.js and jackolantern-strict-check.js (new mouth-mode gates: max-channel delta ceiling 64, ink-drop tolerance 15, computed panel fill-opacity within 0.02 of 0.18). Mutants M1-M7 (panel opacity, opaque overlays, darkening overlays) all go red; real file green 3/3; sweep exit 0.
REMAINING, from review 2 (evidence: session 72e304c4 scratchpad rv6/): (1) DROP the ink-drop check. It false-reds legible words (webkit 12px "mmm" drops 25, "hmm" 18, chromium 20px "MM" 16) and is redundant, since the delta ceiling catches every mutant it does. The ceiling is sound: 0.18 alpha caps any channel change at about 46. (2) Fix overclaimed comments: mutant margins are about 2x not 3x, the ink-drop numbers go away with (1), the suppressed case in jackolantern-check.js takes no crop, and jackolantern-check.js is Chromium only.
close_reason: Not a flicker bug: the 0.18 #E86F1C mouth panel tints the match for the whole hold, by design (human decision 2026-09-21). jackolantern is exempted whole-key in occlusion-sweep.js; both jackolantern checkers now gate mouth mode with a per-pixel tint ceiling of 64 (principled bound 0.18x255=46, real max 42) and a computed panel fill-opacity check. M1-M7 overpaint/darken mutants all red on both engines; mmm/MM/WWW/Halloween fixtures green; sweep exit 0. Cosmetic comment nits left: strict:38 'mutant min 132' covers opaque mutants only; check.js:14 says 'above' for a launch below. Note for oculist-4rso: the jack checkers are now the only pixel gate and run by hand.

title: Register PACK_LABELS.halloween and seed the pack ON once, for new and existing installs
description:
Register the halloween pack and seed it ON by default, for new installs and for
existing users, exactly once, in a way a user can undo permanently.

The human chose "enabled by default" over oculist-tdj.3's off-by-default design. The
pack is free and preloaded; being packed is how a user REMOVES it, not a paywall.

THE TEMPLATE TO COPY, do not invent a new one. background.js already solves this
exact problem for the default blocklist:
  - extension/content.js:38, seededDefaultBlocklist: false in the settings defaults,
    with the comment explaining why it must round-trip through SETTINGS_KEYS.
  - extension/content.js:57, 'seededDefaultBlocklist' in SETTINGS_KEYS.
  - extension/background.js:236, seedDefaultBlocklist(done): updateSettings() with an
    early `if (settings.seededDefaultBlocklist) return false;`, mutate, set the flag.
  - Called from chrome.runtime.onInstalled, which runs on UPDATE as well as install,
    so existing users pick the default up once. The flag keeps it to exactly once.

STEPS
1. extension/content.js, settings defaults: add seededHalloweenPack: false, beside
   seededDefaultBlocklist, with a comment in the same voice -- written by
   background.js, never read here, present only so saveSettings() does not drop it.
2. extension/content.js SETTINGS_KEYS: add 'seededHalloweenPack'. A key missing here
   is dropped on the next whole-object write and the pack re-seeds itself on every
   extension update, which is exactly the bug the blocklist comment warns about.
3. extension/background.js: add seedHalloweenPack(done), modeled on
   seedDefaultBlocklist: early-return on the flag, coerce settings.enabledPacks to an
   array if it is not one, push 'halloween' if absent, set the flag. Call it from the
   same chrome.runtime.onInstalled listener the blocklist seeding uses.
4. extension/content.js:958: PACK_LABELS.halloween = 'Halloween'. packLabel() already
   falls back to a title-cased id, so this is cosmetic-but-required -- the settings
   panel must read "Halloween", not a slug.

EDGE CASES, all of which the flag handles and none of which may regress
- A user who turns the pack OFF must never have it re-seeded, on any later update.
  The flag is already true by then. Assert this.
- The seed must not clobber a pack list that already contains other pack ids.
- settings.enabledPacks stored as a non-array must not throw here (oculist-nq1x's
  first bead guards the READ; this is the WRITE side and needs its own coercion).
- knownPacks() is driven off effectsRegistry, so until the first effect carries
  pack: 'halloween' the settings panel shows NO pack toggle even though the pack is
  seeded on. That is correct and expected -- a toggle for a pack with nothing behind
  it is worse. Do not add a placeholder entry to make the toggle appear early.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Fresh profile: after onInstalled, settings.enabledPacks contains 'halloween' and
  seededHalloweenPack is true.
- Upgrade profile (settings present, enabledPacks empty, flag absent): same result
  after one update.
- Turn the pack off, then fire onInstalled again: enabledPacks stays without
  'halloween'. This is the test that matters most; write it first.
- enabledPacks stored as a string: seeding replaces it with ['halloween'] and throws
  nothing.
- node --test (whole suite) passes, including the existing oculist-tdj.5 pack
  settings-control coverage.
close_reason: Halloween pack registered and seeded ON once, copying seedDefaultBlocklist's flag-guarded onInstalled template. Reviewer mutation-tested the accommodation made to test/settings_race.test.js (a file the bead did not name): un-sequencing the onInstalled writes, parallelising the two seeds, and dropping the seededHalloweenPack early return each turn it red, so the uniform flush(30) did not make any assertion unfalsifiable, and the calls.get 2-to-3 change is derivable (blocklist get plus confirming re-read, plus the pack seed's single get that returns on the already-true flag). Chaining into the existing listener was necessary; the parallel wiring reproduces the oculist-9s9 bug. Write-side Array.isArray coercion is load-bearing on its own, not leaning on nq1x.1's read guard. No placeholder registry entry, so knownPacks() still returns nothing and no toggle appears early. Suite: implementer reported 335/335, reviewer saw 4 failures on each of two runs with DIFFERENT failing sets and 44/44 in isolation at concurrency 1 -- the oculist-qpl flakiness, not this change.

title: Guard availableEffects() against a malformed stored enabledPacks before any pack ships
description:
availableEffects() (extension/content.js:934) reads the pack list as
  var packs = settings.enabledPacks || [];
and its own comment, written under oculist-tdj, says plainly that this is safe today
only by coincidence: the Array.isArray coercion that repairs a malformed stored value
runs AFTER this function is first called on the load path, and SETTINGS_KEYS happens
to order 'effect' before 'enabledPacks'. No entry carries a `pack`, so indexOf is
never reached and the bad value never gets dereferenced.

The moment a registry entry carries pack: 'halloween', indexOf IS reached, and a
stored enabledPacks that is a string, a number, an object or null throws inside
availableEffects() -- which is on the load path and on every settings-panel render.
An exception there does not degrade to core-only; it takes the picker and the effect
resolution with it.

This bead closes that before any pack ships. It is the first bead of the epic.

STEPS
1. In availableEffects(), replace the `|| []` with a real guard:
   var packs = Array.isArray(settings.enabledPacks) ? settings.enabledPacks : [];
   A non-array stored value must degrade to core-only, not throw.
2. Replace the comment block above it. It currently documents the sequencing
   coincidence as a live hazard; it should now record that the guard is here
   precisely because the coincidence is not load-bearing, and that the later
   Array.isArray coercions on the storage-change and load paths still stand (they
   repair the stored value; this one only protects the read).
3. Do not touch the coercion sites at extension/content.js:8201 and :8280. They
   repair settings.enabledPacks for the writers; this guard protects one reader.
   Both are wanted.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A unit test drives availableEffects() with settings.enabledPacks set to each of:
  a string, a number, null, undefined, a plain object, and a valid array. Every
  non-array case returns exactly the core entries and throws nothing; the array case
  is unchanged.
- The test FAILS against the current `|| []` for at least the string and object
  cases -- prove it red before making it green.
- node --test (whole suite) passes.
close_reason: Guarded availableEffects()'s enabledPacks read with Array.isArray, so a malformed stored value degrades to core-only instead of throwing or, worse, silently admitting a pack. Reviewer independently re-derived the red (string/number/object fail against the old || [], null/undefined pass either way) and mutation-tested the fixture to prove it exercises the real pack filtering, not just the guard branch. Full suite 330/330 for the reviewer; the implementer's 3 failures were concurrency flakes that did not reproduce. The two test-only __ocTest hooks sit on the pre-existing isolated-world surface and are not page-reachable. New finding worth carrying: a STRING enabledPacks never threw, it silently admitted a pack, because 'seasonal'.indexOf('seasonal') is 0 -- a wrong-answer failure the bead only predicted as a crash.

title: [epic] Halloween effect pack: eleven effects, preloaded and free
description:
Ship the Halloween effect pack: eleven character effects, promoted out of
artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html into extension/content.js behind the
pack mechanism oculist-tdj already built, seeded ON by default and free.

DECIDED BY THE HUMAN 2026-09-20
- The pack mechanism is NOT rebuilt. oculist-tdj shipped it and is closed: registry
  entries take an optional `pack` field, availableEffects() is the single read of
  settings.enabledPacks, PACK_LABELS/packLabel/knownPacks drive the settings-panel
  toggle, and a one-time discovery notice exists. Zero entries carry a `pack` today,
  so the mechanism has never run against a real pack. This epic is its first user.
- No separate loadable pack FILE, no new loader, no injection path, no manifest
  permission, no remote asset. Effects live in extension/content.js like every other
  effect and are gated by the `pack` field alone.
- The pack is seeded ON at install and on update, and it is free. A user who turns
  it off stays off.
- ELEVEN effects: the nine oculist-1ta character prototypes plus Flappy and
  Cheshire, which the human moved out of core into this pack (see oculist-e2m,
  oculist-e2m.5 and oculist-e2m.6, all amended 2026-09-20).
- The CORE effect count stays at twelve forever. Packed effects are listed in the
  packed slice of each enumeration site, never in the core count.

DEADLINE. oculist-296.6 works backwards from 2026-10-31 to a 2026-10-17 store
submission. The human confirmed 2026-09-20 that this is not expected to slip. If it
does, the pack ships with fewer effects rather than later: cut promotion beads, not
the packaging beads or the fidelity bead.

PROMOTION CONTRACT (every promotion bead in this epic follows it verbatim)

Each promotion bead names one prototype function in
../artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html and ports it into
extension/content.js. The prototype is a sketch in viewport coordinates with
hardcoded colors; the shipped contract is stricter on every axis. READ animateTrail
in extension/content.js before starting -- it demonstrates every rule below -- and
read the close reasons of the prototype beads the bead names, because they record
beats that were deliberately cut and must not come back.

1. function animateX(rect). FIRST statement is the zero-rect guard:
   if (!rect || rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) return;
2. DOCUMENT coordinates, not viewport: rect.left + window.scrollX, rect.top +
   window.scrollY, position:absolute. The prototype uses position:fixed. A
   scrolled-page assertion is the only thing that catches a regression here.
   Viewport-fit decisions (does the figure fit above/beside the match) are still
   made from the PRE-SCROLL viewport rect -- room on screen is a viewport question
   even though the element is positioned in document space. Getting this backwards
   is the likely bug in any effect with a placement fallback; assert it.
3. Every element: class "oc-beacon oc-beacon-transient", pointer-events:none,
   z-index 2147483641 (line/trail layer) or 2147483642 (sprite/flash layer),
   appended to document.documentElement.
4. EVERY WAAPI animation is hung off the element cancelBeacons() actually selects,
   as el.__waapiAnims = [anim, ...]. destroyBeacon() reaches nothing else -- an
   animation not listed there fails gate G5. Animations on child nodes hang on the
   parent SVG, animateTrail's own precedent.
5. Each animation gets .finished.then(remove).catch(remove), so a cancel still
   cleans up.
6. Colors from getEffectiveColors().beacon with a literal fallback; size through
   getBeaconScale(); EVERY duration through getBeaconDuration(ms), with phase
   boundaries scaling with it rather than staying absolute. A character effect may
   keep a fixed identity palette where the prototype established one (the pumpkin's
   orange, the skeleton's ivory) and use the effective beacon color only where the
   neighbouring shipped character effects use it as an accessibility accent. No
   filters, no recoloring of the source text.
7. Lite Mode (settings.performanceMode): keep the recognizable silhouette and the
   effect's defining beat; drop glows, box-shadows and multi-state flicker. State
   in the bead's close reason exactly what Lite Mode drops.
8. Reduced motion is handled centrally in animate() and never reaches these
   functions. Do not add a check.
9. Start-point cascade, for any effect that travels from somewhere to the match:
   lastMouseX/lastMouseY if known, else the find bar (wrap) centre, else viewport
   centre -- animateTrail's cascade verbatim. Find-in-page is keyboard-driven, so
   the cursor is frequently null and that fallback is load-bearing. The mirrored
   branch must work for real, not just compile.
10. The original match DOM and its glyph pixels are untouched in every sampled
    frame. No effect paint enters a protected rectangle the prototype established.
11. No Math.random. Determinism is what the frame-comparison proofs rest on.

REGISTRATION -- five sites, four of them enforced by
test/effect_enumeration_sync.test.js. Read that file's header comment first; it
already understands the core/packed split (oculist-tdj.4) and scopes each site to
its own slice.
  a. effectX: 'Label', in the i18n object (near line 781).
  b. x: { label: i18n.effectX, run: animateX, pack: 'halloween' }, at the END of
     effectsRegistry. Do not reorder existing entries.
  c. extension/welcome.html:291, the "Optional effect packs:" sentence. Add the
     label in registry order. On the FIRST promotion, replace the literal
     placeholder "None in this release." Do NOT touch the core count digit.
  d. extension/welcome.html:425, the packed <option> block appended after the
     marker comment -- not the core mockup list.
  e. docs/index.html:497 and docs/index.html:611, the packed slices, same rule as
     (c). The core-twelve prose at :497 is untouched.

TEST -- one new file test/<effect>_effect.test.js, modeled on
test/trail_effect.test.js (Playwright + node:test + helpers/wait, tall-spacer
fixture). Every promotion covers, at minimum:
  - Document-space correctness: window.scrollTo(0, 500) before asserting.
  - Placement: each placement mode the prototype supports, at viewport edges, and
    the fallback when no legal placement fits.
  - Cancellation mid-animation: no .oc-beacon-transient nodes survive.
  - Natural completion: nothing remains in the DOM.
  - Lite Mode, toggled for real through chrome.storage.sync.
  - Pack enumeration: absent from the picker with enabledPacks empty, present when
    halloween is enabled, stored selection NOT rewritten when the pack is disabled,
    runtime fallback safe, selection restored on re-enable.

DONE-CRITERIA, every promotion bead
  - node --test test/effect_enumeration_sync.test.js FAILS after step (b) and
    before steps (c)-(e) -- run it and confirm, which proves the sites are
    load-bearing -- then PASSES once (c)-(e) are done.
  - node --test test/<effect>_effect.test.js passes.
  - node --test (whole suite) passes, in particular waapi_beacon_cancel.test.js and
    beacon_fade_persistent_overlays.test.js, which police the beacon lifecycle this
    effect now joins.
  - The core effect-count digit is unchanged.
  - Selecting the effect and pressing Enter on a match plays it correctly on a
    scrolled page, an unscrolled page, and at a viewport edge.

title: Shipped beacon can fade immediately after drawing on a long smooth scroll
description:
Found by the reviewer on oculist-1ta.12, in the SHIPPED extension, not the playground. User-facing.

An earlier claim in that bead's implementation report said extension/content.js already handled this correctly. That claim was wrong on this axis, and the reviewer measured it.

THE MISMATCH, all in extension/content.js:
• :5341 — scrollTimeout = setTimeout(onScrollEnd, 600) draws the beacon at 600ms even while the browser's smooth scroll is still running.
• :5412-5417 — triggerAutoScrollFlag() suppresses the scroll-fade for a fixed 800ms.
• :5543-5546 — handleScroll() calls fadeActiveBeacons() the moment that flag clears.

So on a scroll long enough that Chrome's smooth scroll outlasts 800ms, the extension's OWN scroll events arrive after the suppression window has closed and fade a beacon that was drawn only moments earlier. The user asked to find text, the beacon appears, and it immediately dissolves.

MEASURED IN THE PLAYGROUND, which reproduces the same 600/800 shape: Chrome's smooth scroll ran to 1034ms at a 3000px scroll distance and 1546ms at 12000px, both well past 800ms. 3000px is mundane. The playground effect self-dissolved 400ms after appearing instead of running its full 2200ms.

NOT YET REPRODUCED IN THE SHIPPED EXTENSION ITSELF — the finding is by code inspection of the three sites above plus the measured timings of the identical pattern. FIRST STEP IS TO REPRODUCE IT for real: a long page, a match far enough down that the smooth scrollIntoView runs past 800ms, and observe whether the beacon fades right after appearing. If it does not reproduce, find out what else protects it and record that, because the three line numbers above say it should.

FIX DIRECTION: stop keying the suppression to a fixed duration that can be shorter than the scroll it is suppressing. Keep the flag alive until the auto-scroll has actually stopped (scrollend, or last-scroll-event plus a grace period) rather than 800ms from when it started. Note :5313 already records that native scrollend and the debounce timer can both fire, so the machinery to know when scrolling really ended is present.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A reproduction case, or a recorded explanation of why it does not reproduce.
- A beacon drawn after a long smooth scroll survives its full intended lifetime.
- The existing scroll-staleness behaviour still holds: a genuine user scroll after the beacon is drawn still fades it.
- node --test passes in full.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. Reproduced first: the new test/beacon_survives_long_smooth_scroll.test.js goes red against unmodified content.js (reviewer re-proved this by reverting the file), confirming the 600ms draw / 800ms fixed suppression / handleScroll fade race. Fix keeps the suppression alive until scrolling actually stops - scrollend plus a 300ms grace re-armed by scroll events - instead of a fixed 800ms. Reviewer audited termination on six paths (no scrollend, no scroll at all, instant/reduced-motion, second navigation mid-scroll, destroy mid-scroll) and found no way to strand the flag. User-scroll staleness still guarded by a second test asserting the opacity 0 signature of fadeActiveBeacons, distinct from natural expiry. Follow-ups filed: oculist-30k, oculist-4fh, plus a suite-flake bead.

title: Effects land in the wrong place if the user scrolls mid-animation
description:
Reported by Chris 2026-09-05 against the playground prototypes.

SYMPTOM: scroll while an effect is running and its final landing spot is wrong. The travelling element and the thing it lands on are placed where the match WAS in viewport space, not where it is now.

CAUSE: the playground mounts every effect with baseStyle() at line 213, which is position:fixed, and reads the match once via matchRect() at line 172, which is getBoundingClientRect() and therefore viewport-relative. Nothing re-reads it or follows scroll. The scrollend listener at :3720 only settles the pre-fire scrollIntoView; it does nothing during the animation. So any scroll between fire and landing shifts the match by the scroll delta while the effect stays pinned to stale viewport coordinates.

THE FIX, DECIDED BY CHRIS 2026-09-05: when the user initiates a scroll, DISSOLVE THE ANIMATION AWAY. Its endpoint is no longer valid, so it should leave rather than chase the match. Do not implement document-coordinate tracking; that option was considered and rejected.

This matches existing shipped precedent rather than inventing a policy: extension/content.js already fades beacons out on scroll via fadeActiveBeacons(), and its reduced-motion path at :4023 records the reasoning that a brief opacity fade is a smaller dose of motion than leaving a stale beacon on screen. Read that comment and fadeActiveBeacons() before writing, and follow the same shape.

REQUIREMENTS
1. Trigger on the user INITIATING a scroll, not on scroll settling. A beacon that stays wrong for the whole scroll and only fades at scrollend is the bug with extra steps.
2. Dissolve, do not cut. An abrupt disappearance reads as a glitch. Match the fade idiom already used in these effects.
3. The pre-fire scrollIntoView at :3722 must NOT trigger the dissolve. That scroll is the effect's own doing and happens before the animation starts, so distinguish it rather than letting the effect kill itself on fire. This is the main trap in this bead.
4. After dissolving, tear down completely: .fx count 0, no orphaned WAAPI animations, no listener left attached. A scroll listener that outlives the effect is a leak, and content.js:1061 and :5372 both record prior bugs of exactly that kind.
5. Firing again after a scroll-dissolve must work normally.
6. Respect reduced motion, consistent with how these effects already treat it.

SCOPE TO ESTABLISH FIRST: baseStyle() is shared by every effect in the playground, so determine whether the staleness hits all of them or only the two new candidates (fxBatFlight, fxArrowShot). Report which. Implement the dissolve for the two new candidates; do not change other effects without saying so.

DO NOT REGRESS. The occlusion guarantees for both candidates were expensive and are verified: zero changed pixels inside the match rect across 19 scenarios. Re-run those sweeps, and add scrolling scenarios, which no previous sweep covered.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Initiating a scroll at any point during either effect dissolves it away cleanly; nothing is left pinned to a stale position.
- The effect's own pre-fire scrollIntoView does not trigger the dissolve. Verify by firing normally and confirming the effect runs to completion.
- Occlusion sweep still zero changed pixels for the established static scenarios, plus new scroll-during-animation scenarios.
- No listener, animation, or DOM node survives the dissolve; firing again works.
- No reflow, determinism preserved.
- Say explicitly whether the shipped extension or the two effects pending promotion in oculist-e2m carry the same staleness. File a separate bead if they do; do not fix them here.
close_reason: Scroll during either candidate effect now dissolves it rather than leaving it pinned to a stale viewport position. Failed first review on a self-dissolve at ordinary scroll distances (600ms fire fallback vs an 800ms fixed suppression window) and on cancel() snapping elements back instead of freezing them; both fixed on retry. Re-review measured full ~2200ms lifetimes at spacers 0-30000 under CPU throttling to 100x, dissolve on a real wheel in 10/10 cases, 0.0px rect displacement at freeze, and zero occlusion across 14 scenarios x 2 effects

title: Pack field, availableEffects resolver, and the enabledPacks setting
description:
The mechanism. No UI in this bead.

FILES: extension/content.js, extension/settings-migration.js.
Branch first - the inner repo is on main and must not be committed to directly.

STEPS
1. Add an optional `pack` field to effectsRegistry entries (content.js:880). No
   existing entry gets one; absent means core. Nothing changes behaviourally yet.
2. Add `enabledPacks: []` to the settings object (content.js:8). Persist it the same
   way every other key is persisted, and add it to settings-migration.js so existing
   users get the default rather than undefined. Read how the other keys migrate; do
   not invent a new mechanism.
3. Add ONE function, availableEffects(), returning the subset of effectsRegistry whose
   entries either have no `pack` or whose pack is in settings.enabledPacks.
4. Route EVERY registry read through it. There are four, and missing one is the
   obvious way to get this wrong - a disabled effect that still fires:
   - content.js:5739, the settings-panel picker enumeration
   - content.js:7686, the storage-change coercion
   - content.js:7696, the same coercion's second site
   - content.js:7768, the load-time coercion
   Search for `effectsRegistry` and confirm you have found them all; the list above
   was taken from a grep but verify it rather than trusting it.
5. IMPORTANT BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, do this deliberately: the existing coercion writes
   `settings.effect = 'hud'` when the selected effect is not found. That must NOT
   happen merely because a pack was disabled, or the user permanently loses their
   choice. Resolve to hud at RUN time (animate() at content.js:3930 already does
   `effectsRegistry[effectKey] || effectsRegistry.hud`) and leave the stored value
   alone. Keep the existing mutate-on-genuinely-unknown-key behaviour for real garbage
   values - an effect key that is in no pack and not in the registry at all is still
   corrupt input and should still be coerced.
6. Check the existing coercion tests still pass and update any that assert the
   mutation you just narrowed. settings_race.test.js, page_settings_race.test.js and
   display_preset_migration.test.js are the likely ones; find them rather than
   assuming.

DONE-CRITERIA
- With enabledPacks empty, behaviour is identical to today for all twelve effects.
- Adding a `pack: 'test'` field to one entry removes it from the picker, and selecting
  it via storage falls back to hud at run time WITHOUT rewriting settings.effect.
- Re-adding 'test' to enabledPacks restores that effect as the selection.
- A genuinely unknown effect key is still coerced to hud as before.
- `node --test` passes in full.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. Five registry read sites routed through availableEffects(), including animate() which the brief missed. Pack-disabled no longer mutates settings.effect; genuinely-unknown still coerced. enabledPacks defaults via the settings literal, not settings-migration.js, verified by trace. 308/308. Committed 7b324a2.

title: Optional effect packs
description:
Let users add or remove groups of effects. Decided with the human 2026-09-05.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT POSSIBLE. Chrome MV3 forbids remotely hosted code, so a genuine
downloadable add-on is a store-policy rejection, not an engineering problem. Every
effect ships inside the package; what the user controls is which ones are ACTIVE.
Approach chosen: ship all, gate by a settings toggle (approach A of three considered;
B was lazy injection via chrome.scripting.executeScript, rejected because injection
races against content.js init are the bug family this codebase fights hardest and the
Oct 13 freeze leaves no room for it; C was separate companion extensions, rejected
because it multiplies store listings and review cycles).

USER-FACING FRAMING IS A CONSTRAINT, NOT A PREFERENCE. Never "plugin", never "add-on",
never anything that reads as downloadable content. Say "effect pack" or "seasonal
effects". The repo already carries this rule because that framing is what makes a
store reviewer look twice, and this release folds everything into ONE submission that
cannot afford to bounce.

DESIGN
• effectsRegistry entries gain an optional `pack` field. Absent means core.
• One settings key, enabledPacks, an array of pack ids, persisted with the rest and
  added in settings-migration.js.
• A SINGLE resolver, availableEffects(), is the only thing that reads pack state. The
  registry is enumerated once for the picker (content.js:5739) and coerced in three
  places (7686, 7696, 7768). Filtering some and not others yields a disabled effect
  that still fires, which is the obvious way to get this wrong.
• Do NOT mutate settings.effect when a pack is disabled. Today's coercion rewrites it
  to 'hud'; doing that on pack toggle destroys the user's choice permanently. Coerce
  at resolution time and leave the stored value alone so re-enabling restores it.
• Default OFF, with a single dismissible prompt pointing at the toggle.
• No manifest change and NO NEW PERMISSIONS. That property is the main reason this
  approach was chosen; do not give it up without saying so.

PACK LAYOUT, ASSUMED - CORRECT IT IF WRONG. The `pack` field is a string, so any
number of packs works. Proposed for the October release: core stays exactly the twelve
effects that ship today, so no existing user's experience changes; 'halloween' holds
the seasonal ones (Bat Flight, Reanimation Jolt, Headless Horseman, and the Cheshire
grin if wanted); a second pack holds the non-seasonal new ones (Flappy, the archer,
the foot-tapper) since those are not Halloween and should not be in a Halloween pack.

KNOWN CONSEQUENCE, NOT A FOOTNOTE. test/effect_enumeration_sync.test.js hand-lists
every effect across four doc sites plus a literal count digit, and it exists precisely
because those lists went stale before. Packs break its assumption that the registry is
one flat roster every user sees. That test and those four sites have to learn about
packs BEFORE any packed effect is promoted into the registry, or promotion turns the
suite red.

This epic blocks the promotion beads in oculist-e2m and oculist-1ta - every one of
them adds a registry entry that now needs a pack decision.
close_reason: All six children closed. Packs ship gated, documented, prompted and now regression-guarded.

title: Flappy and Cheshire beacon effects, playground to shipped
description:
AMENDED 2026-09-20. BOTH EFFECTS ARE HALLOWEEN PACK EFFECTS, NOT CORE EFFECTS.
The human put Flappy and Cheshire in the Halloween pack, alongside the nine
character prototypes from oculist-1ta. They register with pack: 'halloween' and
are listed in the packed slice of every enumeration site; the core effect count
stays at twelve. The pack itself is seeded on by default and is free, so being
packed does not make either effect harder to reach on a fresh install. The
descriptions of oculist-e2m.5 and oculist-e2m.6 carry the exact registration
deltas. oculist-e2m.7's count sweep must not bump the core digit.

Two new beacon effects requested by name (not surfaced by scoring).

AMENDED 2026-09-04. This epic originally inherited its framing from oculist-3rv
(effects round, roster refresh, v1.8.0). That was a mistake: inner-repo commit
20d818c, "chore(beads): abandon the v1.8.0 effects experiment", called the whole
round off the day before — closing all eleven children of oculist-3rv and dropping
branch epic/oculist-effects-v1.8.0 and its single commit. Nothing from that
experiment ships. These two effects are a SEPARATE, later request and stand on
their own. There is no v1.8.0 label on this work and no dependency on oculist-296.

FLAPPY — a small bird flies from the cursor to the match on a Flappy Bird
trajectory: constant horizontal velocity, vertical velocity integrated under
constant gravity and reset to a fixed upward impulse at each flap. The result is a
sawtooth of parabolic arcs, not a sine wave. Physics generates the GEOMETRY once at
fire time; there is no runtime rAF loop. The sampled polyline is handed to CSS
offset-path with offset-rotate:auto, which is animateTrail's exact idiom and which
also gives Flappy Bird's own rotation rule (nose follows the velocity tangent) for
free. Arrival: the bird perches on the match's TOP EDGE (never its centre — a sprite
over the glyphs costs S2 x4 and S7 x2 and buys nothing on S1) and the absorption
flash animateTrail already uses fires on the match rect.

CHESHIRE — a hand-drawn cartoon cat fades in above the match, then its body fades
away while its wide toothy grin holds, settles, and pops before fading. "Remains
above the match" means it outlasts the body, NOT that it persists: a permanent
overlay would break the .oc-beacon-transient scroll-fade contract.

DESIGN CONSTANTS (settled with the human)
- Flappy arrival: perch + absorption flash. S1 is weighted x4 and a 24px sprite
  cannot carry it alone.
- Cheshire: small pop (scale 1.12 -> 1), NO TEETH GLOW. A glow was specified
  originally and attempted twice; both implementations measurably reduced the grin's
  legibility at exactly the 120ms the pop is meant to capture attention (an animated
  drop-shadow washed the mouth fill; a white halo layer cost 34% of the mouth-fill
  pixels and raised lavender wash 5.4x). The human dropped it 2026-09-04. The pop
  alone carries the beat.
- The gamedev.stackexchange post the human linked could not be fetched (blocked).
  The trajectory is built from the model SHAPE, which is what matters since flight
  time comes from getBeaconDuration() and distance from geometry. Gravity and flap
  impulse are named tunables; pinning the post's numbers is a one-line change.

PROCESS: prototype both in artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html, fired from
their own "New candidates (post round 6)" sidebar divider — NOT via the retired
fire-by-index blind harness. Score on a fresh sheet. Then promote whatever clears
into extension/content.js with tests and docs.

CONSTRAINTS
- Branch: epic/oculist-flappy-cheshire in the OUTER repo (Projects/oculist) for the
  playground and score sheets. The inner code repo (repo/) is on main and will need
  its own branch before anything touches extension/content.js.
- The Fable 5.1 round-6 candidates and the blind testing artifact they shipped with
  are ABANDONED: playground candidates 31-38, the #fire-index input, the
  SHIPPED_LABELS divider block and its frozen numbering, and
  artifacts/outputs/effects-round6-scores.md. They stay in place, untouched and
  unused. Do not extend, re-index or score against any of them.
- The G1-G6 gates and the S1-S9 weighted rubric are NOT abandoned; they predate round
  6 and come from ~/.claude/plans/plan-a-blog-post-parallel-wall.md.
- Score sheets stay private, under Projects/oculist/artifacts/outputs/.
- No user-facing copy may use the word "plugin".

title: Extend waapi_beacon_cancel.test.js: registry-derive keys, mount/anchor/zero-rect asserts, reduced-motion describe
description:
Extend test/waapi_beacon_cancel.test.js so its per-effect loop is derived from the registry and covers the assertions a smoke test would add. No new browser-launching test file (52 already launch; npm test runs --test-concurrency=4 and a 53rd risks the 180s starvation PRIME.md warns about).

title: Assemble the final dashboard paste-set and run the pre-submission sweep
description:

WHY THIS EXISTS: oculist-rnr produced a submission that drifted out of date before it was ever used, because nothing re-checked the artifacts as a set at the moment of submission. This task is that final gate. Its output is something the human can work straight through at the Developer Dashboard without re-deriving anything.

2. Verify the zip is newer than the newest commit touching extension/. If any extension/ commit postdates the zip, STOP and report: the zip is stale again and oculist-296.2 must be rerun. This is the exact failure this epic exists to correct, so check it rather than assuming.

comments.text:
ADDED STEP, from the oculist-296.1 review (2026-09-02): RE-STAMP THE CHANGELOG 1.7.0 DATE as part of assembling the paste-set.

Why. oculist-296.1 set the heading to '## [1.7.0] — 2026-09-01', the last commit date in the reconciled set. That is deliberately provisional. Keep a Changelog dates a RELEASE, and v1.7.0 is not released (only v1.5.0 is tagged). title: Keep named-condition shortcut in the wizard, persist only functional presets
description:
REVISED 2026-08-30 after the human raised that stripping clinical vocabulary is an accessibility regression. Operating systems name these conditions in their own accessibility settings (macOS and Windows colour filters both list Protanopia/Deuteranopia/Tritanopia), and a user with a known diagnosis should not have to re-derive it by comparing swatches.

DESIGN: split clinical naming from clinical STORAGE by lifetime. Keep the condition names in the UI as a one-click shortcut; use the answer TRANSIENTLY, in memory, to select a preset; persist only the functional result from oculist-rnr.12. Nothing about the user's health is ever written to disk or synced.

Current wizard (extension/welcome.html:236-272) asks clinically AND persists the answer. Steps 1 and 3 are the clinical ones ('Do you experience color blindness?' with Deuteranopia/Protanopia/Tritanopia options; 'Do you experience eye strain').

Steps:
1. Keep the named-condition options in the wizard UI. Do NOT delete the clinical vocabulary from welcome.html. A user who knows their diagnosis keeps the direct path.
2. ADD a second entry point alongside it: a sample-comparison path for users who do not know or prefer not to say. Step 1 offers both - pick a named option, or compare rendered colour samples and choose the clearest. Both paths must reach the same set of presets.
3. Make the clinical answer TRANSIENT. welcome.js:159-167 resolves the selection; from there it must map straight to the functional preset key from oculist-rnr.12 and persist ONLY that. The condition string must never be written to chrome.storage.sync, chrome.storage.session, chrome.storage.local, localStorage, or any other sink, and must never be transmitted.
4. Audit the whole wizard path for incidental persistence of the clinical answer: intermediate wizard state, resume-after-reload state, the setupWizardCompleted flag's payload, and anything popup.js reads back. If the wizard persists partial progress, ensure the clinical selection is not part of what is stored.
5. Accept the UX consequence and handle it deliberately: because the condition is not stored, reopening settings later shows the FUNCTIONAL preset name, not 'Deuteranopia'. Make that display sensible and non-confusing (e.g. a clear preset name plus a way to re-run the picker). Do not fake persistence by stashing the condition somewhere.
6. Preserve accessibility throughout. Every option, named or sample, must be keyboard reachable, have an accessible name describing the visual result, and not rely on colour alone to be distinguishable. This wizard serves users with vision differences; the change must not degrade it for them.

Edge cases:
- Do NOT change which preset a given answer produces. Behaviour stays identical for every existing choice.
- The sample path must be genuinely usable by someone with the deficiency it serves: samples need a non-colour distinguishing cue (label, shape, or position), since a user may not discriminate the colour axis being demonstrated.
- If a sample-based step 1 needs assets that do not exist, use text descriptions of the visible result ('warmer reds', 'stronger blue-yellow separation') for that path rather than dropping it. Report what you did.
- Step 3's eye-strain wording should become preference-framed ('How much animation do you want?') since 'do you experience eye strain' is a symptom question with no diagnostic shortcut value. Steps 2 and 4 likewise: ask about the visible result.

Done-criteria:
- The named-condition shortcut still exists in the wizard UI.
- A sample/preference path exists alongside it, reaching the same presets.
- grep across ALL storage sinks confirms no clinical string is ever persisted: no condition name in chrome.storage.*, localStorage, or any transmitted payload.
- The wizard produces the same presets and the same rendering outcomes as before.
- Every option keyboard reachable with a descriptive accessible name; samples distinguishable without relying on colour.
- npm test passes at exactly 212 tests, 212 pass, 0 fail, PLUS a test asserting the clinical selection is not persisted by the wizard.

title: Convert visionProfile from clinical labels to functional preset keys, with migration
description:
HUMAN DECISION 2026-08-30: Oculist moves from the Clinical Profile row to the Functional Preset row of the CWS data-classification mapping. Persist rendering values, not condition names. Existing users get MIGRATE AND OVERWRITE.

Current state (verified):
- visionSettings (content.js:19) is ALREADY purely functional: colorPalette, customColors{matchColor,activeColor,beaconColor}, beaconSize, animationSpeed, borderStyle, textLabels, magnifier, motionSensitivity. Consumed at content.js:498-535, 3029, 3071, 3100, 3169, 3365, 4665. Leave this field alone.
- visionProfile is the ONLY clinical artifact. Values written: 'color-blind-deuteranopia', 'color-blind-protanopia', 'color-blind-tritanopia' (welcome.js:34,42,50), 'low-vision' (welcome.js:26), 'eye-strain' (welcome.js:58), 'custom' (popup.js:110,210), null (popup.js:191, welcome.js:659).
- visionProfile is LOAD-BEARING, not decorative: content.js:2873 branches on 'eye-strain'; content.js:5092 renders a display label. Both must keep working.

This bead changes the STORAGE SCHEMA and its consumers ONLY. The wizard's question wording is a separate bead (oculist-rnr.13) - do NOT reword questions here.

Steps:
1. Replace the visionProfile field with a functional key. Proposed name: displayPreset, holding functional values. Mapping, preserving current behaviour exactly:
   - 'low-vision'                -> 'high-contrast'
   - 'color-blind-deuteranopia'  -> 'rg-adjust-deut'
   - 'color-blind-protanopia'    -> 'rg-adjust-prot'
   - 'color-blind-tritanopia'    -> 'by-adjust'
   - 'eye-strain'                -> 'reduced-motion'
   - 'custom'                    -> 'custom'
   - null                        -> null
   If you find a better functional vocabulary that stays behaviour-identical and carries no clinical term, use it and say so in your report. The hard rule: NO stored value may name a medical condition.
2. Update SETTINGS_KEYS (content.js:44) and the defaults block (content.js:18).
3. Update every consumer: content.js:2873 (the eye-strain branch), content.js:5092 (the display label - it must render functional wording now, not 'Color Blind'), popup.js:110/151/191/210, welcome.js:659.
4. MIGRATION, load-bearing. On settings load, if a stored oc-settings carries the old visionProfile field, map it through the table above into the new key, WRITE the migrated settings back, and DELETE the old visionProfile field from chrome.storage.sync. After migration no clinical string may remain in storage. Put the migration where settings are first read, and make it idempotent - it must be safe to run on every load and a no-op once migrated.
5. Handle the null/absent cases: a user who never ran the wizard, and a user mid-wizard. Neither may throw.

Edge cases:
- The settings write path echoes through chrome.storage.onChanged and has self-write detection (content.js:48-60, pendingSelfWrites). A migration write MUST NOT tear down the panel or trigger an echo loop. Read that comment block before writing the migration.
- popup.js:110 and :210 set 'custom' when the user hand-edits a value; that behaviour stays.
- Do NOT change visionSettings, and do NOT change any rendering behaviour. This is a rename plus migration; the extension must look and behave identically before and after.

Done-criteria:
- grep -rniE 'deuteranopia|protanopia|tritanopia|color-blind|colorblind|eye-strain|low-vision' extension/*.js returns NOTHING outside welcome.html question text (which oculist-rnr.13 handles).
- No stored value names a medical condition.
- Migration maps old to new, writes back, deletes the old field, and is idempotent.
- Rendering behaviour is unchanged for every preset.
- npm test passes at exactly 212 tests, 212 pass, 0 fail, PLUS new tests covering the migration: each old value maps correctly, migration is idempotent, and absent/null profiles do not throw.

title: popup.html hardcodes version 'v1.5.0', manifest.json is 1.7.0
description: Discovered during oculist-rnr.3 and confirmed by review. extension/popup.html:473 hardcodes 'v1.5.0' while extension/manifest.json is 1.7.0. Every user who opens the toolbar popup in the v1.7.0 build sees v1.5.0, and the string is legible in screenshots/05-vision-profiles.png, which is bound for the store listing. Shipping a v1.7.0 listing whose screenshot reads v1.5.0 invites reviewer suspicion that the package does not match the listing. Fix the SOURCE of the recurrence, not just the digits. Hardcoding '1.7.0' recreates this bug at the next release. Steps: 1. In extension/popup.js, set the version text at runtime from chrome.runtime.getManifest().version rather than leaving it in markup. Give the span a stable id or reuse an existing selector; keep the leading 'v' prefix so the rendered string stays 'v1.7.0'. 2. In extension/popup.html:473, leave the span empty (or with a neutral placeholder) so no version literal remains in markup. Verify no other file hardcodes a version string: grep -rn 'v1\.[0-9]' extension/ and fix any other stale literal found the same way. 3. Re-run the capture so the store screenshots show the correct version: node scripts/screenshots.js 4. Confirm screenshots/05-vision-profiles.png now reads v1.7.0, and that all 5 PNGs remain exactly 1280x800. Edge cases: - chrome.runtime.getManifest() is synchronous and available in popup context; do NOT wrap it in an async storage call. - If the popup renders before the DOM node exists, set the text after DOMContentLoaded or wherever popup.js already does its initial render. Follow the file's existing initialisation pattern. - Do NOT bump any version number anywhere. manifest.json is already correct at 1.7.0. - If the recapture changes other screenshots incidentally, that is fine, but all 5 must remain 1280x800 and 02-multi-term-list.png must still show 3 chips with the active/dim distinction. title: Four new beacon effects (registry 9 to 13)
description:
Add Speed Lines, Chrono Tunnel, Light Cycle and Cyber-Vision to effectsRegistry, taking it from 9 effects to 13. Visual design is APPROVED and mocked up live at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2ecca129-a2f3-478d-8a3c-d84ad87f72f5 - this epic is implementation, not design exploration. Open the mockup before starting any effect bead; it is the spec.

TWO DECISIONS ALREADY MADE BY THE OPERATOR, do not revisit:
1. Light Cycle ships ALONGSIDE the existing trail effect. animateTrail is NOT removed. The two overlap visibly (both trace an L-path to the match) and that is accepted for now; a follow-up bead can revisit once both are live.
2. Chrono Tunnel's hue RIDES getEffectiveColors().beacon with a bounded sweep, NOT the full 360-degree spectrum of the mockup. Oculist is a vision-accessibility product with a user-set beacon colour and a motionSensitivity setting; full-spectrum cycling would ignore both.

SHARED CONTRACTS every effect must follow, verified in extension/content.js:
- Signature animateX(rect); bail immediately on !rect || rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0.
- Container div, className 'oc-beacon', position:absolute at DOCUMENT coords (rect.left + window.scrollX, rect.top + window.scrollY), pointer-events:none, z-index 2147483640, appended to document.documentElement NOT body. See drawStaticActiveBorder (content.js:2038) and animateElectronCloud (content.js:1895) for the working pattern.
- Colour from getEffectiveColors().beacon. Size from getBeaconScale(). EVERY duration wrapped in getBeaconDuration(base) so the animationSpeed setting works.
- Canvas effects MUST set container.__rafId = animFrameId on every frame, or cancelBeacons() (content.js:818-825) cannot cancel them and beacons leak across searches.
- Self-removal via setTimeout(function(){ container.remove(); }, total).
- Lite Mode: settings.performanceMode scales counts and geometry DOWN inside the effect function.
- Reduced motion is handled CENTRALLY by animate() (content.js:2599-2623), which short-circuits to animateReducedMotion() BEFORE dispatching to the registry. Individual effects must NOT add their own reduced-motion branch.
- i18n label near content.js:577-585; registry entry near content.js:682-690.
- Plain var/function inside the IIFE. No ES modules, no new dependencies.

TESTING: node --test plus Playwright, run as OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE=3 npm test (160 tests at epic start; plain npm test flakes on the dev box, see oculist-li8). Budgets derive from test/helpers/wait.js, never hardcoded. Test hooks live under window.__ocTest. Model on test/dispersion_bloom.test.js and test/trail_effect.test.js. Every effect needs coverage that FAILS against a plausible wrong implementation, covers its Lite Mode path, and asserts no .oc-beacon element leaks.

title: Shipped v1.5.0: find-in-page self-matches Oculist's own overlay text
description:
CONFIRMED SHIPPED DEFECT in released v1.6.0. Already fixed on epic/oculist-l6m by
oculist-l6m.4; this bead exists so the fix is tracked and a patch release can be considered
rather than the fix being buried in a feature commit.

Cause: buildPageIndex()'s traverse() recursed into any child.shadowRoot with no exclusion.
#oc-wrap is attachShadow({mode:'open'}) and appended to document.body, so traverse
(document.body) walked Oculist's own overlay text into the searchable flat text.

Repro on released v1.6.0, on a page containing zero occurrences of the word "of":
1. Ctrl+F, search "cat" -> overlay shows "1 of 3"
2. Search "of" -> overlay shows "1 of 1"
The match does not exist on the page. It is the overlay's own count text.

Same class of failure for i18n.noMatch ("no match") and for every settings-panel label
while the gear panel is open.

Fix applied in .4: added `child !== wrap` to the element-skip guard in traverse().
Verified by reverting only that guard in a copied tree and driving both builds through
Playwright.

Done: decide whether this warrants a v1.6.1 patch release ahead of the v1.7.0 feature
merge, and record the decision here.
notes:
CORRECTION: this bead originally said 'shipped v1.6.0'. The oculist-l6m.10 review established that 1.6.0 NEVER SHIPPED (only v1.5.0 is tagged, dist/ holds no 1.6.0 artifact, and commit 26d10f6 sets the convention that a dated CHANGELOG heading means released). The affected released version is therefore v1.5.0, the current Chrome Web Store build. The hotfix decision is whether to patch v1.5.0 ahead of the v1.7.0 feature merge, or let v1.7.0 carry the fix.
SKIPPED by the /goal follow-up run, deliberately and not as an oversight. This bead's content is a decision reserved to the human (patch v1.5.0 ahead of the v1.7.0 merge, or let v1.7.0 carry the fix). An implementer dispatched at it would be inventing the answer. Left open and unclaimed.

title: Working-list session storage plumbing (oc-worklist)
description:
Give the content script read/write access to a session-scoped working list.

Steps:
1. repo/extension/background.js: at service-worker startup call
   chrome.storage.session.setAccessLevel({accessLevel: 'TRUSTED_AND_UNTRUSTED_CONTEXTS'}).
   Wrap in try/catch; older Chrome without setAccessLevel must not break the worker.
2. repo/extension/content.js: add loadWorkList() and saveWorkList(list) around
   chrome.storage.session key 'oc-worklist', shape {terms: string[], activeIndex: number}.
3. Both helpers check chrome.runtime.lastError. A failed read resolves to
   {terms: [], activeIndex: -1} so the overlay degrades to today's single-term behaviour
   with no error shown to the user.
4. Do NOT touch 'oc-settings', SETTINGS_KEYS, or the pendingSelfWrites echo-suppression.

Edge cases: storage.session may be undefined in a content script if step 1 failed; guard
for it. Reads must never throw into the overlay mount path.

Done: a test asserts a saved working list round-trips, and that a rejected/failed read
yields the empty default rather than throwing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Multi-term search lists (v1.7.0)
description:
Let the user hold a list of search terms, run them against the current page, and carry
the list to the next page. One term is active at a time with the full existing beacon
treatment; the rest stay dim-highlighted. Named lists persist in sync storage.

Approved design: ../artifacts/plans/v1.7.0-2026-08-25-multi-term-lists-design.md
(from repo root: /Users/ccho/Documents/Projects/oculist/artifacts/plans/v1.7.0-2026-08-25-multi-term-lists-design.md)

Shape of the change:
- performSearch() splits into buildPageIndex() + findRanges(); performListSearch() runs
  the index once and findRanges per term.
- searchRanges stays the active term's ranges, so findNext/highlightActiveRange/beacons/
  viewport markers need no changes.
- Three CSS.highlights registries with explicit priorities: dim(0) < match(1) < active(2).
- Working list in chrome.storage.session (oc-worklist); saved lists in chrome.storage.sync
  one key per list (oc-list-<id>).
- No new manifest permissions.

Non-goals: merged cross-term navigation, auto-running a list on page load, list management
in the popup.
close_reason: Closed

title: Stop DOM-mutation rescan from scrolling the viewport back to the active match
description: Oculist's MutationObserver-driven rescan called highlightActiveRange(false), which ran element.scrollIntoView(...) and yanked the viewport back to the active match whenever the page mutated (lazy-load, infinite scroll) while the user was scrolling elsewhere. Fix: added skipScroll parameter to highlightActiveRange, passed true from rescanAfterMutation, and gated the scroll branch on !skipScroll. Interactive navigation (typing search, prev/next, replay) is unaffected.
close_reason: Closed

title: Reanimation Jolt arc pulses at Animation Speed fast: 250ms onsets (4 Hz), 180ms gap
description: From the oculist-nq1x.8 review 2026-09-23. The arc flashes twice per clip, a tiny area, which passes WCAG 2.3.1 (fewer than 3 flashes in any second) at every speed. But the contract's durFactor scaling puts the two pulse onsets 250ms apart at fast (4 Hz) with a 180ms gap, which sits inside the bead's literal '3-50 Hz' G4 wording and below oculist-4v2u's 'at least 350ms apart' criterion, which was measured at normal speed. Decide: accept (two pulses total cannot sustain a frequency), or floor the inter-pulse gap at 350ms regardless of Animation Speed.

title: chip_row.test.js 'Enter with a new term adds a chip' loses the chip under contention
description:
Measured 2026-09-22 while proving oculist-vr2p (npm test concurrency/timeout flake).
Third distinct failure signature seen alongside oculist-e5c5/oculist-6d95 -- filing
separately since its mechanism is unclear and it is not a poll-timeout (so not
addressable by that bead's sanctioned fix shape of honouring OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE
or tuning concurrency).

test at test/chip_row.test.js:373:3
'Enter with a new term adds a chip, activates it, and next-match still works'
AssertionError: chipTerms() returned [] immediately after addTerm('quarklet'), expected
['quarklet']. Fails fast (106ms-342ms), not a timeout.

Seen twice this session under contention: once in a synthetic 6-worker CPU-load repro
of the full suite (scratchpad/before_full_contend1.log, this same assertion, same
actual/expected), and once in final6.log of the post-vr2p-fix 8-run proof (alongside
two other unrelated failures in the same run -- available_effects_malformed_packs's
oculist-e5c5 race and a genuine stale_mount_guard LONG_TIMEOUT contention timeout, so
that run was under unusually heavy load overall). 0 occurrences in ~15 other full-suite
runs this session, isolation runs not attempted.

addTerm() (test/chip_row.test.js:210) already page.waitForFunction()s for the chip to
land (with POLL_TIMEOUT) AND waits for the chrome.storage.session persistWorkList()
write to settle before returning -- so by the time the failing assert.deepStrictEqual
runs, the chip should already be confirmed present. Something removes or fails to
render it in the gap between that wait resolving and the very next
page.locator(CHIP_TERM).allTextContents() call, only under heavy load. Not
investigated further: could be a stale/false-positive read in the waitForFunction poll,
a debounced re-render clobbering the chip row when the page's main thread is heavily
CPU-starved, or an ordering issue with a neighboring test/hook. FIX SHAPE: not
determined -- start by reproducing reliably (scripts/under-cpu-load.sh against just
this file, or a tight loop) before proposing a fix.
close_reason: Root cause: the mount-time loadWorkList restore (first get denied pre-grant, retried late) overwrote chips added since mount. Fix: per-mount touched/replaced flags; a late restore is kept as the old restore when untouched, dropped after add-then-remove or loadSavedList, else merged (restored first, user's terms kept under the 10-term cap, user's term active, rescan, save). Deterministic delayed-get tests red then green for each rule; chip_row/list_search/list_menu 3/3 under 8-worker load; npm test 405/405.

title: boneassembly_effect.test.js mid-sequence timing assertions have thin margin and can fail under load
description:
Measured 2026-09-22 while proving oculist-vr2p (npm test concurrency/timeout flake).
Different mechanism from that bead, filed separately per its own instruction not to
touch timing-behavior waits.

test at test/boneassembly_effect.test.js:392:3
'the figure survives past the earliest scatter-in piece's own finish, stays mounted
through the collapse, and is still present just before the natural end'
AssertionError: count of [data-ba-piece] elements 0 !== 8 at the ~2250ms checkpoint
(2696.379125ms total test time; full run/final3.log this session).

CAUSE: the test uses page.waitForTimeout(800)/(700)/(750) (real wall-clock Node-side
sleeps, not covered by OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE or any polling helper in
test/helpers/wait.js) to check the DOM at fixed elapsed offsets (~800ms, ~1500ms,
~2250ms) against the animation's own timeline, which naturally ends at ~2370ms
(COLLAPSE_START 1430 + COLLAPSE_DUR + HEAP_HOLD + FADE_DUR). The last checkpoint
(~2250ms) has only ~120ms of margin before the figure's own natural removal.

Under contention (concurrent Playwright/Chromium processes from the rest of the
suite -- the same contention oculist-vr2p's fix reduces but does not eliminate),
Node/Playwright-side scheduling (the CDP round trip for page.evaluate(), the
waitForTimeout() timer itself) can lag behind the browser's own animation clock
(WAAPI/compositor-driven, governed by real time independent of main-thread
contention). If that lag pushes the actual elapsed time past ~2370ms before the
evaluate() call fires, the figure has already been removed by the time the test
checks, and the assertion (correctly reporting a real difference) fails.

This is a genuine "wait that asserts timing behaviour" per oculist-vr2p's own
brief -- raising it is explicitly out of that bead's sanctioned fix shape, so
filing rather than fixing. FIX SHAPE (not investigated further): either give the
final checkpoint materially more margin before the natural end, or replace the
fixed waitForTimeout+snapshot with a poll that asserts "still mounted continuously
until instant X" without depending on Node-side timer/IPC precision, or read the
WAAPI animation's own currentTime instead of wall-clock elapsed.

Evidence: 1 failure in 5 full-suite runs at the post-vr2p-fix config
(OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE=3, --test-concurrency=2) this session
(scratchpad/runs_final.tsv row 3, final3.log). Introduced same-day by 9bba8bf
(oculist-nq1x.5, Bone Assembly promotion) which added this file; its own close
reason already noted "npm test 345/345 on 2 of 3 runs, the third a pre-existing
load timeout also seen on main" without distinguishing this failure mode from the
one oculist-vr2p was filed for.
close_reason: Duplicate of oculist-nq1x.17 (same boneassembly_effect fixed-wait presence test).

title: Promote Vine Swing into the Halloween pack
description:
Promote Vine Swing into the Halloween pack.

FOLLOW THE PROMOTION CONTRACT in the description of the parent epic oculist-nq1x
VERBATIM -- the shipped lifecycle rules, the five registration sites, the minimum
test set and the shared done-criteria all live there and are not repeated here.
Read it before you read anything else. Read animateTrail in extension/content.js
next. Then read the sources below.

SOURCE
- Prototype: fxVineSwing, artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html:6426
- Playground registry key and label: vineswing: { label: 'Vine Swing', run: fxVineSwing }
- Prototype bead history, READ THE CLOSE REASONS: oculist-1ta.4
  They record beats that were deliberately cut and defects that were already fixed.
  A redraw or a "cleanup" that restores one of them is a regression, not an
  improvement.

REGISTRATION, the effect-specific values for the contract's steps (a) and (b)
  a. effectVineSwing: 'Vine Swing',
  b. vineswing: { label: i18n.effectVineSwing, run: animateVineSwing, pack: 'halloween' },
     at the END of effectsRegistry. Do not reorder existing entries.
Test file: test/vineswing_effect.test.js

EFFECT-SPECIFIC NOTES
- The figure swings in on an anchored vine, so it needs room ABOVE the match. The
  above/below placement decision is made from the pre-scroll viewport rect per
  contract rule 2 -- the likely bug, and the thing to assert first.
- The swing arc sweeps a wide area; verify no paint enters the match rect at any
  sampled frame of the arc, not only at arrival.

BLOCKED ON the pack registration bead (PACK_LABELS.halloween and the default-on
seeding). Do not introduce the pack id, the label or the default here. If
PACK_LABELS.halloween is missing when you start, stop and report it.


AMENDED 2026-09-23 (oculist-8qrc): checked against fxVineSwing, artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html:6426, and oculist-1ta.4's close reason.

WRONG. "The above/below placement decision is made from the pre-scroll viewport rect... the likely bug" is not how this effect works, and this is the same class of template-copied error nq1x.6 made. fxVineSwing has NO above/below decision: the vine is UNCONDITIONALLY anchored off-screen above (PIVOT_Y starts at -70, always above the viewport top; oculist-1ta.4's own description: "The vine is anchored OFF-SCREEN above"). There is no below option and nothing to fall back to. When the match sits close to the viewport top, the code does not switch sides -- it shortens the vine length L (down to a floor of L_FLOOR=120, below which "it no longer reads as a swing") and, if that alone is not enough, pushes PIVOT_Y further off-screen, so that releaseFeetY (the deepest point of the arc) is clamped to never exceed r.top - SAFE_MARGIN (12px) by construction, for any r.top. 1ta.4's close reason confirms this was tested and holds: "min clearance 13.86px in the near-top-of-viewport probe." The thing to assert first is therefore this length/pivot clamp at a match near the viewport top (both pre-scroll, since rule 2 does still govern this fit calculation), not a placement-side switch that does not exist.

CORRECT. The second note ("verify no paint enters the match rect at any sampled frame of the arc, not only at arrival") matches the code precisely: REACH_TOWARD/REACH_AWAY are derived by sampling every degree of the swing's entry sweep (theta in [-theta0Mag, 0]) against the figure's bounding corners, specifically so the whole arc -- not just the landing point -- stays clear of #match.

No missing prototype-bead citations: oculist-1ta.4 is the only prototype-history bead for this effect (a single clean pass with no later defect series or v2 redraw, unlike its siblings), so the existing citation list is complete.
close_reason: Vine Swing promoted into the Halloween pack (animateVineSwing, content.js). Final review PASS after one retry: resize hard cut (hardCutVineSwing) is load-bearing (widening 1120->1200 reflow: delta 206 without it, 0 with) and its listener returns to baseline on completion and cancel; cursor-independence test now pins the swing figure and landing box within 3px; mirrored branch pins the scale(-1,1) art and far-side-of-Px start on both branches. Top-of-viewport L_FLOOR/PIVOT_Y clamp pinned per the AMENDED note (no above/below decision exists). Each fix proven red by mutation. vineswing 14/14, npm test 507/508 (one tentaclerise load flake, passes alone; oculist-6fhj). REACH_TOWARD cannot be made the binding term by any fixture (documented). Rule 9 exception per oculist-i8zu. Lite Mode drops nothing (no filter or box-shadow in the shipped art).

- Prototype bead history, READ THE CLOSE REASONS: oculist-1ta.2, oculist-1ta.9, oculist-1ta.11, oculist-1ta.15, oculist-1ta.17, oculist-1ta.18, oculist-1ta.19, oculist-1ta.20

EFFECT-SPECIFIC NOTES
- oculist-1ta.9: the archer's corner could flip between fires when the match sits at
  viewport centre. Corner selection must be stable across repeated fires on the same
  match -- assert it by firing twice and comparing, not by inspecting the code.
- The bycocket and feather went through four shape beads (.17 through .20) to read at
  78px. Port the final geometry exactly; the earlier shapes were rejected at size.

  before writing the new one; do not duplicate what it already covers.

BLOCKED ON the pack registration bead (PACK_LABELS.halloween and the default-on
seeding). Do not introduce the pack id, the label or the default here. If
PACK_LABELS.halloween is missing when you start, stop and report it.


AMENDED 2026-09-23 (oculist-8qrc): checked against fxArrowShot, artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html:4529, and the close reasons of every prototype bead touching this effect.

WRONG. "oculist-1ta.15 set STRIKE_GAP to 12" is incorrect. 1ta.15's own close reason: "STRIKE_GAP 12->8, the smallest value that sweeps completely clean, per Chris's instruction." The shipped/current value in the code is `var STRIKE_GAP = 8;`, confirmed again by 1ta.19's close reason ("Reviewer independently confirmed the sweep clean at STRIKE_GAP 8") and by oculist-uxa0's close reason (cliff reconfirmed: "8 clean / 7 dirty"). Porting STRIKE_GAP=12 as this note instructs would ship the exact "reads less planted" defect 1ta.15 was filed to fix. It is also fragile in the other direction: oculist-uxa0 corrected the exact magnitude -- STRIKE_GAP=7 fails by 1px at font sizes 25-26 at a wide 1280x900 viewport (not 1-2px at 22-26, an earlier, superseded reading) -- 8 is "one pixel above a cliff," so it must be ported as exactly 8, not rounded or "cleaned up."

CORRECT, the other three notes: the corner-stability instruction (1ta.9 -- note this was closed by disproving the premise mathematically rather than by adding a guard; the closed-form margin is 3.1-6.7px across all 46 left-plan scenarios, so it never actually flips, but "assert by firing twice and comparing" is still the right test), the bycocket/feather geometry (1ta.17 through .20), and the existing test/arrowshot-forced-below.check.js from oculist-c6pk are all verified against the code and the close reasons.

MISSING. The prototype bead history list cites only cosmetic/geometry beads (1ta.2, .9, .11, .15, .17-.20) and omits the two beads that define the impact-plan chooser's actual safety mechanism: oculist-aouc ("occlusion-sweep FORCED-LANDING block: arrowshot's unguarded plan fallback overlaps the match at degenerate full-width geometry" -- the fallback-push logic, capped so the flight never reverses, verified across 1.83M grid and 400k random geometries) and oculist-q4nl ("short viewports with a centred match put the archer on the match row" -- the baseline-vs-candidate safety check that only takes an improving fallback). These are the most load-bearing, least obvious part of this effect's geometry; a "cleanup" of the fallback-push arithmetic is exactly the kind of regression these two beads exist to prevent.
