AMENDED 2026-09-23 (oculist-8qrc): checked against fxBatFlight, artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html:3887, and the close reasons of every prototype bead touching this effect.

WRONG, note 1's start-point description and its conclusion (corrected on reviewer's finding). The start point is NOT off-screen. For a right/left landing (effects-playground.html:4134-4137), startX is `Math.min(vw - 4, Math.max(vw - INSET, r.right + GAP + BAT_W / 2))` on the right or `Math.max(4, Math.min(INSET, r.left - GAP - BAT_W / 2))` on the left -- both land ON-screen, 4 to 40px inside the viewport edge, derived from r.right/r.left. For an above/below landing (effects-playground.html:4150-4152), startX = endX and startY = endY +/- 220 (clamped to the viewport) -- derived from the match's own endX/endY/mcy. The file-wide absence of lastMouseX/lastMouseY proves nothing about whether rule 9 applies: NO playground effect reads the cursor (the playground has no mouse tracking at all), while rule 9 governs the SHIPPED port -- extension/content.js:890 tracks lastMouseX/lastMouseY module-wide for exactly this purpose. On its face, rule 9 DOES apply here, because the bat travels to the match.

However, the prototype's header comment (effects-playground.html:3880-3881: "the flight's whole x-range stays outside the match's own x-range by construction") and the code at effects-playground.html:4129-4132 ("Approach from the same side as the landing side, so the bat's x stays on that side of the match for the WHOLE flight") establish that this effect deliberately pins its x-range to the landing side for the entire flight, not just at arrival. Starting from lastMouseX/lastMouseY (or the find-bar/viewport-centre fallback) instead could put the launch point on the wrong side of the match, or directly above/below it, walking the flight path across the match mid-transit -- a direct conflict with rule 10 (the match and its glyph pixels must be untouched in every sampled frame).

RESOLVED, see RULE 9 DECIDED below (was: DECISION NEEDED (Chris)) before dispatch: honor rule 9 within the landing-side constraint (e.g. clamp a cursor/find-bar start to the chosen side rather than using it verbatim), or record an explicit rule 9 deviation grounded in rule 10. Not resolved here.

MISSING. The prototype bead history list omits oculist-1ta.8 ("Mist fade-out can tint the match in the below-landing fallback"), even though the parent epic's own close reason for nq1x.6 states plainly that 1ta.8 "belongs to oculist-1ta.1, Bat Flight/Dracula." fxBatFlight DOES have a full beside-then-above-then-below placement fallback (right, then left, then above, then below, never over the match) with a mist column whose fade-out overshoots via scaleY(1.25); for the 'below' landing specifically, transform-origin is switched to 50% 0% (rather than the default 50% 100%) so that overshoot grows downward, away from the match, instead of tinting it. Porting a "simplified" or unconditional transform-origin would reintroduce the exact regression 1ta.8 fixed. Also carried in 1ta.8's close reason: at the time, the standard occlusion sweep (batflight's 96 grid scenarios) never exercised the above or below landing at all (0 of 96, because scrollIntoView keeps the match centered so a side always fits) -- filed as oculist-ey2e. THAT IS NOW HISTORICAL: oculist-ey2e is CLOSED, and the prototype's occlusion-sweep.js FORCED block now produces below/below/above/above rows for batflight and fails if 1ta.8's fade-anchor fix is reverted. Still, the shipped test suite (test/batflight_effect.test.js) is separate from that prototype harness, so the new test MUST force an above and a below landing itself (e.g. a full-width match near the viewport top, the same recipe 1ta.8's reviewer used) rather than assume coverage carries over.

RULE 9 DECIDED 2026-09-23 (Chris, oculist-i8zu): EXCEPTION. Do NOT implement the lastMouseX/find-bar/viewport start-point cascade for this effect. Bat Flight keeps the prototype start: on-screen 4-40px inside the landing-side viewport edge (effects-playground.html:4134-4137), or endX with endY+/-220 for above/below (:4150-4152). The flight's x-range stays on the landing side by construction (:3880-3881, :4129-4132); a cursor or find-bar start could route the bat across the match, which rule 10 forbids. Rule 9's other half still applies: the mirrored branch must work for real and be tested.

Reviewer PASS: 15/15 batflight tests, npm test 460/460, nine mutations each turned a test red (scroll offset, 1ta.8 below fade-origin, mirrored launch side, whole-flight occlusion, rule 9 cursor independence, forced above/below, WAAPI cancel, Animation Speed, Beacon Size). title: Suppress the pack-discovery notice when every known pack is already enabled
description:
The pack-discovery notice (extension/content.js:4848, oculist-tdj.3) exists for one
reason, stated in its own header comment: packs default OFF, so a shipped pack would
otherwise be undiscoverable behind opt-in settings UI nobody has a reason to open.
It was chosen explicitly OVER defaulting a pack on.

The human has now chosen to default the Halloween pack on. With that seeding in
place, the notice nudges every user toward a toggle that is already enabled -- an
interruption that teaches them nothing and costs a dismissal.

The notice must stay in the codebase: a future pack may ship off by default, and a
user who turns Halloween off and later wants it back is exactly who it serves.

STEPS
1. In maybeShowPackDiscoveryNotice(), add one condition: show the notice only when at
   least one pack in knownPacks() is NOT in settings.enabledPacks. When every known
   pack is already enabled there is nothing to discover.
2. Put the reasoning in the comment, including the pointer to the seeding bead, so
   the next reader does not restore the old behaviour thinking the notice is broken.
3. Do NOT touch dismissPackDiscoveryNotice(), settings.packsNoticeDismissed, the
   reduced-motion path, the no-reflow path or the CTA path. oculist-tdj.6
   regression-guards all four and they are unchanged by this bead.
4. Do NOT mark the notice dismissed as a side effect of suppressing it. Suppressed is
   not answered: a user who later disables Halloween must still get the nudge, and
   flipping packsNoticeDismissed would silently deny it to them forever.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Default install (halloween seeded on, no other packs): the notice never appears,
  and settings.packsNoticeDismissed is still false afterwards.
- Halloween disabled by the user: the notice appears on overlay open, as before.
- A second pack added to the registry but not enabled: the notice appears even though
  halloween is on.
- packsNoticeDismissed true: never appears, unchanged.
- node --test (whole suite) passes, in particular the oculist-tdj.6 guards.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. maybeShowPackDiscoveryNotice suppresses the notice when every knownPacks() entry is enabled, without writing packsNoticeDismissed. Four tests cover the done-criteria, mutation-proven. Two comment findings fixed. Full suite 350/350 (implementer run); reviewer run had one unrelated load timeout, filed as oculist-434k.

title: Bone Assembly: the headless skeleton dashes after its rolling skull
description:
Chris asked for this 2026-09-18 after previewing the effect. The skull-less skeleton now CHASES the rolling skull instead of standing still while it leaves.

CURRENT STATE, all verified. Sequence is scatter, snap, skull-roll, collapse. The skull detaches, rolls toward the match and settles upright; the body stays exactly where it assembled and collapses into a heap there. DUR 2430. Read the close reasons of oculist-1ta.25, .29 and .33 before touching anything: they record the geometry, the traps and three passes of clearance measurement.

THE CHANGE. While the skull rolls, the headless body runs after it. The skull stops at the match; the body arrives beside it and collapses into a heap there.

CHRIS RULED 2026-09-18: arrives, then collapses. The collapse beat SURVIVES, relocated next to the word rather than cut.

THE DASH IS CONCURRENT WITH THE ROLL, not after it. 'Dashing after the rolling skull' means chasing it while it is still rolling. This is also why the change should cost little or no runtime: reuse the existing roll window rather than appending a new beat.

DO NOT LET DUR GROW. It is already 2430ms, up from 1930 when this effect first shipped, and the oculist-1ta.33 reviewer judged it as feeling long. If you need room, take it from the 300ms heap hold and the 200ms fade at the end, which that reviewer identified as the place where the eye has nothing new to watch. Report the new DUR and where any time came from.

THE HARD PART, AND IT IS A REAL INVERSION OF THIS EFFECT'S GEOMETRY

Until now the body NEVER MOVED toward the match. Its clearance came from sitting still at a safe distance, and only the skull approached the word. Three passes of measurement established that the skull, not the body, was the binding constraint, and oculist-1ta.29's review proved by counter-mutation that even the roll was not really binding. THAT FINDING NO LONGER APPLIES. Once the body travels inward, the body is likely the binding constraint, and every clearance number in those close reasons was measured against a stationary figure.

So:
1. Re-derive REACH_INWARD from the body's actual dash path, not its rest position. The existing runtime scan (REST_CX/REST_R and the minX/maxX accumulator) assumes a stationary figure; extend it to cover the dash, the way oculist-1ta.29 extended it for the roll. Do not bolt on a parallel calculation.
2. Bound the SWEPT path of every piece across the dash, including the run-cycle poses, not just the arrival position. A limb extended mid-stride reaches further than the same limb at rest.
3. The body must stop SHORT of the skull, on the far side from the match, so the skull stays the closest thing to the word. The heap must not extend past the skull toward the match. State the resting gap between the body and the skull, and between the skull and the match.
4. Current worst-case clearance is 8.267px at 1280x900 font 22, with zero negatives, and it has tightened three passes running (10.4 to 9.5 to 8.3). Do NOT spend more of it. If the dash cannot be made clean without going below roughly 8px, stop and report rather than shaving the margin.

THE RUN CYCLE. Use discrete whole-frame poses swapped by hard cuts, two or three of them, exactly as the epic's other figures do. Smooth small tweens have repeatedly rendered invisibly in this file. The legs are currently static; this is new art. At roughly 60-70px total figure height the run has to read as running and not as jitter, so judge it by looking, not by the keyframe list.

MUST NOT REGRESS, all verified under oculist-1ta.33
- Paint order: gSkull is the LAST child of mirrorG so it paints above the body. This matters MORE now, because a chasing body will overlap the skull far more than a stationary one did. Deleting that line takes the skull's overpainted fraction from 12 to 68 percent. Keep it, and check the skull stays visible while the body is behind or over it.
- The roll never reverses direction: zero positive-rate samples across the whole motion on both engines. ROLL_SETTLE_DEG is a literal -360 for exactly this reason. Do not restore Math.round(ROLL_DEG_TOTAL/360)*360, which evaluates to 0 and spins the skull backwards.
- Determinism to this bead's standard: WITHIN-ENGINE repeat runs byte-identical at seeked frames, on chromium and webkit separately. Cross-engine numeric agreement is a weaker, different test and does not substitute. Seek getAnimations to fixed timestamps with the fire and first seek in ONE page.evaluate, and do NOT put scrollIntoView in that evaluate: the scroll lands after armScrollDissolve, dissolves the effect, drops getAnimations from 18 to 1 and produces a false diff.
- G4 structurally 0: animated properties are transform plus one monotonic figWrap opacity fade, no filter. A run cycle built from opacity-swapped poses WILL introduce opacity animations, so if you build it that way G4 must be re-measured at 4ms or finer with a 16x16 tile area detector against a synthetic 5Hz square-wave control. Do not measure at 40ms and do not use a per-pixel reversal count, which flags every effect in this epic by construction. Do not use neon as the control; it does not flicker on webkit (see oculist-x27b).
- Sweep exit 0 with boneassembly 96/96 grid, 4/4 forced, 12/12 edge at maxPixels 0, and batflight and arrowshot unaffected. occlusion-sweep.js must end byte-unmodified with no exemption added.
- Census: 106 of 112 rows exercise real on-canvas clearance. A green sweep alone cannot prove clearance, since a mutant that mounts nothing reports clean. Report the per-row census.
- Conventions: class fx, baseStyle, mount, local DUR, WAAPI only, no animated filter, no negative z-index, every 3-plus-keyframe list ending on explicit offset 1, registry entry unchanged and still last.
- Timed DOM mutation is invisible to the gate: occlusion-sweep.js neutralizes setTimeout during measurement. Use WAAPI keyframes and static DOM structure.

MUTATION PROOF REQUIRED. Shrink the dash clearance or disable the suppression backstop on a SCRATCH copy, confirm the sweep goes red, restore, re-run clean. Expect the 4 FORCED rows to stay green even mutated; they render off-canvas, a known unfalsifiable caveat.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Scatter, snap, skull-roll with the body dashing after it, arrival, collapse: all visible and in that order, with the dash overlapping the roll.
- The body reads as RUNNING at natural size, judged on a 1x frame strip.
- The skull stays visible whenever the body is near or over it.
- The skull remains the closest element to the match; the heap does not extend past it toward the word.
- The matched word is never occluded, at any instant, including arrival and heap.
- Worst-case clearance no worse than about 8px, zero negatives, re-derived from the dash path.
- DUR does not grow; say where any reclaimed time came from.
- No Math.random; within-engine determinism byte-identical on both engines.
- Sweep exit 0; batflight and arrowshot unaffected; census reported.
- Nothing remains in the DOM; clearFx mid-effect leaves nothing.
- VERIFY BY LOOKING: 1x frame strip covering the detach, the chase, the arrival and the heap, inspected, plus a 1x frame of the run cycle specifically judged for whether it reads as running.
close_reason: Accepted after 1x chase-read fix: skull lead plus slimmer leg silhouette; full occlusion gate, cross-engine determinism, teardown, and visual strip all pass; DUR unchanged at 2430ms.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
REVIEW 1, 2026-09-18: every objective done-criterion PASSES, independently re-measured, several with more margin than the implementer claimed. One criterion is unconfirmed and is a look call for Chris, not a code defect. Bead left open pending that.

THE CENTRAL RISK IS ANSWERED. The skull still binds, not the dashing body. Painted geometry over 96 scenarios at 4ms on both engines: minimum skull gap to match 12.117px chromium and 12.112px webkit; minimum BODY gap 15.716px, and that occurs at t=172ms during the SCATTER, not the dash; minimum body gap during and after the dash is 19.787px. So the body never comes within 3.6px of the skull's closest approach and stays 7.7px behind it during the chase. minX/maxX confirmed unchanged at -30.5/72.633, REACH_INWARD_LOCAL confirmed at 55.5.

AND THE DERIVATION IS LIVE, NOT A LUCKY CONSTANT, which is the better finding. A COUPLED mutant with DASH_DX_TOTAL -45 in both the scan and the animate stays clean at 13.638px with zero negatives, but the BODY now binds at 13.638 while the skull relaxes to 24.305. The accumulator re-binds correctly when the body really does travel far enough. Crossover is near -30.

THE LEG BOUND IS EXACT, PROVED EMPIRICALLY. Rotation origin is the hip endpoint, not the midpoint (a midpoint pivot would give 11.42). Sweeping every 5 degrees from 0 to 355 at every 20ms dash position on both engines, the maximum painted radius about the hip is 17.74911 local, matching the claimed R_NEAR_LEG_PIVOT of 17.749 to five decimals at every angle. Frozen at the WORST angle found, 70 degrees rather than the shipped 45, at the worst dash position, the body's gap is still 18.46px against the skull's 12.11.

THE THREE INHERITED CLAIMS ARE NOW FRESHLY MEASURED. Clearance worst case 11.668px on webkit at edge-right-1280x900-natural, 12.117px chromium, zero negatives. Census 106/112 re-instrumented on both engines, matching exactly, with a mount-nothing mutant reporting 0/112 on the same probe so it cannot hide behind a green sweep. Skull visibility: maximum overpaint 14.9 percent at t=850, against 79.8 percent with the paint-order line deleted, so that line remains load-bearing.

DO NOT TREAT 8.267 AND 11.67 AS THE SAME METRIC. The reviewer's instrument reproduces 8.268px at a dash of -35, suspiciously close to the inherited 8.267px figure, which suggests the lineage number and this one measure different things. The bar of 'no worse than about 8px' is met either way, but the comparison is not apples to apples.

THE IMPLEMENTER'S G4 NOISE DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG AND THE RECORD IS CORRECTED HERE. G4 is still structurally 0 and the criterion is met: the only opacity keyframes in fxBoneAssembly are the single monotonic figWrap fade, and the run cycle is transform-only. But the marginal flagged tile is NOT harness jitter. On a deterministic seek clock with bit-identical repeat runs, attribution by mutation gives: run cycle OFF and dash ON, 0/208 tiles; dash OFF and run cycle ON, 4/208 at 4.5 rev/s; both off, 0/208. The residual is caused entirely by the LEG HARD CUTS, and the dash's translation actually reduces it. Shipped boneassembly reads 2/208 at 3.3 rev/s against a 5Hz control at 16/208 and 9.5 rev/s, which is about a third of the control and at parity with shipped horseman, and it vanishes one deadband step up. Not a failure, but real rather than imaginary.

WORTH KEEPING: a naive deadband flags shipped arrowshot at 38 tiles and horseman at 8, which is the 'flags every effect by construction' trap this epic already recorded. The reviewer calibrated to the tightest deadband at which four certified-clean neighbours all read 0 while the 5Hz control still reads 9.5 rev/s.

THE MUTATION'S TINY MAXPIXELS IS EXPLAINED, NOT SUSPICIOUS. At -45 the painted body crosses the match's right edge by only 0.289px, so only 2 to 3 pixels can flip. The sensitivity curve is -20 giving 12.117px clear as shipped, -30 giving 12.452, -35 giving 8.268, -40 giving 3.989, and -45 giving -0.289 and red. That is roughly 25 local units of dash headroom; the mutation was simply picked at the threshold.

THE UNCONFIRMED CRITERION: DOES THE BODY READ AS RUNNING AT 1X. The mechanism is present and not subtle in the abstract, since a pose swap changes 23 percent of the visible figure with the skull present and 39 percent without, alternating at 7.1Hz. But the reviewer does not read it as running at 1x, and measured why: THE ROLLING SKULL IS PAINTED ON TOP OF THE LEGS AND ROLLS ALONG EXACTLY THEIR BASELINE, occluding them 29.3 percent on average and 46.9 percent at peak. The .33 paint-order fix, correct on its own terms, is what hides them; on the paint-order mutant leg occlusion drops to 8.2 percent. The legs are also stubby at 12.65 local units long and 10.2 wide, about 11 by 9 screen px, so a 45 degree rotation of a near-round capsule changes the silhouette far less than the numbers suggest. The dominant read at 1x is 'the skull is tumbling through the body' rather than 'the skeleton is striding'.

THE LEVER, IF CHRIS DOES NOT READ IT AS RUNNING, IS THE ROLL AND DASH OVERLAP, NOT KICK_ROT_DEG. The legs and the rolling skull currently occupy the same 700ms and the same baseline band.

TWO MINOR NOTES. The far-leg pivot hard-snaps from 45 to 0 degrees at t=1429, one frame before collapse: deliberate, documented, identical on both engines, and one more hard cut in a run of hard cuts at the same cadence, but it is a visible snap at the arrival beat. And at rest the near arm reaches 8.4px further toward the word than the skull does, which is pre-existing geometry costing no clearance, noted so the raw skull-dominance numbers are not misread.

GATE: sweep exit 0 with boneassembly 96/96 grid, 4/4 forced, 12/12 edge at maxPixels 0, batflight and arrowshot unaffected. Determinism byte-identical at 21 seeked frames across two independent browser launches, chromium and webkit separately. Clean teardown, no reflow, conventions intact, DUR still 2430, occlusion-sweep.js byte-unmodified.

title: Skull roll polish: paint the skull above the body during the roll, and land it upright-ish
description:
Two craft findings from the oculist-1ta.29 review, 2026-09-17. Neither is a correctness defect; both undermine the beat Chris actually asked for. Chris ruled on the second one the same day.

FINDING 1: THE DETACH IS HIDDEN. gSkull is the FIRST child of mirrorG, so it paints BEHIND every other piece. From about t=830 to t=950 the skull is substantially occluded by the pelvis and legs, and the beat reads as 'the head sank into the body, then a ball emerged from behind the hips' rather than 'the skull detached and rolled off'. The visible portion is unambiguously rotating, which is why this passed review, but roughly the first third of a 400ms roll is lost. The reviewer's suggested fix: re-append gSkull to mirrorG at the roll, or author it last.

FINDING 2: THE LANDING IS UPSIDE DOWN. The skull rests at -150.15 degrees. At 4x that reads as an inverted skull; at 1x the reviewer read it as 'a pale disc with three dark dots', ambiguous between a skull, a domino and a bowling ball. At this size the eye-sockets-above-jaw arrangement is the only thing carrying the skeleton read, and inverting it costs that.

CHRIS RULED 2026-09-17: land upright-ish. Accept some loss of the exact rolling-without-slipping relationship in exchange for legibility at natural size.

DO NOT pad the travel to a full revolution. One revolution is 91 local units against 33 units of actual travel, so the skull would roll nearly 3x further and end well past the word, which would break the clearance. The reviewer named this explicitly as the wrong fix.

TWO ROUTES, PICK ONE AND SAY WHICH AND WHY
- Retune ROLL_R_LOCAL so the derived rotation lands near a multiple of 360. Keeps one consistent relationship throughout, but the radius then no longer matches the skull's real radius, so the roll is uniformly slightly wrong rather than exactly right.
- Keep the derived rotation for the travel and add a small settle rotation at the end. Keeps the roll itself physically exact and confines the compromise to the last beat, but introduces a rotation that is not distance-derived.
Whichever you choose, the skull must still READ as rolling: rotation and translation must visibly agree during the travel. Judge on a 1x frame strip.

FINDING 3, TRIVIAL: skullSelfReach's comment claims the jaw is the dominant painted term. The reviewer measured the true dominant term as the main ellipse plus its non-scaling stroke; the jaw only dominates the triangle-inequality BOUND, which stays conservative. Correct the comment.

WHAT MUST NOT REGRESS, all verified under oculist-1ta.29
- Clearance: minimum 13.764px geometric across 1747 interpolated scenarios, 12.36px pixel-true, zero negatives. The gap is scale-bound as 11.0 + 3.693*scale with scale clamped to [0.75, 0.875]. A landing-angle change moves painted extents, so re-derive rather than assume.
- Sweep exit 0: boneassembly 96/96 grid, 4/4 forced, 12/12 edge at maxPixels 0, batflight and arrowshot unaffected.
- Determinism: byte-identical seeked frames on chromium and webkit. Measure by seeking getAnimations to fixed timestamps with the fire and first seek in ONE page.evaluate. Do NOT put scrollIntoView in that same evaluate: the scroll event then lands after armScrollDissolve and dissolves the effect, dropping getAnimations from 18 to 1 and producing a false diff. Scroll first, let it settle, then fire and seek.
- G4 structurally 0: five animate calls, all transform-only except one monotonic figWrap opacity fade. A z-order change must not introduce an opacity animation. If it does, re-measure at 4ms or finer with a 16x16 tile area detector against a synthetic 5Hz square wave control.
- Census 106 of 112 rows exercising real on-canvas clearance.
- Conventions: class fx, baseStyle, mount, local DUR, WAAPI only, no animated filter, no negative z-index, every 3+-keyframe list ending on explicit offset 1, registry entry unchanged and still last, occlusion-sweep.js byte-unmodified.

WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU TUNE CLEARANCE. The oculist-1ta.29 review proved by counter-mutation that the roll is NOT the binding clearance constraint: the skull's rest reach of -28.0 local barely exceeds the pre-existing nearArm scatter bound of -26.6, and omitting the roll from the clearance scan entirely still leaves the sweep clean, costing only about 3.4px against roughly 14px of true slack. R_SKULL_SELF and its scan line are margin, not load-bearing. Do not treat the roll as the binding constraint.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The skull is visible throughout the roll, including the detach. No part of the roll is hidden behind the body.
- The skull comes to rest approximately upright, eye sockets above jaw, and reads as a skull on a 1x frame rather than a featureless disc.

- Clearance re-derived and still clean; sweep exit 0; batflight and arrowshot unaffected.
- Determinism, G4, teardown, reflow and conventions all unregressed.

Skull roll polish landed. PASSED on the second review after one retry.

FIX 1, PAINT ORDER: mirrorG.appendChild(gSkull) re-parents the skull to last child, so it paints above the whole figure in SVG document order. Mutation-proved load-bearing: deleting that one line drives the skull's overpainted fraction from 11.8 percent to 67.6 percent at t=830. The residual 11.8 percent is a thin antialiased arc on the outline; the interior is fully intact.

The implementer deliberately chose a STATIC reorder over a roll-scoped timed re-append, because occlusion-sweep.js neutralizes setTimeout during measurement, so a timed DOM mutation would be invisible to the gate. Confirmed true by the reviewer against the harness's own live neutralization control. Recorded separately via bd remember, because it generalizes: ANY timed DOM mutation in an effect is untested by the sweep.

FIX 2, THE LANDING, FAILED ONCE AND THE FAILURE IS WORTH REMEMBERING. ROLL_SETTLE_DEG was written as Math.round(ROLL_DEG_TOTAL/360)*360, which evaluates to 0. Rounding to the NEAREST multiple of 360 is precisely the direction-reversing choice here: 0 is 150.15 degrees away, -360 is 209.85 away. So the skull rolled left spinning counter-clockwise, then spun CLOCKWISE back to upright without moving, peaking at +4048 deg/s, 7.7 times the roll rate, in reverse. It read as the skull un-rolling in place.

The retry targets a literal -360 instead, reaching the same upright pose by CONTINUING the travel's own counter-clockwise rotation. Verified: 1ms sampling of the live unwrapped transform from 700 to 1440 gives ZERO positive-rate samples on chromium and webkit, with the settle decaying monotonically. Mutation-proved: reverting only ROLL_SETTLE_DEG to 0 restores 300 positive-rate samples and the sign flip.

TIMINGS: TD 100ms, travel 300ms restored to .29's signed-off -421.5 deg/s, settle widened 60 to 300ms, ROLL_DUR 400 to 700, COLLAPSE_START 1130 to 1430, DUR 2130 to 2430. Offsets are now computed from the ms constants rather than hardcoded fractions.

ONE HONEST QUALIFICATION ON THE FIX. It is not one continuous deceleration, and the code comment saying so is overstated. At t=1130 translation stops instantly, 1.56 to 0 px per frame, while rotation SPEEDS UP 2.7x, 7.17 to 19.49 degrees per frame. There is no reversal and no snap, and at 1x on a 22px skull the reviewer reads it as 'hit its mark and spun down' rather than a flick, but the seam is findable if you know where to look. Filed as follow-up. The monotonic-decay claim is true only INSIDE the settle.

DETERMINISM, to the standard this bead requires rather than the weaker one first reported: within-engine repeat runs give byte-identical seeked frames, chromium 21/21 and webkit 21/21, fresh browser per run. The retry had reported only cross-engine numeric agreement at eps 0.01, which is a different and weaker test; the required standard holds byte-exact on both engines.

CLEARANCE TIGHTENED FOR THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE PASS AND THE TREND IS WORTH WATCHING. On the reviewer's metric: baseline 9.470px, current 8.267px, at 1280x900 font 22 at t=1300, zero negatives. An exhaustive per-angle sweep at the rest translate in 0.25 degree steps gives a global worst of 8.2646px, and the 300ms settle's longer dwell introduces NO new worst case. Notably the new -360 rest pose is ROOMIER than the old one, 14.93px versus 9.48px. Still about 4.6x the 1.8px outline with zero negatives, but three passes have each taken slack.

GATE: sweep exit 0 with boneassembly 96/96 grid, 4/4 forced, 12/12 edge at maxPixels 0 and maxEnd 2370 consistent with the DUR growth; batflight and arrowshot unaffected; npm test 321/321. G4 structurally 0 with 18 animations, animated properties transform and opacity only, no filter, and all ten 3-plus-keyframe lists ending on explicit offset 1 including the new 4-keyframe roll list. The reviewer spot-checked this pass's numbers and found no false claim of that class; the correction took. Two remaining looseness notes, both harmless: 'animCount 18 everywhere' is actually 18 then 17, matching baseline, and one maxEnd figure was derived rather than measured.

The reviewer's read for Chris: it does feel long, but the settle is NOT the culprit, since about 250 of its 300ms is perceptible rotation and only the last 50ms is imperceptible tail. title: Bone Assembly: the skeleton rolls its skull to the match, then collapses
description:
Chris asked for this redesign 2026-09-17, after previewing the effect. He chose the sequence explicitly: scatter, snap, skull-roll, collapse. The roll REPLACES the settle hold. The collapse stays.

CURRENT STATE. fxBoneAssembly ships as scatter, snap, 110ms settle hold, collapse. It was closed 2026-09-17 under oculist-1ta.25 with the collapse verified: the skull falls from 55px above the feet baseline to 2.6px, eight pieces staggered with a shared arrival. Read that bead's close reason before touching anything; it records the geometry and the traps.

THE NEW BEAT. After the skeleton snaps together, its skull detaches and rolls along the match's baseline toward the word, coming to rest near it. Then the body collapses into a heap as it already does.

STEPS

1. Remove the settle hold (SETTLE_HOLD, currently 200ms nominal, of which about 110ms is true stillness after the click pulse) and put the roll in its place. ACCEPTANCE: no dead air between the snap and the roll.

2. Detach the skull from the assembled figure and roll it along the baseline toward the match. It must read as ROLLING, not sliding: the skull rotates about its own centre in the direction of travel, at a rate that matches the distance covered, so it does not look like it is skating. ACCEPTANCE: judged by eye on a 1x frame strip, the rotation and the translation agree.

3. Decide and state where the skull comes to rest. It must NOT occlude the matched glyphs, which is the epic's standing disqualifier. Resting just outside the match rect with the same clearance discipline the rest of the effect uses is the expected answer. ACCEPTANCE: the sweep is clean with the skull at rest, not merely in transit.

4. Collapse the remaining seven pieces as they already do. The skull is no longer part of the heap, so the heap is now seven pieces. Check the heap still reads as a pile rather than a scatter with its largest element missing, and say what you saw. ACCEPTANCE: inspected 1x screenshot of the heap hold.

5. Re-run the full gate and re-derive the clearance. ACCEPTANCE: node occlusion-sweep.js boneassembly exit 0, and batflight and arrowshot unaffected.

THE TRAP, NAMED. The rolling skull travels TOWARD the match, which is exactly the direction the clearance math protects. The inward slack is currently 6.10px, measured at 2ms across the whole timeline with stroke-inclusive bounding boxes. The roll will consume that slack and then some, so REACH_INWARD must be re-derived from the roll's actual path, not assumed. A skull rotating about its own centre sweeps a circle of radius equal to its own half-diagonal, which is larger than its resting bounding box: bound the swept circle, not the static box. Re-run the sweep after.

ALSO
- Determinism: hand-author the roll. No Math.random.
- G4 is currently 0 and structural, because the only animated properties are transform and one monotonic opacity fade. A rolling skull is pure transform, so keep it that way. If you add any opacity cut, G4 must be re-measured at 4ms or finer with an area detector, never a per-pixel count and never at 40ms sampling.
- The point beat was deliberately cut under oculist-1ta.25 because it duplicated Foot Tap and Point's signature pose. Do not reintroduce a pointing gesture.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Scatter, snap, skull-roll, collapse: all visible and in that order.
- The skull reads as rolling, not sliding, judged on a 1x frame strip.
- The matched word is never occluded, including with the skull at rest.
- The seven-piece heap still reads as a heap.
- No Math.random; identical on every fire.
- Sweep exit 0; batflight and arrowshot unaffected.
- Nothing remains in the DOM; clearFx mid-effect leaves nothing.
- VERIFY BY LOOKING: screenshot the snap, the roll mid-travel, the skull at rest, and the heap, at natural size, and inspect them.
close_reason:
The skeleton now rolls its skull to the match. PASSED first review.

SEQUENCE: scatter 0-640, click 640-730, roll 730-1130, collapse 1130-1570, heap hold to 1870, fade to 2070. DUR 1840 to 2130. The settle hold is gone and ROLL_START is SNAP_DONE_T + CLICK_DUR exactly, so there is no dead air. The collapse is unchanged and still verified.

THE ROLL IS PHYSICALLY DERIVED, NOT HAND-PICKED. Rotation is deg = dx * (180/pi) / ROLL_R_LOCAL with ROLL_R_LOCAL 14.5, applied at every keyframe rather than in aggregate. Measured from the live getScreenCTM at 12 instants on both engines, the actual rotation agrees with distance over radius to within 0.017 degrees through both segments. It reads as rolling, not sliding.

THE IMPLEMENTER FOUND A SHARPER VERSION OF THE NAMED TRAP. Plain ellipseReach bounds only the main skull ellipse and silently ignores the jaw's offset, which is adequate for the old plus or minus 35 degree scatter wobble and wrong for a 150 degree roll. They added skullSelfReach, a per-sub-shape triangle-inequality bound over all four sub-ellipses, giving R_SKULL_SELF 17.5, and extended the existing runtime accumulator rather than bolting on a parallel calculation.

TWO OF THE IMPLEMENTER'S NUMBERS WERE WRONG AND THE REVIEWER CORRECTED THEM, BOTH IN THE SAFE DIRECTION.

First, the reported resting clearance of 10.59px against a GAP floor of 10 understated reality by about 3px. The true minimum across 1747 interpolated scenarios is 13.764px geometric with ZERO negatives and zero suppressed rows, and 12.36px pixel-true including antialiasing. The gap is scale-bound rather than viewport-bound: gap = 11.0 + 3.693 * scale, and scale is clamped to [0.75, 0.875], so it ranges [13.77, 14.23] and there is no worst case hiding between grid samples. So the headline risk this bead was written around does not exist.

Second, and worth recording because it falsifies this bead's own premise: THE ROLL DID NOT CONSUME THE SLACK. The skull's rest reach of -28.0 local barely exceeds the pre-existing nearArm scatter bound of -26.6. The reviewer proved it by counter-mutation: understating the roll in the clearance scan entirely still leaves the sweep clean, because omitting it costs only about 3.4px against roughly 14px of true slack. R_SKULL_SELF and the new scan line are MARGIN, NOT LOAD-BEARING. Good engineering, but future work should not treat the roll as the binding constraint.

The forward mutation does hold: rolling 24 local units further than the scan accounts for turns the sweep exit 1 with 96/96 grid and 12/12 edge dirty, every one of the 108 dirty rows reporting atTime 1160ms, precisely the roll-rest window. So the gate does catch a roll that reaches the word.

DETERMINISM HOLDS, measured properly. The implementer saw mid-animation frames drift under 1 percent between runs and honestly flagged it as weaker than this epic's standard. Seeking getAnimations to 17 fixed timestamps with the fire and first seek in ONE page.evaluate gives byte-identical frames on chromium and webkit at three viewport and font combinations, and the roll transform matrices are bit-identical across engines. The drift was a harness artifact.

A HARNESS TRAP WORTH KEEPING FOR THIS EPIC: putting scrollIntoView and runEffect in the same evaluate lets the scroll event land after armScrollDissolve, which dissolves the effect and drops getAnimations from 18 to 1, producing a false determinism diff. Scroll first, let it settle, then fire and seek.

GATE: exit 0 with boneassembly 96/96 grid, 4/4 forced, 12/12 edge at maxPixels 0, and batflight and arrowshot unaffected. Census confirmed exactly at 106 of 112 rows exercising real on-canvas clearance, measured directly rather than inferred: all 96 grid rows on-canvas, 10 of 12 edge rows on-canvas, with the two 320x900-96px rows genuinely off-canvas at figure minX 331.5 and 320.4 against a 320px viewport. No row is vacuous in a new way. G4 remains structurally 0: five animate calls, all transform-only except the one pre-existing monotonic figWrap fade, so nothing new can alias. Clean teardown, no reflow at 20ms layout sampling, clearFx mid-roll leaves nothing, zero console errors, all three 3-keyframe lists end on explicit offset 1, occlusion-sweep.js byte-unmodified.

THE SEVEN-PIECE HEAP STILL READS AS A HEAP. Vertical spread closes from 28.55px to 5.25px, all seven pieces move downward. title: Remove Foot Tap and Point (candidate 48), keeping the numbering gap
description:

1. Delete the fxFootTap function (effects-playground.html, the block headed '48. Foot Tap and Point', around line 7015-7550) and its effectsRegistry entry at around line 9895. ACCEPTANCE: 'fxFootTap' and 'foottap' appear nowhere in the file except where step 3 deliberately leaves them.

2. LEAVE NUMBER 48 AS A GAP. Galloping Throw stays 49, Wand Cast and the rest keep their current numbers. Do not renumber anything. Leave a one-line comment where 48 was, recording that the slot is intentionally vacant and why, so a future reader does not 'fix' the gap. ACCEPTANCE: every surviving candidate's number is unchanged from HEAD, verified by diffing the numbered header comments.

3. Repoint the roughly 8 comments in other effects that cite fxFootTap as the side-selection exemplar. fxWandCast and fxTentacleRise both implement the same idiom and both survive, so cite one of those instead. Do not delete the explanation, just change which function it points at. ACCEPTANCE: no surviving comment refers a reader to a function that no longer exists.

4. Remove foottap from occlusion-sweep.js and any of its tables. This is the one case in this epic where editing the harness is authorized, because the key genuinely no longer exists. Removing a key must not change any other key's behaviour. ACCEPTANCE: the harness runs clean for the remaining effects and does not error on a missing foottap key.

5. Re-run the gate: node occlusion-sweep.js batflight arrowshot must stay exit 0 and fully clean, and so must wandcast, tentaclerise, boneassembly and horseman. ACCEPTANCE: exit 0 for all of them.

EDGE CASES TO HANDLE, NOT DISCOVER LATE
- Do NOT touch the fire-index max or the SHIPPED_LABELS block. If removing the registry entry would change the sidebar's index-based divider slice, say so before acting rather than silently shifting which effects land under 'New candidates (post round 6)'.
- foottap has been used as a G4 calibration comparator in this epic's reviews. Once it is gone those comparisons cannot be reproduced. Note it in the close reason; do not keep the function alive just for that.
- If any check script under artifacts/prototypes other than occlusion-sweep.js references foottap, handle it the same way.

DONE-CRITERIA

- Every other candidate's number is unchanged.
- No dangling reference to fxFootTap anywhere, in code or comments.
- The full sweep gate is exit 0 for every surviving effect.
close_reason:
Foot Tap and Point removed from the playground. PASSED after one correction pass.

WHAT WENT: the fxFootTap function (was effects-playground.html:7015-7554), its effectsRegistry entry, and every foottap reference in occlusion-sweep.js. Editing the harness is normally forbidden in this epic and was authorized here only because the key genuinely ceased to exist. Zero fxFootTap or foottap references remain in either file. The only surviving mentions are deliberate: two in fxBoneAssembly's comment recording why its point beat was cut (historical rationale, now carrying a clause noting the effect was itself removed), and about 13 rows in occlusion-sweep-results.md, which is an append-only measurement log where rewriting past results would falsify the record.

THE HARNESS EDIT IS PROVABLY BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING, verified two independent ways rather than asserted. Statically, diffing occlusion-sweep.js with comments stripped yields exactly four non-comment changes: three forced-left rows dropping foottap from keys and expect, and LANDING_SOURCE_FIRST_FX emptied from one element to none. Every one is read through a key === 'foottap' predicate, so for any other key the evaluated value is bit-identical. Empirically, reanimate is the only surviving key scoped to the three touched rows, and its full sweep is BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after, including all three forced-left rows. NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT membership is unchanged at 21 keys.

TWO PREMISES IN THIS BEAD'S OWN DESCRIPTION WERE WRONG, and both misled the first implementation. They are recorded in full in the bead's correction comment.

title: arrowshot-fallback-check.js should gate on its own reconstruction of main, and pin the 8d9p geometries as named grid cases
description:
Raised by the oculist-8d9p reviewer, 2026-09-17. This is the durability half of 8d9p: the fix restored safety but RELOCATED the staleness trap rather than removing it.

THE SHAPE. effects-playground.html now carries TWO hand-maintained models of main's behaviour: the old RUN-7 BASELINE block (~5248-5262) and the new legacy nearest-nominal candidate (~5285-5302). Shipped behaviour is defined as main's output unless the fraction pick strictly beats it. Nothing in the tree would go RED if main's clamp changed and the legacy block did not follow. No assertion compares them, no gate runs the comparison, and the only mode that can observe the failure class is --random, which arrowshot-fallback-check.js's own header calls EXPLORATORY, NOT A GUARD. The deterministic grid cannot reach the class at all: the 8d9p regression was about 0.4% of fallback geometries, 2-7 violations at N=2000. That is exactly how the BASELINE block rotted unnoticed after oculist-q4nl merged into main.

WHAT IS ALREADY BETTER: the reconstruction is now cheaply observable. The reviewer's check is about 30 lines, forces takeCandidate = false so the file's output IS its Main-equivalent, drives that and the real main file over identical geometries, and counts divergence. It ran the grid in seconds, is deterministic, and goes red on a one-character drift (flipping the legacy tiebreak <= to < diverges on 1300 of 5000).

FIX: move that comparison into arrowshot-fallback-check.js as a GATING assertion, the target's Main-equivalent must equal the baseline file's chooser with 0 differences, and pin the 8d9p failing geometries as named grid cases so the deterministic mode can see the class without --random.

DONE-CRITERIA: the check fails loudly when the legacy block and the baseline file's chooser disagree, proven by mutating the legacy tiebreak; the named 8d9p geometries (e.g. vw=748.8507593888789 vh=219.70593559090048) appear as grid cases and would have caught the original 96-violation regression without --random; the assertion runs in grid mode, in seconds, with no --random needed; a clean tree still passes 0 differences.

RELATED: oculist-oxzs is the same shape one level up, a guard that re-derives instead of observing. Consider whether one mechanism serves both.
close_reason: Closed obsolete after the selected rollback removed a37c29d's hand-maintained Main-equivalent reconstruction entirely. With no duplicate reconstruction left in effects-playground.html, the proposed reconstruction-vs-main gate and 8d9p-specific cases no longer protect a live code path.

title: oculist-tklc's archer clamp diverges from main at short viewports: 96 violations at 40k random, invisible to the grid
description:
Exposed 2026-09-17 by oculist-wp7d, the moment --baseline could sample random geometries for the first time. Adjudicated REAL, not a harness artefact, by the wp7d reviewer using three independent discriminators.

THE RESULT. node arrowshot-fallback-check.js --baseline <git show main:...effects-playground.html> --random 40000 gives 40000 geometries (16649 guarded, 23351 fallback), FAIL with 96 violations: guardedDiff=0, cleanOnBaselineButChanged=33, newlyBackward=25, worse=38. Those are exactly the four safety counts oculist-tklc's done-criteria required to be 0 against main. main was e6014fa at time of measurement.

WHY THE GRID MISSED IT. The same command WITHOUT --random passes 0/0/0/0 over 9035 fallback geometries. The grid never samples this region. tklc's grid evidence was real but incomplete, and until wp7d landed there was no way to run the vs-main comparison over a random sample at all.

PROVEN REAL, THREE WAYS. (1) Self-comparison, baseline = byte-copy of the working file, --random 20000: PASS 0/0/0/0, so the random plumbing invents nothing. (2) Five failing geometries reproduce in an independently written chooser extractor with no loop and no shared state, e.g. vw=748.85 vh=219.71 gives working launchY=-10.36 archerTop=-63.41 against main launchY=233.16 archerTop=180.10, same endY and same plan. (3) Feeding only those five geometries through the GRID code path (no --random) also reds, 13 violations, so it is geometry-dependent, not mode-dependent.

SHAPE. 39 violations over 15 distinct viewports at 20k, vh range [202, 407] -- short viewports only. Plan tally: cleanOnBaselineButChanged {bottom:14}, newlyBackward {bottom:10}, worse {bottom:14, left:1}, so predominantly but NOT exclusively plan=bottom. Scales about linearly, roughly 0.3-0.4% of fallback geometries: 2000 gives 2/7/6 across seeds 1/5/6, 20000 gives 39, 40000 gives 96. Independent seeds all red, so not a seed artefact.

MECHANISM. tklc's on-screen-fraction clamp pushes the archer off the TOP on short viewports (archerTop -59 to -63 at vh around 200-220), taking launchY negative and painted clearance from main's +0.49/+7.5/+53.2 to -8.1/-8.6/-10.5. The consequence is newlyBackward: the flight now runs toward #match. That is a safety-bar violation by this project's own standard, and it is the opposite of what Chris's option 3 was chosen to achieve, so it reads as a bug in the rule's implementation at short viewports rather than a question about the rule.

THE FORK FOR CHRIS, if the fix is not clean: (a) correct the clamp so the fraction rule cannot take painted clearance backward, keeping option 3; (b) revert tklc's commit fc8d994 from the branch; (c) accept, on the grounds that main is already painted-dirty in these geometries. The newlyBackward count argues against (c).

DONE-CRITERIA: --baseline against a real main copy reports 0/0/0/0 at --random 40000 and on the grid; occlusion-sweep.js centered-500x180 and 500x220 stay clean; the archer-still-overlaps and fully-off-screen counters do not regress against the values recorded in tklc's close reason.
close_reason: Resolved by the human-selected rollback: outer-repo commits a72b676 and 2b0471f revert a37c29d and fc8d994, restoring the pre-option-3 Arrow Shot chooser without retaining inert reconstruction machinery. Fresh verification: arrowshot-fallback-check deterministic grid PASS (9035 fallback geometries, guardedDiff=0, cleanButDiffers=0, newlyBackward=0, worse=0); random seed 1 at N=1000 PASS 0/0/0/0; occlusion-sweep arrowshot PASS with 96/96 grid, 7/7 forced-landing, and 12/12 edge-placement clean at maxPixels=0.

comments.text:
REVIEWED 2026-09-17: safety fix lands, but the bead does NOT close. Reviewer verdict NEEDS-WORK, and the reason is a decision for Chris rather than more code.

FIXED AND VERIFIED. 0/0/0/0 against real main at 40k random seeds 1, 5 and 6, and on the grid. Reverting only the SELECT restructuring reproduces exactly 96 violations with the same counts and the same first geometries, so the restructuring is load-bearing. The pass-1 reconstruction of main was checked against the real main file over 57621 geometries (grid plus random 20000 at seeds 1 and 7) with ZERO divergence in plan/corner/endX/endY/launchY/archerTop, and a one-character tiebreak flip diverges on 1300 of 5000, so that zero is a measurement rather than an insensitive harness. occlusion-sweep arrowshot clean, centered-500x180 and 500x220 maxPixels 0. Committed as a37c29d so the branch does not carry the backward-flight regression while this is decided.

WHY IT STAYS OPEN: OPTION 3 IS NOW INERT. Pass 2 adopts the fraction candidate only when archerClearCand > archerClearMain, which is the direct negation of Chris's rule, prefer the direction keeping more archer on screen EVEN WHEN the other clears by more. Measured: archers brought newly on screen versus main go from 752 grid and 919 at random-20k under tklc to 0 and 0 here. Archer fully off-screen returns to main's own 1592 grid and 3188 random, exactly. Newly-off-screen versus pre-q4nl goes 937 grid and 3126 at 40k, i.e. all the way back to main, against the 215 and 1273 recorded in tklc's close reason. So this bead's own done-criterion about not regressing tklc's counters FAILS.

NOT FIXABLE BY A BETTER GATE. The reviewer tested a simpler formulation gated purely on the three safety properties, dropping the strict archer-clearance term: newly-off-screen 974 on the grid, slightly WORSE than main's 937. The two bars are in genuine conflict because painted clearance rewards running off screen, so no cheap gate satisfies both.

THE FORK FOR CHRIS. (a) Keep a37c29d as-is: safe against main, option 3 inert, and about 95 lines of option-3 machinery that never fires. (b) Revert fc8d994 and a37c29d both: identical shipped behaviour to (a) with far less code, and honest about it. The reviewer's note: keeping the machinery while it never fires is the worst of the three.

title: occlusion-sweep has no automated control catching a setInterval-not-dropped regression
description:
UPDATE (oculist-gmp, same session, following coordinator instruction that the interval shape is this bead's own criterion 3, not separable): closed by extending runNeutralizationControl with a second canary.

Original gap (still recorded for context): a scratch mutant of installTimerNeutralizationHook's window.setInterval wrapper that increments suppressedIntervalCount but still calls realSetInterval.apply did not cause any exit-1 in occlusion-sweep.js, because NEUTRALIZATION_CANARY_KEY ('matchstrike') makes no setInterval calls, so --check-neutralization never exercised the interval wrapper at all.

Fix applied directly in occlusion-sweep.js (not here): added INTERVAL_NEUTRALIZATION_CANARY_KEY = 'scramble' (fxScramble is the playground's only setInterval caller, one unconditional `setInterval(fn, 40)` per invocation) and a second stage inside runNeutralizationControl that fires it neutralized, asserts hook.suppressedIntervalCount moved, then snapshots the mounted char spans' combined textContent immediately after firing and again after INTERVAL_NEUTRALIZATION_CONTROL_WAIT_MS (200ms, chosen short since a leaked 40ms-interval only needs a couple of ticks to prove itself, unlike the 700ms the setTimeout canary needs to outlast matchstrike's one-shot 400ms mount). A leaked interval mutates existing span textContent rather than mounting a new .fx element, so the .fx-count check built for matchstrike could not have seen this; the span-textContent snapshot is the absence-of-effect signal used instead.

Verified: the interval-not-dropped mutant (counts but still schedules, same shape as the setTimeout mutant this bead's criterion 1 already proved) now exits 1 via --check-neutralization: "scramble's interval-driven span text changed 200ms after runEffect(scramble) returned, even though suppressedIntervalCount reported 1 dropped call(s)...". Clean real tree: both canaries OK, exit 0, no false positive. Added wall-clock cost of the second canary alone: ~200-220ms (measured: setTimeout-only hardened stage averages ~1.12s over 3 runs, both-canaries averages ~1.34s over 3 runs, matching INTERVAL_NEUTRALIZATION_CONTROL_WAIT_MS almost exactly).

Recommend closing this issue as resolved by oculist-gmp's change -- I did not close it myself since implementers don't close beads. If a broader concern remains after review (e.g. general run-to-run determinism gating for scramble/rockfallthud/etc. outside the interval-drop question specifically), consider re-scoping rather than closing outright, but I found no such narrower residual gap during verification.
close_reason: Closed as resolved by the work it prompted, not separately: the gap it recorded (an un-dropped setInterval exits 0 because --check-neutralization's only canary, matchstrike, makes no setInterval calls) is now gated by oculist-gmp's second canary. Reviewer verified the interval-not-dropped mutant goes 0 -> 1 with the failure naming the scramble stage, and reported nothing real remaining in this bead.

title: framecollapse: box-shadow blur (6px) exceeds its own PAD clearance (5px), bleeding into #match's rect at rest/near-landing -- separate from hq40's start-position fix
description:
Isolated while fixing oculist-hq40's start-position defect in fxFramecollapse (effects-playground.html ~line 3057).

MEASURED: with fxFramecollapse's escapeEdgeStart fix applied (hq40) AND the bars' box-shadow temporarily stripped in a scratch copy, node occlusion-sweep.js framecollapse reads fully CLEAN: grid 96/96, FORCED-LANDING 4/4, EDGE-PLACEMENT 12/12. With the box-shadow restored (the real file), the same three blocks stay dirty (95/96, 4/4, 12/12) at maxPixels up to 1685-1552, atTime=400ms (not 0ms) -- i.e. near the bar's landed/framing position, not its start.

PROVEN SCOPE (independent review, post hq40 close-out): this defect now owns 100% of framecollapse's 95 dirty grid rows and 10 of framecollapse's 12 dirty EDGE-PLACEMENT rows (the other 2 edge rows and all 4 FORCED-LANDING rows were the separate start-position defect hq40 fixed, confirmed independently). With hq40 landed, this is the ONLY thing keeping node occlusion-sweep.js framecollapse red -- fixing it should take framecollapse's grid block to 96/96 clean outright.

CAUSE: each bar's CSS is box-shadow:0 0 6px rgba(249,115,22,0.6) (effects-playground.html, fxFramecollapse's bar styling, same block as the fix). PAD=5 is the clearance gap between a bar's landed position and #match's rect. Because the box-shadow's blur radius (6px) exceeds PAD (5px), the glow's own tail paints over part of #match's rect once a bar is at or near its landing frame, independent of any position defect.

Direct pixel probe (320px viewport, 48px font, t=400ms, row 58 of #match's 60-row clip, comparing a pre-oculist-7l2m and a post-7l2m/pre-hq40 snapshot) shows the glow-tail's per-channel delta straddling DIFF_THRESHOLD=8 for a red-saturation reason, not a narrow db/dg margin: against a #sidebar button's dark background (#2a2a33, measured (42,42,51)) the delta reads (dr=12, dg=3, db=3) -- red is the counted channel, clearly over threshold. Against #match's own highlight background (#fff3b0 = (255,243,176)) the identical glow-tail delta reads (dr=0, dg=7, db=8) -- red is pinned to 0 because #fff3b0's own red channel is already saturated at 255 and the glow (red-heavy, orange) cannot push it higher; db=8 is also not >8. This threshold-adjacency, keyed on red-channel saturation against a light background, is also why oculist-7l2m's sidebar-removal fix moved framecollapse's numbers in the opposite direction from every other affected key (see occlusion-sweep-results.md's # oculist-7l2m section, updated with the full corrected explanation) -- not a separate mystery, the same halo defect.

FIX SHAPE (not investigated in depth): increase PAD past the blur radius, or reduce/remove the box-shadow, or clip the glow the way oculist-dxpq's fxEdgeticks keyhole clip-path does. Whoever picks this up should re-check whether other effects share the same PAD-vs-blur-radius mismatch (results.md's 7l2m section already flags tether and tracer as likely siblings: "PAD=5 clearance smaller than its own 10px box-shadow blur" / "PAD=4 clearance smaller than its own 10px glow blur").

NOTE: every occlusion-sweep.js measurement, including all figures above, is Chromium-only by harness construction (occlusion-sweep.js:2944 launches chromium and nothing else) -- no second-engine cross-check exists for any of this.
close_reason: Raised Frame Collapse PAD from 5 to 9 so the 6px glow tail clears #match. Verified 96/96 grid, 4/4 forced, and 12/12 edge scenarios clean at maxPixels=0.

title: occlusion-sweep: four clearance-contract keys (shattercrack, hardfreeze, linesqueeze, flappy) read full-coverage 9360 at every viewport and gate the exit code -- pre-existing, not sidebar artifacts, and not on NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT
description:
Umbrella bead for the four saturation-ceiling keys surfaced by oculist-7l2m's
narrow-viewport re-measurement. Filed as one bead by Chris's call rather than
four, on the theory that a shared cause (full-viewport artwork) is likely --
but see the WARNING below.

MEASURED, by the oculist-7l2m implementer and independently re-measured by its
reviewer on both the HEAD playground and the responsive-fixture one:

  shattercrack  9360 at 320/360 before AND after the fixture fix
  hardfreeze    9360, same
  linesqueeze   9360, same
  flappy        9360, same

9360 is not a defect magnitude, it is the CEILING: arithmetically the rounded
clip area at 320/48 (156 x 60), identical before and after. Do not read the
number itself as signal.

THREE THINGS THAT ARE ESTABLISHED:

1. NOT SIDEBAR ARTIFACTS. shattercrack's narrow rows are bit-identical with
   and without the sidebar occluding the match (1092...9360 at every font),
   proving the count does not come from measuring under the sidebar. This is
   the opposite of gustswirl, which oculist-7l2m showed WAS suppressed by the
   sidebar (344 -> 627 at 320/48).

2. THEY GATE. None of the four is on NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT (whose
   members are matchstrike, stamp, comet, scanline, emberignite, inkbloom,
   horseman, lens, glitch, gravity, zoompunch, depthdive, scramble, neon,
   underline). node occlusion-sweep.js shattercrack exits 1 with dirty=96/96.
   So these four are live failing gates, not N/A rows.

3. PRE-EXISTING. Proven on the HEAD playground as well as the fixed one. The
   oculist-7l2m fixture change neither caused nor masked them.

THE OPEN QUESTION, which is the actual work here: is each of these four
by-design full coverage (in which case it belongs on
NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT, read and justified per key the way oculist-d48k
did for its eight), or a genuine full-coverage defect? The oculist-7l2m
implementer initially labelled all four by-design; its reviewer rejected that
label as unsupported, since none of the four has been read against its fx*
body the way d48k's triage required. That reading has NOT been done.

WARNING, from the same lineage of beads: d48k's own history shows this class
splits. It triaged nine sibling keys and moved eight while deliberately
leaving lockon out, because lockon turned out to be a real defect
(oculist-rnbo, then oculist-x2g1). Do not assume one verdict covers all four.
If the reading shows they differ, split this bead rather than forcing a

title: occlusion-sweep: fxFramecollapse's viewport-edge-flush start bars are a confirmed defect (grid 95/96, forced 4/4 maxPixels=1697, edge 12/12 DIRTY) -- same class as x2g1, worse exposure
description:
Found while doing the oculist-x2g1 step-6 grep for other corner-start
effects with the same exposure lockon had. MEASURED by the oculist-x2g1
reviewer (this bead originally said "unmeasured" -- that was wrong, fixed
here).

effects-playground.html fxFramecollapse (around line 3002) builds four
orange bars that literally rest at the viewport's own edges before any
transform runs:
  { left: 0,       top: 0,       w: vw, h: TH, ... }   // top bar
  { left: 0,       top: vh - TH, w: vw, h: TH, ... }   // bottom bar
  { left: 0,       top: 0,       w: TH, h: vh, ... }   // left bar
  { left: vw - TH, top: 0,       w: TH, h: vh, ... }   // right bar
Each is mounted with `opacity:0` in baseStyle but its FIRST animation
keyframe is `{ transform: b.from, opacity: 0.9 }` where b.from is
'translate(0px,0px) ...' -- i.e. no positional offset at all, so the bar
paints at its literal rest position (a full-width/full-height 3px strip
flush with a viewport edge) at 90% opacity from t=0, before any of the
800ms flight to the match's padded box has happened.

MEASURED (node occlusion-sweep.js framecollapse):
  grid: DIRTY 95/96
  FORCED-LANDING: DIRTY 4/4, maxPixels=1697 at atTime=0ms on forced-below-1
  EDGE-PLACEMENT: DIRTY 12/12
This is a real, confirmed defect of the same class x2g1 fixed in
fxLockon (start position collides with #match before travel), and unlike
lockon it hits the ordinary 96-scenario grid and EDGE-PLACEMENT too, not
just FORCED-LANDING -- worse exposure than lockon had. Apply the same
minimum-translation-plus-clearance-pad approach x2g1 landed in fxLockon's
escapeMatchCorner, adapted to framecollapse's full-viewport-spanning bars
(pushing a bar's start position off its literal edge rather than a small
ARM-sized corner box).

CORRECTION (fxEdgeticks): the original write-up of this bead said
fxEdgeticks "is already covered by the existing
FORCED_LANDING_SIDEBAR_EXEMPT machinery" -- right conclusion (edgeticks
reads CLEAN on forced-below-1/2), wrong reason. FORCED_LANDING_SIDEBAR_EXEMPT
is unrelated; edgeticks is clean because of oculist-dxpq's keyhole
clip-path inside fxEdgeticks (effects-playground.html:2763), which clips
each tick's paint to punch #match's own rect out of it -- so edgeticks
never paints over #match's rect in the first place, on its own merits,
independent of any harness-side exemption. Both forced-below rows read
maxPixels=0 because of that clip-path, not because of an exemption table
entry.
close_reason: escapeEdgeStart() pushes each of fxFramecollapse's four bars perpendicular to its own edge by overlap + the effect's own PAD when that bar's start rect intersects #match. Geometric, one rule, four call sites, byte-identical when already clear. Characterisation corrected the bead's own premise: the grid's 95/96 is NOT this defect -- it is halo bleed (box-shadow blur 6px > PAD 5px) at t=400ms, proven by stripping the box-shadow alone taking the grid to 96/96 CLEAN. The genuine start-position collisions were all 4 FORCED-LANDING rows (738/780/87/129 @0ms halo-stripped) and the 2 edge 320x900-96px rows (357px each); the fix eliminates all of them, verified by a halo-stripped run reading 96/96, 4/4, 12/12 at maxPixels=0. Also resolved oculist-7l2m's open framecollapse negative-swing anomaly: not masking (.fx z-index 2147483645 > sidebar 100) but a DIFF_THRESHOLD=8 boundary artifact, red channel dr=12 against #2a2a33 versus dr=0 against #fff3b0 where red is saturated at 255 -- 150 of the 152px swing on row 58 alone. Remaining framecollapse red is entirely oculist-0ip3's halo defect.

title: occlusion-sweep/fxLockon: short-flight brackets (flightDist < APPROACH_PX) are motionless for the first 70% of the animation, then snap back-eased for the last 30% -- forced-below-1/2's degenerate corner-flush geometry, distinct from x2g1
description:
Measured while fixing oculist-x2g1 (lockon's start-position collision).
Reviewer-corrected mechanism (the original write-up called this "a
residual 4px graze independent of the fix" -- that graze was in fact
caused by x2g1's own escapeMatchCorner lacking a clearance pad, and x2g1
fixed it directly; it is now CLEAN. This bead is about a different,
still-open thing the same investigation surfaced.)

THE REAL DEFECT: fxLockon's flight-in for a bracket uses two keyframe
legs -- an ease-out first leg from offset 0 to 0.7 covering "the bulk of
the distance", then a back-eased final-approach leg from offset 0.7 to 1.0
covering a fixed APPROACH_PX=40px entry distance (nearDx/nearDy = dx0/dy0
scaled by approachScale = min(1, APPROACH_PX / flightDist)).

When the total flightDist for an axis is ITSELF less than APPROACH_PX (40),
approachScale clamps to 1, which makes nearDx/nearDy equal to dx0/dy0 --
i.e. keyframe offset=0 and keyframe offset=0.7 hold the IDENTICAL
transform value. WAAPI interpolates between equal values as a no-op, so
the bracket is MOTIONLESS for the first 70% of the animation's 450ms
duration (315ms), then does its entire, real travel compressed into the
back-eased final 30% (135ms) -- a visibly different (snappier, delayed)
motion than every other bracket in every other scenario, where flightDist
is hundreds of px and the ease-out leg does most of the visible work.

This is exactly the forced-below-1/2 regime: #match sits flush with the
viewport corner (r.left=r.top=0), so the padded landing target is only
~8px from the literal corner and the top-left/top-right brackets'
flightDist is ~11-13px, far under 40. Measured (pre-x2g1-pad-fix, on
oculist-x2g1's escapeMatchCorner before it had a clearance pad): this
degenerate "motionless-then-snap" regime is what let the bracket paint
into #match at t=320ms -- a 64px raw graze pre-x2g1, later measured at 4px
after x2g1's first (unpadded) escape attempt, and now 0px after x2g1's
pad fix landed. The pixel-count symptom is gone; the underlying
short-flight-distance regime (motionless start, all motion compressed
into a back-eased snap) is still there and is a distinct, real animation-
quality defect, not a pixel-occlusion one -- occlusion-sweep won't catch
it again now that x2g1's pad gives it clearance, but it will still look
wrong if anyone watches the actual playground with a viewport that makes
#match sit close to a corner.

Suggested next step: guard against flightDist < APPROACH_PX in fxLockon's
per-bracket animate() setup -- e.g. skip straight to a single-leg
back-eased (or ease-out) animation when the near point would coincide with
the start point, instead of encoding a no-op ease-out leg followed by a
compressed snap.
close_reason: fxLockon's two-leg flight-in gave leg0 a fixed 70% of the TIME for (1-approachScale) of the DISTANCE, so as flightDist approached APPROACH_PX=40 that share collapsed toward zero and the bracket sat motionless then snapped. Fixed with a single back-eased leg at flightDist <= APPROACH_PX and splitOffset = min(0.7, 1 - approachScale) above it, so the time split tracks the distance split and the two cases meet continuously. Reviewer-verified on chromium AND webkit: degeneracy measured at 96.04/69.92/50.00/2.44/0.00 percent at flightDist 1009/133/80/41/40; the bead's own forced-below scenario (flightDist 19.6977px) goes deadStart 315ms to 0ms while its long-flight siblings stay byte-identical; normal geometry unchanged (diffRows=0, maxDelta=0) above flightDist 133.33; rnbo's bound preserved, with path-length/flightDist identical to 4dp everywhere including the 40-133.33 band this alters. The <= guard is load-bearing at the ulp. occlusion-sweep CANNOT see this defect -- lockon's unchanged MD5 94d13bc621566e768de2cf452d475464 is a regression guard only, confirmed independently by the orchestrator. Evidence recorded in occlusion-sweep-results.md's oculist-hvu6 section.

title: occlusion-sweep: 96-scenario grid also has real #sidebar baseline occlusion at 320/360px viewports, masking or inflating narrow-viewport dirty counts for ~a dozen clearance-contract keys
description:
Found while implementing oculist-m1df's baseline-occlusion subtraction
(computeBaselineOcclusion in occlusion-sweep.js, near comparePixels).

That fix was scoped to FORCED-LANDING only, per its own bead text and
done-criteria. But computeBaselineOcclusion is generic (walks the live DOM
for whatever paints above #match at baseline, not keyed to #sidebar), and
briefly wiring it into runScenario() (the 96-scenario grid) during
development surfaced a real, separate finding worth its own investigation:

MEASURED (direct probe, 320x900 viewport, 48px font, real playground,
unmodified): #match's rect is left=25.6 top=419.6 right=181.2 bottom=479.4.
#sidebar's rect is left=40 top=0 right=320 bottom=900 (right:0; width:280px
at a 320px viewport computes left=vw-280=40). Overlap region in x is
[40, 181.2] -- roughly 90% of #match's own 155.5px width sits under
#sidebar's fixed column at this viewport, for the ORDINARY grid (no
FORCED_PLACEMENTS pinning involved), because body's right padding (a fixed
320px, see effects-playground.html's body{padding:64px 320px 140px 8vw})
plus 8vw left padding leaves almost no room at 320-360px viewport widths --
the prose paragraph's natural line wrap puts #match close enough to the
right edge that #sidebar (height:100vh, so it occludes ALL y, not just a
narrow band) covers most of it.

CONSEQUENCE, already measured with the subtraction wired in (scratch only,
not shipped): matchstrike's grid-wide maxPixels moved 9356 -> 9346 (a real,
if small, number movement on an N/A/advisory key). A follow-up
narrow-viewports-only sweep (SCENARIOS.viewports trimmed to just 320x900 and
360x900, all 47 keys, sweepEffect only, BEFORE this fix / at HEAD) found
these CLEARANCE-CONTRACT (exit-code-gating) keys already reporting
"0/24 scenarios clean, 24 dirty" at HEAD, independent of any occlusion fix:
gustswirl (470), tether (344), speedlines (2038), shattercrack (9360),
hardfreeze (9360), ripplesurge (442), rockfallthud (869), linesqueeze (9360),
tracer (110), paperlift (190), framecollapse (529), flappy (9360). Several
of these (shattercrack, hardfreeze, linesqueeze, flappy at 9360 = the
saturation ceiling) look like genuine full-coverage defects unrelated to the
sidebar; others (tracer=110, paperlift=190) are small enough that the
sidebar-occlusion mechanism could plausibly explain most or all of them --
this was NOT resolved, only the raw BEFORE numbers were captured.

WHAT'S NEEDED: for each of the ~12 keys above, determine (with the
subtraction wired in, AFTER numbers) whether the narrow-viewport grid dirty
pixels are genuinely inside #sidebar's occluded band (a real oculist-m1df-
class false-dirty, safe to subtract) or partly/wholly outside it (a real,
separate flanking-figure/coverage defect at narrow viewports, unrelated to
the sidebar, that subtracting occlusion would incorrectly zero out if this
were later generalized to the grid without checking). This needs the same
"before/after every key, explain every move" discipline oculist-m1df used
for FORCED-LANDING, scoped to just these 12ish keys and the 2 narrow
viewports x 12 fonts = 24 scenarios each (cheaper than a full 47-key x
96-scenario re-sweep). Likely also worth asking whether the grid's own
side-fit tests (r.left/r.right against vw, see the FORCED-LANDING BLOCK
docstring) should account for #sidebar's real footprint the same way
FORCED-LANDING's forced-below/-above rows now implicitly do via this
subtraction -- if #sidebar eating most of a 320px viewport is *why* these
effects have nowhere clear to land, that is the same structural defect class
oculist-ey2e's FORCED-LANDING block exists to catch, just triggered by
narrow width instead of an artificial pin.

Scratch evidence (BEFORE-narrow sweep across all 47 keys, real playground,
unmodified code) is not preserved anywhere durable -- re-run
`node occlusion-sweep.js <key>` at the 320x900/360x900 scenarios to
reproduce, or trim SCENARIOS.viewports to just those two temporarily the way
this investigation did.
close_reason: A single @media (max-width:480px) makes #sidebar position:static and drops both body paddings to 5vw, so #match is genuinely visible at 320/360 instead of ~90 percent hidden under the sidebar's fixed column. 480 over 768 because only 320 and 360 overlap and no scenario width exists in 481-499. Reviewer-verified not to leak upward three ways: single max-width media query so inert above by construction, rects byte-identical at 481/500/700/900/1280/1440, and deterministic shattercrack row-identical across all 96+4+12 rows, with the probe shown non-blind by mutating the breakpoint to 1600px. The finding inverts the bead's fear: none of the twelve narrow-viewport keys was a sidebar artifact, all twelve stay dirty, and the sidebar was SUPPRESSING real dirt (gustswirl 344->627). The record's three annotations are now confirmed: the single-draw caveat sits immediately above the 288-row table with its 13 percent spread verified, gustswirl is described as the largest of several rather than the only key moved (tracer +11..+29 and ripplesurge +25..+81 on all 12 of their 320px rows), and the framecollapse negative-swing item is no longer open -- oculist-hq40 explained it as a DIFF_THRESHOLD=8 red-saturation artifact. title: fxWandCast: side-selection fallback overlaps the figure onto the match when neither side fits (wide match at narrow viewport) -- unrelated to the rx floor, found while measuring oculist-tvqw
description:
WHAT. fxWandCast's side-selection (sideRight.fits / sideLeft.fits, effects-playground.html ~7794-7798) has a fallback -- `landing = sideRight.fits ? sideRight : (sideLeft.fits ? sideLeft : sideRight)` -- that defaults to sideRight even when NEITHER side fits. The hard viewport clamp on figLeft (a few lines below) then drags the whole fairy figure onto TOP of the match instead of beside it.

WHEN IT FIRES. Only when the match is wide enough relative to the viewport that the flanking-figure budget (GAP + REACH_INWARD + REACH_OUTWARD, ~66px at max figure scale) cannot fit on either side. Bisected at the 320x900 (narrowest) viewport, match anchored 10px from the left edge, chromium: clean through fs=76 (match width ~246px), first non-glyph dirty pixels at fs=77 (~250px, count=31), first glyph ink at fs=80 (~259px, glyphAtMax=242/242). At fs=96 (~311px, the oculist-tvqw EDGE-PLACEMENT addition), maxPixels=915 with 95 glyph-ink pixels (chromium) / 873 with 85 glyph-ink (webkit).

WHY IT IS NOT THE RX FLOOR. Re-ran the identical scenario against a scratch mutant with the STRICTLY derived rx floor ((r.width/2 + ORBIT_EDGE_MARGIN)/cos(30deg)) instead of the shipped one: maxPixels/glyphAtMax were statistically the same (913/95 vs 915/95 chromium; 875/86 vs 873/85 webkit) -- widening rx does not fix this. The 1280x900 (wide) viewport never shows this defect at the same match width (stays 0/0 clean both floors), confirming it is a viewport-width-relative side-fit failure, not a sparkle-clearance problem.

REPRODUCE. node occlusion-sweep.js wandcast in artifacts/prototypes/, after oculist-tvqw's EDGE_FONTS 96px addition lands -- edge-left-320x900-96px and edge-right-320x900-96px are the two dirty rows.

SCOPE NOTE. Do not conflate with oculist-tvqw (the rx floor's own cos(30) algebra) or the pre-existing FORCED-LANDING 0/4 red (a third, separate defect). This is specifically the side-selection fallback's "neither side fits" case.
close_reason: fxWandCast's side-selection fallback no longer places the figure on the match. The guard now tests real box overlap AFTER the existing clamp -- figLeft/figTop vs the match rect -- rather than whether either side fit before clamping, and suppresses the render only when the clamped placement genuinely intersects. A first attempt used the fit-before-clamp test and was refuted by review: it deleted four previously-CLEAN renders (edge-left 70/72/74/76, clean at 50 samples, where the clamp had parked the figure at the viewport edge). The narrowed guard restores those byte-identically and still suppresses every genuinely-overlapping case. Reviewer widened the probe to ten widths against a byte-verified HEAD baseline: every edge-right width 70-96 was dirty before (687/681/679/680/687/695, then 710/716/710/691) and all suppress now; on the left, everything suppressed (84-96, previously 172/232/645/912) was dirty beforehand, so no previously-clean row is suppressed on either side. Normal path unchanged by evidence a zero-grid cannot fake: .fx count 8/8 on chromium and webkit. Mechanism confirmed independently -- both named rows have sideRight.fits=false and sideLeft.fits=false and clamp to an identical figLeft=279.08 regardless of which edge the match is anchored to, so this is the fallback and not oculist-tvqw's rx floor. Also reclassified FORCED-LANDING's 0/4 as the same defect at more extreme geometry rather than a third one (FORCED_PLACEMENTS pins #match to width:100vw so both fit flags are false by construction), while recording plainly that those four rows now read no-fx and the block is therefore unfalsifiable for this key. wandcast still exits 1 on a 1px edge-right-natural row, which is oculist-73l6 and pre-existing. Filed: wkfc (orbit/travel dirt from 78px, proven by per-element rects to be outside the figure's box), 73l6.
