title: occlusion-sweep: lockon's forced-below-1/2 FORCED-LANDING rows stay DIRTY (maxPixels=198, atTime=0ms) independent of the overshoot fix -- full-width #match at top:0px collides with a bracket's own viewport-corner start position before any animation runs
description:
FINDING (from oculist-rnbo, while fixing lockon's overshoot-bounce clearance
defect). After fixing the corner-bracket bounce (bounded the back-easing
overshoot to a fixed final-approach distance instead of the whole flight),
the main 96-scenario grid and EDGE-PLACEMENT block for lockon both went
0-dirty. FORCED-LANDING did not: forced-below-1 (500x180/16px) and
forced-below-2 (500x260/24px) stay DIRTY, maxPixels=198, atTime=0ms --
identical numbers before and after the bounce fix (confirmed via git stash:
same maxPixels=198/atTime=0ms on unmodified main). atTime=0ms means the
overlap exists at the very first sample, before the flight-in animation has
moved the bracket anywhere -- i.e. it is not the animation bounce.

These rows pin #match to `position:fixed; left:0; top:0px; width:100vw` (see
FORCED_PLACEMENTS / the forced-below comment block in occlusion-sweep.js).
fxLockon's top-left/top-right brackets start their flight AT the viewport
corners (0,0) and (vw-ARM,0). With #match spanning the full viewport width
at top:0, a bracket's own starting position already sits inside #match's
rect before any travel happens. This is a placement collision baked into the
forced-below geometry, not the overshoot easing rnbo fixed.

Not attempted here -- out of scope for rnbo, which is scoped to the
easing/overshoot defect only. Options for whoever picks this up: skip these
brackets' fly-in start point when #match already covers the corner (e.g.
start from just outside #match's edge instead of the literal viewport
corner), or treat this the same way FORCED_LANDING_SIDEBAR_EXEMPT treats
edgeticks's sidebar collision, if it's judged to be the same class of
harness/layout artifact rather than a paintable defect -- needs a judgment
call the rnbo brief didn't cover.
close_reason: fxLockon's corner brackets no longer start inside #match. escapeMatchCorner() does a minimum-translation separation of each bracket's ARM x ARM start box against the real match rect, plus fxLockon's own 8px pad so the escaped start has clearance rather than landing tangent (the flight travels back inward immediately, so zero margin still painted 4px). Geometric, not harness-keyed; all four brackets on one path; clear corners byte-identical. lockon now exits 0 with grid 96/96, FORCED-LANDING and EDGE-PLACEMENT all CLEAN (maxPixels=0), verified independently by the orchestrator (MD5 94d13bc621566e768de2cf452d475464). The 99px was isolated from the original 198px by oculist-m1df removing the sidebar-artifact half. Filed: hvu6 (degenerate short-flight regime), hq40 (fxFramecollapse, same class, worse).

title: occlusion-sweep accepts an unknown effect key and reports 96/96 CLEAN with exit 0, so a typo'd key silently passes the gate
description:
Found incidentally by the oculist-d48k reviewer, 2026-09-13, via a mis-quoted multi-key invocation.

node occlusion-sweep.js <key-that-does-not-exist> does not error. It reports 96/96 CLEAN at maxPixels=0 and exits 0.

That is the worst possible failure mode for a gate: a typo in a key name produces a confident green. Anything driving this from CI, a script, or a commit hook would read that as the effect passing. It also means every historical green for a mistyped key was vacuous.

The 96/96 CLEAN comes from sweeping a nonexistent effect, which paints nothing, so every scenario diffs clean.

FIX DIRECTION: validate the key against the known effect list before sweeping, and exit non-zero with a clear message naming the unknown key. Cheap, and it is the kind of guard the rest of this harness already applies elsewhere.

DONE-CRITERIA
- An unknown key exits non-zero and names the key.
- A known key is unaffected.
- Multi-key invocations validate every key before running any of them, so a typo in the third key fails before the first sweep starts rather than after.
close_reason: Unknown effect keys are now rejected before any control or sweep runs, validated against window.EFFECTS read once from the page so it cannot drift from the playground's registry. Reviewer PASS 2026-09-13 with causal proof: the pre-change file reports typo-key-xyz as CLEAN on base/forced/edge at exit 0, and the bug is gone with the change. A mutation dropping batflight from window.EFFECTS made the guard reject batflight and report 46 known keys, proving the list is live rather than a copy. Typo in third position fails in 0.65s with empty stdout against 258.9s for a real sweep. --control, --check-neutralization and --playground's path argument all unaffected; no leaked browser on the error path. Outer repo commit 3081324. Nits filed as a follow-up.

title: occlusion-sweep: fxLockon's corner brackets overshoot their own 8px match-clearance pad and graze #match, causing dirty=96/96
description:
Filed by the oculist-d48k implementer, 2026-09-13, while triaging the nine
sibling deferred-mount clearance-contract keys reported by oculist-xh9p.

FINDING. Unlike its eight siblings (lens, glitch, gravity, zoompunch,
depthdive, scramble, neon, underline -- all moved to
NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT by oculist-d48k as by-design coverage), lockon's
dirty=96/96 on the plain 96-scenario grid is a genuine flanking-clearance
defect, not by-design.

fxLockon (effects-playground.html) explicitly computes an 8px pad around
#match (`var pad = 8; var left = r.left - pad, top = r.top - pad, right =
r.right + pad, bottom = r.bottom + pad;`) and positions its four
corner-bracket divs' resting targets at that padded boundary, never on
#match itself. Read plainly, the brackets are designed to stay clear.

The brackets fly in from the four viewport corners via a synchronous WAAPI
.animate() using `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)` -- a "back"/overshoot
easing whose curve exceeds progress=1 partway through before settling back
to 1 (the 1.56 control point is the overshoot amount). That overshoot
carries a bracket's rendered position transiently PAST its padded resting
point, back toward #match, before it springs back to rest. Measured
directly (getBoundingClientRect() on the .fx elements at fixed seek times,
1280x900 viewport, 24px font, match rect left=205.3/top=435.1/right=283.0/
bottom=464.5): at t=200ms the top-left bracket's rendered box was at
left=209.6/top=453.8/right=227.6/bottom=471.8, which overlaps #match's rect
(border-top and border-left strips both fall inside #match's own x/y range)
despite the bracket's own 8px pad design.

This shows up in the sweep as a real but non-saturating dirty count: 96/96
scenarios dirty, maxPixels=544 (well under the ~9350 full-coverage ceiling
seen on by-design keys like glitch/lens/horseman), atTime consistently
mid-flight (200-400ms, inside the 450ms bracket-flight animation) across
scenarios -- consistent with the overshoot bounce, not a resting-position
overlap.

FIX DIRECTION (not attempted here, out of scope for d48k). Either tune the
easing/pad relationship so the overshoot amplitude stays within the 8px
pad, or add a few px of extra pad to absorb the known overshoot, then
re-verify against the sweep.

DONE-CRITERIA
* node occlusion-sweep.js lockon reports 0/96 dirty on the 96-scenario grid
  (or the corner-bracket overshoot is otherwise demonstrated not to reach
  #match at any sampled time).
* FORCED-LANDING and EDGE-PLACEMENT blocks for lockon are also clean, or
  independently justified if not.
* The fix is verified against the harness, not just visually.
close_reason: fxLockon's overshoot is now bounded to a fixed 40px final approach instead of scaling with the corner-to-target flight distance. Padding was ruled out analytically first: 9.78% overshoot over a 90-1216px flight is 19-120px against an 8px pad, and raising the pad raises the distance too. Reviewer PASS 2026-09-14, verified by mutation (sweeping a HEAD copy via --playground reds all three blocks) and by a dense 3ms probe across the full flight: first leg strictly monotonic and never crossing the target, handoff continuous at 315ms, peak overshoot 3.91px, 0 of 151 frames painting inside the match rect. Grid 96/96 dirty maxPixels=544 -> CLEAN 0/96 maxPixels=0; EDGE-PLACEMENT 8/8 maxPixels=352 -> CLEAN 0/8. FORCED-LANDING stays 2/4 at atTime=0ms, before any motion, justified under done-criterion 2 and left to oculist-x2g1. Real margin is ~1.09px worst case because the 3px border is inset from the 8px pad; recorded in both files. Outer repo commit b26a21c. NOTE FOR CHRIS: the motion is visibly different -- 12x smaller bounce -- see the bead comments.

title: occlusion-sweep: all nine of blink's sibling deferred-mount clearance-contract keys (lens, lockon, glitch, gravity, zoompunch, depthdive, neon, underline, scramble) already report ISSUES FOUND with dirty=96/96 on the synchronous-only 96-scenario grid, before any deferred-mount content exists -- check whether some belong in NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT (e.g. zoompunch/depthdive scale/rotate the whole page including #match by design) rather than being genuine flanking-figure defects
description:
Filed by the oculist-xh9p implementer, 2026-09-13, from xh9p's mandatory scoping step.

FINDING. All nine of blink's sibling deferred-mount clearance-contract keys -- lens, lockon, glitch, gravity, zoompunch, depthdive, neon, underline, scramble -- already report ISSUES FOUND with dirty=96/96 on the plain 96-scenario grid, using only the synchronous-only measurement, before any deferred-mount content exists and before the deferred-mount question even applies. With blink already known dirty, all ten are dirty today.

This inverted xh9p's premise: xh9p worried that a key could be declared CLEAN on a count known to be a lower bound. No key is currently clean, so that risk is real as a method hole but dormant. xh9p is parked on this bead.

THE QUESTION. 96/96 is total saturation, which is a suspicious number for a 'flanking artwork accidentally overlaps the match' defect and a natural one for 'this effect covers or transforms the match by design'. Several of the nine look like the latter: zoompunch and depthdive scale or rotate the whole page including #match, and scramble mutates the mark's own glyphs. Those would belong in NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT on the same footing as matchstrike, comet, stamp, inkbloom and horseman (oculist-1la5), not be treated as defects to fix.

Others in the list have no obvious by-design reason to cover the match and may be genuine defects.

So: triage the nine. For each, decide whether saturation is intrinsic to what the effect does, or a real flanking-clearance defect.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Each of the nine is classified by-design or defect, with the evidence for the call.
- Keys that are by-design are moved into NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT with the reasoning recorded where the exemption is declared.
- Keys judged genuine defects are filed as their own beads, not fixed here.
- No key's verdict changes except the ones deliberately reclassified; the exempted six, batflight and arrowshot are unaffected.
- Interacts with oculist-3rl (scramble's exit code) and oculist-m1df (a separate FORCED-LANDING measurement flaw).
close_reason: Nine keys triaged. Eight exempted in TWO classes: by-design coverage (lens, glitch, gravity, zoompunch, depthdive, scramble) and emberignite's knowingly-tolerated halo-overrun class (neon, underline, per oculist-aun, which had explicitly warned against flattening them together). lockon judged a genuine defect, still gating at exit 1, filed as oculist-rnbo. Final reviewer PASS 2026-09-13: every figure in the corrected fxUnderline passage reproduces exactly across two byte-identical runs -- grid max 1031 on 900x700/48px at t=400ms, 1280x900/24px peaks at 536, and the peak-time histogram confirms 37 of 96 scenarios at t=440ms. Outer repo commit ca2a71d. Also filed oculist-q8ig from this work.

comments.text:

coverage" to emberignite's "knowingly-tolerated halo overrun" class
(oculist-aun), cited by name; do not re-flatten them back into by-design if

Final text of the two relabeled entries:

--- fxNeon and fxUnderline intro ---
fxNeon and fxUnderline are NOT the same class as the six keys above --
read the correction against oculist-aun's emberignite entry above before
touching either. Both belong to emberignite's "knowingly-tolerated halo
overrun" class, not "by design coverage": in both, the effect's own box
never overlaps the match rect, and 100% of the measured dirt is
box-shadow/blur bleed past DIFF_THRESHOLD, not artwork placed on #match.
A first pass on this bead mislabeled both as by-design and is corrected
here -- do not re-flatten them back into the by-design bucket if this is
revisited, same instruction oculist-aun already gave for emberignite.

--- fxNeon ---
fxNeon: the tube's box (border + all its OUTER box-shadow glows) sits
pad=8 OUTSIDE the match rect on every side and never overlaps it. Only
the box-shadow's `inset 0 0 10px` term paints inward, and that inset
blur (10px) exceeds the 8px pad -- an incidental halo overrun, same
shape as emberignite's blur bleed, not intrinsic artwork placement.
The one piece of artwork that IS genuinely on #match -- the 'wash'
radial-gradient overlay centered at the match's own (cx,cy) -- is
mounted from setTimeout(fn, 400), so this harness's neutralization
drops it entirely; it never renders during a sweep. The recorded
maxPixels=1409 is therefore the inset-blur halo alone and EXCLUDES the
wash -- it is not evidence the wash is safe, only that this harness
never sees it (LOWERBOUND, same caveat as gravity's dropped flash
above).

--- fxUnderline ---
fxUnderline: the dash/trail's own box sits at y = r.bottom + 2 -- a
0.5px gap from the match's own bottom edge at the geometry measured
(dash top 465.0 vs match bottom 464.5), not the 8px-style pad neon
uses, but still never overlapping the rect itself. 100% of the
measured dirt is box-shadow blur (up to 10px) bleeding across that
sub-pixel gap, peaking at t=440ms mid-flight (maxPixels=1031 on a
1280x900/24px scenario). The terminal burst's ~4px corner overlap and
the dash's later width-snap to r.width are BOTH mounted from
setTimeout bodies this harness drops -- neither renders during a
sweep, so neither is what produces the measured dirt; citing them as
if they did was the first-pass error here. FORCED-LANDING classifies
this key's landing as `below` in all four forced rows -- the same
label batflight (the canonical flanking-figure/clearance-contract
effect) gets, not `overlap` or `no-fx` the way every genuinely
by-design key above reports. That landing label is corroborating
evidence for the halo-overrun reading, not by itself dispositive.

--- EDGE-PLACEMENT note ---
EDGE-PLACEMENT NOTE for both: putting a key on this Set silences it in
all three blocks the sweep runs -- the 96-scenario grid, FORCED-
LANDING, and EDGE-PLACEMENT (the block that exists specifically to
catch edge-clamp defects the grid structurally can't reach, e.g.
fxWandCast's, oculist-1ta.26). For a halo-overrun tolerance rather
than full by-design coverage, that means neon and underline also stop
being checked for an edge-clamp-class defect near a viewport edge,
which is a real cost of keeping them on this Set rather than dropping
them -- worth naming for these two specifically, since it is not
implied by "the blur bleeds a little" the way full coverage implies
"nothing else to check" for lens/glitch/scramble above.

Not closing -- leaving for review.

title: fxWandCast's back sparkles still paint 45px-squared onto the glyphs during the resize dissolve's 180ms fade
description:
Found by the oculist-1ta.27 reviewer, 2026-09-12, which could NOT reproduce that bead's implementer's claim that the bleed was eliminated.

MEASURED. Pixel-diff inside #match's live rect, threshold 8, the same technique occlusion-sweep.js uses, at the 1180px to 1172px width shift (a small same-line move, the case oculist-1ta.27 named as worst) across 16 midT values sampled every 40ms from +30ms to +300ms after the resize:

  no-resize control: 0 at every midT, so anything below is genuinely resize-induced
  before 1ta.27's fix:  max 59 px-squared, sustained 29-59 across midT 700-1600
  after 1ta.27's fix:   max 45 px-squared (43 on a repeat run), nonzero at midT 1100, 1200, 1400, 1500, 1600

So the resize dissolve REDUCED the bleed, it did not remove it. Screenshot at midT 1500 +30ms confirms it visually.

WHY IT SURVIVES. fxWandCast's backWrap punches a STATIC evenodd clip-path hole at the fire-time rect plus a 2px CLIP_MARGIN, computed once and never updated. The dissolve fades opacity to 0 over DISSOLVE_DUR=180ms. For those 180ms the sparkles are still painting, and the hole is still at the old rect, so anything the resize moved under them is unmasked.

This is outside oculist-1ta.27's own Accept clause, which was nodes and animations reaching 0 and #match unmutated, both of which that bead met. It is filed separately rather than folded in.

TWO WAYS TO FIX, not chosen here:
1. Update backWrap's clip-path on the resize trigger before starting the fade, so the hole follows the new rect for the duration of the fade.
2. Hide the back layer outright at trigger time instead of fading it, accepting a harder cut for that one layer while the rest of the effect fades.

Option 2 is cheaper and probably sufficient, since the back layer is the only one with a match-shaped hole to go stale. Option 1 is more correct if any other layer ever grows one.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The 16-midT sweep at the 1180 to 1172 shift reads 0 px-squared at every sample.
- The no-resize control still reads 0, so the fix is not just masking the measurement.
- The scroll dissolve is unaffected: re-run the 1ta.12 check.
- occlusion-sweep wandcast's EDGE-PLACEMENT and 96-grid results are unchanged, since this touches wandcast's clip-path and oculist-mbmy is separately open against that same clip logic.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS, all four done-criteria demonstrated with numbers. Option 2 (hard cut) via an opt-in dissolveHardCut flag on the generic dissolveEffect(); fxWandCast's backWrap sets it. 16-midT sweep at the 1180->1172 shift: max 51px^2 pre-fix (nonzero across midT 1180-1600) -> 0 at every sample; no-resize control 0 in both directions. Reviewer verified the new harness resize-dissolve-backwrap-check.js is a real oracle by reverting the fix and watching it go red, plus an independent probe (25px^2 pre, 0 post). Shared dissolve path arithmetically unchanged for the other 46 effects; all four scroll-dissolve checks pass; occlusion-sweep wandcast byte-identical to the post-mbmy baseline. No remaining exposure window: a second resize inside the 180ms cannot re-expose the stale hole. Cost: at most six unglowed 8px back-arc dots cut rather than faded, on the interrupt path only. Outer-repo commit b41b5b1 on goal/p3-cleanup.

title: fxWandCast's edge-clamp occlusion is unfixed: 35px inside the match rect, 1px of it glyph ink
description:
Recorded while closing oculist-1ta.26, which added the sweep coverage that makes this visible but was explicitly scoped to not change any effect.

THE DEFECT. With #match about 10px from the right edge at 320x900, fxWandCast paints 35px inside the match rect, 1 of them glyph ink, per the original oculist-1ta.6 second review. The cause is an rx clamp that only engages within about 25px of an edge, so the effect's back-arc sparkles land on the glyphs instead of clearing them.

IT IS UNFIXED TODAY, and was never fixed. The oculist-1ta.26 reviewer measured the edge block against the 1ta.6 commit 3734771 and against current HEAD and got IDENTICAL results both times: 0/8 clean, maxPixels=61, with edge-right-320x900-natural at exactly 35px in both. The defect was invisible rather than absent, because the 96-scenario grid never placed the match near an edge.

Reproduce: node occlusion-sweep.js wandcast in artifacts/prototypes/. The EDGE-PLACEMENT block is the relevant one; the 96-grid still reports 96/96 clean.

NOTE fxWandCast is also already red in its FORCED-LANDING block (0/4 clean, maxPixels=898 at HEAD). That is a separate defect from this one. Do not conflate them, and say which you are fixing.

DONE-CRITERIA
- wandcast reports 8/8 clean in the EDGE-PLACEMENT block, at both natural and 48px fonts, at both 320x900 and 1280x900, on both sides.
- No glyph ink is painted at any edge placement.
- The 96-grid stays 96/96 clean, so the fix does not trade the common case for the edge case.
- The rx clamp's engagement threshold is documented where it is set, since 'only within about 25px of an edge' is the property that made this invisible.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS, all four done-criteria met and reproduced 3x per tree on chromium. EDGE-PLACEMENT 0/8 dirty maxPixels=61 -> 8/8 clean maxPixels=0 (both fonts, both viewports, both sides); 96-grid unchanged at 96/96 clean maxPixels=0; clamp engagement threshold documented at the clamp. Cause was frontEl, the top-level unclipped front-arc sparkle, plus a flat rx floor that beat rxViewportCap near any viewport edge and ignored the 30deg THETA0 landing bound. The cos(30deg) divisor is load-bearing: the reviewer's mutant dropping it goes 4/8 clean. Two costs measured and recorded in the source: sparkles now reach 5.8-7.9px outside the viewport at edge placements where HEAD was 0.0 (accepted trade, viewport edge is not the contract), and the floor is not the strictly derived one so clearance at the 30deg landing is ~6.3px not 12px with a shortfall that grows with match width -- filed as oculist-tvqw. FORCED-LANDING left red as a separate defect; its 898 -> 897 shift is deterministic across 3 runs each way, not noise. Outer-repo commit 2a7e4aa on goal/p3-cleanup.

title: occlusion-sweep: ten clearance-contract keys can be declared clean on a count known to be incomplete
description:
Raised by the oculist-e2w implementer and confirmed by its reviewer, 2026-09-12. Nothing regressed; the hole predates e2w and was previously undocumented. e2w labelled it, this bead is about closing it.

THE HOLE. occlusion-sweep.js drops every setTimeout an effect schedules during runEffect, for determinism. Fourteen fx* functions mount top-level artwork from inside a later setTimeout, so that artwork never exists during a sweep and those keys' pixel counts are a LOWER BOUND on real occlusion.

Four of the fourteen (matchstrike, comet, stamp, inkbloom) are already in NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT and do not drive the exit code. The other TEN are ordinary clearance-contract keys whose lower-bound counts DO drive pass/fail: blink, lens, lockon, glitch, gravity, zoompunch, depthdive, neon, underline, scramble.

So the sweep can print CLEAN for one of those ten on a number that is known to be incomplete. The verdict is not wrong so much as unfounded.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST A BIGGER e2w. Closing it means taking a design fork that e2w deliberately did not take, because e2w's whole point was to label honestly rather than to change what is measured:

OPTION A. A second, un-neutralized coverage pass for the affected keys only, accepting that it is non-deterministic and treating it as advisory rather than gating.
OPTION B. A seam that drains deferred mounts SYNCHRONOUSLY: run the dropped timer callbacks immediately after runEffect returns instead of discarding them, so the artwork exists without waiting on real time. Preserves determinism if the callbacks do not themselves depend on elapsed time. Needs checking against the fourteen bodies.
OPTION C. Move the ten into NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT, so an unfounded clean verdict becomes an explicit N/A. Honest, and the cheapest, but it gives up gating on ten effects.

Option B looks the most promising and is the one to evaluate first. Do not start implementing before choosing.

SCOPING STEP, from the e2w reviewer, worth doing before any design work. Of the ten, only blink is confirmed dirty today. The false-clean risk is whichever of the remaining nine currently report CLEAN, since those are the ones whose verdict rests on the incomplete count. Establishing that list is nine sweeps, roughly 30 minutes, and it tells you how big this actually is before you pick an option.

ADJACENT, worth at most a sentence in whatever lands here: fxSearchlight (effects-playground.html:1066) and fxLetterwave (:1341) call .animate() on already-mounted elements from inside dropped timers. Their sampled rendering is also not the full effect, but that is a different class from deferred mounts and mostly over-measures rather than under-measures.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The nine-sweep scoping step is done and the actually-at-risk keys are named.
- One of the three options is chosen, with the reasoning recorded in occlusion-sweep.js rather than only here.
- If B is chosen: determinism is demonstrated, not assumed. Repeated runs byte-identical, and the fourteen callback bodies checked for elapsed-time dependence.
- Whatever lands, no key is left printing CLEAN on a count the file itself describes as a lower bound.
close_reason: Collapsed to one live key and closed it. d48k had already moved eight of the ten into NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT; blink is DIRTY at essentially every scenario so its lower bound cannot produce a false clean; that left lockon as the only key printing CLEAN on a count the file itself labelled LOWERBOUND. Option B, scoped to that key: fxLockon's two non-cleanup dropped callbacks are replayed, maxEnd extended 450->1350ms (samples 13->35), and animations colliding with the synchronous flight are cancelled. Reviewer-verified with seven mutations: thickening the ring border reds all three blocks (the CLEAN is founded on a rendered, sampled ring); deleting the cancel flips FORCED-LANDING to a false CLEAN (the fix is load-bearing); exactly 4 cancellations, all bracket-bounce transform, no over-cancel; the delay-triple guard exits 1 loudly when violated. x2g1's maxPixels=99 survives byte-identical. Residual guard hole filed.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
SCOPING STEP DONE, 2026-09-13. The result inverts the bead's premise.

None of the nine report CLEAN. All nine (lens, lockon, glitch, gravity, zoompunch, depthdive, neon, underline, scramble) print ISSUES FOUND with dirty=96/96 on the plain 96-scenario grid, from the synchronous-only measurement alone, before the deferred-mount question applies. With blink already known dirty, ALL TEN clearance-contract keys are dirty today. The false-clean risk is real as a method hole but DORMANT: no key currently rides on it. Done-criterion 4 is satisfied vacuously right now.

OPTION B EVALUATED AND REJECTED, with evidence.
Narrow elapsed-time test passes: no performance.now(), Date.now() or .currentTime in any of the fourteen bodies. But all fourteen schedule, as their largest-delay top-level setTimeout, an unconditional els.forEach(el => el.remove()). Draining the dropped callbacks literally runs that cleanup in the same synchronous batch as the mounts and erases the artwork before sampling. Measured on blink: countAfterRunEffect=2, delays=[160,280,900], countAfterDrain=0.

A refined variant (skip only the single largest-delay top-level entry) does leave artwork standing (blink 4, zoompunch 1, depthdive 1, scramble 2) and body style still restores via cleanupAndAssert -> runEffect('__none__') -> clearFx. But it is materially more engineering than the bead implies:
  - it rests on an unstated, untested convention that the last/largest-delay top-level timer is pure cleanup, true for all fourteen today but nothing declares or enforces it, so a future effect breaks it silently and reintroduces exactly this risk;
  - maxEnd and the sampleTimes grid are computed from getAnimations() BEFORE any deferred mount exists, so draining after runEffect still under-samples the deferred content's own animation duration. That is a second undesigned fix;
  - no tie-break if two top-level calls ever share the max delay.

REMAINING FORK IS A vs C, and it is now entangled with oculist-d48k.
C (move the ten into NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT) would convert ten CURRENTLY-FAILING gates into N/A. That is suppressing ten live failures unless those failures are themselves expected, which is precisely what d48k is about (zoompunch and depthdive scale the whole page including #match by design and may legitimately belong in the exemption). So C cannot be judged correct until d48k is triaged.
A (un-neutralized advisory pass) avoids B's cleanup-erasure problem but, as a literal flag flip, still samples against the synchronous-only maxEnd/sampleTimes and so would not actually observe deferred content without its own extension.

No files modified. Parked for a human call on A vs C.

title: fxHorseman's rear/throw beats cannot fit on-screen at 320x900/360x900 (and other narrow/large-font combos) while GAP_CLEAR stays intact -- SPRITE_W (150px) exceeds available space left of #match
description:
Filed while fixing oculist-ire2 (fxHorseman rearX clamp). ire2's fix makes
rearX always equal r.left - GAP_CLEAR (full clearance preserved everywhere,
verified), but that alone cannot put the rear/throw beats on-screen at
320x900 or 360x900, and the same conflict recurs at other grid combos.

MEASURED (Playwright, effects-playground.html, SPRITE_W=150, GAP_CLEAR=120):
  320x900: r.left=25.6  -> rearX=-94.4 (0px of rendered rear-pose art on-screen;
    its rightmost rendered point is only ~38px right of center, still ~56px
    short of x=0)
  360x900: r.left=28.8  -> rearX=-91.2 (same, 0px on-screen)
  500x400 (all fonts):        r.left=40.0  -> rearX=-80.0 (0px on-screen)
  700x1000 @ font=48px:       r.left=56.0  -> rearX=-64.0 (0px on-screen)
  900x700  @ font=48px:       r.left=72.0  -> rearX=-48.0 (0px on-screen)
  1440x800 @ font=48px:       r.left=115.2 -> rearX=-4.8  (marginal)
  1280x900 / 1280x600 (all fonts, the validated-correct case): r.left=205.3
    -> rearX=85.3, ~2px of the tail's absolute tip clipped -- imperceptible,
    matches today's shipped/reviewed look.

Root cause is sprite size, not GAP_CLEAR's magnitude: even at GAP_CLEAR=0
(rear pose's right edge touching the match's own left edge), the rear pose's
own wound-back arm (visible during the "rear" beat, before the throw) sits
~95px to the left of the sprite's right edge. At 320px, r.left=25.6px, so
even zero gap leaves that arm ~70px off-screen. SPRITE_W=150px is itself
close to half the viewport width, with almost nothing left of the match to
put it in.

Proposed trades (not chosen here -- needs a design decision):
  1. Scale SPRITE_H/SPRITE_W down responsively at narrow viewports (e.g.
     below ~500px) so the rear pose's footprint fits in the space actually
     available left of the match.
  2. Reduce GAP_CLEAR's fraction responsively when it doesn't fit, floored
     at a small positive value (never zero/negative) -- helps only
     marginally per the math above, since sprite width dominates the
     shortfall, not gap size.
  3. Accept and document that the rear/throw beats are only guaranteed
     visible above some minimum r.left / viewport width, and treat the
     narrowest grid rows as a known limitation of this effect rather than
     a defect to eliminate.

Screenshots proving 0px visibility at 320/360 across gallop/rear/throw
(with arc/burst/exit unaffected) are in the ire2 implementer's session
scratchpad; not committed to the repo.
close_reason: Option 3 (document the limitation) chosen by Chris and landed. Thresholds measured by painted-pixel diff with DOM-removal isolation: rear body r.left~82, throwing hand ~115, wound-back arm ~149 (binding). Reviewer PASS 2026-09-13 on the second review, reproduced independently on chromium and webkit and cross-checked against a closed-form derivation from the polygon source (81.93/115.06/147.41). Outer repo commit 4f8b979.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
CORRECTION from the oculist-ire2 review. This description presents '0px of rendered rear-pose art on-screen' as a consequence of ire2's fix. It was already 0px before that fix: at 320x900 the rear pose artwork's rightmost point sat at x=-0.8 under the OLD clamp, and the rear and throw frames were pixel-identical to the effect-free baseline in both revisions. The old clamp's '15px on-screen' was the sprite box's empty right margin, not artwork.

That shifts the weighing of the three trades. Option 1 (scale the sprite responsively) is not recovering something the fix took away, it is adding visibility that never existed at these viewports. Option 3 (document a minimum viewport width for the rear/throw beats) is correspondingly stronger than the description implies, since nothing regressed.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Documented in fxHorseman's top-of-function comment (effects-playground.html). Measured thresholds (Playwright, r.left swept directly at fixed 1280x900 vw, since r.left is not monotonic in viewport width alone): rear-pose arm visible from r.left>=~61px, throwing hand visible from r.left>=~109px (zero-crossing between r.left=108 -0.7px and r.left=109 +0.3px). Root cause/pre-existing/trade-rejected rationale written into the comment per Option 3. oculist-1ta.7's criterion text was not found anywhere in the tree (grepped for '1ta.7', 'criterion 1', 'all six beats', 'gallop, rear, throw' -- zero hits outside bead text), so left unqualified per instructions -- nothing to edit. occlusion-sweep.js horseman: control OK, neutralization-control OK, horseman N/A (exempt per oculist-1la5) with 0 harness-failed, exit 0. Diff is a pure 24-line comment insertion, no executable code touched, so GAP_CLEAR/pumpkin-launch math is unchanged by construction. Note: the brief's 'ponytail: prefix per this repo's convention' has zero precedent anywhere in the tree -- not used.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Correction to the description's own figures, per FAIL review: the ~70px and ~38px off-screen numbers in this bead's description are wrong, same box-vs-artwork mistake ire2 already flagged once before -- they came from getBoundingClientRect() on a rotated SVG group and/or from dropping the SPRITE_W/2=75px offset between rearX (sprite center) and the local coordinate the shortfall was measured from. Re-measured by painted pixels (DOM-removal isolation per group, pixel-diff vs the effect-free baseline, opacity swaps do not isolate here because fill:forwards animations override them): rear pose's body first paints at r.left ~82-83px; throwing hand crosses x=0 at r.left ~115-119px; the wound-back arm crosses LAST, at r.left ~149-150px, and is the true binding threshold, not the hand. At 320px with GAP_CLEAR simulated to 0 (rearX=26): throwing hand's own shape is only ~2px short of the screen edge, wound-back arm only ~3-4px short -- both nearly on screen, not ~70px off. Reducing GAP_CLEAR would genuinely buy visibility; the real reason not to is that it spends the flanking clearance the rear pose exists to maintain (what ire2's unconditional rearX = r.left - GAP_CLEAR fix protects), not that the trade is a non-fix. Comment above fxHorseman (effects-playground.html ~7082-7128) corrected to match; Option 3 decision and GAP_CLEAR itself untouched.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Partial retraction of the 2026-09-13 17:21 comment, per the oculist-9q4m review. That comment lumped the ~70px and ~38px off-screen figures together as both wrong. Only the ~70px figure is wrong. The ~38px figure is CORRECT: measured rightmost painted point of the rear-pose artwork = spriteLeft + 113.07, sprite center = spriteLeft + 75, so the rightmost point is +38.07 from center, matching the ~38px this bead's description used. The description's derived rear-pose artwork ~56px short of x=0 at the relevant r.left is likewise correct, not a box-vs-artwork error. Do not distrust either figure based on the 17:21 comment; only the ~70px number in that comment (and the stale in-code claim it corrected) was ever wrong. Separately, effects-playground.html around line 7294 (a different, still-stale comment asserting that zeroing GAP_CLEAR still falls short by ~50-60px) has been corrected/retracted in place under oculist-9q4m; it is now consistent with this bead's ~82-150px painted-pixel thresholds.

title: fxArrowShot: short viewports with a centred match put the archer on the match row, and no sweep row covers it
description:
arrowshot overlaps the match in short viewports where the match is centred, and no sweep row covers that case.

Found by the oculist-aouc reviewer, 2026-09-10. Pre-existing at HEAD, and not made worse by aouc.

MEASURED, with the reviewer's extra placements (scratchpad sweep-rv.js; not durable, so re-derive them):
- centered-500x180: 1268 dirty px on the new code, 1544 at HEAD.
- centered-500x300: 588 dirty px on both.
The dirty pixels come from the top-left archer sitting on the match row. The fallback's launch point is fixed by the archer's corner, so no endpoint push can clear it. The aouc fix documents this as an accepted last-resort degrade.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN forced-below-1. A match centred by a real scrollIntoView in a short viewport is an ordinary real-world case: a small browser window, or a phone in landscape. The full-width pinned match that forced-below-1 uses is synthetic. The 96-grid has no viewport short enough to reach it.

STEPS
1. Add short-viewport rows to occlusion-sweep.js's FORCED_PLACEMENTS: a centred match at 500x180 and 500x300, scoped with `keys` to arrowshot, or to every key if cheap. Show them dirty today.
2. Fix fxArrowShot's corner choice so that in the fallback the archer's own box, feather included, clears the match. For example, pick the corner whose launch point clears, or move the archer off-screen as the aouc fix does for the feather.
3. Accept: the new rows go clean, the 96-grid output is byte-identical for every key, and the existing forced rows stay clean.
close_reason: The fallback now computes main's own result as a baseline and takes the whole-body archer clamp only when it strictly improves the archer, does not worsen the flight, and reverses nothing. Final review measured against real main over the 1.83M grid and 400k random (fresh seed): 0 clean-on-main-but-changed, 0 newlyBackward, 0 worse, 0 guardedDiff, 0 newly dirty. centered-500x180 goes 699 to 0 and 500x220 goes 438 to 0, with the 96-grids byte-identical. arrowshot-fallback-check.js gains a --baseline mode that catches the first attempt's regression, and its archer assertion is report-only.

title: occlusion-sweep FORCED-LANDING block: arrowshot's unguarded plan fallback overlaps the match at degenerate full-width geometry
description:
Found while implementing oculist-ey2e's FORCED-LANDING block in occlusion-sweep.js.

REPRO: node occlusion-sweep.js arrowshot, with #match pinned via harness-only
inline CSS to position:fixed; left:0; top:0; width:100vw; display:block;
text-align:center at viewport 500x180, font-size 16px (FORCED_PLACEMENTS'
'forced-below-1' row -- the same full-width-at-top recipe oculist-1ta.8's
reviewer used to force batflight's below landing).

RESULT: DIRTY, maxPixels=315 at atTime=1320ms (of a 2150ms animation).
Direct inspection at t=1320 (see the probe capture) shows the flight-arrow
.fx element's bounding rect (left=190.6 top=9.8 right=253.2 bottom=49.4)
overlapping #match's rect (left=0 top=0 right=500 bottom=28.78) -- the arrow
box dips into the match's row while airborne, before settling below it.

WHY: fxArrowShot's impact-plan chooser (effects-playground.html, function
fxArrowShot starting ~line 3918) picks among 'left'/'top'/'bottom' plans each
gated by its own MARGIN floor (leftDx/topDy/bottomDy > MARGIN). When a
full-width match leaves none of the three candidates clearing MARGIN, the
code falls through to the "Nothing clears the floor" branch (~line 4036),
which picks whichever of the three is least-bad -- with NO clearance
guarantee at all, unlike the fits-gated candidates every other branch uses.
That branch's own comment already flags it as a "least bad" degrade, but
occlusion-sweep.js never previously exercised any geometry that reaches it.

SCOPE NOTE: this is a finding about fxArrowShot's own fallback geometry, not
a defect in occlusion-sweep.js. The 8 new FORCED-LANDING scenarios added by
oculist-ey2e are otherwise clean for both batflight and arrowshot (3/4);
only forced-below-1 trips this for arrowshot. forced-below-2 (500x260,
font 24) stays clean for arrowshot -- the floor is viewport-height-sensitive.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Either give the "nothing clears the floor" branch a real clearance
  guarantee (e.g. degrade to whichever plan overlaps least while still
  bounding the overlap, or accept an off-screen degrade the way batflight's
  own last-resort 'below' landing does) or document why an unguarded overlap
  is acceptable in this last-resort branch specifically.
- occlusion-sweep.js's FORCED-LANDING block (forced-below-1: 500x180 @ 16px)
  goes clean for arrowshot after the fix.
close_reason: Final review passed every merge-bar item and both criteria. The fallback pushes only on a painted overlap of the arrow in flight or quiver, is capped so the flight never reverses, and a painted safety check undoes any push that made things worse. Across 1.83M grid and 400k random geometries: 0 clean-in-main-but-changed, 0 forward flights turned backward, 0 worse than main. forced-below-1 goes from DIRTY 315 to clean, and the 192 grid lines are identical to main. arrowshot-fallback-check.js guards it permanently.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: From the oculist-ey2e reviews, 2026-09-10: arrowshot's FORCED_PLACEMENTS rows carry no expect entries, so the landing check does not cover it. When fixing this, add expect entries for arrowshot. Also note that only forced-below-1 reaches the unguarded fallback: forced-below-2 takes the guarded bottom plan (bottomDy 109.9) and both above rows take the guarded top plan.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
RUN 5 (2026-09-11): FAILED REVIEW TWICE ON A REAL DEFECT. Run stopped. Work is committed and pushed on outer-repo branch goal/arrowshot-fallback-clearance, with the bead left open. DO NOT MERGE until the defect below is fixed, unless Chris accepts it.

WHAT WORKS, verified by two reviews:
- forced-below-1 is clean. Minimum clearance across every .fx shape at 2ms steps is 56.74px, where HEAD gives -20.58.

title: ensureVisible still skips effects near the page ends, under a horizontal scrollbar, and on mixed calc() padding
description:
ensureVisible still silently skips the effect in three cases the oculist-ag8w formula does not model. Same failure class as ag8w: a correct, uninterrupted scroll read as an abort, with no error.

Measured by the oculist-ag8w reviewer, 2026-09-10, against effects-playground.html ensureVisible and finish (~lines 7315-7401).

1. NO CLAMP AT THE PAGE ENDS (the big one). When the document cannot scroll far enough to centre the match, the settled position differs from the centred target and the 4px tolerance skips the effect.
   - Near the end: with 50px of trailing space the delta is 5.00 and the effect is skipped; with 0px it is 55.00. Roughly, any out-of-view match in the last ~357px of a 700px-viewport document is silently skipped.
   - Near the top: with the match in the first paragraph and the page scrolled to the bottom, the delta is -154.5 and it is skipped.
   On a real page, a match in the first or last screenful is common.
2. HORIZONTAL SCROLLBAR. finish() centres on window.innerHeight, but the scrollport is scrollingElement.clientHeight. With classic scrollbars and horizontal overflow those are 700 and 685, so the settled delta is -7.25 and the effect is skipped (.fx 0), with or without scroll-padding. Using clientHeight gives 0.25. This is invisible in the harness because headless Chromium hides scrollbars. Add a row launched with ignoreDefaultArgs ['--hide-scrollbars'].
3. MIXED calc() PADDING. scroll-padding-top: calc(10% + 20px) makes intendedTop NaN, so the comparison never skips and aborts draw again (End abort, max .fx 3). This is the harmless direction, the old flicker rather than suppression, but a NaN guard is cheap.

FIX DIRECTION. Either clamp the target to what the page can actually scroll to (0 to scrollHeight - clientHeight) and switch to clientHeight, or take ag8w's option 2: compare against where an uninterrupted scroll really settles, which sidesteps modelling scrollIntoView at all. Option 2 would cover all three cases.

DONE-CRITERIA
- An out-of-view match in the last screenful of a long page draws its effect.
- A match in the first paragraph, fired from the bottom of the page, draws its effect.
- With visible scrollbars and horizontal overflow, the effect draws.
- calc() mixing percentage and length does not produce NaN.
- Genuine aborts are still suppressed in each of those layouts, and every prefire-scroll-abort-check.js row still passes.
close_reason: Option 2 landed: ensureVisible measures the scroll target with an instant scrollIntoView probe instead of modelling it. Reviewer PASS 2026-09-13, verified by mutation: A.3 (+0ms abort row) reds when the double rAF is reinstated, G.1 settle-time reds when the scrollBehavior forcing is removed, G.3 reds when the probe scrollend guard is removed. Own R3 sweep 21/21 clean at +0..+40ms vs 15/21 bad on the mutant. Gate 8/8 runs 36 PASS / 0 FAIL, both engines. Outer repo commit 780f457.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
PARKED after two failed reviews, 2026-09-13. Stop condition for the /goal run. Work is on branch raj4-wip, commit 8b14b10, NOT on goal/p3-cleanup and not merged.

APPROACH IS ENDORSED, KEEP IT. Option 2: measure the scroll target instead of modelling it. A synchronous instant scrollIntoView, read scrollingElement.scrollTop, revert; finish() compares the real settled scrollTop against that. resolveScrollPadding() deleted entirely -- the browser already handles scroll-padding/margin including calc(), the real scrollport, and clamping to [0, scrollHeight - clientHeight]. Both reviews said this direction is right and worth salvaging rather than reverting.

WHAT IS DONE. All four filed failure modes red pre-fix, green post-fix. Gate 34 PASS / 0 FAIL across repeated runs. Abort rows proven discriminating by mutation (stubbing the comparison turns A.1, A.2, C.6, D.2, D.4, E.2, F.2 and G.2 red).

REVIEW 1 found two regressions, both now fixed and independently re-verified by review 2:
- FATAL: CSS html { scroll-behavior: smooth } made the probe's revert animated, so it beat the real scroll and the page never reached the match (fx:0, top:0 both engines). Fixed by forcing scrollBehavior auto around both halves of the probe and restoring the inline value. Real scroll still genuinely animated: 41 intermediate scrollTop values chromium, 11 webkit.
- The probe's own scroll/scrollend pair tore down oculist-1ta.12's suppression on every fire. Fixed by draining behind a double rAF.

REVIEW 2 FOUND A THIRD REGRESSION, which is why this is parked. The double rAF leaves ~12ms before markPreFireScroll() arms in which a genuine abort is silently ignored: the effect draws and the page is pulled back off the user's scroll position. Measured with an in-page setTimeout scroll, 3 reps per offset: fx3/top993 at +0/+4/+8/+12ms, jitter boundary through +28ms, caught from +32ms. Removing the deferral catches it at every offset, and so does HEAD -- a regression against both, not pre-existing. This is done-criterion 5.

NEXT STEP, from the review. Do not keep the double rAF. Keep markPreFireScroll() synchronous and instead have endSuppression ignore the FIRST scrollend after a probe. That closes the window and should keep G.3 green.

TWO MORE THINGS TO FIX BEFORE THIS CAN CLOSE:
- Add an abort row at +0ms so this window cannot regress again. Every current abort row waits 40ms, just outside it, which is why the gate stayed green -- and means a slow frame could push a gate abort into the window and turn those rows spuriously red.
- The R1 fix has NO discriminating row: removing the scrollBehavior forcing entirely leaves the whole gate green, exit 0. Add an assertion that catches it (settle time, or the absence of an early frame near the target).

MINOR: the test hook window.__raj4SuppressScrollDissolve (effects-playground.html:377) is read-only and has precedent (window.EFFECTS, window.runEffect), but the bead-id name will age poorly. Rename when this lands.

title: Bone-assembly prototype (generic skeleton)
description:
A scatter of bones flies in beside the match, snaps together into a small skeleton that points at the word, then collapses into a heap and fades.

Requested by the human 2026-09-10, mid-run on oculist-1ta.

RIGHTS: none. A generic skeleton is not a character. Label it "Bone Assembly".

CONVENTIONS (same as every effect in this epic)
- File: /Users/ccho/Documents/Projects/oculist/artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html. Prototype only. Do NOT touch extension/content.js.
- Read fxFlappy, fxCheshire, fxFootTap and fxWandCast first. They set the conventions: viewport coordinates via baseStyle() position:fixed, class "fx" on every mounted element so clearFx() reaches it, mount(), a local var DUR, hardcoded colors, WAAPI only, and the right-else-left-else-clamp side logic.
- Register LAST in effectsRegistry, in the "New candidates (post round 6)" divider. Do not reorder entries.
- Deterministic: hand-authored coordinates, NO Math.random(). Scattered pieces are where it creeps in, so hand-author every start point and arc.
- MUST NOT occlude the matched glyphs at any point. Verify at the natural match size and across the occlusion-sweep.js grid, including 320x900 and 360x900.
- Must clear the DOM completely, cause no reflow, and leave #match and its text unmutated.
- Transform and opacity only. No animated filter. No negative z-index (see oculist-1ta.6).
- A WAAPI keyframe list whose last offset is below 1 interpolates back toward the un-animated transform. Always end on an explicit offset:1 keyframe.
- Do NOT touch #fire-index or its max, SHIPPED_LABELS or its frozen numbering, effects-round6-scores.md, or other candidates. Do not commit.

LEGIBILITY IS THE RISK. Four figure effects in this epic have fought legibility at 50-70px. A skeleton is thinner still, and ivory bones on the #faf9f5 page have almost no contrast. So:
- Draw bones as ivory fill with a dark 1.5-2px outline, so they read on a light page.
- Use chibi proportions: the skull is about 40% of the figure's height, with dark eye sockets and a jaw line. The skull carries the "skeleton" read, and ribs and limbs just need to be present.
- Keep it to 6-8 pieces: skull, ribcage, pelvis, two arms, two legs, optionally a spine. More pieces become noise at this size.
- Target about 60-70px total height, flanking the match.

SEQUENCE
1. SCATTER-IN. The pieces fly in from hand-authored points around the figure's landing spot, each on its own short arc with its own rotation. Stagger them so the eye tracks a gathering, not one blob.
2. SNAP. They lock into a standing skeleton with a small overshoot and settle, a visible "click" moment. Every arc must stay clear of the match rect.
3. POINT. One arm raises and points at the match (two or three discrete poses, hard cuts), with an optional single jaw clack. Keep it under the G4 rate.
4. COLLAPSE. The skeleton drops into a heap at its feet (pieces fall and rotate, staggered), holds briefly, and the heap fades. Nothing persists.

G6 RISKS, which must read as clearly distinct unlabelled:
- Foot Tap and Point (oculist-1ta.5): a figure pointing at the match.
- Reanimation Jolt (oculist-1ta.3): a figure coming to life beside the match.
- Shatter Crack: pieces.
The differentiator is ASSEMBLY and COLLAPSE. The point is secondary: if it makes the effect read as Foot Tap, cut it and say so.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Scatter, snap, point, collapse: all visible and in that order.
- It reads as a skeleton at natural size. Judge this by looking at a 1x frame, not a zoomed one.
- The matched word is fully legible throughout. occlusion-sweep.js reports its raw result and the batflight and arrowshot gating stays 96/96 clean.
- No Math.random(). Identical on every fire.
- No area reverses luminance 3 or more times per second.
- Nothing remains in the DOM afterwards, and clearFx mid-effect leaves nothing behind.
- VERIFY BY LOOKING AT THE RENDER. Screenshot the scatter, the snap, the point and the collapse at natural size and inspect them, plus an unlabelled side-by-side against Foot Tap and Point and Reanimation Jolt.
close_reason:
Implemented as fxBoneAssembly, registered last in effectsRegistry as 'Bone Assembly'. PASSED on the second review, after one repair pass.

THE POINT BEAT WAS CUT under the bead's own licence ('The point is secondary: if it makes the effect read as Foot Tap, cut it and say so'). Review 1 established it was Foot Tap and Point's signature pose at the same size on the same side, differing only in fill and the skull. The sequence shipped is scatter, snap, settle hold, collapse. The reviewer re-shot the comparator rather than take that on trust: Foot Tap is a black silhouette with one arm extended horizontally beside the word; Bone Assembly's settle is an outlined ivory skeleton with both arms hanging at its sides. Distinct in pose, fill and silhouette.

REVIEW 1 FAILED because beat 4 did not exist. Pieces moved at most 4.5px, one of them upward, with no stagger, and the skull ended 43px above the feet baseline. It read as a shrug.

THE COLLAPSE IS NOW REAL, measured by the reviewer independently on both engines. Skull centre falls from 55.12px above the feet baseline at t=830 to 2.62px at t=1280 on chromium, 55.13 to 2.63 on webkit, and 55.12 to 2.62 at 320x900/font48. All eight pieces move downward: skull +52.5, spine +31.5, ribcage +21.0, arms +19.25, legs +5.25, pelvis +4.38. The vertical spread of the eight centres collapses from 49.9px to 6.1px. At 1x it is a compact overlapping pile about one word-height wide sitting on the baseline, not a lowered figure. COLLAPSE_STAGGER is genuine: at 60ms in, only the skull and ribcage have moved at all, while nearLeg and nearArm are still exactly at rest at t=1000. All eight land together at COLLAPSE_START + COLLAPSE_DUR, and the frame hash at t=1280 equals the hash at t=1560, so nothing is left mid-air and the heap hold is truly static.

THE 490MS RECLAIMED FROM THE POINT BEAT went to a 200ms settle hold plus a longer, staggered collapse (COLLAPSE_DUR 320 to 440, HEAP_HOLD 220 to 300). DUR is now 1840, down from 1930. Worth knowing: the nominal 200ms hold is not all stillness, since the click pulse occupies 640-730, so true stillness is 110ms. The reviewer judged it a real beat rather than dead air.

CLEARANCE IMPROVED FROM EXACTLY ZERO SLACK. Review 1 measured inward slack at 0.000px. Removing TIP_FULL is what bought the margin, and the reviewer verified that by hand rather than accepting it: the old minX of -32.700 came precisely from boneReach(NEAR_SHOULDER, TIP_FULL, ARM_W), the pose that no longer exists, and the new -26.633 comes from nearArm's scatter start. Brute-forced at 2ms over the whole timeline with getBoundingClientRect on every painted ellipse and line, stroke included, covering the heap positions and the clickG pulse window: true minimum figure-to-match x gap is 16.10px against a GAP floor of 10, so 6.10px of inward slack. Identical at 320x900/f96 and 1280x900/f96, 15.49px at 360x900 natural. The implementer reported 17.16px; the reviewer's 16.10px is the more conservative instrument and is the number to trust. The clickG 1.12 pulse is still dominated rather than folded into the derived scan, but by about 21 units, so it is not a live risk.

GATE: sweep exit 0 with boneassembly clean on grid, forced and edge at maxPixels 0, and batflight and arrowshot unaffected at 96/96, 7/7 and 12/12. Mutation (GAP -60 plus backstop disabled) turns the grid 0/96 and edge 0/12 red at maxPixels up to 1983, so the green is falsifiable. Determinism byte-identical over two fires at 9 frames on both engines. Clean teardown, clearFx mid-effect clean, #match outerHTML byte-identical, zero console errors. occlusion-sweep.js byte-unmodified with no occurrence of boneassembly, so no exemption was smuggled.

G4 IS ZERO AND NOW STRUCTURAL. After the cut, the function makes exactly four animate() calls: three animate transform only, one animates figWrap opacity monotonically 1 to 0. No filter, no fill or colour animation, no per-piece opacity, and the old poseHalf/poseFull style.opacity hard cuts are gone, so there is no hard cut left to alias against. Confirmed on pixels anyway at 4ms sampling with a 16x16 tile area detector against a synthetic 5Hz control: 0 tiles at 3 or more reversals per second, worst 2/s, on both engines.

A MEASUREMENT LESSON WORTH KEEPING FOR THIS EPIC. A naive per-pixel reversal count flags every effect here (foottap 607px, reanimate 1709px, boneassembly 4264px at floor 0.1 and 4ms sampling), because a two-toned bone sweeping past a single pixel is three reversals by construction. That is motion, not flash. The area formulation is the correct instrument. Separately, 40ms sampling is too coarse for hard-cut poses: the flagged count falls as sampling gets finer, which is aliasing rather than flicker.

NO REFLOW, instrumented rather than inferred: documentElement and body scrollWidth and scrollHeight constant across the whole fire at 20ms sampling, at mid-page 900x700 and at top-edge and bottom-edge match placements, both engines.

TWO NON-BLOCKING OBSERVATIONS. The heap bottom sits about 11px below the feet baseline, so at a bottom-edge placement the last ~5px of the pile is clipped by the viewport edge: cosmetic, no occlusion, no reflow. And the 4 FORCED-LANDING rows stay clean even under mutation because the figure renders off-canvas there, which is the known unfalsifiability carried over from review 1, not introduced by this pass. The honest census is 106 of 112 rows exercising real on-canvas clearance.

Screenshot evidence at artifacts/outputs/boneassembly-review2-screens (untracked, matching the wandcast, tentaclerise and horseman precedents).

comments.text:
