Sampling-rate sweep at floor 0.02: 40ms gives 1427px, 16ms gives 413px, 8ms gives 219px, 4ms gives 3px, 2ms gives 0px. The number FALLS as sampling gets finer, which is point-sampling aliasing of fast bone motion rather than flicker. At the implementer's own 40ms and floor 0.05 the reviewer's detector reports 1362px. Converged ground truth is 0 on both engines. Worth carrying forward for any future G4 work in this epic: 40ms sampling is too coarse for hard-cut poses.

AMBIGUITY RESOLVED IN THE IMPLEMENTATION'S FAVOUR. The 60-70px height clamp written as Math.max(60, Math.min(70, 2.6*r.height)) matches the sibling convention exactly; six other effects in the file use the identical idiom (lines 4067, 6275, 6627, 7075, 8298, 9179). No change needed.

The jaw clack the bead marked optional was built, inspected at natural size, found to be a visually indistinguishable 2px shift, and cut. That was the right call and removing it changed no other beat's timing.

Screenshots: artifacts/outputs/boneassembly-review-screens/ in the outer repo (untracked).

title: Tentacle-rise prototype (Cthulhu)
description:
Tentacles rise from beneath the match's line, curl their tips toward the word like a pair of brackets, a pair of eyes opens beneath it, and everything sinks back out of sight.

Requested by the human 2026-09-10, mid-run on oculist-1ta.

RIGHTS: clean. Lovecraft, "The Call of Cthulhu", Weird Tales, February 1928. Works published in 1928 entered the US public domain on 2024-01-01, and Lovecraft died in 1937, so life+70 jurisdictions cleared in 2008. There is no enforced character trademark of the kind that complicates Tarzan. Chaosium's marks cover its game titles, not the creature. Still follow the epic: draw a GENERIC octopoid, and label by motion ("Tentacle Rise"), not "Cthulhu".

CONVENTIONS (same as every effect in this epic)
- File: /Users/ccho/Documents/Projects/oculist/artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html. Prototype only. Do NOT touch extension/content.js.
- Read fxFlappy, fxCheshire, fxFootTap and fxWandCast first. They set the conventions: viewport coordinates via baseStyle() position:fixed, class "fx" on every mounted element so clearFx() reaches it, mount(), a local var DUR, hardcoded colors, WAAPI only, and the right-else-left-else-clamp side logic.
- Register LAST in effectsRegistry, in the "New candidates (post round 6)" divider. Do not reorder entries.
- Deterministic: hand-authored coordinates, NO Math.random().
- MUST NOT occlude the matched glyphs at any point. Verify at the natural match size and across the occlusion-sweep.js grid, including 320x900 and 360x900.
- Must clear the DOM completely, cause no reflow, and leave #match and its text unmutated.
- Transform and opacity only. No animated filter.
- Do NOT use negative z-index to put anything "behind" the page. oculist-1ta.6 found that it goes under body's opaque #faf9f5 background, not just under the chip, and it cannot carry to real pages. Hide part of the figure with a STATIC clip-path on a wrapper instead, e.g. the waterline below.
- Do NOT touch #fire-index or its max, SHIPPED_LABELS or its frozen numbering, effects-round6-scores.md, or other candidates. Do not commit.
- A WAAPI keyframe list whose last offset is below 1 interpolates back toward the un-animated transform. oculist-1ta.6 hit this. Always end on an explicit offset:1 keyframe.

SEQUENCE (the default design; deviate only with a stated reason)
1. RISE. Two thick, tapering tentacles, one just outside each end of the match, rise from a hidden "waterline" a little below the match's line. A static clip-path on their wrapper hides everything below the waterline, so they read as coming up out of the page. The rise is a translateY.
2. CURL. Each tip curls inward toward the word, like "(" and ")" framing it. Use two or three discrete whole-frame poses swapped by hard cuts, not a smooth path morph: discrete poses survive small scale, and smooth small tweens have rendered invisibly in this file. A few sucker dots on the inner curve carry the "tentacle, not vine" read.
3. EYES. For the hold, a pair of glowing eyes (yellow-green, slit pupils) opens beneath the word between the tentacles, set in a small dark dome clipped at the waterline. The eyes carry peripheral capture, so give them the brightness. One slow blink at most.
4. SINK. The tentacles uncurl through the same poses in reverse and slide back below the waterline, the eyes close, the dome sinks, and nothing persists.

G6 RISKS, which must read as clearly distinct unlabelled:
- Vine Swing (oculist-1ta.4), another curving green-dark stroke near the match.
- Tether Snap and Pointing Arrows (shipped), both of which bracket or point at the match.
The differentiator is the creature: it RISES FROM BELOW and HAS EYES. Neither of those has an agent emerging from the page.

G4: the eye glow and blink must stay under 3 luminance reversals per second over any sizeable area.

AMBIGUITIES TO FLAG, not silently resolve
- The dome and eyes sit below the word, so they will overlap the next line's text. Neighbouring-text overlap has been accepted before, but match overlap never has. Keep the dome as small as legibility allows and report its size.
- If the match is at the very top or bottom of the viewport, say where the waterline goes.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Rise, curl, eyes, sink: all visible and in that order.
- The tentacles read as tentacles, not vines, at natural size. Judge this by looking.
- The matched word is fully legible throughout. occlusion-sweep.js reports its raw result and the batflight and arrowshot gating stays 96/96 clean.
- No Math.random(). Identical on every fire.
- No area reverses luminance 3 or more times per second.
- Nothing remains in the DOM afterwards, and clearFx mid-effect leaves nothing behind.
- VERIFY BY LOOKING AT THE RENDER. Screenshot the rise, the curl, the eyes and the sink at natural size and inspect them, plus an unlabelled side-by-side against Vine Swing and Tether Snap.
close_reason:
Implemented as fxTentacleRise, registered last in effectsRegistry as 'Tentacle Rise'. PASSED on the second review after one retry.

All done-criteria met, independently re-run by the reviewer: sweep exit 0 with tentaclerise 96/96 grid, 4/4 forced-landing, 12/12 edge-placement, maxPixels 0 everywhere, and batflight and arrowshot still fully clean. Zero Math.random; two fires byte-identical on chromium and webkit. Clean teardown, #match outerHTML byte-identical, no reflow, no console errors, clearFx mid-effect clean. occlusion-sweep.js is byte-unmodified and 'tentaclerise' appears nowhere in it, so it passes the standard 0-pixel rule with no exemption.

ROUND 1 FAILED on done-criterion 2. At 360x900 across all 12 fonts the left tentacle was suppressed, and the surviving lone dark-green curved limb read as a vine growing through the text, which is the exact G6 collision with Vine Swing the bead warns about. Two further findings: two edge rows rendered zero tentacles, and waterlineY was never clamped to the viewport so a match near the bottom edge lost the eyes beat entirely.

THE RETRY FOUND A DIFFERENT ROOT CAUSE than the one proposed. The clearance box was over-wide, but the actual defect was the viewport-edge floor clamp Math.max(4, ...), which pulled the box 6-17px INTO #match at 360px. Narrowing the box alone could not have fixed it. REACH_MIN_X/REACH_MAX_X are now derived from the real ribbon-fill geometry across all three poses rather than hand-picked, GAP=14 became MARGIN=2 (0.7px for half the non-scaling stroke's screen-constant bulge plus 1.3px for AA and rounding), the floor clamp became EDGE_ALLOW=20, and suppression became both-or-neither so a lone limb can never read as a vine. All 96 grid rows now mount both tentacles, up from 82.

2PX OF CLEARANCE IS REAL BUT THIN, verified rather than assumed. The reviewer re-derived the painted extent from scratch at x in [8.539, 31.313] local units, confirmed getBoundingClientRect excludes stroke on both engines, and bracketed the clean/dirty boundary by mutation: MARGIN 0 gives 51/96 dirty, 1.0 gives 5/96 dirty, 1.5 and 2.0 are clean. 2448 interpolated scenarios between the sampled viewports and fonts all mount both limbs with minimum clearance 1.987px and no negatives. Headroom is roughly 0.5-1.0px, not comfortable.

G4 measured, not argued: largest contiguous region at 3 or more opposing luminance transitions per second is 65px, about 0.3% of the WCAG sizeable-area threshold. The flagged pixels are 1-2px antialiased slivers at the limb edges during rise and sink, NOT the eyes.

NO VACUOUS GREENS: 0 of 112 harness rows render nothing. 100 of 112 exercise tentacle clearance; the other 12 render the dome only. Worth knowing for future work on this effect: a green sweep alone cannot prove clearance, since mutating MARGIN to -1 reports 96/96 clean by mounting zero tentacles in every row. The per-row limb census is what rules that out.

TWO ACCEPTED CONSEQUENCES, both the bead's own flagged ambiguities, now answered. The dome is 34x18px flush below the word and does overlap the next line's first word: neighbouring-text overlap, which this epic has accepted before, never match overlap. And when #match sits within 22px of the viewport bottom the dome and eyes are suppressed entirely rather than cropped off-screen, so the eyes beat does not play there. Threshold verified exact. That is about 2.4% of uniformly random placements at vh=900 and effectively 0% for the scroll-into-view flow the extension actually uses, where r.bottom is near vh/2.

Filed oculist-tlg2 (P3) for the one latent thin spot: EDGE_ALLOW can erode MARGIN to ~0 because the overlap guard tests fill-only extent and ignores the 0.7px stroke bulge. No glyph ink is touched, and the shipped grid never samples that band, so it did not block this close.

Screenshot evidence at artifacts/outputs/tentaclerise-review-screens (untracked, matching the wandcast and horseman precedents).

title: Fast-assertion race family: tests that read wrong values in under 2s under concurrency, green in isolation
description:
Characterised by the oculist-8qq reviewer on 2026-09-06, with 7 full-suite runs and 20 isolation runs behind it. This is the SECOND flake family, and the one oculist-8qq's chosen lever cannot touch.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS. oculist-8qq scaled the poll budget, which eliminated every failure that exhausted the old 5000ms ceiling. These failures are not that. They fail FAST, in 372ms to 2194ms, by reading a WRONG VALUE rather than by running out of time. There is no budget behind them, so no value of OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE affects them. Of 13 failing tests the reviewer observed, 6 were this family.

MEASURED: each of these files passed 5 of 5 runs in isolation, in 2-4s. Under --test-concurrency=4 they produce wrong values:
- instant_scroll_close_reopen_no_stale_draw - failed 2 of 7 runs, the most frequent single offender, and never named in oculist-8qq's original data.
- chip_row:360 - deep-equal, got ['quarklet','alpha','beta'] where ['alpha','beta'] was expected.
- color_picker_persistence:104.
- vision_profile_survives_ungoverned_toggle - got 'low-vision' where 'custom' was expected. ALREADY FILED SEPARATELY as oculist-p8u, which identified the specific cause: a missing await after selectOption(). Fix that one there, not here.

THE HYPOTHESIS p8u SUPPORTS: these are all the same shape as p8u, an assertion that reads state before it has settled, where the code happened to be fast enough to get away with it until four browsers competed for the CPU. If that is right, the fix per file is to await the transition the assertion depends on, and p8u is the worked example.

ALSO IN THIS FAMILY, structurally: beacon_survives_long_smooth_scroll's checkAt deadline is real wall clock inside a 2100ms beacon lifetime and deliberately does not scale (see oculist-4fh). Under enough load it can miss regardless of budget. Do not fix that by scaling it; oculist-4fh explains why.

FIRST STEP: fix oculist-p8u, then check whether the same missing-await shape explains chip_row:360, color_picker_persistence:104 and instant_scroll_close_reopen_no_stale_draw.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Each named file's assertion waits for the state it depends on.
- Each passes repeatedly under --test-concurrency=4, not only in isolation.
- No fixed sleeps added. A sleep converts this family into the timeout family.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS on the second review, with independent mutation proofs in both directions. Three files, three distinct unawaited transitions. chip_row:360: persistWorkList()'s chrome.storage.session.set() is fire-and-forget, so a still-in-flight write could land after the next test's remove('oc-worklist') and resurrect a chip - exactly the reported ['quarklet','alpha','beta']. addTerm() now waits for the write to reach storage (skipped on the cap-hit path, which never persists). Passed review unchanged on the first pass. color_picker_persistence:104: a fixed 900ms sleep guessed how long two competing storage.onChanged echoes take. Replaced with a quiet-window wait observing #oc-wrap's SHADOW ROOT - the first attempt observed document.body, which MutationObserver cannot cross, making the wait a bare 400ms sleep and the tornDown assertion tautological. Assertion is now strictly stronger than HEAD: whole-window tornDown === false plus connected read from the originally captured node rather than a re-query. instant_scroll_close_reopen_no_stale_draw: two races. The 120ms sleep assumed m1's 50ms inViewDrawTimer had fired before Enter #2, but Enter #2 cancels a still-pending timer, silently dropping a legitimate draw; now waits on __ocRedrawCount > 0. Second race: the test's premise needs two CDP round trips to beat a real 50ms timer, a wall-clock coin flip under contention. The isolated world's setTimeout is stretched 50ms to 4000ms, installed only after m1's own unpatched draw fired, so __ocDestroy always wins deterministically. The first attempt left the settle window at 400ms, so the orphaned timer fired 3.6s after the assertion had already read count === 1, neutering the test; QUIET_MS raised to 4600ms. Reviewer ruled the 4600ms window a settle detector rather than a disguised sleep, on measurement: clean 5.09s vs mutant 9.1-9.4s, i.e. the window restarts when the orphan draw lands, so it observes the timer rather than outlasting it; and 4600 is derived from a constant the test itself installs, not a guess about machine speed. Mutation-verified independently: removing clearActiveImmediateDrawTimer() fails 2 !== 1 in 5 of 5 concurrent runs and 2 of 2 full suites; injecting a 60ms panel rebuild fails both colour tests. Reviewer's own counts: 10/10 concurrent runs of the three files, 3/3 full suites at 320/320. No fixed sleeps, no assertions loosened, beacon_survives_long_smooth_scroll untouched per oculist-4fh. The list_menu.test.js:286 failure seen once by the implementer did not reproduce in 3 full suites plus 6 co-scheduled runs; pre-existing flake, unrelated. Residual risk filed as a follow-up: the quiet window is anchored to m1's draw, leaving a ~600ms CDP-overhead margin rather than a structural guarantee.

title: Full suite flakes at --test-concurrency=4: 1-3 unrelated failures per run, all green in isolation
description:
Measured during the oculist-z8n review on 2026-09-06. PRE-EXISTING - reproduced at HEAD before that bead's fix, so it is not caused by it.

npm test runs node --test --test-concurrency=4 test/*.test.js. Across six full-suite runs the reviewer saw a DIFFERENT, non-overlapping set of 1-3 failures each time:
- with the z8n fix: 315/316 (stale_mount_guard), then 313/316 (vision_profile_survives_ungoverned_toggle, list_search), then 313/316 again.
- at HEAD without the fix: 313/316 - dim_highlight and draft_ownership, plus the genuine z8n failure.

Every one of those files passes when run alone. The pattern - different files each run, green in isolation - is resource contention between four concurrent Playwright browsers on a loaded machine, not a logic bug in any single test.

WHY IT MATTERS: a suite that fails differently every run trains everyone to re-run instead of read the failure, which is how a real regression gets waved through. It also makes any /goal run's 'node --test passes in full' criterion unreliable.

DIRECTIONS TO CONSIDER, not yet decided:
- Lower --test-concurrency, and measure what that costs in wall clock (currently ~85s).
- Find whether the flaky files share a resource (a fixed port, a temp profile dir name, a shared fixture path) rather than just CPU.
- Check whether OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE is honoured by the timing constants in the files that flake - the z8n review found at least two hardcoded literals that ignore it, so a contended box cannot buy headroom.

FIRST STEP: run the full suite several times at concurrency 4 and again at 1 or 2, and record which files fail at each setting. Decide from data, not from the list above.
close_reason:
Investigation complete and Chris's chosen lever implemented: OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE=2 in the npm test script. Reviewer PASS on the change, verified independently (scale reaches POLL_TIMEOUT 10000, LONG_TIMEOUT 30000, and the launchPersistentContext action default 60000; no other consumer of the script exists).

CLOSING WITH THE HEADLINE PROBLEM ONLY PARTLY SOLVED, deliberately. Across 7 measured runs, zero failures cited the old 5000ms ceiling, so the family this bead documented - 5 of its original 6 failures - is gone. But the suite still flakes, for a reason this bead did not know about: 6 of 13 observed failures fail FAST, in 372ms to 2194ms, by reading a wrong value with no budget behind them, so no timeout value can help them. That second family is now filed with far better evidence than this bead could have carried, and oculist-p8u is its worked example. Leaving this bead open would double-track it.

Also honest about the measurement: the machine carried external load averages of 6 to 61 throughout, against an idle baseline of 95.2s, so the pass-rate comparison is not valid and no claim is made that the suite is now reliable. The value 2 is not the binding constraint; raising it would not have saved a single fast-assertion failure.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Evidence added during the oculist-3rq review, 2026-09-06. WIDENS THIS BEAD'S SCOPE: test/vision_profile_survives_ungoverned_toggle.test.js flaked once when run IN ISOLATION, not only under --test-concurrency=4. It then passed 4 times in a row, and also passes against unmodified content.js, so it is flake rather than a regression. That matters because this bead's premise is resource contention between four concurrent browsers; a file that flakes alone does not fit that premise and points at a timing assumption inside the test itself. Also seen in the same review: a full-suite run went 316 pass / 2 fail / 1 cancelled with resize_overlays.test.js and vision_profile_survives_ungoverned_toggle.test.js failing, and the very next full run went 319/319 with no changes in between.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Measurement pass, 2026-09-06, hard-timeboxed to ~30 min. 8 full-suite runs total: 5 at --test-concurrency=4, 3 at =2, 1 at =1 (idle machine, no synthetic load, no concurrent invocations - both ruled out of scope by oculist-3sx).

RAW TABLE (single-invocation `node --test --test-concurrency=N test/*.test.js`):

setting | run | duration | result | failing file(s) : error shape
c4 | 1 | 113s | FAIL | theme_system_dark_os (waitForSelector timeout 5000ms=POLL_TIMEOUT, +2 cancelled children); vision_profile_survives_ungoverned_toggle (2 assertion failures, no wait at all)
c4 | 2 | 92s  | FAIL | resize_overlays (waitForCondition timeout 5000ms on displayPreset='high-contrast', +1 cancelled child)
c4 | 3 | 89s  | PASS | 320/320
c4 | 4 | 86s  | PASS | 320/320
c4 | 5 | 96s  | FAIL | closed_overlay_settings_change (waitForContentScriptReady timeout, POLL_TIMEOUT-bound, +1 cancelled); resize_overlays again, identical failure to run 2
c2 | 1 | 160s | PASS | 320/320
c2 | 2 | 137s | PASS | 320/320
c2 | 3 | 166s | FAIL | destroy_during_scroll_no_stale_draw (waitForCondition timeout 5000ms, "smooth-scroll debounce timer was never armed") - a file never previously named in this bead
c1 | 1 | 266s | PASS | 320/320 (matches the ~232-245s memory record within noise)

Failure rate: c4 3/5 (60%), c2 1/3 (33%), c1 0/1. Mean wall clock: c4 95.2s, c2 154.3s (+62%), c1 266s (+180%, matches prior memory).

DISTINCT FILES THAT FAILED ACROSS THESE 8 RUNS: theme_system_dark_os, vision_profile_survives_ungoverned_toggle, resize_overlays (x2), closed_overlay_settings_change, destroy_during_scroll_no_stale_draw - 5 distinct files, 3 of which (theme_system_dark_os, closed_overlay_settings_change, destroy_during_scroll_no_stale_draw) had never been named anywhere in this bead's history before this run. Combined with the 7 already on record, at least 9 distinct files have now independently produced this failure family. That is itself a finding: the affected set is not a short, fixable list, it keeps growing.

FAILURE-SHAPE BREAKDOWN, the most decisive finding: of the 6 total file-failures above, 5 are the identical shape - a waitForCondition/waitForSelector call hitting POLL_TIMEOUT (5000ms, unscaled at the default OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE=1 that npm test uses) inside an already-launched context. Only 1 (vision_profile) has no wait at all.

HYPOTHESIS VERDICT, split by failure shape rather than forced into one answer:
- Contention hypothesis (failures scale with concurrency, vanish at 1): SUPPORTED for the 5 POLL_TIMEOUT-shaped failures. They appear at c4 (3 distinct files) and c2 (1 distinct file, different from any c4 failure), frequency drops from 60% to 33% to 0% as concurrency drops - directionally exactly what more-browsers-competing-for-scheduling predicts against a fixed budget. But c2 does NOT show the failure vanishing, only thinning: run c2-3 failed with a brand-new file. n=1 at concurrency 1 is too small to certify zero.
- Isolation-flake hypothesis: SUPPORTED, narrowly, for vision_profile_survives_ungoverned_toggle only. Its failure is an assertion with no wait/budget behind it at all - the test's own comment documents an intentional assumption that the change listener's DOM update is synchronous after selectOption(), so there is nothing for a timeout knob to fix. This matches the bead comment's isolation-flake data point (flaked alone once, passed 4x after). Concurrency plausibly widens the race window but is not the root cause.

SHARED-RESOURCE GREP (cheap, no clock cost): no fixed port (all use server.listen(0, ...), OS-assigned), no shared temp/profile dir (all use chromium.launchPersistentContext('', ...), which Playwright gives its own ephemeral dir per call, consistent across all 51 launching files), no shared file writes. The one shared thing across every POLL_TIMEOUT failure is exactly that: the fixed, machine-wide, per-file-identical 5000ms constant in test/helpers/wait.js, contended for real scheduler time by however many Chromium processes concurrency puts on the box at once - not a collision in the classic sense, but a shared budget under shared CPU/scheduling pressure.

RECOMMENDATION. I am not changing package.json. The data does not clearly support it: c2 nearly halves the failure rate (60%->33%) at a real +62% wall-clock cost, but does not eliminate the failure - a brand-new file failed at c2 that has never appeared at c4. That is a worse trade than "fixed", and a single clean c1 run is not enough on its own to reopen the 3x-cost verdict oculist-3sx already priced, though note that verdict was for a DIFFERENT, apparently-untriggerable failure family (the 180s launch hang); this bead's family (POLL_TIMEOUT exhaustion) IS triggerable at default settings - 60% of my c4 runs failed on a single, ordinary `npm test` invocation, no concurrent suites, no synthetic load. That is a materially different and more urgent situation than the one 3sx closed against.

Two concrete follow-ups, filed as separate beads rather than done here:
1. vision_profile_survives_ungoverned_toggle's missing await after selectOption() (line ~64-68 comment: "No wait after selectOption() ... run synchronously") is a real, narrow, load-independent bug, worth fixing on its own regardless of any concurrency decision.
2. The systemic mismatch - a fixed, unscaled-by-default 5000ms budget racing an ever-growing set of files under 4-way browser scheduling contention - needs a decision from Chris on which lever to pull. I was instructed not to propose the existing OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE knob as the answer here (it was already established as inert at default scale, and this bead's brief carried that constraint forward), so I am flagging the mechanical fact without recommending it: every POLL_TIMEOUT failure I measured happened at exactly the value that knob scales, and npm test never sets it above 1. Whether that observation changes anyone's mind about the knob is a call above this investigation's scope.

Did not change any code or config. All 8 runs used a clean checkout, no test-suite files touched.

title: Pack-discovery notice height not accounted for in oculist-6cd's settings-panel max-height cap, causing host overflow at any viewport height
description:
Discovered while writing Playwright coverage for the effect-pack settings checkbox list
(oculist-tdj.5, test/effect_pack_settings_control.test.js).

The settings panel's own max-height (content.js, #oc-settings-panel CSS) is
`calc(100vh - barChromePx)`, where barChromePx is a fixed 44px literal meant to
approximate the bar's own height above the panel (oculist-6cd). That formula does not
account for the pack-discovery notice (.oc-pack-notice, oculist-tdj.3,
maybeShowPackDiscoveryNotice()), which renders BETWEEN the bar and the settings panel
whenever knownPacks().length > 0 and the notice has not yet been dismissed.

Measured directly (real browser, 1280x800 viewport): with 10 known packs and the notice
still showing, the notice itself renders ~46.6px tall. Since the panel's max-height cap
only subtracts the bar's ~44px, not the notice's extra height, the whole host (bar +
notice + panel) can overflow the viewport by roughly the notice's own height — confirmed:
host bottom landed at 843.6px against an 800px viewport (an ~43.6px overflow), and the
same ~43.6px overflow reproduced at a 600px viewport too (it's viewport-height
independent, since the formula's constant-per-viewport error doesn't scale with vh).

This was never caught before because no real effectsRegistry entry has carried a `pack`
until this bead's test fixture (oculist-tdj.1 shipped the field with zero consumers), so
knownPacks() was always empty and the notice was never eligible to render on the real
tree — settings_panel_viewport_overflow.test.js's own coverage of the oculist-6cd fix
never exercises this path.

Reproduction: any account with >=1 known pack and packsNoticeDismissed still false, on a
viewport short enough that the settings panel needs its max-height cap to actually engage.
Fix should account for the notice's rendered height in the panel's cap (or in the host's
own bounds) whenever the notice is present, mirroring how barChromePx already accounts for
the bar.

test/effect_pack_settings_control.test.js works around this by dismissing the notice
before taking any geometry measurements, so it does not catch a regression to this
specific interaction.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. Reproduced red first at three assertions (host bottom 823.98 of 800, 643.59 of 600, and max-height not growing back after dismissal); reviewer re-proved that red by reverting content.js. Fix adds packNoticeChromePx, measured when the notice is shown and reset when it is dismissed, folded into a hostChromePx that both the settings and lists panels subtract. The lists-panel extension beyond the bead's literal wording was verified justified: the reviewer proved the notice and the lists panel genuinely coexist (max-height 309.4 = 400 - 44 - 46.6 at a 400px viewport), and packNoticeChromePx is 0 whenever the notice is absent, so nothing shrinks gratuitously. Re-injection is idempotent (one style element, textContent replaced) and the zero-height measurement race does not occur, since the element is connected and styled before measurement. Follow-up on stale measurement filed.

title: Reshape the bycocket: triangular crown and a slim quill feather
description:
Chris reviewed the hat 2026-09-05: 'usually, the bycocket is triangular shaped on the top and the feather is a slim one rather than lollipop shaped.'

He is right on both. The current crown is a rounded dome and the plume is a fat oval. A bycocket's crown comes to a point or an angular ridge, and the feather is a slim quill.

ABSORBS oculist-1ta.18, which is about the same forms and would otherwise be a second pass over the same geometry:
• The front brim point renders in the shadow tone AND lands against the same-hued bow limb, so it neither reads as a point nor separates from the bow (:4020, brimFrontD). The back flip and the plume currently carry the whole read.
• The hat's BASE tone is squeezed to 12 pure pixels at archerH 78 by its own two clip ellipses (75 highlight, 113 shadow). Redrawing the crown is the moment to fix that.
Close 1ta.18 when this lands.

WHAT TO DRAW
1. Crown: triangular or angular-ridged, not domed. The peak is the silhouette cue that says bycocket rather than generic cap.
2. Brim: turned up at the back, pointed at the front, and the front point must be distinguishable from both the crown's shadow tone and the bow limb behind it. Give it a lighter tone, or 2-3 units of clearance from the limb, or both.
3. Feather: slim quill, not a lollipop.

THE FEATHER IS A TRAP AND THE PREVIOUS ROUND WALKED INTO THE OPPOSITE SIDE OF IT. It was drawn fat precisely because thin shapes vanish at 78px, which is the clamped floor for ordinary body text and the common case. Every artwork defect in this epic has been art correct in the source and invisible in the render: a 1.1px specular that produced no white pixel, a 6% tone ramp, a shadow ellipse centred outside its own triangle, a highlight band on the razor tip of a fin. So do not solve slimness by shrinking the blob.

Make it read through LENGTH and CONTRAST rather than bulk: a long slim quill, swept, with its outline carrying the shape and red against the cream page doing the work. It must be unmistakably a feather at 78px and unmistakably slim. Prove it by sampling the render at archerH 78 with a pixel histogram, no zoom, and report the count and raw RGB triples.

DO NOT REGRESS
• STRIKE_GAP is 8 and sits ONE PIXEL above a cliff: 7 dirties the match rect by 2px at font sizes 22-26. The hat is part of the archer sprite, so a taller or wider crown can move the geometry the sweep depends on. Re-run the sweep; do not reason about it.
• Ring geometry: ringStroke 8, padIn 16, keeping the inner stroke edge exactly 12px inside the containment boundary. Do not touch, and do not touch rx = w2*sqrt(2) + pad.
• ARROW_LEN, ARROW_H, MARGIN, the three-plan chooser and corner derivation unchanged.
• Every form keeps an outline and three discrete hard-edged tones, one light direction from the upper left.
• Determinism, fixed as_ prefix, unique clip ids, teardown, scroll-dissolve, no reflow, no Math.random, no animated filter or drop-shadow. Label stays 'Arrow Shot'.

SWEEP COVERAGE MATTERS: cover a WIDE 1280x900 at font sizes 20-30 plus the established scenarios. A scenario set that hides the sibling paragraphs is blind to this defect class entirely (oculist-1ta.16), and a narrow-only sweep already produced one false negative in this epic.

DONE-CRITERIA
• The crown reads as triangular or ridged, not domed, at 78px.
• The feather reads as a slim quill at 78px, proven by histogram, and is visibly not a lollipop.
• The front brim point separates from the crown shadow and the bow limb.
• Hat base tone has meaningfully more than 12 pure pixels at 78px.
• Occlusion sweep zero across font sizes 20-30 at 1280x900 and the established scenarios, with a liveness control.
close_reason: Crown lowered from a 30-on-36 cone to a 13-on-36 angular peak, front beak enlarged so its 16-unit run exceeds the crown's own height and dominates the silhouette, feather reshaped to a slim anchored quill. Took two rounds: round 1 made the crown an almost-equilateral spike that read as a party hat. Reviewer independently confirmed the sweep clean at STRIKE_GAP 8 across 25 scenarios with byte-identical frames, the cliff unmoved at 6/7, and reproduced the feather and hat histograms exactly

title: Give the archer a bycocket and red feather, and thicken the target rings
description:
Chris reviewed the redrawn Arrow Shot 2026-09-05: 'The archer is much better, but give him a bycocket hat with red feather to be more recognizable. Also, make the target lines thicker.'

RIGHTS NOTE, so this is recorded as deliberate. The epic's default is a GENERIC figure with the label naming the motion, because three of the six characters carry live trademarks. Robin Hood is NOT one of them: the epic lists him as CLEAN (folklore). A bycocket and feather is a folklore silhouette, not a protected design, and the epic explicitly says the human may overrule the generic-figure default. Chris has. The LABEL stays 'Arrow Shot' - he asked for a recognizable figure, not a rename.

PART 1: THE HAT
A bycocket is a brimmed hat with the brim turned up at the back and pointed at the front, worn with a feather. It is the single most recognizable Robin Hood cue.

DECIDE AND REPORT: the archer currently wears a hood, added in oculist-1ta.11 specifically because the earlier head read as hair. A hat over a hood may read as clutter at 78px, which is the clamped floor for ordinary body text and the common case. Replacing the hood with the bycocket is likely cleaner and more recognizable. Try both, pick by looking at 78px, and say which you chose and why.

THE FEATHER IS THE RISK. Every artwork failure in this epic so far has been art that is correct in the source and invisible in the render: a 1.1px specular that produced no white pixel, a 6% tone ramp, a shadow ellipse centred outside its own triangle, a highlight band on the razor tip of a fin where it has no area. A thin feather at 78px will vanish exactly the same way. Give it real area, and prove it renders with a pixel histogram at 78px, not at a zoom.

PART 2: THICKER TARGET RINGS - AND THE HAZARD THAT COMES WITH IT
Current geometry, around :4129: padIn 14, padMid 26, padOut 38, ringStroke 4.

The innermost ring's PATH sits at w2*sqrt(2) + 14, and the stroke straddles that path, so the stroke's inner edge is 14 - 4/2 = 12px inside the containment boundary. THAT 12px IS THE ENTIRE MARGIN KEEPING THE RINGS OFF THE GLYPHS. Thickening the stroke eats it directly: at stroke 8 it drops to 10, at stroke 12 to 8. Raise padIn by at least half the stroke increase so the inner edge keeps its current 12px clearance.

Also: padMid and padOut are spaced 12 apart, so a stroke approaching 12 makes the three rings merge into a band. Space them out as the stroke grows. And boxHalfW/boxHalfH are rxOut + ringStroke, so grow those too or the outer ring gets clipped by its own SVG box.

DO NOT change the rx = w2*sqrt(2) + pad formula itself. It is what guarantees the innermost ring contains the match rect for any aspect ratio, it was derived after a sweep caught the naive sizing cutting through the corners of a wide short match at rest, and it is the only reason the rings may frame the word at all.

VERIFICATION
Occlusion sweep, per-pixel diff of the match rect against a no-effect baseline, zero changed pixels. Cover font sizes 20-30 AND a wide 1280x900 viewport: oculist-1ta.17 records that a sweep covering only narrow viewports returned a false negative on a real defect that reproduces at 1280x900, font sizes 22-26, at t=1400. Include a positive control.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The archer reads as Robin Hood at 78px: bycocket silhouette and a feather visible as a distinct red shape, both proven by histogram at that size.
- The hat carries an outline and three discrete tones with hard edges, like every other form.
- Rings are visibly thicker and still read as three separate rings, not a band.
- Occlusion sweep zero across font sizes 20-30 at 1280x900 and the established scenarios.
- ARROW_LEN, ARROW_H, MARGIN, STRIKE_GAP, the three-plan chooser and the sqrt(2) ring formula all unchanged.
close_reason: Bycocket with red feather replaces the hood (the hood read as a generic cowl with no character cue at the 78px floor, and layering both was cluttered); target rings thickened 4->8 with padIn raised 14->16 so the inner stroke edge keeps its exact 12px clearance from the containment boundary, and ring spacing widened 12->16 so the three stay separate. Reviewer measured the feather at 124 red px at archerH 78 including 19 pure #d64550 and 29 pure #f0808a, confirmed three separate rings by centre-row scan, and swept zero changed pixels with a liveness control proving the harness still catches the old regression

title: Occlusion sweep harness has a viewport-coverage blind spot
description:
Found while adjudicating oculist-1ta.11, and it undermines confidence in earlier passes rather than just this one.

Two sweep harnesses disagreed: the implementer's reported 0 of 154 runs clean both before and after the fix, while the reviewer's reproduced the failure exactly. It was NOT a rendering-path difference. Both require the same repo/node_modules/playwright 1.61.0 and the same bundled Chromium 149.0.7827.55.

The cause was scenario coverage. The implementer's sweep (scratchpad 1ta11-final/sweep.js) only used viewports 900x700, 360x700 and 320x900. The defect reproduces at a WIDE 1280x900 and shows nothing at 320x900. Re-running the reviewer's own pre-fix sweep at 900x700 also gave max=0, confirming the blind spot rather than a flaky measurement.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS BEAD: every occlusion guarantee in this epic rests on a sweep like this, and several were run by the under-covered harness. A sweep that cannot see a whole class of viewport is a false guarantee, and the whole point of the zero-pixel criterion is that it is trustworthy.

STEPS
1. Settle one canonical scenario list covering wide, tall, narrow and short viewports, and font sizes across the range that actually renders (the failure was size-dependent, only at 22-26).
2. Put it somewhere reusable rather than rewritten per bead. Each rewrite has come out different, which is how this gap appeared.
3. Re-run it against the closed prototypes (oculist-1ta.1, 1ta.2, 1ta.10, 1ta.11) and report whether the zero-pixel claims still hold under the wider list.
4. Keep the positive control mandatory. It has already caught one silently-broken harness.

DONE-CRITERIA
- One shared scenario list, used by any future sweep.
- A re-run against all four closed prototypes, with results stated per prototype.
- Any prototype that fails under the wider coverage gets its own bead rather than a quiet fix.
notes: Commit 42ad041 refers to this bead as 'oculist-1ta.17'. That id was wrong; 1ta.17 is the bycocket/rings bead and this one is 1ta.16. The commit was already pushed when the mistake was found, so the message was left alone rather than rewriting published history.
close_reason: Canonical occlusion sweep at artifacts/prototypes/occlusion-sweep.js with an exported SCENARIOS list (8 viewports x 12 font sizes incl. 1280x900 and 22-26px), mandatory positive control, WAAPI pause-and-seek sampling. Re-run: batflight (1ta.1, 1ta.10) 96/96 clean, arrowshot (1ta.2, 1ta.11) 96/96 clean. Reviewer reproduced the run, sabotage-tested the control and a mid-timeline occluder; PASS. Three minor gaps filed as a follow-up.

title: Scroll-dissolve staleness fix (oculist-1ta.12) needs to be extended to fxFlappy/fxCheshire (oculist-e2m) and the rest of the playground's effects
description:
oculist-1ta.12 fixed effects-playground.html's scroll-mid-animation
staleness bug (fixed-position overlays pinned to a one-shot viewport rect,
wrong after a scroll) for fxBatFlight and fxArrowShot only, by dissolving
the effect away on a genuine user scroll (armScrollDissolve/dissolveEffect
in the playground's <script>), matching the shape already shipped in
extension/content.js's fadeActiveBeacons()/isAutoScrolling.

The underlying cause is NOT candidate-specific: every effect in the
playground is built on the same baseStyle() (position:fixed) + one-shot
rect() (getBoundingClientRect() at fire time) foundation, with no scroll
listener of its own. That means the staleness bug is playground-wide,
present in every fx* function in effects-playground.html, not just the two
that were just fixed.

Two effects carry this staleness and are closer to shipping than the rest:
fxFlappy and fxCheshire (oculist-e2m, "pending promotion" to the shipped
extension). Confirmed by inspection: neither has any scroll handling, and
both use the same baseStyle()/rect() pattern as batflight/arrowshot did
before the fix.

Scope for this follow-up:
1. Apply the same armScrollDissolve()/dissolveEffect() wiring (shared
   helpers already added near baseStyle() in effects-playground.html) to
   fxFlappy and fxCheshire, prioritized since they're closest to shipping.
2. Decide (and likely file a further bead) whether to apply the same
   treatment to every remaining playground effect (sonar, comet, lockon,
   scribble, confetti, jelly, fireflies, glitch, gravity, searchlight,
   zoompunch, blink, lens, letterwave, stamp, and the round 3-6 effects) --
   architecturally they have the identical bug, though some are short
   enough in duration that a mid-flight scroll is unlikely to be observed
   in practice.
3. Re-run the occlusion + scroll-dissolve sweep methodology established in
   oculist-1ta.12 for each effect touched.

Does NOT apply to the shipped extension itself: extension/content.js
already fixed this class of bug via fadeActiveBeacons() triggered from its
ambient handleScroll() listener (gated by isAutoScrolling so its own
scrollIntoView doesn't self-trigger it) -- that is the precedent this fix
followed, not a gap.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. Chris chose the shared-foundation scope, so the arming moved into rect() and mount() collects the run's elements, giving all 45 effects the dissolve in one place. The five effects that had copy-pasted per-effect wiring, two from oculist-1ta.12 plus three added later, lost it: armScrollDissolve now has exactly one call site and releaseScrollDissolve is gone entirely, so there is no double-arming. A MutationObserver releases the listener when an effect finishes normally, which is the oculist-30k defect class; the reviewer tested rather than read it, confirming the effect nodes really are direct children of html so a childList observer without subtree does fire. Teardown measured on both paths: 45 of 45 effects return to the baseline listener count after natural completion, 12 of 12 after a scroll dissolve, and 30 rapid re-fires leave a delta of zero. The pre-fire scrollIntoView still does not self-dissolve, 10 of 10 through the real UI path, because arming in rect() sits inside the existing suppression window. Canonical occlusion sweep still 96/96 clean with zero pixels. Six effects that mutate raw page state outside mount() are out of scope and filed as oculist-ak5; deferred-mount partial coverage filed separately.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
CORRECTION ON THE RECORD, from oculist-aun, 2026-09-09. Independently established by both the implementer and the reviewer.

THE CLAIM AS RECORDED. This bead's close note says 'Canonical occlusion sweep still 96/96 clean with zero pixels' and its commit message says 'The canonical occlusion sweep is still clean'.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY COVERS: batflight and arrowshot. Nothing else.

EVIDENCE. artifacts/prototypes/occlusion-sweep-results.md line 3 reads 'Ran with node occlusion-sweep.js batflight arrowshot' and contains exactly two SUMMARY lines, both 96/96. A workspace-wide grep for '96/96' returns only those two lines. That artifact was produced by oculist-1ta.16, whose close note reads 'Re-run: batflight (1ta.1, 1ta.10) 96/96 clean, arrowshot (1ta.2, 1ta.11) 96/96 clean.' This bead reused that phrase to argue its scroll-dissolve refactor caused no regression; commit d410749 touched only effects-playground.html. There is no evidence anywhere in the repo of the sweep being run against a third effect key before oculist-aun.

SO THE CLAIM WAS NARROW, NOT WRONG. It says nothing about the playground's other 43 effects, and in particular never covered the deferred-mount six (matchstrike, comet, stamp, inkbloom, scanline, emberignite) that the oculist-ucs reviewer later measured as dirty. There is no contradiction between this bead and those numbers: they measured disjoint effect sets.

ALSO NOTE, for anyone relying on '96/96' as a denominator: 96 is a constant, 8 viewports x 12 font sizes. 'dirty=96' and '96/96 clean' are the same denominator read from opposite ends.

TWO SEPARATE HARNESS DEFECTS were found while establishing this and are filed as oculist-hgt (the setTimeout neutralization is dead at HEAD) and an escalation on oculist-1ta.21 (the unsampled endpoint produced a false CLEAN for inkbloom).

title: Redraw the Bat Flight artwork with cel shading
description:
Chris reviewed the Bat Flight prototype 2026-09-05 and returned IMPROVE on artwork quality: it should be cartoon-like the way fxCheshire is, with some realism and cel shading.

THE GAP. Every element of fxBatFlight is a flat single-tone fill: the bat is a plain black silhouette, the figure is flat purple with a flat skin-tone face. fxCheshire, the reference, has a defining outline, a translucent lavender head, green eyes with specular highlights, a pink nose, whiskers, and a hard-edged white grin. It reads as a drawn character; the bat reads as a cut-out.

WHAT CEL SHADING MEANS HERE, as an objective bar both implementer and reviewer can check:
1. A defining outline, darker than the base tone, on every solid form.
2. At least three discrete tones per form: base, a shadow tone, and a highlight tone.
3. HARD edges between tones. A gradient is airbrushing, not cel shading. The one exception is the mist column, which is atmosphere rather than a form.
4. One consistent light direction across every element of the effect. Pick it, state it in a comment, and apply it to the bat, the mist and the figure alike.
5. Where a character has a face, the eyes carry a specular highlight, as the Cheshire cat's do.

SCOPE
- The bat sprite, both wing frames.
- The caped figure.
- Keep the mist column as-is unless the new palette needs it retuned.

DO NOT REGRESS. These were expensive to get right and are verified:
- Placement fallback chain and clearance math. If a sprite's dimensions change, BAT_W feeds the clearance calculation, so re-run the occlusion sweep rather than assuming.
- The discrete wing flap must still actually fire, both states.
- offset-rotate stays 0deg so the wingspan stays horizontal.
- Determinism, no Math.random.
- No animated filter, and no filter-based shading such as drop-shadow. Cel shading here means drawn shapes, not a CSS filter.
- Clean teardown, no reflow.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Rendered side by side with fxCheshire at real size, the bat and the figure read as the same class of artwork. Judge by looking, not by counting fills.
- Every form has an outline and at least three discrete tones, consistent with one light direction.
- Occlusion sweep still zero changed pixels inside the match rect across the scenarios oculist-1ta.1 established.
- Screenshots of the bat mid-flight and the final figure at real size, plus a side-by-side against the Cheshire cat.
close_reason: Bat and caped figure redrawn as outlined, cel-shaded vector cartoon in the same family as fxCheshire. Failed first review on eleven specific artwork misses (2-tone wings, 1-tone ears, no eye specular, bowtie wingspan, sticker-like cape highlight, blob head shadow, a two-dot face, a 1.1px specular that rendered no white pixel, an unstroked hair path, flat collar spikes, an invisible 6% skin ramp); all fixed on retry. Re-review confirmed each in the rendered pixels, plus zero occlusion across 14 scenarios and 1484 frames after BAT_W changed 65->90

title: Redraw the Arrow Shot artwork with cel shading
description:
Chris reviewed the Arrow Shot prototype 2026-09-05 and returned IMPROVE on artwork quality: it should be cartoon-like the way fxCheshire is, with some realism and cel shading.

THE GAP. The archer is the weakest artwork in the epic and two independent reviews said so unprompted: at 78-112px the body is a blob, one trapezoid for both legs, a rounded-rect torso, a stub arm, a head circle that reads as detached, and a hood path that renders as a plain skin-tone circle. The bow and arrow carry the whole archery read. Flat single-tone fills throughout.

THE BAR is fxCheshire: a defining outline, a translucent lavender head, green eyes with specular highlights, a pink nose, whiskers, a hard-edged white grin. It reads as a drawn character.

WHAT CEL SHADING MEANS HERE, as an objective bar both implementer and reviewer can check:
1. A defining outline, darker than the base tone, on every solid form.
2. At least three discrete tones per form: base, a shadow tone, and a highlight tone.
3. HARD edges between tones. A gradient is airbrushing, not cel shading.
4. One consistent light direction across every element, stated in a comment.
5. The archer needs a face with eyes carrying a specular highlight, and a silhouette that reads as a person: separate the legs, attach the head to the torso with a visible neck or collar, and make the hood read as a hood.

SCOPE
- The archer sprite in both rest and draw poses.
- The flight arrow, including the fletching.
- The target rings may take shading, but their GEOMETRY is proven and must not change: rx = w/2 * sqrt(2) + pad guarantees the innermost ring contains the match rect, and the entrance settles from scale 1.15 rather than growing from below 1. Do not touch either.

DO NOT REGRESS. All of this was verified across 19 scenarios and cost a retry:
- Three-plan impact chooser gated on absolute clearance, and the corner derived from the winning plan. ARROW_LEN feeds MARGIN, so if the arrow sprite's length changes, re-run the occlusion sweep.
- Fletching must still read at natural size unmagnified. It was enlarged from 46x16 to 58x26 once already because it rendered as a bare stick.
- Target still dissolves in before the arrow arrives; quiver still decays exactly to rest.
- Bowstring contrast, fixed to #1a1a1e, must survive any palette change.
- Determinism, no Math.random, no animated filter, clean teardown, no reflow.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Rendered side by side with fxCheshire at real size, the archer reads as the same class of artwork and as a person rather than a blob.
- Every form has an outline and at least three discrete tones, consistent with one light direction.
- Occlusion sweep still zero changed pixels inside the match rect across the scenarios oculist-1ta.2 established, including the six that failed the first review.
- Screenshots of the archer at rest and at full draw, the arrow in flight, and a side-by-side against the Cheshire cat.
close_reason: Archer, bow, arrow and fletching redrawn as outlined cel-shaded forms in the same family as fxCheshire and the bat figure; the archer now reads as a hooded person rather than a blob. Took three passes: first review failed on a duplicate clipPath id that silently clipped two of the arrowhead's three tones to the archer's head silhouette, two-tone boots, and a hood that read as hair; second failed on a 1-2px occlusion regression at font sizes 22-26, isolated to STRIKE_GAP and cleared by raising it 6->12. Final sweep zero across font sizes 20-30

title: Playwright coverage for the effect-pack settings control
description:
The pack checkbox list added in oculist-tdj.2 has no test in the repo. It was verified end-to-end by the reviewer, but only in a throwaway harness against a temporary registry entry, because zero registry entries carry a pack today, so knownPacks() returns [] and the whole section renders nothing.

Consequence: settings_panel_enter_activation.test.js and overlay_panel_focus_aria.test.js pass without ever touching a pack row, even when packs exist. The control is live but unguarded, and oculist-tdj.3 builds a discovery prompt pointing at it.

STEPS
1. Add a test that injects a packed effectsRegistry entry (follow how the other settings-panel Playwright tests build their fixture) rather than depending on a real pack shipping.
2. Assert: packed effect absent from the picker with the pack off; present after toggling, with no reload; absent again after toggling back.
3. Assert keyboard operation with BOTH Enter and Space, tab-reachability, and that the computed accessible name is the pack label alone (the checkbox glyph must stay aria-hidden).
4. Assert focus survives rebuildSettingsPanelPreservingFocus by data-oc-key.
5. Assert the panel still fits the viewport with enough packs to hit the .oc-checkbox-list 160px cap.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The test fails if the pack toggle stops filtering the picker.
- The test fails if the checkbox loses its accessible name or its Space handling.
- node --test passes in full.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. New test/effect_pack_settings_control.test.js guards pack filtering, Enter+Space activation, accessible name (glyph aria-hidden), data-oc-key focus survival across rebuild, and the 160px checkbox-list cap. Reviewer independently ran 5 break/fix checks, all red for the right reason. Full suite 311/311.

title: One-time dismissible prompt pointing at the pack toggle
description:
Packs default OFF, so without discovery a seasonal event is a feature nobody finds.
The human chose a single dismissible prompt over defaulting the pack on.

FILE: extension/content.js.

STEPS
1. Show the notice ONCE, the first time the overlay is opened after a pack becomes
   available. Persist the dismissal in settings (a boolean, migrated like the rest) so
   it never returns - on any device, since settings sync.
2. It must be dismissible without acting on it, and dismissing counts as answering.
   Do not re-prompt on the next release.
3. Place it inside the overlay's own subtree. It must not reflow the host page, must
   not touch anything outside .oc-, and must respect the reduced-motion path - see
   effectiveMotion() and animate()'s 'reduced' branch at content.js:3910.
4. COPY: "seasonal effects" or "effect pack". Never "plugin", never "add-on". One
   sentence and a way to reach the toggle. This is a find-in-page tool and the notice
   sits in front of someone trying to find text - it should be small, quiet, and
   easy to get rid of.
5. Keyboard reachable and screen-reader announced, consistent with
   overlay_panel_focus_aria.test.js. It must not steal focus from the find input,
   which is the whole point of the overlay.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Appears once, never again after dismissal, and survives a reload and a sync to
  another profile.
- Does not steal focus from the find input.
- No host-page reflow; nothing outside the overlay subtree is touched.
- Suppressed or static under prefers-reduced-motion.
- `node --test` passes in full.
close_reason: One-time pack discovery notice in the overlay shadow root, gated on packsNoticeDismissed. Reviewer verified with mutation tests that the new Playwright test has teeth, plus focus retention, persistence across a real reload, zero animations under reduced motion, and no host-page reflow

title: Settings-panel control for enabling packs
description:
The UI for turning packs on and off.

FILE: extension/content.js, the settings panel (the picker enumeration is at :5739;
build the control near the other fields).

STEPS
1. Add a section to the settings panel listing each known pack with a checkbox,
   writing settings.enabledPacks.
2. The effect picker must update immediately when a pack is toggled - no reload. The
   panel already rebuilds on settings change; follow that path rather than adding a
   new one, and check settings_panel_rebuild_focus.test.js for how focus is expected
   to survive a rebuild.
3. COPY: every user-facing string says "effect pack" or "seasonal effects". The words
   "plugin" and "add-on" must not appear anywhere user-facing. This is a store-review
   constraint the repo already carries, not a style preference.
4. Accessibility is not optional here: the checkboxes need real labels and keyboard
   operation, consistent with overlay_panel_focus_aria.test.js and
   settings_panel_enter_activation.test.js. This is an accessibility tool.
5. Watch panel height. settings_panel_viewport_overflow.test.js and
   settings_panel_effect_list_overflow.test.js both exist because this panel has
   overflowed before; a new section is exactly what makes it happen again.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Toggling a pack adds or removes its effects from the picker with no reload.
- Keyboard reachable and labelled; the aria and Enter-activation tests still pass.
- The panel does not overflow the viewport at the sizes those two tests cover.
- `grep -rni "plugin\|add-on" extension/ docs/ README.md` shows nothing new
  user-facing.
- `node --test` passes in full.
close_reason: Pack checkbox list in the settings panel, wired to the existing rebuild-preserving-focus path. Reviewer verified end-to-end against a temp packed entry: picker updates with no reload, Enter and Space both operate it, accessible name is the pack label alone, focus survives rebuild, panel fits viewport at the 160px list cap with 9 packs. Test coverage deferred to oculist-tdj.5

title: Headless-horseman prototype
description:
A headless rider gallops in, hurls a blazing pumpkin at the match, and rides off.

RIGHTS: clean. Washington Irving, "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow", 1820. Solidly US
public domain, no live trademark of the kind that complicates Tarzan and Tinker Bell.
Still label it by motion rather than by name.

CONVENTIONS
- File: /Users/ccho/Documents/Projects/oculist/artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html.
  Prototype only. Do NOT touch extension/content.js.
- Read fxFlappy (baked-path travel, pixel sprite, whole-cell sprite animation) and
  fxCheshire (phased fade) first. They set every convention: viewport coordinates via
  baseStyle() position:fixed, class "fx" on every element so clearFx() reaches them,
  mount(), a local var DUR, hardcoded colors, WAAPI only.
- Register LAST in effectsRegistry, in the "New candidates (post round 6)" divider.
- Deterministic: hand-authored coordinates, NO Math.random().
- Must clear the DOM completely, cause no page reflow, leave #match unmutated.
- Do NOT touch #fire-index or its max, SHIPPED_LABELS or its frozen numbering,
  effects-round6-scores.md, or the other candidates. Do not commit.

WHY THIS ONE SHOULD READ BETTER THAN THE OTHER FIGURE EFFECTS
Four effects in this epic put a humanoid near the match, and legibility at ~50-70px is
the recurring failure - the Cheshire cat had to lose its body, the first bird was
rejected as unrecognisable. The horseman has a structural advantage: the canonical
image is a SOLID DARK SILHOUETTE, and a filled black horse-and-rider reads at small
size where an outlined detailed figure does not. Lean on that. The horse's gallop
should be a few discrete whole-frame poses rather than a smooth tween - discrete poses
survive scaling, and fxFlappy's first smooth wing squash animated perfectly and
rendered invisibly.

SEQUENCE
1. The rider gallops in from the side, silhouette only, at the height of the match's
   line or just above it. Horizontal travel via a baked offset-path, as fxFlappy does.
2. He rears - a brief pitch-up - and hurls the pumpkin.
3. The pumpkin arcs to the match on a ballistic curve, spinning as it goes. This is the
   bright element and it carries the whole effect's peripheral capture: glowing orange
   against a dark rider, it should be the thing the eye catches.
4. It bursts at the match: a short expanding glow, then gone. Do NOT cover the matched
   word - burst outward from the match's edges, or above it, the way the shipped
   absorption flash in animateTrail sizes itself to the rect.
5. The rider continues off the far side and is gone. Nothing persists.

TWO GATES THIS EFFECT IS ESPECIALLY LIKELY TO TRIP
- G4, flicker: a flaming pumpkin invites rapid luminance reversal. Keep any flicker

Effect key 'horseman', sidebar label 'Galloping Throw', registered last in the New candidates divider. Solid dark silhouette with discrete gallop poses rather than a smooth tween, per the epic's own finding that outlined detail dies at 50-70px.

OBJECTIVE GATES, reviewer-verified independently.

MET: criterion 1's six beats are present and ordered at 1280x900 (gallop 0-850, rear 850-1140, throw 1140-1230, arc 1140-1560, burst 1560-1880, exit 1880-2730). The gating sweep stays exit 0 with batflight and arrowshot 96/96 each.

G4 IS NOT A DISQUALIFICATION, measured three ways against a synthetic 8Hz positive control. WCAG general-flash count is 0. The match rect does reverse luminance 4 times in a 520ms window, but from TWO separate events rather than one wobbly fade: the burst minimum at t=1650 and the horse-transit minimum at t=1980. WCAG 2.3.1 counts opposing-change pairs above the general flash threshold, which makes this 2 flashes/s over about 5% of the reference field. Passes the standard the bead cites; ambiguous only under a literal reading of 'no area reverses 3 times'. Worth knowing it is the worst of the candidate set on the match rect (flappy 2, batflight 0).

THREE THINGS NEED YOUR RULING.

1. BURST LEGIBILITY. Criterion 2 says the word must be fully legible at the burst. It is not: 100% of the match rect changes for about 240ms and contrast drops to 1.70:1 from a 19.7:1 baseline, so the word survives as a shape rather than as text. BUT it is strictly gentler than the shipped flash the bead itself names as the model: fxFlappy peaks at opacity 1 and 1.08:1 over 340ms, fully opaque. The bead's two clauses conflict, 'do NOT cover the matched word' against 'the way the shipped absorption flash sizes itself to the rect', and only you can say which wins.

2. THE EXIT CROSSES THE WORD. The horse reaches 75% of the match rect in flat black for about 60ms at t=1980. title: Wand-and-sparkle-swirl prototype (Tinker Bell)

  times in oculist-e2m a report claimed something read clearly when it did not.

SPECIFIC TO THIS EFFECT
1. G6 RISK: Bloom and Electron Cloud already ship, and both are "particles around the
   match". Swirling sparkles risks being a third of the same thing. The difference has
   to be that these are CAUSED - they issue from the wand tip on the wave, travel to
   the match, and only then orbit. Bloom disperses and Electron Cloud orbits; neither
   has an agent producing them. Lead with the causal beat.
2. The orbit should trace an ellipse around the match rather than a circle, so it
   reads as wrapping the word in 3D rather than sitting on top of it. Sparkles behind
   the word should pass BEHIND it - a lower z-index for the back half of the orbit -
   which is a strong depth cue and costs nothing.
3. Sparkles must not sit over the glyphs long enough to impede reading. Passing behind
   is fine; a static sparkle field on top of the word is not.
4. Determinism matters more here than anywhere else in this epic: particles are the
   classic place Math.random() creeps in. Hand-author the orbit phases.
5. The figure is small. It probably reads better as a silhouette with wings than as a
   detailed figure at this size.
6. RIGHTS: Barrie's Peter Pan is US public domain, but Disney's fairy DESIGN is its
   own copyrighted work - do not reproduce it. A generic winged fairy with a wand is
   the safe reading, with a motion-based label. See the epic.

  Bloom and Electron Cloud when all three are viewed unlabelled.
- Back-half sparkles pass behind the word; the word stays readable throughout.
- No Math.random() anywhere; identical on every fire.
- Nothing remains in the DOM afterwards.
- Screenshots of the wave, the travel, and the orbit, plus a side-by-side against
  Bloom and Electron Cloud.

Review 2's remaining gap (match 10px from a viewport edge, 27-62 dirty px) no longer reproduces, having been closed out by mbmy, tvqw, 73l6, giy7 and 3dd8. New axes probed and clean on both engines: match 6px from the top and bottom edges, a wrapped two-line match, and a 900x360 short viewport. The one edge signature that does still reproduce is oculist-wkfc (320x900 edge-left, font 78-96, ~190px at 640ms in the travel-bezier window), which stays separately tracked and was not counted here. No code change was needed: the effect was already merged to outer main. comments.text:

The ellipse is centred 0.32h below the word, so its side extremes then fall inside the match's vertical band, 4px off the rect, and the unclipped FRONT sparkles cross the rect's lower corners around t900-990 and t1320-1410. - 320x900, match 10px from right edge: 35 dirty px, 1 glyph-ink px (257 and 9 at 3x)
- 320x900, match 10px from left edge: 27 dirty px, 0 glyph-ink px

Either drop the ellipse centre so the front arc stays below the rect bottom whatever rx is, or clip the front arc too in that case. Then verify with the match placed 10px from each viewport edge. The sweep does not cover that placement, see the harness bead filed alongside.

ALL ELSE PASSED in review 2: sweep wandcast, batflight and arrowshot 96/96 clean; 0 Math.random; two fires identical; .fx 0 to 8 to 0; #match outerHTML identical; no reflow; clearFx mid-run clean; G4 fine (at most 1097px at 3+ flashes/s, WCAG limit 21824px); diff confined to the function plus its registry line; 320 and 360 wide fine at the playground's own layout; unlabelled composite against Bloom and Electron Cloud reads as three different effects.

SPECIFIC TO THIS EFFECT
1. The swing is a PENDULUM, and like fxFlappy's flight the physics should generate the
   geometry once at fire time rather than run per-frame. Angle follows
   theta(t) = theta0 * cos(sqrt(g/L) * t); sample it into the arc, bake the result.

   swing - the giveaway is that a real pendulum is fastest at the bottom.

   stay attached to the figure's hands for the whole arc; a vine that detaches or
   stretches is the obvious failure here.
3. Release: the figure lets go near the bottom of the arc and carries on to the match
   on a short ballistic arc, landing beside or above it. The vine swings on and exits.
   Letting go at the arc's bottom is what makes the motion read as deliberate.
4. Legibility at size is the risk, as with every figure in this epic. A simplified
   silhouette beats a detailed one.
5. Generic vine-swinging figure and a motion-based label - "Tarzan" is a live
   trademark. See the epic.

  a pendulum rather than an eased curve.

1. Archer dissolves in at a corner. Pick the corner giving the longest clear run to the
   match, and avoid the playground's fixed right-hand sidebar - a flight drawn over the
   control panel is noise. Dissolve in on opacity, roughly 200ms.
2. Draw and loose. A brief nock-draw-release read, then the arrow departs.
3. The arrow ARCS - a shallow ballistic curve, not a straight line - via offset-path
   with offset-rotate:auto so the shaft always points along its own travel. Fletching
   must be visible at size; a thin line with no feathers reads as a stick.
4. The target dissolves in AT THE MATCH before the arrow arrives, so the eye is led to
   the destination ahead of the projectile.
5. The arrow strikes the target, with a short damped quiver, two or three cycles,
   decaying to rest. A quiver still moving when the effect clears reads as a glitch.
6. Archer, bow, arrow and target all dissolve out. Nothing persists.

THE ONE REAL DESIGN TENSION - RESOLVE IT THIS WAY
A bullseye centred on the match would cover the matched word, and nothing in this
project may do that. Draw the target as concentric rings whose INNERMOST ring is larger
than the match rect, so the rings FRAME the word and it sits in the clear centre. The
arrow then plants at the leading or top edge of the match rather than on the glyphs.
This keeps the human's design intact and the word fully readable. If you find a better
resolution, say so rather than silently covering the text.

DONE-CRITERIA
- All six beats above are visible and in that order, with the target arriving before
  the arrow.
- The matched word is fully legible at every frame, at natural size and at the largest
  beacon size.
- Nothing remains in the DOM afterwards; clearFx() reaches everything.
- VERIFY BY LOOKING AT THE RENDER. Screenshot the dissolve-in, the arrow mid-arc, the
  target appearing, the strike, and the dissolve-out, and inspect them. Three times in
  oculist-e2m a report claimed something read clearly when it did not.
notes: First review FAILED: arrow shaft occludes the matched word in 6 of 20 scenarios, persistently, incl. plain 900x700 at 48px (130px at t1400, occluding t1080-t2140) and the same match at top:300 (250px). Confirmed live/unpaused, not a seek artifact. Root cause: :3436 useTop picks the larger of two clearances but commits to a backwards flight when both are negative; :3297-3300 corner tie-break swings on 0.26px, which flips the outcome between clean and occluding. Ring math, entrance scale, fletching, quiver, determinism and teardown all verified good. One retry dispatched.
close_reason: Arrow Shot prototype: archer dissolve-in, draw and loose, ballistic arc with visible fletching, target rings framing the match, damped quiver to rest, full dissolve-out. Failed first review on arrow-shaft occlusion in 6 of 20 scenarios; fixed with a three-plan impact chooser gated on absolute clearance. Re-review swept 19 scenarios x 111 samples plus three live unpaused runs, all zero changed pixels inside the match rect, with a positive control proving the harness detects the effect

title: Bat-to-figure prototype (Dracula)
description:
A bat flies to the match, then transforms into a caped standing figure on arrival.

CONVENTIONS (identical for every effect in this epic, read them once):
- File: /Users/ccho/Documents/Projects/oculist/artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html.
  Prototype only. Do NOT touch extension/content.js.
- Read fxFlappy (travel + physics + pixel-art sprite) and fxCheshire (a figure placed
  above the match, phased fade) first. They set every convention: viewport coordinates
  via baseStyle() position:fixed, class "fx" on every mounted element so clearFx()
  reaches them, mount(), a local var DUR, hardcoded colors, WAAPI only.
- Register the effect LAST in effectsRegistry so it renders in the "New candidates
  (post round 6)" sidebar divider. Do not reorder existing entries.
- Deterministic: hand-authored coordinates, NO Math.random(). The shape must be
  identical on every fire or scoring is not repeatable.
- MUST NOT occlude the matched glyphs at any point. S2 is weighted x4 and S7 x2, and
  this pairing has already caused two regressions in oculist-e2m. Verify at the
  natural match size, not just the largest.
- Must clear the DOM completely when finished, cause no page reflow, and leave #match
  and its text unmutated. No restorer.
- Prefer transform and opacity. An animated filter forces a main-thread re-raster and
  costs S4 (weighted x3) - a teeth glow was cut from fxCheshire for exactly this.
- Do NOT touch #fire-index or its max, the SHIPPED_LABELS block or its frozen
  38 + i + 1 numbering, artifacts/outputs/effects-round6-scores.md, or the other
  candidates. Do not commit.
- VERIFY BY LOOKING AT THE RENDER. Serve the prototypes directory, click the effect
  button, screenshot the key frames and inspect them. Three times in oculist-e2m a
  report claimed something read clearly when it did not: an invisible wing, an
  invisible grin crescent, a tail that read as a stray mark. A claim that something
  reads well is only worth making if you have looked at the pixels.

SPECIFIC TO THIS EFFECT
1. Travel: reuse fxFlappy's approach - generate the path once, hand it to offset-path
   with offset-rotate:auto, one WAAPI offsetDistance animation. A bat's flight is
   erratic rather than parabolic: a shallow sine weave layered on the approach reads
   as bat-like and is visibly different from Flappy's sawtooth (G6 against a candidate
   in the same divider).
2. The bat is a small silhouette, wings beating. Whole-cell or discrete wing states
   read better at size than a smooth squash - fxFlappy's first wing animated
   perfectly and rendered invisibly.
3. The transformation is the payoff and the hard part. Do NOT cross-fade two sprites
   naively; at this size that reads as a smudge. Use a brief vertical smoke/mist
   column that wipes the bat out and the figure in, so the eye is given something to
   follow.
4. The figure stands BESIDE or ABOVE the match, never over it. A full human figure is
   the tallest thing in this epic - if it cannot read at the size it renders, make it
   a cloaked head-and-shoulders rather than a whole body. The Cheshire cat had to
   become a head with no body for exactly this reason.
5. Generic caped figure. No name in the label - call it something like "Bat Flight".
   See the epic for why.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The bat visibly flies in, transforms, and a legible figure remains beside the match.
- The matched word is never covered, at natural size and at the largest beacon size.
- Nothing remains in the DOM afterwards; clearFx() reaches everything.
- Screenshots of the flight, the transformation midpoint, and the final figure.
close_reason: Bat Flight prototype: weaving flight, discrete wing flap, mist-column transformation, caped head-and-shoulders figure. title: Public-domain character beacon effects
description:
Six character-driven beacon effects requested by the human 2026-09-05. Prototype each
in artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html, fired from its labelled button in the
"New candidates (post round 6)" sidebar divider.

THE SIX
1. Bat flight, bat turns to a caped figure on arrival (Dracula).
2. An arrow shot into the match (Robin Hood).
3. A figure shocked into life at the match (Frankenstein).
4. A figure swinging in on a vine (Tarzan).
5. A cartoon figure tapping a foot and pointing (Mickey/Minnie).
6. A fairy waving a wand, sparkles swirling around the match (Tinker Bell).

PROCESS - NO SCORING ROUND. The human decided 2026-09-05 to skip the blind scoring
process used for the shipped twelve. Each prototype is built, rendered, and put in
front of them; they return pass, fail, or improve. Do NOT create score sheets or
scoring beads for this epic.

The G1-G6 GATES STILL APPLY as build constraints, because they are objective and
cheap to check, and a failure on any of them is disqualifying regardless of taste:
G1 no reflow, G2 no substitution of the match's own glyphs, G3 no side effect outside
the effect's own subtree, G4 no luminance reversal at 3-50 Hz (WCAG 2.3.1,
photosensitive-seizure risk), G5 every animation cancellable, G6 visibly distinct from
every already-shipped effect. The S1-S9 weighted rubric is no longer scored, but its
priorities still explain WHY the constraints below matter - peripheral capture and
context preservation were its two heaviest axes.

RIGHTS STATUS, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The human described all six as public
domain. Three are, cleanly. Three are more complicated, and the complication is
trademark, which copyright expiry does not touch:

• CLEAN: Dracula (Stoker 1897), Robin Hood (folklore), Frankenstein (Shelley 1818).
• TARZAN: the 1912 novel is US public domain, but "Tarzan" is a registered trademark
  actively enforced by Edgar Rice Burroughs, Inc.
• MICKEY/MINNIE: only the Steamboat Willie (1928) versions entered the US public
  domain in 2024. The modern designs - red shorts, white gloves, the rounded modern
  head - remain under copyright, and Disney holds live trademarks it enforces.
• TINKER BELL: Barrie's Peter Pan is US public domain, but Disney's Tinker Bell
  DESIGN is its own copyrighted work. Separately, Great Ormond Street Hospital holds
  a perpetual UK right in Peter Pan under a specific statutory provision.

HOW THAT BINDS THE WORK: prototypes are private and carry no exposure. The decision
point is promotion into extension/content.js, which ships publicly. Every prototype
therefore draws a GENERIC figure, and effect labels describe the MOTION rather than
naming the character ("Bat Flight", not "Dracula"). The human can overrule this at
promotion; it is recorded so the choice is deliberate rather than accidental.

DESIGN RISK COMMON TO FOUR OF THE SIX. Dracula, Frankenstein, Tarzan and Mickey all
put a humanoid figure near the match. The Cheshire cat in oculist-e2m had to become a
head with no body to read at ~70px, and the first bird was rejected outright as
unrecognisable at 26px. A whole human figure is harder still. Each must be legible at
the size it actually renders, and none may occlude the matched glyphs - that pairing
has already caused two regressions in oculist-e2m.

TWO RISK G6 AGAINST SHIPPED EFFECTS:
• The Frankenstein jolt against the shipped Lightning.
• The Tinker Bell sparkle swirl against the shipped Bloom and Electron Cloud.
Both must read as clearly different when shown unlabelled beside those.

ROSTER SIZE, FLAGGED NOT DECIDED: twelve effects ship today, two more are pending in
oculist-e2m, and these six would make twenty. The abandoned oculist-3rv epic existed
partly to CUT the roster. Worth deciding whether this is an addition or a replacement
before promotion, not after.

CONSTRAINTS
• All six edit the same playground file, so they are chained one at a time. Never run
  two of them against the same worktree concurrently.
• Prototypes land on a branch in the OUTER repo (Projects/oculist). The inner code
  repo is on main and needs its own branch before anything touches
  extension/content.js.
• The Fable 5.1 round-6 candidates and the retired blind harness (playground
  candidates 31-38, the #fire-index input, the SHIPPED_LABELS block and its frozen
  numbering, and artifacts/outputs/effects-round6-scores.md) stay untouched and
  unused.
• No user-facing copy may use the word "plugin".
