title: Add 'Speed Lines' effect (manga radiating focus lines + hitstop)
description:
Add a new beacon effect to repo/extension/content.js mimicking manga/anime 'speed lines' (a.k.a. focus lines): straight lines radiating from the impact point across a wide radius, evoking the classic manga panel technique used at a moment of impact, combined with a brief hitstop flash.

Steps:
1. In the `i18n` object (content.js:118-178), add `effectSpeedLines: 'Speed Lines'` near the other `effect*` keys.
2. Write `function animateSpeedLines(rect) { ... }`, placed near the other `animate*` effect functions. Guard clause first: `if (!rect || rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) return;`.
3. Visual composition, `position:fixed` (viewport-anchored, same convention as `animateIris` at content.js:466):
   a. A brief hitstop flash: full-viewport white overlay, opacity spikes 0 -> ~0.5 -> 0 fast (~100-150ms), lower peak opacity than a full flash effect since the lines carry most of the visual weight here.
   b. 12-20 thin straight lines radiating outward from the match center at evenly distributed angles (`360 / count` degrees apart), each a rotated absolutely-positioned div (`width: 1-3px scaled by getBeaconScale()`, long length e.g. 40-60% of viewport diagonal, `transform-origin` at the near end so it grows outward from the match like a manga speed line). Animate each line's length via `transform: scaleX(0) -> scaleX(1) -> scaleX(0.3)` (grows fast, recedes) with a fast easing, staggered fade-out.
   c. Color: use `getEffectiveColors().beacon` for the lines (see note below on accessibility), optionally blended with white near the origin for a 'hot core' look, consistent with how `animateAnimeLaser` mixes accent color + white (content.js:380-400).
4. Every created element must have `className = 'oc-beacon'`.
5. Color must come from `getEffectiveColors().beacon` as the primary driver, not hardcoded black/white-only — this project's Vision Accessibility Suite depends on every effect reflecting the user's active beacon color for color-blind palette support, so don't design a monochrome-only variant even though real manga speed lines are typically black ink on white.
6. Scale line length/width/count by `getBeaconScale()`; reduce line count under `settings.performanceMode` (Lite Mode), same pattern as `animateAnimeLaser`'s `sparkCount` (content.js:428).
7. Append all elements to `document.documentElement` once at the end, not incrementally.
8. Clean up: `setTimeout` to `.remove()` every element, timed via `getBeaconDuration(totalMs + 100)`.
9. Register in `effectsRegistry` (content.js:215-223): add `speedlines: { label: i18n.effectSpeedLines, run: animateSpeedLines },`. Do not reorder or touch other entries.
10. Do not modify any other effect function, i18n locale files, or build.js.

Edge cases:
- Zero-size rect must no-op.
- Keep this visually distinct from the sibling 'Impact Burst' task (star-shaped burst) — this effect is straight uniform radiating lines, not a star polygon. If both tasks land, they should not look like near-duplicates.
- No new npm dependencies.

Acceptance criteria (done-criteria for review):
- `npm test` passes unchanged, including test/settings_panel.test.js's alphabetical-order and effect-existence assertions.
- 'Speed Lines' appears as a selectable radio option in the Settings panel's Highlight Effect list.
- Triggering the effect creates only `.oc-beacon`-classed nodes, all removed from the DOM within ~2s of firing.
- No files changed outside repo/extension/content.js.
acceptance_criteria: npm test passes; 'Speed Lines' selectable in settings panel; effect fires without throwing on a zero-size rect (no-op) and a real rect (creates+removes only .oc-beacon nodes); visually distinct from the Impact Burst star shape; no files changed outside repo/extension/content.js
close_reason: Implemented and reviewer-verified: Speed Lines effect added to effectsRegistry, all tests pass, no DOM leaks, visually distinct from Impact Burst.

title: Add 'Impact Burst' effect (comic star-burst impact frame)
description:
Add a new beacon effect to repo/extension/content.js that mimics an anime/manga 'impact frame': a hard white flash + a jagged comic-style star burst snapping onto the active match, evoking a punch/hit moment (reference: anime impact frames — hard cut to white/flash, sharp radiating burst shape, brief hitstop, then release).

Steps:
1. In the `i18n` object (content.js:118-178), add `effectImpactBurst: 'Impact Burst'` alongside the other `effect*` keys (near line 177).
2. Write `function animateImpactBurst(rect) { ... }` placed near the other `animate*` effect functions (e.g. after `animateAnimeLaser` at content.js:324 or `animateIris` at content.js:466 — follow whichever sibling function's structure is closest). Guard clause first: `if (!rect || rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) return;` (copy this exact pattern from animateAnimeLaser).
3. Visual composition (three layered elements, all `position:fixed` since the effect is viewport-anchored on the match, same convention as `animateIris`):
   a. A brief full-viewport white flash overlay (inset 0) that spikes opacity 0 -> ~0.85 -> 0 very fast (~100-150ms total) to simulate a 'hitstop' flash-cut. Use `getBeaconDuration(...)` for all durations, never a raw literal.
   b. A jagged star-burst shape centered on `rect` (use `clip-path: polygon(...)` with 8-12 alternating long/short points to fake a comic impact star), filled with `getEffectiveColors().beacon`, sized relative to `rect` and `getBeaconScale()`. Animate transform scale with an overshoot easing (e.g. `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`) so it 'snaps' in rather than eases smoothly — 0.2 -> 1.3 -> 1, then fades.
   c. 6-10 short radiating spike lines around the match (thin rotated divs, angle evenly distributed like a starburst), colored with `getEffectiveColors().beacon`, scaling outward and fading — reuse the randomized-placement-loop pattern from the spark generation in `animateAnimeLaser` (content.js:428-456) for consistency, but evenly spaced angles instead of random (bursts read as more 'impact', sparks read as more 'explosion').
4. Every created element must have `className = 'oc-beacon'` (required for the extension's cleanup/resize/DOM-scan logic — grep `.oc-beacon` usage in content.js to confirm all touchpoints before finishing).
5. Color: primary visual color must come from `getEffectiveColors().beacon`, not a hardcoded black/white-only palette — this project has a Vision Accessibility Suite with color-blind palettes that depend on every effect surfacing the user's active beacon color, so don't design an effect that reads correctly only in one color scheme. White is fine for flash/highlight accents (other effects mix white + accent color), just not as the *only* color.
6. Scale all counts/sizes by `getBeaconScale()`, and downscale element/spike counts under `settings.performanceMode` (Lite Mode), same as `animateAnimeLaser`'s `sparkCount` logic (content.js:428).
7. Append all elements to `document.documentElement` once at the end (not incrementally) to avoid layout thrashing, per the existing comment convention in `animateAnimeLaser`.
8. Clean up: `setTimeout` to `.remove()` every element created by this effect, timed via `getBeaconDuration(totalMs + 100)`, mirroring `animateIris`'s multi-element cleanup (content.js:521-524).
9. Register in `effectsRegistry` (content.js:215-223): add `burst: { label: i18n.effectImpactBurst, run: animateImpactBurst },`. Do not reorder or touch the other 7 entries.
10. Do not modify any other effect function, the settings-panel sort logic, i18n locale files, or build.js.

Edge cases:
- Zero-size rect must no-op (return early), same as all sibling effects.
- Must not throw if called back-to-back rapidly (user pressing next-match fast) — rely on the same fire-and-forget DOM node pattern the other effects use; do not add any global mutable state beyond what's local to the function call.
- No new npm dependencies.

Acceptance criteria (done-criteria for review):
- `npm test` (repo/package.json → `node --test test/*.test.js`) passes unchanged, including test/settings_panel.test.js's alphabetical-label-order assertion and existing effect-existence assertions.
- 'Impact Burst' appears as a selectable radio option in the Settings panel's Highlight Effect list (auto-sorted alphabetically by the existing code — no manual sort-order edit needed).
- Manually triggering the effect (e.g. via the extension's find bar on a page, or a quick jsdom/script smoke check) creates only `.oc-beacon`-classed nodes, all of which are removed from the DOM within ~2s of firing (no leaked nodes).
- No changes outside `repo/extension/content.js`.
acceptance_criteria: npm test passes; 'Impact Burst' selectable in settings panel; effect fires without throwing on a zero-size rect (no-op) and on a real rect (creates+removes only .oc-beacon nodes); no files changed outside repo/extension/content.js
close_reason: Implemented and reviewer-verified: Impact Burst effect added to effectsRegistry, all tests pass, no DOM leaks.

title: Prototype impact-frame beacon effects
description: Add anime/manga-style 'impact frame' visual effects to the beacon effectsRegistry in repo/extension/content.js: hit-flash freeze frames, radiating manga speed lines, comic-style star bursts. Inspired by anime impact-frame conventions (hard flash cut, radiating black/white speed lines, jagged burst shapes, brief hitstop). Each effect is prototyped as an independent, selectable option alongside the existing 7 effects (hud/iris/sweep/flame/lightning/electron/arrows) — not a replacement.

comments.author: Chris Cho

title: Full npm test flakes under load: list_search 2000-match cap timeout and availableEffects malformed-enabledPacks subtests cancelled
description: Seen 2026-09-23 during the oculist-nq1x.11 goal run. list_search.test.js 'exceeding the 2000-match total cap' timed out once (chrome.storage.sync echo, 15s) in a full run at --test-concurrency=2 and passes alone in 8.5s; a clean-HEAD full run cancelled 7 subtests of 'availableEffects() guards a malformed settings.enabledPacks' ('did not finish before its parent'). Neither reproduced consistently. Related: oculist-f7vx, oculist-qpl. Done when the cause is identified (timeout budget vs real race) and a repeated full-suite run shows neither.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: 2026-09-23 nq1x.12 run: more full-suite-only timeouts, each passing in isolation, a different victim per run: tentaclerise_effect 'cancellation mid-animation' (15s waitForFunction), color_picker_persistence 'beacon colour input stays mounted across a simulated slider drag', and on clean HEAD reanimate 'degenerate fallback' (~16s). Looks like general load flakiness at --test-concurrency=2, not per-test bugs.

title: Front sparkles and other unclipped effect layers paint onto a reflowed match during handleResize's 100ms debounce
description: Found in the oculist-nq1x.10 re-review. After the backWrap hard cut, a 1200->1160 resize mid-orbit still leaves 6-15 dirty match pixels (t=900/1100/1500) from Wand Cast's front sparkles, because handleResize only calls cancelBeacons() after a 100ms debounce that a continuous drag keeps resetting (content.js ~9611, ~7978). 1184 was clean. The prototype behaves the same and the debounce applies to every shipped effect, so this is cross-effect. Decide first whether to cancel or hide transient beacons on the first resize event (leading edge) rather than after the debounce; done when a mid-animation resize that reflows the match produces zero dirty match pixels for the effects tested.

title: Wand Cast: resize listener (once:true) outlives the run and retains detached backWrap until the next resize
description: Found in the oculist-nq1x.10 re-review. animateWandCast registers a window resize listener with once:true for the oculist-3dd8 hard cut (hardCutBackWrap, content.js ~6199-6205). If no resize happens, the listener stays registered after the effect finishes, holding its detached backWrap; many runs pile up listeners. The comment 'it never outlives this one beacon run' is inaccurate. Done when the listener is removed at natural completion and at cancel (e.g. removeEventListener in the cleanup), the comment is corrected, and a test asserts no retained listener or backWrap after a completed run.

title: batflight_effect.test.js 'viewport edges' times out intermittently under full-suite load
description: Seen once in a full npm test run on 2026-09-23 during the oculist-nq1x.10 implementation; passes in isolation and did not reproduce in two later full runs. Reviewer's inferred cause (not reproduced): batflight_effect.test.js:833 calls setViewportSize then replays immediately, so the resize handler's 100ms-debounced cancelBeacons() (content.js handleResize) can kill the new mount before the wait sees it; suite load widens the race. wandcast_effect.test.js avoids it by waiting for navigation to settle after resize. Done when the test waits past the resize debounce (or equivalent) and a stress run (e.g. 10 full-suite runs or the file under parallel load) shows no timeout.

title: Reanimation Jolt at Beacon Size XL in a narrow window widens the page while it plays
description: From the oculist-nq1x.8 review 2026-09-23. In the degenerate placement fallback at XL in a 320px viewport the figure paints out to x=358, so document scrollWidth grows 320 -> 358 for the effect's lifetime and the page briefly gains a horizontal scrollbar. The match is never covered. Fix direction: clip the wrapper to the viewport width (overflow hidden on the full-viewport wrapper) or clamp the fallback's outward edge.

title: No Animation Speed coverage for Bone Assembly, Flappy, Galloping Throw, Jack-o'-Lantern or Trail effects
description: From oculist-s0vr (2026-09-23): grep of test/*_effect.test.js finds no animationSpeed/durFactor/getBeaconDuration assertion in boneassembly, flappy (comment only, line ~316), horseman, jackolantern or trail. Port cheshire_effect.test.js's Animation Speed test shape: collect every rendered animation's getComputedTiming() delay and duration at normal, then assert both scale by the fast (0.5) and slow (1.75) factors within 1ms; prove red with durFactor=1 and with one unscaled delay. Restore speed without a same-value chrome.storage.sync write.
close_reason: Animation Speed tests for Bone Assembly, Flappy, Galloping Throw, Jack-o'-Lantern and Trail via a shared collectAnimationTimings helper (Cheshire moved onto it). Flappy pins its flight geometry and asserts flap count across speeds. Passed second review: each red on durFactor=1 and an unscaled delay, isolated and concurrent runs green

title: flappy_effect.test.js Beacon Size test: the finally's same-value reset to M masks M-stage failures as a 15s echo timeout; relabel 'glyph intrusion'
description: From the oculist-rnqe review 2026-09-23. (1) The rewritten Beacon Size L/XL test's finally resets Beacon Size to M; when the setting is already M the chrome.storage.sync write never echoes, so an M-stage assertion failure (reproduced with a doubled half-height mutation) surfaces only as 'oc-settings change never echoed' after 15s. Skip the reset when already M, as the XL write already does. (2) The comment calls the painted figure 'glyph intrusion' but it counts every changed pixel in the match rect, mostly above the letters; relabel, or add a glyph-ink count (reviewer measured ink covered 0-3/311). (3) Check (2), (overlap-3)/wrapHeight within 50% of M, is loose (tolerates ~5px extra drop at XL); check (3) carries the size-drift detection. Consider tightening.
close_reason: finally skips the same-value M reset so M-stage failures surface as the real assertion (red-proofed); painted-pixel count relabelled; ratio tolerance tightened 0.5 to 0.15 from measured <1% drift, 20 green runs

title: Late working-list merge: capped merge can drop a user term that duplicates a restored one; merge rescan resets next-match to 0 of N and briefly replaces a draft's highlight
description: Follow-ups from the oculist-v1jg reviews 2026-09-23 (content.js mount loadWorkList callback, merge branch). (1) Cap: a full 10-term restored list t0..t9 lands late after the user added t9 then quarklet; the result is [t0..t8, quarklet] and the user's t9 is gone, because dedupe counts t9 as restored and the restored-side trim cuts it. Fix: when trimming restored terms, keep those also present in workListTerms and cut from the rest. (2) The merge calls performListSearch(), which resets activeIndex/searchRanges, so a user who pressed next-match before the restore landed goes back to '0 of N'. (3) If a draft is being typed, that scan replaces the draft's highlight until the next debounce. All are narrow races (restore delayed past a user action); none observed outside forced delays.
close_reason: Late merge keeps user terms that duplicate restored ones under the cap, preserves the next-match position, and defers the rescan while a real draft owns the highlight (reference-identity predicate, termRanges remapped by value). Passed second review, 6 mutations each pinned by its own test, 95/95 twice

title: list_search.test.js:277 'each chip shows its own hit count' failed once under full-suite load
description: Seen 2026-09-22 during the oculist-4afn retry's npm test run (397/398): test/list_search.test.js:277 'each chip shows its own hit count...'. Passed 7/7 run alone immediately after. oculist-4afn touches only the Galloping Throw pumpkin landing offset. Same contention family as oculist-434k, oculist-ilkz, oculist-v1jg.
close_reason: Same root cause as oculist-v1jg: the late mount restore reset termRanges, blanking counts. Fixed by 772ad82 (access-probe wait) and the v1jg merge; list_search 'a late mount-restore brings every chip's count up to date' is red on the old content.js and green now; list_search 0 red in 7+3 loaded runs after the fixes.

title: jackolantern_effect.test.js: three weak spots in the placement coverage
description: Found by the oculist-4rso reviewer 2026-09-22, none blocking: (1) :594-608 asserts clearance against the mouth PANEL rect (viewBox 26..154 x 67..107), which is larger than the CAV box (32..148 x 73..101) the placement math guarantees, so it is weaker than the real 6px contract; (2) mouth mode is exercised only at Beacon Size l and xl, never at S, so the cavity-shrink hazard the code comment names is untested; (3) expectedPlacement() at :70-111 reproduces the shipped formula verbatim, so a placement-formula bug cannot fail the tests that use it (the rendered-box Beacon Size tests do recompute nothing, which mitigates it). Also: MIN_SCALE, the 72px readability floor, is applied before * beaconScale at content.js:3628, so a short match forced below-pumpkin at Beacon Size S renders a ~50px pumpkin, under the floor the comment at :3692 claims.
close_reason: Mouth clearance asserted against the rendered CAV box at 6px (tol 0.05) incl. Beacon Size S; below-pumpkin tests carry a formula-independent above-mode contract; floor comment corrected (72px at M, scales with Beacon Size, no behavior change). CLEAR 6->5 fails 4 tests.

title: Jack-o'-Lantern: no native-scale chromium/webkit render capture for the shipped effect
description: oculist-4rso's acceptance criteria require native-scale Chromium and WebKit captures confirming the SHIPPED render matches the accepted playground effect in both placements and all three light states. artifacts/outputs/ holds jackolantern-proofs (oculist-xl8f) and jackolantern-nq1x15, nothing for the shipped animateJackOLantern. The 4rso reviewer verified geometry and DOM in both engines on 2026-09-22 but nobody compared the shipped render visually. Either capture it or record the criterion as discharged by the prototype proofs.
close_reason: Shipped animateJackOLantern captured in chromium+webkit (dsf1/dsf2), mouth+above, dim/warm/bright; matches the accepted prototype. WebKit via content.js injected into a plain page with a chrome.storage/runtime stub (reviewer judged fair: stub covers no render path). Reproducible byte-identical; mutation-proven to come from shipped content.js. Evidence + scripts: artifacts/outputs/jackolantern-aqlb-shipped/.

title: effect_enumeration_sync.test.js's literal-value regex breaks on an escaped apostrophe in an i18n label (verified: 'Jack-o\'-Lantern' truncates to 'Jack-o\'); document the curly-apostrophe workaround or harden the regex
description: test/effect_enumeration_sync.test.js:84 builds its literal-value matcher as '([^']*)' with no escape awareness, so an i18n label containing an apostrophe truncates. oculist-4rso worked around it by using a curly apostrophe (U+2019) in 'Jack-o'-Lantern Flicker'; an escaped straight quote breaks the test. Make the regex escape-aware so a future label is not forced into a particular apostrophe character.
close_reason: Literal matcher now escape-aware ('((?:[^'\\]|\\.)*)' + single-pass unescape of \' and \\); unit test red on the old pattern and on a missing unescape; stale content.js comment replaced.

title: Cheshire: no coverage for Animation Speed scaling or the below-match settle direction
description: test/cheshire_effect.test.js covers Beacon Size but not durFactor (Animation Speed) scaling, and does not assert the settle direction on the below-match placement branch. The e2m.6 reviewer measured both as correct in a harness on 2026-09-22 (drift re-signs to -0.06 relative at every size in chromium and webkit), so this is a coverage gap, not a known defect. Same gap likely applies to the other packed effects.
close_reason: cheshire_effect.test.js: Animation Speed test asserts every rendered WAAPI delay and duration scales by the speed factor at fast/slow (red under durFactor=1 and under an unscaled grin delay); below-match settle test forces each placement (geometry-verified) and asserts the grin drifts down above and up below (red with the drift not re-signed). File 10/10 twice; npm test 407/407.

title: flappy_effect.test.js Beacon Size test computes the landed bottom edge instead of reading the rendered box
description: The L/XL Beacon Size test in test/flappy_effect.test.js derives the bird's bottom edge from the motion path end plus its own copy of the scale factor. It never reads getBoundingClientRect of the rendered sprite, so disabling the getBeaconScale transform alone would not fail it. Assert on the rendered box after landing instead. Reviewer note 2026-09-22: a mirrored flight at XL lands with bottom edge ~370 vs match top 359 (glyphs still uncovered, sprite tilt from the prototype's flight physics); a rendered-box assertion should decide whether that tolerance is acceptable.
close_reason: Beacon Size test now reads the rendered sprite at the pinned landed frame (t=900): height ratio 1.5/2.25, tilt-normalized overlap vs M, painted intrusion at XL <= 2x M both directions. Red with the scale transform disabled (x1.001); old test passed under it. Mirrored XL acceptable: reviewer glyph-ink count 3/311 at XL mirrored vs 0-1 at M, paint stops at row 3-4 (prototype perch design, effects-playground.html:3471).

title: draft_ownership.test.js:365 dim-registry assertion failed once under full-suite load
description: Seen 2026-09-22 in the oculist-e2m.5 review's npm test run (355/356): test/draft_ownership.test.js:365, the dim registry assertion during a draft. Passed 6/6 twice run alone with OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE=3. Unrelated to effects. Not reproduced on clean main. Same contention family as oculist-434k and oculist-v1jg.
close_reason: Same race as oculist-434k: beforeEach's raw session remove was denied pre-grant, the previous test's oc-worklist survived, and a late loadWorkList retry reset termRanges, emptying the dim registry (reviewer traced it, content.js:222-290, 9025-9039). Probe wait extracted to test/helpers/session_access.js and used in draft_ownership, stale_mount_guard, worklist_storage. Under load: 9/15 and 7/8 red before, 15/15 and 8/8 green after.

title: stale_mount_guard.test.js 'delayed loadWorkList callback does not clobber' timed out at 45s once under full-suite load
description: Seen 2026-09-22 during the oculist-nq1x.3 review: one npm test run (concurrency 2, timeout scale 3) failed test/stale_mount_guard.test.js 'a stale mount's delayed loadWorkList callback does not clobber a newer mount's restored chip row' with a page.waitForFunction 45000ms timeout. The same file passed twice run alone with the nq1x.3 change present, and the implementer's full run minutes earlier was 350/350 green. nq1x.3 does not touch loadWorkList or mount code. Not yet reproduced on clean main. Same contention shape as oculist-v1jg; triage whether it shares that root cause.
close_reason: Root cause: the test's raw chrome.storage.session set/remove raced background.js's setAccessLevel grant; a denied seed set is dropped silently, so the chip wait ran out its 45s. Fix: access-probe wait in before() (ported from worklist_storage). Under 8-worker load: implementer 5/5 red then 10/10 green; reviewer 6/8 red then 8/8 green with lastError captured. Not v1jg's mechanism.

title: boneassembly_effect presence test: time its checkpoints from mount, not fixed waits
description: From oculist-nq1x.5 review 2. The 'figure survives past the earliest scatter-in piece' test waits fixed 800/1500/2250ms from the keypress; the figure ends at about 2370ms, so Enter-to-mount latency leaves about 100ms of margin on a loaded runner. Acceptance: checkpoints measured from the mount time (for example a MutationObserver or polled mount timestamp), and the test still goes red when per-animation removal is restored in track().
close_reason: Presence test now records removal time on the figure's own clock: a MutationObserver armed at mount stores the figWrap fade's currentTime when pieces leave; asserts removal at >= endMs-30 and all 8 pieces leave together. Under cpu-load 9/90: 0/8 target reds vs HEAD 2/8. Mutants red: per-animation removal, removeFig at 1200/2000/2300, single skull removal. Low, not fixed: a cancelled clock fails with the generic 'never fully left' message after LONG_TIMEOUT rather than the cancel message; window stash is not cleared on failure.

title: Bone Assembly checker: tighten the pelvis-void assertion and widen rib-gap coverage
description:
Filed from oculist-nq1x.4 review 4 (PASS on mechanics, these were non-blocking). Evidence: session scratchpad 72e304c4.../scratchpad/rv4/ (holescan.js, pel-*.log, rib-*.log).

1. MEDIUM. proveAssembledVoids counts a sample as background if ANY of its 4 corner pixels is neither ivory nor dark within 18. Anti-aliased ivory/dark blends pass that. A mutant with holes back at (18,67) still passes 16/16 at (21,69.5) where no hole exists. Fix: use the rib check's tight-background rule (within 10 of the page colour). Acceptance: the holes-moved mutant goes red on both engines and themes.
2. MEDIUM, linked. On Chromium light the pelvis voids never reach the page colour (closest pixel 19-45 levels off across 6 phases). Likely needs a larger hole ry (now 1.4) so item 1's tighter rule passes. Keep hole clearance from the thigh capsule.
3. LOW. Rib-gap check samples only the left half, gaps 1 and 3 over about 1.3 local units. Widen to both halves.
4. LOW. Checker comment claims RIB_OUTLINE_ADD=3.0 is red on both engines and both themes. Dark theme never goes red and WebKit fails only 2 samples. Correct the comment.
5. LOW, human call. On dark pages the dark leg cap barely shows, so the skull's ivory sits 2-3px below the feet's visible ivory.
6. On promotion (oculist-nq1x.5), strip the test-only window.__baSubpixelTestOffset read from fxBoneAssembly.
close_reason: Pelvis-void check tightened to the rib rule (closest of 4 neighbours within 10 of the page colour); holes-moved mutant red 32/32 through the real checker. Tighter rule needed pelvis hole ry 1.4 to 2.1 (minimal; thigh clearance 0.80, outline 0.94), mirrored identically into extension/content.js animateBoneAssembly. Rib-gap check mirror-samples both halves with a 0.5 margin; RIB_OUTLINE_ADD 3.0 and 2.7 still red; comment states the per-engine/theme results. Item 5 accepted by human; item 6 already satisfied (port never had the hook). Checker 3/3, sweep exit 0 maxPixels=0. Evidence crop: artifacts/outputs/boneassembly-nq1x4-v2/nq1x16-pelvis-ry21.png. Low, not fixed: boneassembly_effect.test.js does not pin the hole geometry.

comments.text: Human accepted item 5 (dark-theme skull sink) on 2026-09-21. Out of scope, do not fix.

title: seedHalloweenPack's failure branch has no test coverage
description:
Found by the reviewer of oculist-nq1x.2, 2026-09-21. Not a defect and not a
done-criterion of that bead; filed rather than fixed in-run.

seedHalloweenPack() in extension/background.js has a failure branch -- the
console.error plus "onboarding proceeds anyway" path -- with no test behind it.
The settings_race error tests (a), (b) and (c) all pre-set seededHalloweenPack
in their fixtures so the chained seed is a no-op there and never errors.

The blocklist seed it was modeled on HAS this coverage, under oculist-6tp. This
bead is parity with that: one test that makes the pack seed's write fail and
asserts onboarding still completes and the flag is not falsely set.

Cheap. Do it before the store submission, not after.
close_reason: Added settings_race test mirroring oculist-6tp (c) for seedHalloweenPack: its set() fails, onboarding still opens the welcome tab, seededHalloweenPack stays unset, both error messages logged, no retry. Seven mutants red, including the flag assertion on its own. npm test 346/346.

title: Effect-count sweep, CHANGELOG entry, and store copy launching the pack system
description:
Last bead of the epic. Runs once every promotion has landed, not per promotion.

SUPERSEDES oculist-e2m.7 ("CHANGELOG entry and stale effect-count sweep"), which was
scoped to Flappy and Cheshire alone before they moved into this pack. Close e2m.7
pointing at this bead when this lands.

MESSAGING DECISION (human, 2026-09-22)
The release is announced as the launch of the pluggable effect pack system, with the
Halloween pack as its first example. Marketing and release surfaces (CHANGELOG.md,
README.md, STORE.md, the store listing copy, promo pages under docs/) do NOT name,
list, count or describe the individual pack effects. Users discover them by using the
pack. This does not touch the packed slices of the four enumeration sites that
test/effect_enumeration_sync.test.js polices (extension/welcome.html prose and
settings mockup, both spots in docs/index.html): the promotion beads keep filling those.

WHAT TO SWEEP

1. Stale core effect counts and core effect lists outside the four policed sites.

title: Neon Sign Flicker (fxNeon) appears not to flicker at all on webkit: G4 positive control returns 0 flagged pixels where chromium returns 2094
description:
Adjacent finding from the oculist-1ta.25 review, 2026-09-17. Not investigated, filed so it is not lost.

While validating a G4 measurement pipeline, the reviewer used the shipped 'neon' effect as a known-positive flicker control. On chromium it behaves as expected: largest flagged contiguous region 2094px, max 3 reversals in a 1s window, the same order of magnitude earlier reviews in this epic cite (4002px). On webkit the identical measurement returns 0 flagged pixels.

Two readings, not distinguished: either the measurement pipeline has a webkit-specific fault, or fxNeon genuinely does not flicker on webkit, which would mean the effect does not play as designed there. The reviewer worked around it by building an engine-independent synthetic 5Hz opacity square wave, which flagged 3600/3600 px with max 10 reversals on BOTH engines. That validates the pipeline on webkit and leaves fxNeon itself as the more likely explanation, but it was not confirmed.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE CONTROL. If fxNeon really does not flicker on webkit, then every G4 measurement in this epic that used neon as its positive control is unvalidated on webkit specifically, and any WCAG 2.3.1 reasoning about the shipped neon effect does not describe what Safari users see.

FIRST STEP: seek fxNeon to fixed times on webkit and diff the frames directly, before touching any measurement code.
close_reason: Fixed-time diagnosis proved the reported WebKit G4 zero was a sampling-cadence false negative, not a missing Neon effect: the real opening WAAPI animation was paused and sought at 10/60/120/180/210ms, producing the expected off/bright/off/dim/bright opacity sequence and nonzero adjacent-frame pixel diffs on both Chromium and WebKit. Added a reusable cross-engine check and wrapped each launched browser in try/finally after earlier screenshot failures exposed a cleanup leak. Owner and independent reviewer both passed exact values: Chromium changedPixels 7654/7367/4162/7358, WebKit 6502/6082/3684/6207, one animation each, exit 0. Before/after process audits found no leaked matching Node, Chromium, or WebKit processes. Static independent review also passed.

title: fxTentacleRise: EDGE_ALLOW can erode MARGIN to ~0 because the overlap guard tests fill-only extent, ignoring the 0.7px stroke bulge
description:
Found by the oculist-1ta.24 retry reviewer, 2026-09-17. Not a criterion failure and not currently reachable by the sweep, which is why .24 closed over it.

MECHANISM. planTentacle's 'overlaps' test uses the ribbon FILL extent (PAINT_X, x in [8.539, 31.313] local units). getBoundingClientRect on an SVG polygon excludes stroke, verified on both engines, so the 1.4px non-scaling stroke adds 0.7px of paint beyond what the guard measures. EDGE_ALLOW=20 lets the wrapper be pushed back toward #match until the FILL gap is ~0 while the guard still reads false, so the real margin in that band is the intended 2px minus the unmeasured stroke bulge.

REPRODUCER. #match position:fixed, left:11.4px, font-size:48px, viewport 1280x900, left limb, t=580ms (the poseFull hard cut): fill gap 0.081px. Under the harness's own Math.round(r.left) clip that counts 6 changed pixels, identical on chromium and webkit.

NOT A GLYPH TOUCH. With a strictly-inside clip (ceil(left)/floor(right)) it is 0 pixels at dsf 1 and 2, and 0 across 500+ font and sub-pixel probes hunting the worst case. So no glyph ink is affected. The problem is that the effective margin in a roughly 2px-wide band (r.left just above 31.313*scale - 20) drops below the measured clean/dirty boundary, which the same reviewer bracketed by mutation at MARGIN between 1.0 and 1.5. It would trip this project's own 0-pixel gate if that placement were ever sampled; the shipped grid does not sample it.

FIX DIRECTION. One line: fold the stroke bulge into the guard, i.e. test 'far + 0.7 > r.left' rather than the bare fill extent. Then add the reproducer placement to the sweep so the band is covered.

WORTH KNOWING, from the same review: a green sweep alone cannot distinguish real clearance from a vacuous pass. Mutating MARGIN to -1 reports 96/96 clean because all 96 rows then mount zero tentacles. The per-row limb census is what rules that out.
close_reason: Included the 0.7px non-scaling stroke bulge in both tentacle overlap edges and added the exact 11.4px reproducer plus a 14px two-limb control census. Verified 96/96 grid, 4/4 forced, and 14/14 edge scenarios clean; no-bulge mutation fails the census.

title: arrowshot-fallback-check.js --baseline ignores --random, so the vs-main safety comparison is grid-only
description:
Found by the oculist-tklc reviewer, 2026-09-16, while verifying tklc's done-criteria.

arrowshot-fallback-check.js main() (~lines 1106-1108) returns mainBaseline(...) BEFORE reaching the --random branch, and mainBaseline iterates geometries() (~line 914), the deterministic grid. So there is no way to run baseline-mode (comparison against real git main) over a random sample of any size.

CONSEQUENCE, measured on tklc: the criterion 'the four safety counts stay 0 against main on the grid and 400k random' is only half-satisfiable with committed tooling. Grid is MET against real main via --baseline. At 400k random the run passes 0/0/0/0 but only against originalPick, the harness's synthetic re-derivation of the pre-clamp pick, NOT against main. Any bead recording '0 against main on 400k random' is recording something the tooling cannot currently measure.

FIX: let --baseline honour --random (and --seed), i.e. have mainBaseline iterate randomGeometries(n, seed) when --random is passed instead of returning early on the grid. Pre-existing limitation, not introduced by tklc.

DONE-CRITERIA: 'node arrowshot-fallback-check.js --baseline <main copy> --random 40000' compares against the main copy over 40000 random geometries and reports the four safety counts; the grid path is unchanged; a deliberately-broken chooser still reds the run in both modes.
close_reason: main() now builds one geometry iterable before branching, and mainBaseline consumes it, so --baseline honours --random and --seed. Reviewer PASS on the plumbing. Same-geometry property proven, not asserted: per-iteration fingerprints of the {vw,vh,r} handed to baseChooser vs chooser gave 0 mismatches over 2000 iterations, and a self-comparison against a byte-copy of the working file gave 0 violations over 20000 random geometries. Grid path byte-identical but for the timing token; the pre-change file silently ignored --random (printed no random header, ran the 17621 grid), the post-change file honours it. A broken chooser (INSET 40 to 4000) reds both modes. Only arrowshot-fallback-check.js changed, +20/-11. Outer-repo commit 3b7c962. THIS BEAD DID ITS JOB BY EXPOSING A REAL REGRESSION: the first vs-main random run reds with 96 violations, filed as its own bead.

title: style-attr-byte-exact-check: the oculist-e4d window guard re-derives the effects' timing, so a playground timing edit restores the vacuous pass
description:
Demonstrated by the oculist-e4d reviewer, 2026-09-16, by mutation rather than argued. actualStaleRestoreAbsMs() (style-attr-byte-exact-check.js ~129-140) is a verbatim second copy of the playground's own waveEnd/lastLock/wrapEnd timing (effects-playground.html ~1823/1849 letterwave, ~2459/2479/2497 scramble), keyed on matchLen alone. So it tracks fixture-TEXT drift and nothing else.

MEASURED: change letterwave's stagger from 45 to 90 (effects-playground.html:1819/1823) with the fixture still 6 chars. The real window moves to (1130,1430); the guard still prints window=(905,1205), sampleInWindow=true, exit 0. Decisive second mutation: same timing change PLUS the oculist-6wo guard removed at :1845 still reports 'PASS letterwave (double-fire)', exit 0. An edit to the effect's own timing reintroduces exactly the silent-false-pass class e4d closed, one level up, and the guard vouches for it. Same shape as oculist-l2d and oculist-l92.

SECOND, SMALLER ISSUE from the same review: sampleInWindow is a strict integer comparison with no margin. At a 3-char fixture scramble's sample clears its lower edge by 10ms nominal, and instrumenting the real sample shows it lands 1526-1528ms against a nominal 1520 (playwright round-trip overhead the guard does not model), leaving ~2-4ms. Near an edge the guard certifies a sample that ordinary jitter can push out, i.e. it vouches for a vacuous green.

FIX DIRECTIONS. Observe instead of re-deriving: hook restore/runEffect in the page and compare the sample against the instants actually observed, rather than recomputed ones. Failing that, export the timing constants from the playground so both sides read one source. Separately, require a margin (25-50ms inside both edges) rather than strict inequality.
close_reason: Replaced duplicated timing formulas with pre-load observation of actual terminal timer callbacks and require 25ms clearance from both window edges. Final byte-exact suite passes; 45->90 timing mutation and tightened-margin mutation both fail the guard.

See occlusion-sweep-results.md, oculist-519q section, Summary.

title: prefire-scroll-abort-check I.1: replace the hand-picked SELF_DISSOLVE_SPACER_PX with a bounded search over the documented band, so a load burst cannot produce a false red
description:
Raised by the oculist-knog reviewer, 2026-09-15, as the cheap durable fix it
deliberately did not implement.

CONTEXT. oculist-knog added scenario I.1, the first row that can actually
catch removal of the pre-fire scroll suppression. It works by sizing a spacer
so Chromium's smooth scroll is still running when ensureVisible's 1200ms
MAX_SETTLE_MS fires, which means trailing scroll events land after mount --
the race the suppression exists to absorb. knog also added a vacuity gate:
if zero scroll events land after mount, the row fails loudly telling you the
fixture has gone vacuous, rather than passing while asserting nothing.

THE RESIDUAL PROBLEM. The spacer is a hand-picked constant, 4550px, sitting
about 50px below a cliff. Past that cliff the scroll has not arrived by the
timeout, finish()'s TOLERANCE_PX check rejects, cb() never runs, and the row
reads mounted=false -- a false red on unmodified HEAD.

Load pushes toward that cliff. Chromium's smooth scroll is time-based, so
load does not lengthen it; it starves the ticks, so the position sampled at
MAX_SETTLE_MS is more often short. Observed once by the knog implementer at
ambient load avg 5.08. The knog reviewer could not reproduce it in 8 HEAD runs
at loads 2.8 to 9.2, including under 4 and under 14 spinners on a 10-core box.
Combined observed rate is roughly 1 in 12. Load average BEFORE the run is not
the predictor -- a burst inside the specific 1.2s window is.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING ANYWAY. An ~8 percent random red is the kind of row a
maintainer eventually deletes, and deleting it reintroduces exactly the hole
knog closed: no test anywhere catches removal of the suppression. The failure
is loud rather than silent, which is the safe direction and strictly better
than what preceded it, so this is not urgent -- but the constant is the wrong
knob.

THE FIX the knog reviewer proposed. The harness can now detect both cliffs
itself, so make it search instead of guess: on mounted=false, retry the case
once or twice at lower spacers inside the documented band (4500, then 4450),
and FAIL only if it never mounts anywhere in the band, reporting which spacer
it settled on. Cost is one extra ~2.5s fire in the rare miss. The vacuity gate
still guarantees falsifiability at whichever spacer wins, so both cliffs
become a bounded search rather than a hand-picked number.

MEASURED BAND, for whoever picks this up: usable range is roughly 4450-4600
(~150px), not the ~400px originally recorded. 4800 never mounts 3/3 on HEAD,
as do 5000 and 6000; 4700 fails to mount 2/3 on HEAD; 4400 held 1/3 on the
mutated build; 4200 holds vacuously 3/3 on the mutated build. The timing
margin at 4550 is ~15-25ms: the last genuine scroll lands one frame after
mount.

DO NOT simply widen or re-pick the constant without the search -- that just
moves the cliff, and the next machine finds it again.
close_reason: Replaced the hand-picked SELF_DISSOLVE_SPACER_PX=4550 with SELF_DISSOLVE_SPACER_LADDER=[4550,4500,4450], descending only, retrying only on mounted=false and stopping at the first rung that mounts. Reviewer PASS on the property that matters: the floor cannot be walked below 4450 (inline literal, single call site, no process.argv or process.env anywhere in the file), and the vacuity gate is evaluated at whichever rung mounts, proven by forcing a descent to a vacuous spacer and watching it fail at rung 2/2. Falsifiability held by mutation with the suppression removed: FAIL at 4550, at 4500, and at the 4450 floor 2/2, never searching to a pass, and I.1 remained the only failing row. Unmodified HEAD passes at rung 1/3 with no added cost; a descent costs ~3s. Reviewer also judged the stop-on-mounted predicate correct: vacuity is monotone in the spacer, so descending can only deepen a degenerate mount, never repair it. Stale SELF_DISSOLVE_SPACER_PX reference at line 351 corrected in the same commit. Outer-repo commit 5b5b126.

title: fxWandCast: edge-left match ~259px wide (font 80px) at 320x900 reads 142px dirty at 640ms -- orbit/travel geometry, not side-selection
description:
Discovered while proving oculist-giy7's narrowed suppression guard band     
  (occlusion-sweep.js EDGE_FONTS scratch-extended to 70/72/74/76/80/96, edge- 
  left-320x900). At font=80 (match width 259.3px), the flanking figure's own  
  clamped box does NOT overlap #match (giy7's guard correctly does not        
  suppress, figure renders with 50 samples), but the overall effect is NOT    
  clean: maxPixels=142 at atTime=640ms. Confirmed pre-existing: identical     
  142px@640ms reproduces against the true pre-giy7 original file (git show    
  HEAD at time of discovery), so this is not caused by giy7's fix.            
  atTime=640ms falls inside the sparkle travel-bezier window (CAST_START=450ms
  + stagger, TRAVEL_DUR=260ms), not the figure's static box -- most likely the
  orbit ellipse/travel-bezier clearance math (rx/ry/padX/ORBIT_EDGE_MARGIN, or
  the travel bezier's convex-hull clearance) has a gap for match widths in the
  ~250-310px range that was never exercised by the shipped EDGE_FONTS set     
  (natural/48/96 -- 80px is not shipped). Likely related to oculist-tvqw's rx 
  floor territory but NOT confirmed -- re-derive before assuming. Distinct    
  from oculist-73l6 (edge-right-320x900-natural, 1px@1440ms, much smaller     
  magnitude, different timing window, likely different mechanism -- do not    
  conflate the two without re-measuring).                                     

ONSET CORRECTION (oculist-giy7 reviewer, wider probe): the defect starts at 78px (width 252.8, 67px dirty at 640ms), not 80px. Same mechanism, lower magnitude, identical before and after giy7's fix. Do not anchor this bead to the single 80px sample.

ATTRIBUTION PROVEN BY MECHANISM, not inference: instrumenting per-element rects over 120 frames at fs=76/78/80 against the pre-giy7 playground shows the flanking figure's wrapper (37x48) NEVER intersects #match at any of those widths. The only elements that ever do are the viewport-sized backWrap -- which is clip-path'd to exclude the match rect and paints nothing there -- and the 8x8 sparkles, first touching at ~456-486ms, inside the travel-bezier window (CAST_START=450ms + stagger, TRAVEL_DUR=260ms). giy7's guard is scoped to the figure's box and the figure's box is genuinely clear, so this is not a case that guard should have caught. That is why it is a separate bead rather than giy7 being incomplete.
close_reason: Fixed both proven contributors at the 320x900 edge-left 78/80px boundary. Wand Cast now computes the fairy's full overflow-visible painted bounds (all poses, tip radius, wing/core, scale and mirroring) before mounting, suppressing only when real paint would cross #match; sparkle launches that are otherwise safe stay transparent only until the sampled travel path clears the sparkle's full box+glow reach. Added key-scoped 76/78/80 boundary rows with bidirectional activity gates: 76 must render, 78/80 must be exactly suppressed. RED evidence: original 78 row was 99px dirty at 640ms; an over-broad TIP_RADIUS mutant now exits 1 specifically because 76 becomes inactive. Owner and independent reviewer GREEN: exit 0, controls OK, grid 96/96, forced 4/4, edge 15/15, all maxPixels=0; 76 rendered fx=8/maxEnd=1960ms, 78/80 suppressed fx=0/maxEnd=0ms. Static syntax/diff checks pass and final process audit found no task browsers.

title: effects-playground: below the 480px breakpoint the static sidebar renders ~3100px below the fold, so a human firing an effect at narrow width cannot see the controls
description:
Raised by the oculist-7l2m reviewer, 2026-09-14. Interaction regression, not a
measurement defect -- the sweep is unaffected.

oculist-7l2m made #sidebar position:static below 480px so it stops floating
over #match. It then flows after the <article>, and because it is
height:auto with overflow-y:visible it unrolls all 47 effect rows: measured at
320px, the sidebar renders at y=3168-6744, roughly 3100px below the fold and
3100px from the match.

The controls remain visible and reachable by scrolling, and nothing changes at
481px and above, so this did not block oculist-7l2m. But the playground is a
tool a person actually uses, not only a fixture: at narrow width you cannot
fire an effect and watch it, because the button and the match are 3100px
apart.

FIX DIRECTIONS. Source-order the sidebar before <article> below the
breakpoint, or make it sticky or collapsible there. Either keeps the
non-overlap property oculist-7l2m needs while putting the controls back within
reach.

CONSTRAINT: whatever lands must preserve oculist-7l2m's invariant -- #match
must stay genuinely visible and unoccluded at 320 and 360, with its normal
flanking-figure budget. Re-run the oculist-7l2m section's rect probe after any
change here.

First attempt regressed desktop (closed details skips its subtree, no Fire button at 481+); fixed with an open attribute plus a matchMedia sync script. Reviewer PASS on re-review: desktop identical to HEAD at 481/500/900/1280, #match rect byte-identical to 7l2m's after row in both states, wandcast 96/96 4/4 12/12 exit 0, prefire check 38 PASS.

title: effects-playground: nothing asserts the 24.4px sidebar/match clearance at the 500px scenarios, so a prose, font or padding tweak re-breaks 500px silently below the new 480px breakpoint
description:
Raised by the oculist-7l2m reviewer, 2026-09-14.

oculist-7l2m added @media (max-width: 480px) to effects-playground.html so the
sidebar and the fixed 320px right body padding collapse at narrow widths. 480
was chosen because the sweep has no viewport width anywhere in 481-499, and
because 768 would have wrongly rewritten the already-correct 500x400 and
700x1000 grid rows.

THE GAP. At 500x400 with a 48px font, the clearance between the match's right
edge (195.6) and the sidebar's left edge (220) is only 24.4px, and nothing
asserts it. The breakpoint sits at 480, so 500px scenarios are deliberately
outside it. A future change to the prose, the font stack, the body padding or
the sidebar width can eat those 24.4px and silently reintroduce exactly the
defect oculist-7l2m fixed -- this time at a viewport the breakpoint does not
cover, and with no failure to announce it.

FIX DIRECTION. Assert the invariant rather than the layout: a harness check
that the match rect and the sidebar rect do not intersect at every viewport in
SCENARIOS above the breakpoint, failing loudly if they ever do. That is
cheaper and more durable than widening the breakpoint, which would rewrite
rows that are currently correct.

NOT URGENT: the clearance holds today at every scenario width, verified.
close_reason: assertMatchSidebarClearance() now fails the sweep if #match and #sidebar intersect at any grid scenario above the 480px breakpoint. Reviewer independently reproduced the mutation (sidebar 280->310 exits 1 naming 500x400, overlap 6.0x60.0px), reproduced every clearance number (500x400 tightest at 24.4px), and refuted the forced/edge coverage concern by measurement: those rows pin #match full-width so they intersect by construction, and edge hides the sidebar. Cost 20ms per key run. Reviewer PASS.

title: occlusion-sweep: confetti/fireflies/scribble grid-wide maxPixels are non-deterministic run-to-run (undocumented), same class as oculist-519q
description:
Found while running a full before/after sweep for oculist-7l2m (unrelated CSS fix).
Two consecutive `node occlusion-sweep.js confetti fireflies scribble` runs (same
unmodified effects-playground.html) produced different grid-wide numbers even at
WIDE viewports (1280/1440, nowhere near the oculist-7l2m sidebar fix):
confetti maxPixels 1061 vs 1181 (per-scenario e.g. 1280x900/16px: 321 vs different
value; 1280x900/48px: 1061 vs 1181), fireflies maxPixels 2670 vs 2134, scribble
34/96 vs 35/96 clean (480 vs 480 maxPixels but different clean count).
This is the same class of undocumented run-to-run non-determinism oculist-519q
already tracks for rockfallthud/gustswirl/gravity/scramble, just three more keys.
Evidence lives in the oculist-7l2m before/after logs (before-b1.txt vs after-b1.txt,
same pristine code path for the wide-viewport rows) -- not preserved durably beyond
that session; re-run node occlusion-sweep.js confetti fireflies scribble twice to

title: occlusion-sweep: lockon's deferred-mount drain identifies the cleanup callback solely by delay===1500, so swapping two callback bodies would pass the guard and silently replay the cleanup
description:
Raised by the oculist-xh9p reviewer, 2026-09-14, as a residual low-probability risk -- not a defect today.

WHAT. fireEffectAndGetMaxEnd's key==='lockon' drain (occlusion-sweep.js ~1751) asserts fxLockon's three dropped top-level setTimeout delays are exactly [450, 1050, 1500] and throws FATAL otherwise -- verified loud by the reviewer (moving the 1050ms timer to 1100 exits 1 on the first scenario with the full message). But within that assertion, the CLEANUP callback is identified only by its delay being 1500. The bodies are never inspected.

WHY BODIES CANNOT BE INSPECTED TODAY. The playground's own mountRunEls shim wraps every fx* setTimeout callback in an identical closure, so all three fn.toString() values are byte-identical (reviewer-verified). Source-text matching genuinely cannot distinguish mount from cleanup here, which is why the delay-based design was chosen and is the right call for now.

THE RESIDUAL HOLE. If someone swapped the BODIES of fxLockon's 450ms and 1500ms callbacks -- keeping the same three delays -- the guard would pass and the drain would replay the cleanup (els.forEach(el => el.remove())), erasing the artwork before sampling and producing exactly the unfounded CLEAN that oculist-xh9p closed. Low probability: it requires an edit that keeps the delay triple intact while inverting the semantics.

FIX DIRECTIONS. Either have the drain verify its own effect rather than its inputs (assert the .fx element count did not DROP across the replay -- xh9p already measures 4->5, so a cleanup replay would read 4->0 and could throw), or give the playground a way to tag its own cleanup timers so the harness can identify them structurally instead of positionally.

NOT URGENT. The reviewer classed this as 'a follow-up line rather than rework'.
close_reason: lockon drain now asserts the .fx count does not drop across each replayed callback; swapping the 450ms/1500ms bodies exits 1 with FATAL, unmutated sweep unchanged (96/96, 4/4, 12/12). Reviewer PASS.

title: occlusion-sweep: rockfallthud and gustswirl FORCED-LANDING pixel counts are non-deterministic run-to-run (previously undocumented), risking flaky exit-code gating
description:
WIDENED 2026-09-14 (oculist-m1df reviewer): gravity and scramble are non-deterministic too, not just rockfallthud and gustswirl. Measured under identical code, two runs: scramble forced-below-1 438 vs 393, forced-above-2 1479 vs 1304; gravity forced-below-1 40 vs 98, forced-above-1 12 vs 60. All eight gravity/scramble rows in occlusion-sweep-results.md's m1df before/after table are single draws from a noisy distribution; three of them (gravity forced-below-2, scramble forced-above-1, scramble forced-below-2) recorded after>before, which a pure subtraction cannot produce, and are now relabelled as noise in that table.

WIDENED 2026-09-15 (oculist-jxwz): confetti and fireflies confirmed non-deterministic, across 3 draws here and 2 more by an independent reviewer (5 total). scribble tested and found STABLE across 7 total draws (3 here, 4 by the reviewer including 2 in the exact "confetti fireflies scribble" multi-key command shape the original report used) -- contradicting the 34/96-vs-35/96 claim this bead's discovering issue (oculist-jxwz) opened with; that evidence lived in a deleted before/after log and did not reproduce in any of the 7 draws, independently confirmed. The original confetti 1061 / fireflies 2670 readings were NOT outliers -- the reviewer's 5th confetti draw read 1074, nearly matching 1061; the original report under-sampled a wide distribution, it was not wrong. Full data in occlusion-sweep-results.md's "# oculist-jxwz" section.

MECHANISM, cited to effects-playground.html: confetti (fxConfetti, function starts line 1147) and fireflies (fxFireflies, line 1212) both bake Math.random() output (via the file's rand()/pick() helpers, line 365-366) directly into WAAPI keyframe target values during their synchronous call -- confetti at lines 1156 (particle color), 1161-1162 (launch angle/speed), 1165-1167 (end position/rotation/stagger delay); fireflies at lines 1220 (spawn angle/radius), 1222 (target angle), 1226-1227 (flight-path wobble), 1238 (per-firefly stagger delay). Each function's own single setTimeout call (confetti line 1178, fireflies line 1258) is cleanup-only (element removal after the animation ends), so this harness's setTimeout neutralization -- which only drops scheduled callback bodies -- has no way to reach this randomness: it already ran before any timer fires. This is a different mechanism from rockfallthud/gustswirl/gravity/scramble's un-neutralized setInterval-driven redraws; it is randomness baked into a single synchronous animation setup that neutralization was never positioned to catch. scribble (fxScribble, line 1087) contains zero Math.random/rand/pick calls (grep-confirmed on its body) and its own setTimeout (line 1143) is also cleanup-only; no non-determinism reproduced for it across 7 draws (3 here, 4 by an independent reviewer).

VALUES OBSERVED (5 draws for confetti/fireflies grid, 7 for scribble; NOT characterised bounds -- these are the spread a finite number of draws produced, not a min/max a future draw is guaranteed to fall inside): confetti grid-wide maxPixels 1074-1431 across 5 draws (per-scenario floor 207-223 across 5 draws, i.e. every observed scenario was comfortably dirty, hundreds of px away from 0, though the floor itself is not a guaranteed bound); confetti FORCED-LANDING maxPixels 759-827 across 5 draws; confetti EDGE-PLACEMENT maxPixels 1661-1745 across 5 draws. fireflies grid-wide maxPixels 2146-2401 across 5 draws (per-scenario floor 686-890 across 5 draws, same "far from 0, not a guaranteed bound" caveat); fireflies FORCED-LANDING maxPixels 1256-1968 across 5 draws (the widest relative swing of the two); fireflies EDGE-PLACEMENT maxPixels 2553-2711 across 5 draws. scribble: grid 480/480/480/..., clean-count 35/96 every time, FORCED-LANDING 1717 every time, EDGE-PLACEMENT 2565/clean 4/12 every time -- byte-identical across all 7 draws including per-scenario atTime.

VERDICT-FLIP RISK: neither confetti nor fireflies is on NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT (both gate the match-clearance contract in all three blocks, confirmed by their DIRTY/clean-format summary lines, not N/A). Both read 0/96, 0/4, 0/12 clean in every one of the 5 draws -- every scenario dirty by hundreds to low-thousands of pixels. The observed per-scenario floor stayed far from zero across every draw taken (confetti's lowest observed floor across 5 draws: 207px; fireflies': 686px) -- these are observed minima from a finite sample, not a guaranteed lower bound; a future draw reading lower is expected, not a regression, as long as it stays far from 0. Their variance is real but has not come close to flipping a CLEAN/DIRTY verdict at any scenario observed across 5 draws; it reads as cosmetic noise on an already-conclusive DIRTY read, the same "comfortably dirty" shape as rockfallthud/gustswirl. scribble is also gating (not on NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT) and DOES sit near the boundary -- 35/96 grid scenarios read exactly 0 (clean) and the smallest dirty scenarios read 1-3px, right at the edge -- but produced zero flips across all 7 draws taken of it (this bead's 3 plus an independent reviewer's 4), so no live flakiness risk is demonstrated for it; if it is intermittently non-deterministic (as the now-unreproduced-in-7-draws original report claimed), the mechanism cannot be Math.random or an un-neutralized timer since it has neither, and would have to be sub-pixel/anti-aliasing rounding at the DIFF_THRESHOLD=8 boundary on the ellipse stroke edges -- unconfirmed, not reproduced in any draw taken.
close_reason: Seeded Math.random (mulberry32, reseeded per scenario) plus setInterval neutralization make rockfallthud/gustswirl/gravity/scramble/confetti/fireflies byte-identical run to run and order independent; no key or block verdict changed. Reviewer PASS.

title: prefire-scroll-abort-check: removing the pre-fire scroll suppression outright leaves the whole harness green
description:
Found by the oculist-hiox reviewer, 2026-09-14, by mutation while checking that bead's criterion 2.

Deleting the suppression check entirely from trigger() in effects-playground.html -- reducing it to 'if (settled) return;' -- leaves prefire-scroll-abort-check.js exiting 0 with every row green, scenarios A through H.

WHY THAT IS BAD. The suppression exists to stop an effect dissolving itself the instant it fires, via its own ensureVisible scrollIntoView. That is the severe failure in this area: if it breaks, every effect self-destructs on fire. oculist-hiox's own description calls it out as the case that must not regress. It currently has no test that would catch its removal.

WHY THE EXISTING ROWS DO NOT COVER IT. D.1a, D.1b and D.3 fire via the sidebar with #match out of view at both scroll extremes and assert .fx count = 3 after settle. They pass either way: a direct probe on a no-suppression build held .fx at 3 for 2000ms at both extremes, 3 runs each. The fixture never self-dissolves even unprotected, so those rows are not falsifiable for this property.

That makes them the same shape as oculist-e2w, oculist-ey2e and oculist-mcbk: the test passes for a reason other than the one it claims.

FIX DIRECTION. Find or construct a fixture where an unprotected fire genuinely does self-dissolve -- the suppression was written against a real failure, so the conditions that produced it should be reconstructible -- and assert it. Start from what ensureVisible's probe does now after oculist-raj4: a synchronous instant scrollIntoView, read scrollTop, revert. The scroll events that sequence emits are what suppression exists to absorb.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Removing the suppression check from trigger() makes prefire-scroll-abort-check.js exit non-zero.
- The row naming it is green against unmodified HEAD across repeated runs.
- If no fixture can be made to self-dissolve, record WHY in the file -- that would mean the suppression is no longer load-bearing, which is itself worth knowing.
close_reason: Scenario I.1 now catches removal of the pre-fire scroll suppression. Fixture: a spacer sized so Chromium's smooth scroll is still running when ensureVisible's 1200ms MAX_SETTLE_MS fires, so checkSettled times out, finish() mounts, and 1-2 genuine trailing scroll events land after mount -- the exact race trigger()'s suppression absorbs. Reviewer-reproduced: green 3/3 on HEAD, and the mutation (trigger() reduced to 'if (settled) return;') goes red 3/3 with I.1 the only failing row, dropping ~180ms after mount, matching DISSOLVE_DUR. A first version was refuted: its usable band was ~4450-4600 not the documented ~4400-4800, 4800 false-redded on unmodified HEAD, and at 4200 the MUTATED build exited 0 with every row green -- the defect fully back, silently, which is this bead's own failure mode in a new costume. Fixed by a vacuity gate that counts scroll events landing after mount and fails loudly when zero, so the row announces when it has stopped testing anything and the exact spacer constant stops mattering. Also fixed a latent misdiagnosis: the vacuity branch outranked self-dissolve, and since Chromium dispatches scroll before rAF within a frame, a real regression losing its single event to that boundary would have printed 'retune the spacer' instead of naming the suppression. selfDissolved is now checked first and vacuity requires !selfDissolved. Known residual, recorded in the file and filed as a follow-up: ~1-in-12 false red under a load burst inside the 1.2s window (loud, self-announcing, safe direction). effects-playground.html untouched.

title: occlusion-sweep FORCED-LANDING counts pixels the fixed #sidebar already occludes, so any effect painting there reads dirty regardless of the match
description:
Generalised from oculist-x9fo's characterisation, 2026-09-13. x9fo exempts edgeticks from the symptom; this bead is about the cause, which is not specific to edgeticks.

FORCED-LANDING's forced-below scenarios (occlusion-sweep.js:651,661,671,681) pin #match to width:100vw, left:0. The playground's #sidebar is position:fixed, right:0, width:280px, z-index:100, so at a 500px viewport it covers x=220..500 of that match rect. #match has z-index auto.

The sweep diffs baseline against post-effect over the match rect. Pixels inside the sidebar band were never showing #match at baseline, so a change there cannot be the effect occluding the match. But the diff counts them anyway: measured for edgeticks, 112px at x=243-256 y=0-13, every pixel baseline rgb(28,28,34) which is the sidebar's own #1c1c22, 0 percent glyph ink against computed mark#match color rgb(0,0,0). elementsFromPoint(250,6) returns [sidebar, match, BODY, HTML].

Any effect whose artwork reaches into that band gets the same false dirty. edgeticks is simply the one that does today.

PROPER FIX DIRECTION: subtract from the diff region the area that is already occluded at baseline (the sidebar's rect, or more generally anything painting above #match at baseline), so FORCED-LANDING measures occlusion of the match's VISIBLE area. That is strictly more correct than per-key exemptions.

WEIGH CAREFULLY BEFORE DOING IT. This changes the measurement semantics for every key, so it can turn other reds green. It needs its own review and a before/after of every key's numbers, not a drive-by change. That blast radius is exactly why x9fo took the narrow exemption instead.

If this lands, revisit whether x9fo's FORCED_LANDING_SIDEBAR_EXEMPT entry can be deleted.

DONE-CRITERIA
- FORCED-LANDING no longer counts baseline-occluded pixels.
- Every key's before/after numbers are recorded, and each change is explained.
- A mutation check proves a genuine match-occlusion in the forced block still reds the run.
close_reason: FORCED-LANDING now subtracts the baseline-occluded region (generic DOM walk, not #sidebar-keyed), so it measures occlusion of the match's VISIBLE area. Reviewer-verified: -12040 reconciles to real geometry (280x43), three-armed mutation test reds correctly outside the band, excluded union confined to the sidebar column, grid/EDGE byte-identical. 47-key/197-row before/after recorded in occlusion-sweep-results.md. Scoped to FORCED-LANDING; the same defect stays live at 320/360px grid viewports -- filed as oculist-7l2m.

title: fxEdgeticks FORCED-LANDING is red: the vertical ticks paint 112px onto a match pinned to 100vw
description:
Split out while closing oculist-dxpq, 2026-09-13. This defect predates dxpq and was deliberately out of its scope. It had no bead of its own, which caused two agents in a row to cite oculist-1ta.8 for it -- that is a CLOSED fxBatflight mist bug and has nothing to do with edgeticks. Cite THIS bead instead.

STATE. node occlusion-sweep.js edgeticks in artifacts/prototypes/:
  SUMMARY edgeticks FORCED-LANDING: 2/4 scenarios clean, 2 dirty, maxPixels=112 (112/112/0/0)
The run exits 1 on this block alone. The 96-grid is 96/96 clean and EDGE-PLACEMENT is 8/8 clean, both at maxPixels=0, so this is the only remaining red.

HISTORY OF THE NUMBER. Before oculist-dxpq it was 0/4 clean, maxPixels=334, per-scenario 334/334/222/222. dxpq clipped the two HORIZONTAL ticks against the match rect, which incidentally removed their contribution: 222 of forced-below's 334, and all of forced-above's 222. What survives is the VERTICAL pair, specs[0] and specs[1].

THE GEOMETRY. occlusion-sweep.js's forced-below/above scenarios (:651,661,671,681) pin #match to width:100vw; left:0. A match that spans the whole viewport leaves the vertical ticks nowhere to stand that is not on top of it. This is the same shape as the horizontal case dxpq fixed, so the same remedy is the obvious first thing to try: wrap specs[0]/specs[1] in an evenodd keyhole clip against the match rect, with dissolveHardCut set, exactly as dxpq's tickWrap and fxWandCast's backWrap do.

BEFORE FIXING, SETTLE THE DESIGN QUESTION dxpq left open. Clipping the vertical ticks against a viewport-wide match hides them outright, so the effect renders as nothing at all in that layout. fxWandCast accepted that trade for its back arc and dxpq accepted it for the horizontal pair, but the horizontal pair going missing still leaves a visible effect; the vertical pair going missing may not. The honest alternatives are to clip anyway and accept an invisible effect at that layout, or to decide the forced-landing scenarios are not a layout fxEdgeticks is held to and move the key onto the appropriate exemption, the way oculist-1la5 did for horseman.

CHECK FIRST whether any of the 112 is glyph ink. That is what decided dxpq: its 14px looked like harmless background until the review found one pixel at ~42% ink coverage. Use mark#match's COMPUTED colour rgb(0,0,0) (UA mark { color: MarkText }), not the body's #2a2a2e -- dxpq's first attempt got this wrong.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The 112px is characterised: which tick, which forced scenario, and whether any is glyph ink, measured against the computed glyph colour.
- The design question above is answered in the source, not just here.
- Either FORCED-LANDING reaches 4/4 clean, or edgeticks is exempted from it with the reasoning recorded where the exemption is declared.
- EDGE-PLACEMENT stays 8/8 clean and the 96-grid stays 96/96 clean.
- The harness is chromium-only (occlusion-sweep.js:1868). Do not claim cross-engine coverage.
close_reason: Exempt rather than clip, row-scoped to forced-below only. Reviewer PASS on the row-scoping and the mutation test the bead previously failed: forced-above made dirty exits 1 with those rows DIRTY while forced-below stays n/a, and an expect mismatch on forced-above also exits 1. The reviewer's one finding (a clearanceExempt key's FINAL recap reporting dirty=0 beside maxPixels=30100) was fixed and verified by me directly: horseman [forced] reads dirty=4 again, byte-identical to HEAD. edgeticks exits 0, 96-grid 96/96 clean, EDGE-PLACEMENT 8/8 clean. Outer repo commit e46b324, superseding the wip 7c72a1f. Scoping nits filed as oculist-nq3w.

comments.text:

CHARACTERISATION IS DONE AND SOLID, do not redo it. That colour is the fixed #sidebar's own background (position:fixed, right:0, width:280px, z-index:100), whose left edge is x=220 at a 500px viewport; the dirty region x=243-256 y=0-13 lies entirely inside it. elementsFromPoint(250,6) returns [sidebar, match, BODY, HTML].
