THE HOLE. mount() reads the module-level currentRunEls, not a per-run closure. An old run's pending setTimeout therefore calls the same global mount(), which by then sees the NEW run's array with dissolved === false, and attaches the stale nodes anyway.

MEASURED. Fire matchstrike, scroll at 120ms, fire scanline at 200ms. At 520ms the DOM holds scanline's 2 nodes at the correct rect PLUS matchstrike's 8 deferred nodes at the pre-scroll rect: 40x32@452,334, 64x30@458,335, and 6 embers.

FIX DIRECTION. The array flag is the wrong carrier. mount() needs real run identity: capture the run's own array (or a run token) at rect() time and have deferred mounts check the run they belong to, not whatever run is current when they fire.

ALSO. The comment at effects-playground.html:186-198 over-claims, describing the guard as per-run without the 'while that run is still current' qualifier. Correct it with the fix.

NIT, same area. effects-playground.html:181 sets currentRunEls.dissolved = false, which is dead: line 180 already assigns a fresh array. Left in place rather than shipped unreviewed; delete it here.

DONE-CRITERIA

- Firing a second effect after a mid-flight scroll leaves NO node from the first run at the pre-scroll rect.
- A new effect fired after a dissolve still mounts normally at the correct rect (the ucs reviewer confirmed this does not currently regress; keep it that way).
- The :186-198 comment matches what the guard actually promises.
- The dead assignment at :181 is gone.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS on the second review. The last path where a node lands at a stale rect is closed. ROOT CAUSE: clearFx() does NOT cancel pending setTimeouts, so a superseded run's timers always survive and fire later, and mount() read the module-level currentRunEls rather than a per-run closure, so those late callbacks saw the NEW run's array with dissolved false and attached anyway. FIX, with no fx* function edited: the global setTimeout is shadowed inside the IIFE by a hoisted function declaration, so all 45 effects pick it up automatically. At schedule time it captures scheduledEls = mountRunEls || currentRunEls, which makes identity flow through nested timer chains rather than adopting whatever run is current when the outer callback fires; when the callback runs it restores mountRunEls for that callback's duration via try/finally. mount() then refuses when owner !== currentRunEls (new, a later run has replaced this one) or owner.dissolved (the existing ucs guard). rect() resets mountRunEls to null on a new run, which is load-bearing: without it an effect fired via the sidebar's ensureVisible() setTimeout(finish, 600) path would inherit a stale identity and refuse its own initial synchronous mounts. VERIFIED BY THE REVIEWER, not taken on trust. Bead scenario reproduced exactly: pre-fix 10 .fx nodes at t=520ms with 8 stale at the pre-scroll rect (40x32@450,334, 64x30@458,335, 6 embers); post-fix exactly 2, both at the post-scroll rect, 0 stale. The suppression risk, which would have been worse than the bug, was hunted and is clean: rapid re-fire 50ms apart counting only run 2's mounts gives matchstrike 10, comet 7, stamp 7, inkbloom 8, identical to each effect's clean single-fire baseline; re-fire after a dissolve puts all 10 nodes at the post-scroll rect and 0 at the pre-scroll one; the no-scroll path across all 45 effects with seeded Math.random shows 0 diffs and 0 page errors. A 45-effect supersede sweep found 14 effects whose stale deferred mounts are now refused and 0 effects mounting more than before. clearTimeout pairing verified empirically intact (the shadow returns the native id). FAILED THE FIRST REVIEW on two documentation-shaped defects, both fixed: the new harness asserted only that stale nodes were absent, so neutering mount() entirely still printed PASS, while its docstring claimed it checked scanline's nodes were present at the correct rect; and the comment enumerated the deferred-mount set as six effects including fxScanline and fxEmberignite, which mount synchronously and never had the defect. The harness now asserts exactly 2 scanline nodes at the post-scroll rect and was proven three ways by the reviewer: neutered mount FAILS with found 0, guard removed FAILS with 8 stale, unmutated PASSES. The enumeration is now the measured 14, independently re-derived by the reviewer with their own brace-matching scan and spot-checked by hand, and framed as a snapshot with the re-verification procedure named rather than as a contract. Full suite 321/321; the ucs and ak5 harnesses both still pass. Residual latent hazards filed as oculist-q9r: the shadow drops trailing args (0 of 82 call sites affected today), setInterval is unshadowed, and the harness docstring mislabels which guard clause its mutation falsifies.

title: instant_scroll stale-draw quiet window is anchored to m1's draw, not to the orphan timer's arm time
description:
Measured by the oculist-pzk reviewer, 2026-09-06, while passing that bead. Not a defect today; a detector that is weaker than it looks.

WHAT THE TEST DOES. instant_scroll_close_reopen_no_stale_draw stretches the isolated world's setTimeout so mfar's 50ms orphaned draw timer fires at 4000ms instead, which makes __ocDestroy deterministically win the race the test is about. waitForRedrawCountToSettle() then uses a 4600ms quiet window, long enough that an un-cancelled orphan draw would land inside it and be observed. That is verified: with clearActiveImmediateDrawTimer() removed the test fails 2 !== 1, and the quiet window visibly restarts (clean 5.09s vs mutant 9.1-9.4s).

THE GAP. The quiet window is anchored to __ocRedrawAt, i.e. m1's own draw. The orphan fires at arm_time + 4000, and arm_time sits two CDP round trips AFTER m1's draw. So the 600ms of headroom between 4000 and 4600 is really a margin against CDP overhead, not a structural guarantee that the window still covers the orphan.

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT. It fails safe on the passing path: a slow box only makes the clean test wait longer. The risk is a weaker detector, not a flaky test. The margin held 7 of 7 runs including under full-suite load at concurrency 4.

FIX DIRECTION. Record the orphan's arm time inside the setTimeout patch (around instant_scroll_close_reopen_no_stale_draw.test.js:250) and anchor the quiet window on that instead of on m1's draw. Then the coverage is structural and the 600ms guess disappears.

DONE-CRITERIA

- The quiet window's deadline is derived from the orphan timer's own arm time.
- The mutation check still fails: removing clearActiveImmediateDrawTimer() from __ocDestroy produces 2 !== 1.
- No increase in the clean-path wall clock beyond what the 4000ms stretch already costs.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. The deadline is now anchored on the orphan timer's own arm time, which is what the bead asked for, and the 600ms CDP-overhead margin is gone. Mechanism: the isolated content-script world shares only the DOM with the main world, so the fix follows the same route the existing __ocRedrawCount counter already uses. When the patched setTimeout intercepts the delay===50 call, it appends an invisible marker span; armRedrawCounter()'s MutationObserver sees it and records __ocOrphanArmedAt. The deadline becomes armedAt + 4000 + 500. Verified by instrumentation that the anchor really is the arm and not m1's draw: on the mutant the orphan draw was observed at armedAt + 4004.2, +4004.7 and +4003.2ms. THE DETECTOR CHANGED CHARACTER and the reviewer checked it on that basis. The old design was a quiet window that RESTARTED when the orphan landed, which is what proved it observed rather than outlasted; the new one waits to an absolute deadline, which is outlasting by construction. It is still sound, and the three links were verified: armedAt is recorded in an observer callback one microtask AFTER the append, so the deadline is conservative; the orphan's .oc-beacon append and the counter increment land in the same task checkpoint, measured 2.0 to 4.7ms of lag past the stretch; and waitForFunction resolves at the deadline while the count is read in a LATER round trip, so the count can only have grown. No window exists where the orphan fired but the count had not crossed the boundary before the read. FIRE_JITTER_MS of 500 was ruled legitimate rather than a re-smuggled sleep: the 600ms it replaced had to absorb four CDP round trips plus a waitForSelector and an inputValue read, all process-external and load-sensitive, while the 500ms absorbs one in-page timer dispatch and one observer hop, measured at under 1 percent of the budget. Filed as oculist-4z3 anyway, with the structural alternative the reviewer identified. Mutation verified independently both directions: removing clearActiveImmediateDrawTimer() gives a real AssertionError 2 !== 1 in 4 of 4 solo runs and 6 of 6 under concurrency 4, never a Playwright timeout and never the never-arms guard. The never-arms guard was proven to fire by making the patch intercept a delay that never occurs: a clear error, not a hang and not a silent pass. Assertions byte-identical to HEAD. Clean path did not regress, 5.72 to 6.06s against HEAD's 5.82 to 5.87s, slightly faster since 4500 from the arm lands earlier than 4600 from m1's draw. Reviewer's counts: 12 concurrency iterations at 5 files each, 60 executions, zero failures; full suite 321/321. One new latent coupling filed as oculist-jz0: the marker is not an oculist node, so the extension's own domObserver arms a 350ms rescan against it, currently disarmed in time with about 9x headroom.

title: Pack-notice cap safety rests on an undocumented, untested invariant
description:
Established by the oculist-2mx review, 2026-09-06, which closed that bead as not-a-bug. This is the fragility that made it not-a-bug, written down so it is not broken by accident.

WHY THE STALE MEASUREMENT IS SAFE TODAY. maybeShowPackDiscoveryNotice() has exactly one call site, the build branch (content.js:8067), where the count element is empty and sitting on its 58px min-width floor. Every other bar child is fixed-px and flex-shrink:0, and the bar is nowrap, so min-content equals max-content. The notice is therefore measured while the host is at its NARROWEST, which is the notice's TALLEST. The host width only grows from there, so the notice can only unwrap, so packNoticeChromePx is always an UPPER bound. The cap over-subtracts and never under-subtracts, and the panel cannot overflow.

WHAT BREAKS IT. Two changes flip that upper bound into an under-estimate and produce real overflow:
1. Localizing the i18n dict, particularly 'of' and 'noMatch'. The count is min-width 58px plus nowrap, so it is content-sized, not fixed. The reviewer measured the host growing 480 to 486.03px in plain English just by navigating to '999 of 999'. With a plausible German pair the notice height moved 46.594 to 31.188 after measurement, with no resize at all, purely from typing in the find box.
2. Moving the maybeShowPackDiscoveryNotice() call out of the build branch, so the notice can first appear while a search is already active and the bar is already wide.

CORRECTING TWO THINGS ON THE RECORD, both repeated in earlier beads and wrong:
- The bar is NOT a row of fixed-px controls. .oc-count is min-width plus nowrap, i.e. content-sized.
- The English notice does NOT fit on one line. At 12px/1.4 one line is 31.19px, two is 46.59px. The shipped 46.594px measurement IS two lines at the natural 480px host; it only unwraps above about 645px.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A comment at the packNoticeChromePx declaration (around content.js:1149-1157) states the invariant: measured at minimum bar width, therefore an upper bound, therefore safe.
- A test fails if the notice is ever measured while the bar is wider than its floor.
- No re-measurement machinery added. The invariant is the fix; the guard just keeps it true.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. No behaviour changed; oculist-2mx already adjudicated this not-a-bug, and the deliverable is the written-down invariant plus a guard. Comment at the packNoticeChromePx declaration (content.js:1159-1176) and one test in pack_discovery_notice.test.js. Invariant confirmed to still hold exactly as described: the single call site in window.__ocToggle()'s build branch fires before any search, with .oc-count on its 58px floor, so the bar is at its narrowest and the notice at its tallest, making packNoticeChromePx an upper bound. Guard mechanism: after the notice appears, assert .oc-count is still empty and its rendered width equals its computed min-width within 1px. Indirect by necessity, and the reviewer verified the two things that make it sound. First, the synchronicity argument is true: the build branch is a plain synchronous run with no await, rAF or microtask boundary between the getBoundingClientRect() and the notice becoming visible, and Playwright is out-of-process so waitForSelector cannot resolve mid-task; nothing in that window can shrink the count, so the only error direction is a spurious failure, never a spurious pass. Second, the isolated-world claim is correct, verified by probe: a page.addInitScript() patch of Element.prototype.getBoundingClientRect counted 0 calls, so a main-world hook genuinely cannot reach the content script. The reviewer noted a direct hook was still reachable another way, since createPackedFixtureExtension() already rewrites the fixture's content.js; worth knowing but not a gap. Both documented break scenarios were mutation-tested, which the implementer had only done for one. Scenario 2, the dangerous state it actually produces, is cleanly detected: 7 pass and the guard is the ONLY failure. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD, both found by the reviewer and both now fixed in the comment. (a) .oc-count IS flex-shrink:0 like every other bar child; what sets it apart is that it is content-sized (min-width plus nowrap), not its shrink behaviour. (b) The bead's own text is internally inconsistent about scenario 1: localizing 'of'/'noMatch' does NOT invert the bound. A longer count widens the bar, which unwraps the notice SHORTER (the bead's own 46.594 to 31.188 numbers), so the stale value remains an upper bound and merely becomes more conservative. Only moving the call site inverts it, by recording a short unwrapped notice that then wraps taller once the search is cleared and the bar returns to its floor. The comment now says this, and the guard covers exactly that case. Full suite 321/321.

title: Deferred-mount playground effects get only partial scroll-dissolve coverage
description:
Measured by the oculist-uc1 reviewer, 2026-09-06. A STRICT IMPROVEMENT on what came before, not a regression - these effects had zero coverage until uc1. Filed because 'every effect inherits the dissolve' is only partly true, and the gap should be written down rather than assumed away.

oculist-uc1 moved the arming into rect() so every effect inherits the scroll dissolve. armScrollDissolve's onScroll sets settled = true and removes its listener when it fires. Anything an effect mounts AFTER that point is therefore never dissolved, and lands at the stale rect the dissolve was meant to prevent.

MEASURED: scrolling 120ms into matchstrike dissolved the 2 nodes that were live, and the effect then mounted 8 more at the stale position. Same shape for comet.

AFFECTED, the effects that mount inside a later setTimeout: fxMatchstrike, fxComet, fxStamp, fxInkbloom, fxScanline, fxEmberignite.

NOT A LEAK: they self-clean at the effect's own timeout, so nothing accumulates. The symptom is purely visual, a few nodes appearing at the wrong place after a scroll.

FIX DIRECTION: rather than un-setting settled, the cheaper shape is probably for mount() to check whether the current run has already dissolved and refuse to mount, or mount hidden. That keeps one decision point instead of teaching six effects to check.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Scrolling mid-flight through any of the six named effects leaves no node at a stale position.
- The five effects verified in uc1 still dissolve and still leave no scroll listener behind.
- No effect mounts nodes after its own run has been dissolved.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. One decision point, as the bead steered: armScrollDissolve's onScroll sets dissolved on the run's OWN currentRunEls array object, and mount() early-returns when it sees that flag. No effect function was touched. Run identity works because rect() hands out a fresh array per run and runEffect() is synchronous (clearFx(); eff.run(rect())), so the flag self-resets and cannot leak between runs. Measured by the reviewer, max .fx count after a mid-flight scroll, pre to post: matchstrike 8 to 0, stamp 7 to 1, comet 6 plus a late burst to 0 late, inkbloom 6 to 1 to 0, scanline 2 to 2, emberignite 5 to 5. Every post-fix residual is at or below the mid-flight count, i.e. original nodes fading through the 240ms dissolve, never a new mount. Falsifiability confirmed independently in both directions on isolated copies: pre-fix FAIL with 8 nodes mounted after the dissolve, post-fix PASS with 0. The uc1 five (batflight, arrowshot, reanimate, vineswing, foottap) still dissolve to 0 with a scroll-listener delta of 0; still 1 ambient listener after all 11 effects complete and after 30 rapid matchstrike re-fires. No-scroll path is byte-identical in behaviour, peak and final .fx counts unchanged for all 11 effects; the guard is unreachable without a scroll. A 45-effect sweep with a mid-flight scroll produced zero page errors and zero residual nodes. Two corrections to the bead's own list: fxScanline AND fxEmberignite both mount everything synchronously and never had this defect, so the real deferred-mount set is matchstrike, comet, stamp, inkbloom only. The adversarial overlapping-run case was checked explicitly: the feared 'effects stop working after a scroll' regression does NOT exist, a new effect fired after a dissolve mounts normally at the correct rect. The mirror case does remain and is unchanged by this diff, filed as a follow-up. Occlusion dirtiness on five of the six is pre-existing, identical numbers at HEAD and after; filed separately. Full suite 320/320.

title: effects-playground: 6 effects mutate raw page state (body transform/mark color/article innerHTML) outside the mount()/rect() dissolve foundation
description:
Found while implementing oculist-uc1 (foundation-level scroll-dissolve for effects-playground.html, via rect()/mount()).

Every fx* function calls mount() at least once, so every effect gets at least partial scroll-dissolve coverage from the uc1 fix. But 6 of the 45 fx* functions ALSO mutate real page state outside any .fx-classed, mount()-tracked overlay element, via addRestorer()'s revert-on-cleanup mechanism -- that state is NOT tracked by currentRunEls and does not dissolve/revert early on scroll:

- fxZoompunch: document.body.animate() scale zoom, transformOrigin computed once at fire time (document-space Y already scroll-corrected via + window.scrollY, so this specific one is largely self-immune to vertical scroll already).
- fxDepthdive: document.body.animate() perspective rotateX/rotateY tilt, same transformOrigin pattern as fxZoompunch.
- fxStamp: a brief (130ms) document.body.animate() shake, self-clears almost immediately regardless of scroll.
- fxLetterwave: sets #match's own text color to transparent while its letter-span overlay plays; not position-dependent, so scroll doesn't make this specific mutation "stale" the way a position:fixed rect does.
- fxScramble: same #match color-hide pattern as fxLetterwave.
- fxShockwave: wraps words of the host <article> in place and animates them via transform (real in-flow content, not position:fixed) -- article.innerHTML is swapped back via addRestorer. Because the wrapped words are normal in-flow content, they scroll together with the match, so their relative geometry (and thus the shockwave's per-word direction/magnitude, computed once from cx/cy) is actually unaffected by a pure vertical scroll -- this one looks structurally scroll-resistant already, not just uncovered.

None of these looked like the same "pinned to a stale viewport rect" bug oculist-uc1 targets -- each either self-corrects within a short fixed timeout regardless of scroll, or (letterwave/scramble/shockwave) isn't position:fixed/viewport-anchored in the first place. Verified by inspection only, not by a dedicated scroll test for each of the 6.

Filed as a follow-up rather than fixed in oculist-uc1 because Chris's decision for that bead was scoped to "the shared baseStyle()/rect() foundation," and these 6 effects' extra page-mutation pieces sit outside that foundation by construction (they don't go through baseStyle()/mount() at all for this part).

Suggested next step: someone should make the call on whether any of these 6 actually need scroll-awareness (my read is probably not, given the self-correcting/scroll-resistant reasoning above), or whether it's just worth a comment in each function saying so explicitly so a future reader doesn't have to re-derive it.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. The call was made by measurement rather than inspection, which is what this bead asked for, and the answer is that NONE of the six needed a fix. The deliverable is six one-line comments naming why each is scroll-safe, plus raw-state-scroll-dissolve-check.js as the harness that establishes it. Measured 12/12 PASS, each effect on both a control and a scrolled-mid-flight arm on a fresh page.reload(), plus 3/3 REFUSED. The harness was proven falsifiable 3 of 3 on isolated copies, one mutation per family: deleting restore() from fxZoompunch's 900ms cleanup FAILS both arms with a stranded transform-origin; making fxLetterwave's colour restore conditional on dissolved FAILS ONLY the scrolled arm while the control passes, which is the strongest evidence that the scroll arm is live rather than vacuous; dropping article.innerHTML from fxShockwave's restorer FAILS both. The highest-value question, whether the just-landed oculist-ucs mount() refusal can orphan an addRestorer cleanup, is answered NO with a non-vacuous reproduction: refusal genuinely engages (control mounts 1/1/7 nodes for zoompunch/depthdive/stamp, 0 after a scroll at 60ms) and in that same refused run the body transform still reverts to none, with 0 .fx and 0 body animations. Mechanism confirmed in source: restorers are drained only by each effect's own unconditional setTimeout and by clearFx(); armScrollDissolve's onScroll sets dissolved and calls dissolveEffect, and never touches restorers. All six comments verified accurate against the code, each naming a concrete mechanism (document-space origin with + scrollY, position-independent colour hide, in-flow words, self-clearing timeout) rather than over-claiming the way the ucs comment did. Diff is 24 insertions and 0 deletions, comment-only, six function bodies untouched, no-scroll path untouched. Full suite 320/320. Two artifacts noted and filed rather than fixed: the empty style attribute (oculist-g46, confirmed benign and correctly P4, though the reviewer found it is non-deterministic for zoompunch/depthdive and partly observation-induced) and fxStamp's body shake continuing after a dissolve.

title: vision_profile_survives_ungoverned_toggle asserts without waiting, so it flakes independently of load
description:
Isolated during the oculist-8qq investigation, 2026-09-06. This is the ONE flaky file in that bead's set that does not fit the contention story, which is why it is worth separating out.

Every other failure oculist-8qq measured was the same shape: a waitForCondition or waitForSelector exhausting the fixed 5000ms POLL_TIMEOUT under four-way browser scheduling load. Those thin out as concurrency drops.

This file is different. Its failure is a bare assertion with no wait behind it at all, and the test's own comment documents that no-wait as an intentional assumption. That matches the separate data point recorded earlier in oculist-8qq: it flaked once when run entirely alone, then passed four times. A file that flakes in isolation is not being starved by its neighbours; it is asserting on state that is not guaranteed to have settled yet.

WHY IT MATTERS SEPARATELY: as long as this file sits in the flaky set, it makes the concurrency numbers look worse than they are and muddies the decision on the systemic tradeoff. Fixing it is narrow and does not depend on that decision.

FIRST STEP: read the comment that documents the no-wait assumption and find out whether it was ever true. The fix is probably to await the state transition the assertion depends on rather than to add a sleep.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The assertion waits for the condition it depends on rather than assuming it has already happened.
- The file passes repeatedly in isolation, and the no-wait comment is either justified by evidence or removed.
- No new sleep. A fixed delay would convert this into the same POLL_TIMEOUT-shaped fragility as the rest of the set.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS on the second attempt. Root cause: popup.js attaches its change listeners only after an await on chrome.storage.sync, while openPopup waited only for the control to EXIST, which is true from HTML parse time. A change event driven at an unwired control is dropped permanently, so the assertion read the old value. The first attempt polled each assertion's outcome and was failed: since the event was dropped, the outcome never arrives, so it only converted an instant wrong-value failure into a 10s timeout. Measured A/B by the reviewer, 18 runs per arm: outcome polling 7 pass, readiness wait 18 pass. The fix waits once for popup readiness in openPopup, via a new shared waitForPopupReady helper keyed on the status text leaving its Checking placeholder. Verified both directions: HEAD fails 4 of 12 six-way concurrent runs, all wrong-value; the fix passes 24 of 24 concurrent and 24 of 24 in isolation. Assertions restored byte-identical to HEAD, so nothing was loosened. Full suite 320/320. The reviewer caught the helper comment overclaiming that every listener sits above the readiness point, which is false for the site toggle on the early-return paths; corrected before commit.

title: __ocDestroy leaves the auto-scroll listeners attached on a page that never stops scrolling
description:
Found by the reviewer on oculist-z8n, 2026-09-06. Bounded and not user-visible; filed so it is not rediscovered.

oculist-z8n replaced the flat 800ms auto-scroll suppression with a scrollend listener plus a scroll listener that re-arms a 300ms grace timer. clearAutoScrollFlag removes both, and it runs on scrollend or when scroll events stop.

__ocDestroy() does not clear autoScrollTimer. It did not clear the old 800ms timer either, so this is not a regression - but the shape changed. Before, the stranded thing was a single timer that fired once. Now, on a page that scrolls CONTINUOUSLY and forever (an infinite auto-scroller, a stuck momentum scroll), the scroll listener keeps re-arming the grace timer, so one listener and one timer stay attached after teardown.

WHY IT IS BOUNDED: a reopen calls triggerAutoScrollFlag, which removes both listeners by reference before re-adding, so they do not accumulate. The cost is one idle listener, not a growing set.

FIX DIRECTION: have __ocDestroy call clearAutoScrollFlag, which already both clears the timer and removes both listeners. Check the other teardown paths take it too.

DONE-CRITERIA
- After __ocDestroy on a continuously scrolling page, no auto-scroll scroll/scrollend listener remains and no timer is pending.
- The oculist-z8n tests in test/beacon_survives_long_smooth_scroll.test.js still pass, including the reverted-fix red check.
- node --test passes in full.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. One line in __ocDestroy: clearAutoScrollFlag(), which already clears the timer and removes both listeners. __ocDestroy is the single teardown funnel (three call sites), so the bead's 'check other teardown paths' is satisfied by construction. New test drives continuous re-targeted smooth scrolls so native scrollend never fires, then asserts the timer is null after destroy; reviewer re-proved it red 4 of 4 on revert. The reviewer also corrected the implementer's own account of the assertion: it asserts null, not an advancing timer id, so the global-id concern does not apply. The added __ocTest getter is one member on a namespace that already ships with about 66 of them, unconditionally, and worklist_storage.test.js already asserts it is invisible from the main world; the reviewer confirmed that isolation in a real browser. z8n's reproduction test verified still red when the z8n fix is reverted, so it was not blunted. Residual test weaknesses filed.

title: beacon_survives_long_smooth_scroll timing literals ignore TIMEOUT_SCALE
description:
Raised by the reviewer on oculist-z8n, 2026-09-06. Not a defect today - it held over six runs, three of them under full-suite contention - but it is the likeliest future flake in that file.

test/beacon_survives_long_smooth_scroll.test.js uses two hardcoded timing literals that do NOT respond to OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE the way the rest of the suite does:
- test 1 asserts the beacon is still alive at appearedAt + 1900, against a getBeaconDuration of 2100. Measured headroom after the 30ms poll interval and two page.evaluate round-trips is only ~140-170ms.
- test 2 waits 600ms for the user-scroll fade.

DO NOT just multiply both by TIMEOUT_SCALE. The two ends do not scale the same way and that is the trap:
- The 600ms window is a timeout and should grow on a slow machine.
- The 1900ms is a deadline sitting INSIDE a 2100ms product lifetime that is real wall-clock and does not grow. Scaling it up pushes the assertion past the beacon's own expiry and turns a passing test red for the wrong reason.

The real exposure in test 1 is the round-trip cost eating the 140ms of headroom, not the 1900 itself. So the fix is more likely to be reducing measurement overhead, or asserting on a recorded appearance timestamp rather than on wall clock at assert time, than scaling a constant.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Both tests still pass at OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE=1 and at a raised scale.
- Test 1 still goes red when the oculist-z8n fix is reverted - re-check that, since it is the reproduction case and must not be blunted.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. The two literals were treated on their own terms, which was the bead's whole point: the 1900ms deadline sits inside a real-wall-clock 2100ms product lifetime and was NOT scaled, and the 600ms fade timeout was scaled by TIMEOUT_SCALE. The deadline's real exposure, round-trip overhead eating its ~140ms of headroom, was removed by collapsing a 30ms Node-side poll plus a separate aliveness evaluate into one in-page waitForFunction that snapshots aliveness at the same tick it crosses the deadline. Reviewer traced the predicate for all three cases (alive, already faded, never drawn) and confirmed a dead beacon still yields a clean AssertionError rather than a Playwright timeout, then proved it: reverting the z8n fix turns test 1 red as a real assertion in 2863ms. Both scales pass (1 and 3). git diff on extension is empty, so the test-only constraint held.

title: Foot Tap and Point: REACH_INWARD mixes viewBox units with px, so GAP 12 delivers ~23px
description:
Found at the second review of oculist-1ta.5. In fxFootTap (artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html, outer repo) REACH_INWARD (~line 5473) is computed in viewBox units but consumed as px (~5478, ~5480) without the scale factor (0.903 at font 24). It over-reserves about 9px, so the stated GAP of 12 yields an actual fingertip approach of 23.5px at the held point and 20.9px at overshoot. Safe direction (never under-reserves), but the point stops further from the word than intended, which costs anchor legibility.

Fix: multiply REACH_INWARD by scale before adding it to the placement, then re-run node occlusion-sweep.js foottap (must stay 96/96 clean) and re-measure the held-point fingertip gap at 900x700/f24 (target 12-14px).

Also: no screenshot captures the mirrored left-side landing; add one by forcing a right-edge match in a throwaway page.
close_reason:
REACH_INWARD and REACH_OUTWARD are both scaled now; the latter is the same unit bug in the same sideRight.fits/sideLeft.fits chain, and the reviewer confirmed it in scope rather than creep, with side selection identical across the full 8x12 grid (96 right before, 96 right after, zero flips).

MEASURED, reviewer reproducing it independently with animations paused and seeked in 5ms steps: full extension went 20.25px to 13.97px, held pose 23.51px to 17.23px. No unscaled term remains: the observed shift matches the predicted (1-scale) correction to within 0.01px, and the whole VB-to-px chain was walked (sideRight.x, .fits, sideLeft, figLeft/figTop, fpWorldX/fpWorldY, MOTION_*), with LEG_LIFT correctly staying unscaled since it is an in-SVG translate.

CRITERION 3 IS NOT LITERALLY MET AND THAT IS ACCEPTED. The 12-14px target was written before anyone had measured the overshoot/held distinction. GAP binds at FULL EXTENSION, per the code's own comment and per the geometry: REACH_INWARD is dimensioned off minX, sampled with the overshoot arm length at every angle, so the floor is GAP + 2*scale = 13.81px and the real overshoot lands at 13.97px, inside target. The held pose then retracts 3.82 viewBox units by design (ARM_PEAK 99 to ARM_SWEEP 90, scaleX 1.1 to 1.0), which is 3.45px, giving 17.24px. That is arithmetic, not a residual bug. Against the bead's actual complaint, that the point stopped too far from the word and cost anchor legibility, this is a 27% improvement. The implementer reported the miss rather than tuning the constant to fit, which was the right call.

Criterion 2 is a real safety check here and it holds: over-reserving was the safe direction, so scaling down moves the finger toward the word. foottap stays 96/96 clean with maxPixels=0, and that number is trustworthy rather than a lower bound, because fxFootTap's two mount() calls are both synchronous and its only setTimeout is the final element removal, so oculist-e2w does not apply. Gates verified: fixed-position pointer-events-none nodes, no reads or writes of #match or document.body, WAAPI only, and cleanupAndAssert clean in all 96 scenarios. Both screenshots reviewed, including the forced mirrored-left landing.

title: Reanimation Jolt forearms are invisible at natural size
description:
Found at review of oculist-1ta.3. In fxReanimate (artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html, outer repo) the two stiff forearms are COAT fill on a COAT body, so at 900x700/font 24 only the two pale fist circles register and the arms themselves vanish. The bust still reads as a person (squared head, brow band, eyes, shoulders), but the stiff-armed rise cue is carried entirely by the fists.

Fix: give the forearms a distinct mid tone or a light edge on the upper-left-lit side so they separate from the coat, matching the three-tone cel convention used on the bat and archer.

DONE: settle screenshot at 900x700/f24 and 1280x900/f24 shows two forearms as separate forms; node occlusion-sweep.js reanimate still 96/96 clean.
close_reason:
The forearms now read as separate forms, and the cause was geometry rather than palette as the first review established. Both arms were re-angled to run from the shoulder seam at y=45/46 up and outward to a tip at y=27-31, so since the coat trapezoid only exists for y>=45 the distal ~20 units sit outside the coat by construction. Fist radius went 6 to 4 and recentred on the new tip so it caps the shaft instead of swallowing it.

MEASURED, reviewer reproducing it independently: the colour-only attempt moved 52 pixels in a 35x9 bbox; this moves 479-493 pixels in a 48x32 bbox at both required scenarios. The reviewer took its own settle screenshots at 900x700/f24 and 1280x900/f24 at deviceScaleFactor 1 and confirmed two straight dark bars leaving the shoulders and ending in pale fists, distinguishable from the pre-change trapezoid blob AT 1:1 rather than only under zoom.

PALETTE RE-JUDGED AND CHANGED. The first attempt's ARM_BASE sat brighter than the coat's entire ramp (rel-lum .126 against COAT_HI .0840). It is now ARM_SHADOW .0131 / ARM_BASE .0316 / ARM_HI .0664, all at or below COAT_HI, with ARM_BASE at 12.2:1 against the page background where roughly 85% of the bar actually sits. At the seam the arm and coat are near-identical in luminance and separation comes from the COAT_OUTLINE stroke, which is acceptable over a 2-3 unit overlap.

OCCLUSION CHECKED BEYOND THE SWEEP, since the figure grew upward. fxReanimate has only right and left landings, with an explicit never-above/below comment, so upward growth cannot grow toward the match. The figure's bbox did not actually grow: the head already reached y=4 and the old fist already reached x=0, so the REACH_INWARD/REACH_OUTWARD inputs are unchanged. The reviewer also forced three left landings and sampled the whole timeline, finding zero pixels inside the match rect, and measured minimum horizontal clearance of 12.0px across the 96 right landings.

THE POSE CHANGED, AND THAT IS A JUDGEMENT FOR CHRIS, not a defect. The silhouette now reads as both arms raised and outward in a V with fists at ear height, where the epic's copy describes a stiff-armed rise held out in front. Worth knowing: the OLD geometry never delivered the forward reach either, it read as arms at the sides. What survives is the stiff quality, both arms rigid straight bars with no elbow bend, and in context with the electrode posts and the two-step sit-up the reviewer read it as a body jerked upright with its arms thrown up, which is coherent for a Reanimation Jolt. If the forward reach is wanted specifically, reopen and the arms need to point along the x axis rather than up.

G6 improved rather than regressed: the diff touches no arc or glow element and shifts weight onto the figure, so it reads less like the shipped Lightning.

Two measured-false claims the new comment introduced were corrected before commit: BOOT_HI does exceed LEG_BASE (.0411 vs .0358), so the real rule is that the boot ramp stays below the leg ramp's TOP; and the 38x10/73px figure was a before/after diff rather than a visible extent.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
RUN STOPPED 2026-09-09 at the 4-hour wall clock. This bead FAILED REVIEW ONCE and the retry was not started, because the fix it needs is a geometry change requiring visual iteration and there was not time to see it through. The partial work IS committed; the bead stays open.

WHAT WAS DONE, and it is a reasonable prerequisite rather than wasted: the forearms got their own three-tone ramp, ARM_BASE #5c6472 with ARM_HI #8b93a2 and ARM_SHADOW #343b48, instead of reusing COAT. The recolour is real and strong where it lands (fill measured going from rgb(90,95,106) to rgb(148,155,168)) and the contrast is fine, not borderline, at roughly 2.8:1 against COAT #2b2f3a.

WHY IT DOES NOT MEET THE CRITERION. The reviewer took its own screenshots and could not tell before from after at 1:1 at either 900x700/f24 or 1280x900/f24. Pixel-diffing the settle frames says why: the diff bbox is 38x10 px and only 73 pixels change across BOTH arms. At 5-6x zoom two lighter nubs appear at the shoulders, and they read as shoulder pads rather than forearms. The stiff-armed rise cue is still carried entirely by the fists.

ROOT CAUSE IS GEOMETRY, NOT PALETTE, which is why a colour retry would fail again:
  var coatD = 'M 10 90 L 15 45 L 55 45 L 60 90 Z';
  var armLD = 'M 15 46 L 21 46 L 9 66 L 3 63 Z';
The arm runs from inside the widening coat trapezoid out past its left edge, but the part that clears the coat (x about 3-9, y about 60-66) sits under the r=6 fist circle, which is drawn after it. Only a sliver of roughly 12 units near the shoulder is ever visible. No recolour of that path can make a forearm read.

WHAT THE NEXT ATTEMPT NEEDS: extend or re-angle armLD and armRD so a visible run of forearm clears BOTH the coat edge and the fist circles, or shrink the fists, or change z-order. Then re-measure that 38x10 visible-extent figure and confirm the arms read at 1:1 without zooming.

ALSO WORTH REVISITING THEN: ARM_BASE is lighter than the coat's own highlight COAT_HI #4c525f, so the arm sits ABOVE the coat's whole tonal ramp rather than beside it. Same hue family, so not arbitrary, but it is not the boot-vs-leg relationship the convention comment cites. Once the arms are actually visible, that relationship should be re-judged against fxArrowShot's LEG/BOOT ramps.

Criterion 2 held throughout: occlusion-sweep.js reanimate is 96/96 clean, and batflight/arrowshot still 96/96 each.

title: Occlusion sweep harness: three small gaps found at review of oculist-1ta.16
description:
Found by the reviewer of oculist-1ta.16; none blocked the pass. File: artifacts/prototypes/occlusion-sweep.js (outer repo).

1. Lines ~28-29 claim the script exits before touching any effect when the control fails. It does not: main() sets exitCode=1 and still sweeps every effect, printing CLEAN per effect from a measurement path already proven broken. Either return early after a control failure or fix the header comment; returning early is the right one.
2. Line ~286: the sample loop steps t in 40ms up to maxEnd, so a maxEnd that is not a multiple of 40 leaves the tail unsampled (arrowshot 2150 -> last sample 2120). Append maxEnd itself as a final sample.
3. Lines ~81-83 hard-code the absolute playwright path, so the harness breaks in any other checkout. Resolve it relative to __dirname (../../repo/node_modules/playwright).

Also record in the header: the setTimeout no-op during runEffect() would hide artwork from any effect that stages elements on a timer, and getAnimations() seeking cannot pause an rAF-driven effect; both would read as a false clean. Every effect in this epic is WAAPI-only by convention, so this is a documentation note, not a defect.

DONE: the three edits made, header updated, node occlusion-sweep.js batflight arrowshot still exits 0 with 96/96 clean each.
close_reason:
All three gaps fixed and the header is finally accurate. Item 1: either control failing now returns before the effect loop, verified by fault injection on both paths (exit 1, no effect section, browser closed). Item 2: the sample loop appends maxEnd only when the 40ms stepping did not already land on it, so an exact multiple is not double-sampled; this removed a recorded FALSE CLEAN, with inkbloom flipping to samples=7, atTime=230ms, maxPixels=47, dirty=96, which is the ink drop landing on the match centre. Item 3: the playwright path resolves from __dirname, verified from a relocated checkout.

FAILED REVIEW TWICE, both times for the same thing: the WAAPI-only header was corrected into a NEW inaccuracy. Round 1 denied that any effect stages artwork in a setTimeout body (fourteen do). Round 2 fixed the bullet but left the paragraph above it asserting the opposite of its own bullet. The /goal stop condition fired, so the orchestrator corrected the preamble directly and stopped rather than dispatching a third attempt.

That edit has now been reviewed independently and PASSES on every claim: the preamble states the assumption already does not hold for setTimeout and holds for rAF only because nothing uses it (grep confirms zero requestAnimationFrame in the playground); fourteen is exact; matchstrike's 400ms body really does mount band, glow and six embers, with the glow at r.left-4/r.top-4/r.width+8/r.height+8; the hook returns 0 without ever calling realSetTimeout, so timers are dropped rather than deferred; and every round-1 and round-2 phrase is gone from the file. batflight and arrowshot are described with the narrow true claim, cleanup-only setTimeout at DUR+100, rather than the false 'no setTimeout at all' that two earlier briefs propagated.

Acceptance criterion holds: node occlusion-sweep.js batflight arrowshot exits 0 at 96/96 clean each. The measurement limitation the header now records is tracked as oculist-e2w.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
ESCALATION from the oculist-aun reviewer, 2026-09-09. Item 2 of this bead (a maxEnd that is not a multiple of 40 leaves the tail unsampled) is not a small gap. It is the sole cause of a recorded FALSE CLEAN.

PROVEN, not inferred. The sample loop is for (let t = 0; t <= maxEnd; t += 40) and never clamps to maxEnd. inkbloom's maxEnd is 230, so samples run 0..200 and t=230, the frame where the ink drop lands on the match centre, is never taken. The reviewer patched ONLY that (append maxEnd as a final sample) in a scratch copy and ran it against the pre-eke playground: inkbloom flipped from CLEAN to ISSUES FOUND, maxPixels=47, dirty=96, atTime=230ms. 47px is about a 7px circle, i.e. exactly the drop.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. oculist-aun opened by treating inkbloom's CLEAN as a real result that distinguished it from five dirty siblings. It was a measurement artifact. An effect that deterministically drops an element onto the match centre measured clean for months because the harness stopped sampling 30ms early.

This bead's own trailing note already anticipated the second half of the same problem (the setTimeout no-op hiding timer-staged artwork, reading as a false clean). That half is now confirmed too and is filed separately as oculist-hgt.

No new bead for inkbloom: fixing item 2 here is the fix.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
RUN STOPPED HERE 2026-09-09: this bead failed review TWICE, which is a /goal stop condition. The work IS committed on branch goal/1ta-followups-and-two-prototypes, but the bead is deliberately NOT closed, because no reviewer passed the final state.

WHAT IS DONE AND VERIFIED GOOD (do not redo):

- Item 1, the early return. Either control failing now closes the browser, prints a FINAL block with control status and an 'effect sweep skipped' line, and exits before the effect loop. Both control paths verified by fault injection: exit 1 with no === <effect> === section printed, no leaked handle. Both controls short-circuit, since a dead neutralization makes deferred-mount numbers noise for the same reason a broken pixel control does.
- Item 2, the unsampled tail. sampleTimes is built by the old 40ms stepping, then maxEnd is appended only when the last step did not already land on it, so an exact multiple of 40 is not double-sampled. VERIFIED: inkbloom flips from the recorded false CLEAN to samples=7, atTime=230ms, maxPixels=47, dirty=96, which is the ink drop landing on the match centre. batflight maxEnd=2080 gives samples=53 with no double sample; arrowshot now samples=55 and includes its 2150 tail. Float jitter in maxEnd traced and ruled benign: downward wobble still appends, upward wobble on an exact multiple costs one redundant screenshot 4.5e-13ms later and changes no result.
- Item 3, the playwright path, now path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'repo', 'node_modules', 'playwright'), verified by running from a relocated directory through a symlinked ../../repo.
- Acceptance criterion holds: node occlusion-sweep.js batflight arrowshot exits 0 with 96/96 clean each. All five reference numbers reproduce exactly (matchstrike 9356, scanline 1560, emberignite 819, stamp 4137, comet 1031).

WHY IT FAILED TWICE, both times the same class of error: the header was corrected into a NEW inaccuracy.

- Round 1 claimed no effect stages artwork inside a setTimeout body, framed the risk as hypothetical, and ended 'Neither currently applies.' Fourteen fx* functions do exactly that; fxMatchstrike mounts a glow div sized to the match plus six embers from inside a 400ms timer.
- Round 2 fixed the bullet but left the paragraph introducing it saying 'That is true of every effect here as of oculist-hgt', contradicting its own bullet four lines below, and still framed it as recorded 'for whoever adds the next effect'.

THE ORCHESTRATOR THEN FIXED THAT PREAMBLE DIRECTLY rather than dispatching a third attempt, since the stop condition had fired. It now says the WAAPI-only assumption ALREADY DOES NOT HOLD for setTimeout and holds for rAF only because no effect uses it yet. node --check passes and batflight/arrowshot still exit 0 at 96/96. That edit is UNREVIEWED, which is the only reason this bead is still open.

WHAT A REVIEWER NEEDS TO DO TO CLOSE IT: read the WAAPI-ONLY ASSUMPTION section against effects-playground.html and confirm every claim in it is true. Nothing else is outstanding.

title: Hat base tone is only 15 pure pixels at the floor size
description:
From the oculist-1ta.19 review. Not a defect; a thin margin worth knowing about.

HAT_BASE measures 15 pure pixels at archerH 78 against HAT_HI 21 and HAT_SHADOW 10, on a hat that owns 442 pixels total. The done-criteria asked for meaningfully more than the old 12, and 15 clears it by three pixels.

The structural cause named in oculist-1ta.18 is genuinely gone: the tones were clipped ellipses that squeezed the base to 12, and they are now wedges built from the crown triangle's own vertices, so nothing can squeeze them. All three tones are visible in the render. Round 1's taller crown gave 37, and cutting the apex from 30 units to 13 to stop it reading as a party hat cost most of that back, which was the right trade.

So this is a consequence of a deliberate choice, not a mistake. Worth revisiting only if the hat is reopened for another reason, or if Chris looks at it and finds the base tone reads as absent.

FIX IF WANTED: widen the middle undrawn strip between the two wedges. Note the trap recorded in the code: the strip is itself a triangle sharing the crown's apex, so its area shrinks with crown height even at a constant width fraction, and an even split zeroes HAT_SHADOW because the right wedge's edges sit on the crown's shallower hypotenuse.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Base tone comfortably visible at 78px, sampled in the render.
- Crown still reads as a low angular peak, not a party hat.
- Occlusion sweep still zero at STRIKE_GAP 8, and the cliff re-probed since hat geometry moves it.
close_reason:
NO GEOMETRY CHANGE, and that is the answer rather than an omission. This bead was explicitly conditional: a thin margin worth knowing about, to be revisited only if the base tone reads as absent. It does not.

CRITERION 1 MET, established by counterfactual rather than by eyeballing a magnification. The reviewer repainted the crown in the live DOM with the base band eliminated (shadow wedge extended left to meet the highlight) and measured the difference at 1:1: 56 pixels change by a mean luma delta of 23/255, max 32. That is well above JND for adjacent regions and plainly visible side by side. So the 15-pure-pixel count is a conservative floor; the tone's real visual footprint is roughly 4x that once antialiased blends carry it.

COUNTS, measured independently with point-in-polygon attribution at archerH 78: crown triangle alone is HAT_BASE 14, HAT_HI 0, HAT_SHADOW 10; whole hat is 15/21/10, reproducing the bead's figures and confirming they are whole-hat aggregates. The 15th base pixel is in the back brim, so the implementer's crown-only 15 was off by one, immaterially.

CRITERION 2 MET: the crown is 13 units on a 36-unit base and the forward beak's vertical run of 16 units exceeds it, so at 1:1 in page context it reads as a low angular bycocket rather than a cone.

CRITERION 3 MET BY MEASUREMENT, not by construction. arrowshot is 96/96 clean at STRIKE_GAP 8. The cliff was re-probed on a patched copy outside the repo: STRIKE_GAP 7 gives 94/96 with 2 dirty at 1280x900 fonts 25 and 26, maxPixels 1, exit 1. So the cliff sits exactly one pixel below 8, where the source comment says it does.

THE OBVIOUS FIX WAS TESTED AND REJECTED ON EVIDENCE. Moving the shadow wedge's inner base point from 37 to 41 widens the middle strip and takes HAT_BASE from 15 to 19, but takes HAT_SHADOW from 10 to 2. That empirically reproduces the trap recorded in the code, where an even split zeroes HAT_SHADOW because the right wedge's edges sit on the crown's shallower hypotenuse. Net loss. A real gain needs crown height, which was already rejected as the party-hat trade.

DISCOVERED: oculist-uxa0. The crown's OWN highlight wedge has zero pure-pixel survival at floor size; all 21 HAT_HI pixels come from the front brim sharing the fill. So oculist-1ta.19's 'all three tones are visible' held only by counting the brim. Does not undermine criterion 1, which is about the base tone specifically.

title: Front brim point of the bycocket does not read at 78px
description:
Flagged by the implementer against itself and confirmed independently by the reviewer in oculist-1ta.17.

artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html:4020 (brimFrontD) — the front brim point renders in the shadow tone AND lands directly against the same-hued bow limb, so it neither reads as a crisp point nor separates from the bow. At the 78px floor the plume and the back brim flip carry the whole read, and the silhouette says 'brimmed hat with a flip' rather than specifically 'bycocket'.

He does read as the folklore archer, so this is polish, not a failure of the bead.

FIX: give the front point a lighter tone than the crown's shadow, or 2-3 more units of clearance from the bow limb, or both.

RELATED, same bead, same file: the hat's BASE tone is nearly squeezed out by its two clip ellipses at the floor size — 12 pure pixels at archerH 78 against 75 highlight and 113 shadow (72/183/269 at 112). Above the zero-pixel failure mode this epic keeps hitting, but thin enough to be worth widening while the hat is open.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The front point is distinguishable from both the crown shadow and the bow limb at 78px, sampled in the render.
- Hat base tone has meaningfully more than 12 pure pixels at 78px.
- Occlusion sweep still zero, including the wide 1280x900 coverage.
close_reason: Absorbed into oculist-1ta.19, which redrew the same forms. Front beak now separates from both the crown shadow (hard outlined HAT_HI against HAT_SHADOW) and the bow limb (zero overlap across all 15 shared rows). Hat base tone is 15 pure px at archerH 78, up from 12, with the clip-ellipse cause structurally removed - thin, and flagged to Chris rather than claimed as comfortable

title: Arrow reads less planted since STRIKE_GAP went to 12
description:
Raised from 6 to 12 in oculist-1ta.11 to clear a 1-2px occlusion regression at font sizes 22-26. That fixed the occlusion, but the reviewer's own read is that the strike is measurably softened: the tip now rests about 6px further out and there is a visible page-background gap between the arrowhead and the highlight rect, where at 6 the tip kissed the edge.

It still reads as stuck in the page aiming at the word (the head overlaps the outer ring, the shaft angles away, nothing floats), so this is a quality nit for Chris to judge by eye, not a defect.

The obvious move is an intermediate value. 8 and 10 were NOT tested and must not be adopted without a full sweep: the failure is size-dependent and only showed at font sizes 22-26, at a wide 1280x900, at t=1400.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Whatever value is chosen, the occlusion sweep is zero across font sizes 20-30 at 1280x900 AND the other established scenarios.
- The arrowhead visibly touches or overlaps the target rings so the strike reads as planted.
- Compare before and after at 4x at both font-size 16 and 24 and judge by eye, not by the number.
notes: Commit 42ad041 refers to this bead as 'oculist-1ta.16'. That id was wrong; the sweep-coverage bead is 1ta.16 and this one is 1ta.15. The commit was already pushed when the mistake was found, so the message was left alone rather than rewriting published history.
close_reason: STRIKE_GAP 12->8, the smallest value that sweeps completely clean, per Chris's instruction to follow the recommendation. Reviewer confirmed the arrow now crosses the gold ring with its tip at the highlight edge and reads embedded rather than floating. Recorded in code that 8 sits one pixel above a cliff: 7 fails by 2px at font sizes 22-26

title: Two cosmetic misses in the Bat Flight figure
description:
Both found in the oculist-1ta.10 re-review, both non-blocking, both roughly one line. Filed rather than patched in after the review passed.

1. THE MOUTH DOES NOT RENDER. artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html:3557 — the path 'M 39 51 Q 45 54 51 51' lands at y roughly 34 to 35.8px at production size, while the head's own bottom outline sits at y 35.8px. The mouth merges into the chin line and is invisible. Move it up far enough to clear the outline.

2. THE HAIR OUTLINE IS A NO-OP. :3506 — HAIR_OUTLINE '#000000' on HAIR '#0d0d0f' is a 5/255 delta, so the stroke only fattens the shape rather than defining it. Either give it a real contrast delta or drop the stroke and say why the form does not need one.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The mouth is visible as a distinct feature at production size, sampled in the render rather than judged from source.
- The hair reads as an outlined form, or the absence of an outline is deliberate and commented.
- No change to the figure's bounding box, so the occlusion guarantee is untouched. Confirm with a sweep rather than by inspection.
close_reason:
Both misses fixed, both verified in the render rather than from source.

MOUTH: moved 'M 39 51 Q 45 54 51 51' to 'M 39 48 Q 45 51 51 48'. Reviewer sampled its own pixel columns at deviceScaleFactor 1, 900x700, 24px match, with animations paused at figure opacity 1. Before, rows 43-45 read (101,97,93)/(33,28,26)/(43,26,18), one fused dark band with zero light pixels between mouth and chin. After, row 41 is pure HAIR (13,13,15), row 43 is pure SKIN (233,222,210) as a genuine light gap, row 44 is SKIN_OUTLINE. The gap holds across x=39/42/45/48/51, and it still separates at 16px, the grid's smallest font, where before it was fused. No nose or eye collision: the nose occupies rows 37-39 with one blended row between. The curve's control point still sits below its endpoints, so the expression is unchanged, just translated up 3 units.

HAIR OUTLINE: dropped rather than given contrast, and the reasoning checks out. Every outline on this figure is darker than its fill (CAPE #3b0764 / CAPE_OUTLINE #150826, SKIN #e9ded2 / SKIN_OUTLINE #2b1a12, BAT_BASE #3a2b52 / BAT_OUTLINE #0a0612, sclera stroked with SKIN_OUTLINE), so lightening HAIR for contrast would have made it the figure's only rim-light. The silhouette reads without it: one antialiased step from page to hair, and a single blend row at the hairline where it meets SKIN, SKIN_HI and SKIN_SHADE. The stroke's only measured effect was widening the band by about a row and deepening it from (13,13,15) to black. The dead HAIR_OUTLINE declaration was removed; grep confirms the only other occurrences are fxVineSwing's own separately scoped var.

BBOX UNCHANGED, measured independently over all 19 non-clipPath shapes at both 24px and 16px: minX 8.01, minY 9.62, maxX 64.08, maxY 86.52. batflight stays 96/96 clean and arrowshot 96/96, which is the behavioural gate.

Noted, not blocking: getBoundingClientRect is stroke-blind on SVG geometry in Chromium, so bbox identity alone does not prove the removed stroke left ink extent unchanged; removing a stroke can only shrink ink, and the sweep is the real gate. Also the mouth is a 1px dark line at 24px and a mid-grey antialiased line at 16px, legible but at the floor of what survives rasterising; stroke-width is the knob if a later bead wants it bolder.

title: Effect is born at the pre-scroll location if a user scroll aborts the scrollIntoView
description:
Found in the oculist-1ta.12 re-review. Cosmetic, pre-existing, and out of scope for that bead.

When a user scroll interrupts the playground's pre-fire scrollIntoView, scrollend fires early. Suppression lifts, the effect is then born at the PRE-scroll location, and it dissolves 190-315ms later. The dissolve is correct behaviour; the flicker of an effect appearing briefly in the wrong place is not.

This predates the scroll-dissolve work: the effect has always been born wherever ensureVisible's completion callback happened to fire. The dissolve just makes it visible as a brief flash rather than a beacon that stays wrong.

FIX DIRECTION: if the pre-fire scroll was aborted by the user, do not draw the effect at all rather than drawing it and immediately dissolving it. The scroll that aborted it has already invalidated the endpoint, which is the same reasoning behind the dissolve itself.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Interrupting the pre-fire scrollIntoView with a user scroll produces no visible effect at the old location.
- A normal, uninterrupted fire is unaffected and still runs its full lifetime.
close_reason:
ensureVisible now detects the OUTCOME rather than the cause. It polls the match's rect via rAF until it stops moving for two consecutive frames (bounded at 1200ms), then compares the settled top against scrollIntoView({block:'center'})'s own intended target, (innerHeight - elHeight)/2, with a 4px tolerance. Beyond that the effect is skipped. All wheel/touchstart/scrollend listeners are gone, so one check covers keyboard, scrollbar, wheel and other-JS scrolls alike.

FAILED REVIEW ONCE, on the input-listener design, and the reviewer measured both of its failure modes. False positives, the blocking one: a zero-delta wheel, a horizontal wheel, a 5px nudge and a wheel consumed by the sidebar's nested scroller each suppressed a LEGITIMATE fire while the page settled correctly. Coverage gaps: keyboard End, PageDown, ArrowDown, Space and other-JS scrollTo/scrollBy all still drew, often fully offscreen at matchTop 1309 against a 700px viewport.

THE FIRST ATTEMPT'S HEADLINE REPRODUCTION WAS NOT AN ABORT. Both the retry and the reviewer measured mouse.wheel(0, 2000) mid-flight failing to relocate the resting position at all: it and the smooth scroll bottom out at the same document limit, landing at 339 with delta 0.00 against a target of 339.14. Keyboard End and scrollTo(0,2000) move it 858px. So the original wheel-based design was aimed at a case that does not exist in this fixture. Scenario A was rebuilt on the two mechanisms that genuinely abort.

Reviewer PASS with independent measurement of both tables at a 1600ms poll window, wider than the check's own 900ms so a draw at the timeout path could not hide: coverage all peak 0 (End, Home, PageDown, ArrowDown, Space, scrollBy, scrollTo x2), false positives all peak 3. The tolerance boundary is exact and monotonic, verified by forcing offsets with scroll-margin-top: deltas 0 through 4 draw, 5 and beyond skip, and legitimate fires land at delta 0.00, so 4px is headroom rather than a knife edge. Holds under reduced-motion and CPU throttling to 20x. The settle loop moves from its second frame so it cannot exit early, skips (the safe direction) if still moving at 1200ms, adds no latency (median 538ms post-fix vs 543ms pre), and under a 2s rAF suspension defers and then draws correctly rather than hanging. The in-view fast path correctly bypasses the comparison, confirmed by a match in-band but 269px off centre still drawing.

The new prefire-scroll-abort-check.js was itself mutation-tested: TOLERANCE_PX=-1 and a mid-flight sampling mutant both make it fail, as does the pre-fix source, so it is falsifiable in both directions.

KNOWN AND ACCEPTED: a suppressed fire does not update lastKey, so Replay afterwards repeats the previous effect.

title: Archer corner can flip between fires when the match sits at viewport centre
description:
Found in the oculist-1ta.2 re-review. Cosmetic, but it touches the epic's determinism constraint, which exists so a human comparing two fires sees the same thing.

artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html:3340 — the left-plan corner tie-break is Math.abs(leftEndY - launchYTop) <= Math.abs(leftEndY - launchYBottom). That is a genuine near-tie when the match sits at the viewport's vertical centre, which is exactly where ensureVisible's scrollIntoView({block:'center'}) puts it. Sub-pixel wobble can flip the archer between top-left and bottom-left across two fires.

Not an occlusion risk: both corners give identical horizontal clearance and both swept to zero occluding pixels. The re-review also measured identical full-viewport SHA1s across two fires at 12 timestamps, so it does not reproduce in practice — but the tie is real in the arithmetic.

FIX: break the tie on something that cannot wobble, e.g. prefer top-left unless the vertical leg differs by more than a pixel or two.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Twenty consecutive fires with the match at viewport centre put the archer in the same corner every time.
- Occlusion sweep still zero.
close_reason:
CLOSED BY DISPROVING THE PREMISE, not by adding a guard. The tie this bead was filed for cannot occur.

Both the reviewer and the implementer derived the closed form independently and agree: d = topLegDist - bottomLegDist = 2*mcy - vh + archerH/19. At viewport centre mcy = vh/2 + e, so d = archerH/19 + 2e, where e is ensureVisible's residual centring offset. archerH is clamped to [78, 112] and measured e stays within [-0.5, +0.39], so d is bounded away from zero BY THE ARCHER'S OWN HEIGHT. Measured across all 46 left-plan scenarios: d in [3.1053, 6.6760], closed form matching the raw comparison to 7.46e-14, predicted corner matching the rendered corner 46 of 46.

A 1px deadband was implemented first and PASSED review, then reverted on the reviewer's own analysis. It was net-negative: it moved the knife-edge from d=0 to d=1, i.e. TOWARD the operating point of d in [3.1, 6.7], cutting margin by 1px rather than adding robustness; it was documented as hysteresis while keeping no state; its branch was unreachable in all 96 grid scenarios, so 96/96 clean never exercised it; and its 0.26px justification was borrowed from a different, superseded comparison, against a measured actual wobble of 0.0px across 20 fires.

What ships instead is the proof, as a comment at the comparison. The final diff is 12 inserted comment lines and zero deletions, so the executable code is byte-identical to HEAD. Both done-criteria therefore hold by construction rather than by sampling: behaviour is bit-identical to a state already measured 96/96 clean, and the 20-fire tally is 20/20 bottom-left with d = 4.105263 on every fire.

The implementer also caught an error in the orchestrator's brief, which cited an upper bound of 6.895; the verified value is 6.676, and it wrote conservative language rather than transcribing the unchecked figure.

title: Mist fade-out can tint the match in the below-landing fallback
description:
Found during the oculist-1ta.1 re-review. Non-blocking, but it is an occlusion finding in an epic where occlusion is the heaviest constraint.

artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html:3173 — the mist fade-out scaleY(1.25) grows about transform-origin:50% 100%, lifting the box top by 0.25*mistH (19-30px), while GAP is only 10 (:2894). In the 'below' landing that puts a faint tint over the bottom 10-15px of the match: measured 1.45% of the match box at a max per-channel delta of 20/255, during the tail of the fade. The word stays fully legible.

'below' is the un-guarded last resort at :2996, reachable only when both sides and above all fail, i.e. geometry that is already degenerate. It degrades to off-screen rather than to overlap, so no glyph is ever covered by the figure itself.

FIX: account for the scaleY growth in the clearance calculation, or anchor the fade-out so the box does not grow upward.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Per-pixel diff of the match rect against a no-effect baseline shows zero changed pixels in the below-landing case, at natural size and 48px.
- The other three landings do not regress.
close_reason:
The mist fade-out is now anchored so it cannot grow toward the match. transform-origin becomes 50% 0% in the fade keyframes for the 'below' landing only, so the 0.25*mistH overshoot grows downward, away from the word, in the one landing where upward meant toward it. The clearance-accounting alternative was rejected because it would spend vertical space in an already-degenerate last-resort landing and push the figure off-screen more often, trading a faint tint for a missing effect.

CRITERION 1 VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY AND EXACTLY. The reviewer forced a real below landing (full-width match at viewport top so both sides and above fail their fit tests, confirmed against the live mist rect: mist top 47 vs match bottom 37, GAP 10, 0.25*mistH = 28) and diffed the match rect against a no-effect baseline at 10ms steps, 209 samples across the full 2080ms rather than one instant. Pre-fix: natural 307/15252 pixels at max delta 22/255, 48px 417/42312 at max delta 23, both peaking in the fade tail at t=1380. Post-fix: ZERO changed pixels and max per-channel delta ZERO at every sample, at both sizes and again at degenerate 500x180 and 500x260. Max-delta-zero is stronger than count-zero.

CRITERION 2 held byte-exactly: full-viewport sha1 at 20ms steps across 105 frames is identical pre and post for left, right and above; only the below landing's hash changed, which is the intended change. The conditional is safe, since landing can only carry one of four side literals and there is no fall-through value.

The downward growth is not a bad trade: in the genuinely degenerate case the pre-fix mist OVERLAPPED the match, and post-fix it clips off the viewport bottom instead. scrollHeight and scrollWidth are unchanged before and after firing, so no reflow and no new scrollbar.

COVERAGE CAVEAT, self-reported by the implementer and confirmed by the reviewer: the sweep never exercises this. batflight's 96 scenarios produce 61 right and 35 left landings and ZERO above or below, because scrollIntoView({block:'center'}) keeps the match centred so a side always fits. So 96/96 clean is not evidence for this bug. Filed as oculist-tt58.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Correction to this bead's close reason: the coverage gap it names as 'oculist-tt58' is actually oculist-ey2e. The id was written before the bead was created and guessed wrong. Nothing else in the close reason changes.

title: Regression-guard the pack notice's reduced-motion, no-reflow and CTA paths
description:
test/pack_discovery_notice.test.js (from oculist-tdj.3) covers three of that bead's five done-criteria: appearance, focus retention, and dismissal persistence. Three are verified-correct but unguarded, so a later change can break them silently.

UNGUARDED
1. Reduced motion. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the notice must render statically. Assert getAnimations().length === 0 on the notice element, not a duration value.
2. No host-page reflow. The notice lives only in the overlay shadow root. Assert document.body and documentElement scroll metrics are unchanged when it appears, and that querySelectorAll('.oc-pack-notice') in the light DOM finds nothing.
3. The Open Settings CTA. Clicking it opens the settings panel AND dismisses the notice permanently.

ALSO
test/pack_discovery_notice.test.js:43 patches its fixture by pinning the exact source text of the cybervision registry entry. It fails loudly rather than silently if that shape changes, but it needs updating when a real packed effect ships. Consider a less brittle fixture patch at the same time.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Each of the three behaviours has a test that fails when that behaviour is removed. Prove it by breaking the code, not by reading it.
- node --test passes in full.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. test/pack_discovery_notice.test.js now guards reduced-motion (getAnimations 0), no host reflow (scroll metrics unchanged + light-DOM count 0), and the Open Settings CTA (opens panel, dismisses permanently across close/reopen). Reviewer independently broke four code paths, each turned the right test red. Fixture patch left strict in both files, deliberately. Full suite 314/314.

title: CHANGELOG entry and stale effect-count sweep
description:
CONDITIONAL: only run this once at least one of oculist-e2m.5 / oculist-e2m.6 has
landed. Describe only the effects that actually shipped.

1. CHANGELOG.md: add the new effect(s) to the unreleased/v1.8.0 section. One line
   each, describing what the user sees, not how it is implemented.

2. Effect-count sweep. test/effect_enumeration_sync.js polices exactly four sites
   (extension/welcome.html prose, extension/welcome.html select mockup, and two spots
   in docs/index.html). Nothing polices the rest, which is how the count went stale
   before. Grep the repo for every other place the effect roster or its COUNT appears
   and fix each: at minimum check README.md, STORE.md, extension/popup.html,
   docs/promo-marquee.html and docs/promo-small.html. Search for the literal digit as
   well as the word — "12 effects", "twelve", and the name of any single effect used
   as an example list.

3. Do NOT touch the live Chrome Web Store listing copy or extension/manifest.json's
   version. Store submission is oculist-296's business and this epic must not move it.

4. No user-facing copy may use the word "plugin" anywhere. Say "effects" or
   "custom animation settings".

DONE-CRITERIA
- `node --test test/effect_enumeration_sync.test.js` passes.
- `grep -rn "12 effects\|twelve effects" --include=*.md --include=*.html .` returns
  nothing stale (adjust the numbers for whatever the true count now is).
- `grep -rni "plugin" README.md STORE.md docs/ extension/*.html` returns no
  user-facing use of the word.
- CHANGELOG.md names each shipped effect exactly once.
close_reason: Superseded by oculist-nq1x.13 (effect-count sweep, CHANGELOG and store copy for the pack-system launch). Flappy and Cheshire moved into the Halloween pack, and the 2026-09-22 messaging decision forbids naming pack effects in the CHANGELOG, so this bead's scope as written no longer applies. Closed by Chris's call 2026-09-23.

title: waapi_beacon_cancel: declare the WAAPI vs canvas partition instead of gating on snapshotCount
description:
Reviewer note on oculist-3rv.1. The per-key loop gates WAAPI playState cancel assertions on snapshotCount > 0. Today exactly the three canvas keys (chrono, electron, speedlines) hit the else-branch (measured counts: hud 23, dispersion 3, chrono 0, cybervision 29, electron 0, flame 35, lightning 8, arrows 2, speedlines 0, iris 2, trail 3, sweep 123). If a WAAPI effect ever stops parenting its Animations under .oc-beacon, or auto-removes them before the snapshot (arrows and iris carry only 2), the cancel assertions silently downgrade to element-removal-only and the suite stays green.

FIX: partition the derived key list once at setup by probing the container in the content-script world (__rafId set vs __waapiAnims non-empty), then assert.ok(snapshotCount > 0) for the WAAPI partition instead of an if.

DONE WHEN: a WAAPI effect whose animations are missing from the snapshot fails the test; the three canvas effects still pass; no hardcoded key list.
close_reason: Closed

title: Options page for effect presets
description:
Small options page ("options_page" in manifest.json): base-effect dropdown, colour picker, size select, speed select, name field, Save, and a list with Delete. No JSON textarea, no validate button, no developer guide.

STEPS
1. Add options.html/options.js; register options_page in manifest.json.
2. Save runs the bead oculist-3rv.5 validator and writes oc-effect-presets via chrome.storage.sync.
3. In-page picker picks the new preset up on the next storage change event with no reload.
4. A 9th preset is refused with a clear message stating the cap of 8.
5. Every user-facing string says "preset" or "custom animation settings". The word "plugin" must not appear anywhere user-facing (options page, README, CHANGELOG, store copy).

DONE WHEN
- Create/save/delete round-trips through chrome.storage.sync.
- New preset appears in the in-page picker with no reload.
- 9th preset refused clearly.
- grep -rni plugin extension/ docs/ README.md shows nothing user-facing new.
notes: Preset experiment. Deferred so bd ready and /goal never surface it. Undefer when the human decides presets ship. Separate branch, not in the v1.8.0 release commit.
close_reason: Closed

title: Preset model: validator, applyPresets(), boot-ordering before hud coercion
description:
Custom effects as presets over the existing engine. A preset binds an existing effect to knobs the settings model already has:
{ "id": "soft-iris", "label": "Soft Iris", "base": "iris", "color": "#38bdf8", "size": "l", "speed": "slow" }

STEPS
1. Runtime: effectsRegistry['preset:' + p.id] = { label, run(rect) { presetOverride = p; try { effectsRegistry[p.base].run(rect) } finally { presetOverride = null } } }. getEffectiveColors (~671), getBeaconScale (~693), getBeaconDuration (~708) consult presetOverride before settings. That is the whole mechanism; no interpreter.
2. Storage: one chrome.storage.sync key oc-effect-presets holding an array, cap 8.
3. Validator (~30 lines, pure node testable, no jsdom): base is a live registry key; color matches /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}$/; size in s/m/l/xl; speed in fast/normal/slow; id charset; label length and no comma, period, or parenthesis (effect_enumeration_sync.test.js label charset trap). Each rejection returns a reason.
4. Boot ordering: merge preset: entries BEFORE the `if (!effectsRegistry[settings.effect]) settings.effect = 'hud'` coercion at ~7696 and ~7768, using get(['oc-settings','oc-effect-presets']) in the single existing boot call at ~7741. Otherwise a selected preset is coerced to hud and persisted on every load.
5. Deletion needs no new code: the same coercion lands the user on hud.

DONE WHEN
- Preset selection survives reload without coercion to hud.
- Deleting a preset falls back to hud with no new code.
- effect_enumeration_sync.test.js green (it parses the registry object literal source; runtime-merged keys never enter it).
- Zero changes to buildSettingsPanel().
- Validator tested in pure node; each bad input rejected with a reason.
- No user-facing string contains "plugin".
notes: Preset experiment. Deferred so bd ready and /goal never surface it. Undefer when the human decides presets ship. Separate branch, not in the v1.8.0 release commit.
close_reason: Closed

title: Static-scan guard: no beacon helper call inside async callbacks in the effects block
description:
Pure node test, no browser, in the style of test/privacy_invariants.test.js.

The preset mechanism (bead 7) sets a synchronous presetOverride during run(rect). It is only safe because every call to getBeaconScale, getBeaconDuration, getEffectiveColors inside the effects block (extension/content.js ~1177-3460) resolves synchronously during run(). This test pins that invariant.

STEPS
1. Read content.js, locate the effects block (between the registry header and the last animateX).
2. Scan for any of the three helper names appearing inside a setTimeout/requestAnimationFrame/Promise callback body. A setTimeout whose delay ARGUMENT is getBeaconDuration(...) is fine; a call inside the callback body is not. Mentions in comments do not count.
3. Fail with the line number and helper name.
4. Prove it red: temporarily move one helper call into a rAF body, watch the test fail, revert.

DONE WHEN
- Passes on current content.js.
- Fails if a helper call is moved into a setTimeout or rAF body.
- No browser launch.
notes: Preset experiment. Deferred so bd ready and /goal never surface it. Undefer when the human decides presets ship. Separate branch, not in the v1.8.0 release commit.
close_reason: Closed

title: build.js zip/extension comparison diverges for symlinks and newline filenames
description:
Found by the oculist-1os reviewer on 2026-09-02, out of scope for that bead and not blocking it. Nothing is broken today: extension/ holds 11 plain files, no symlinks, no exotic names.
