SYMLINKS (the realistic one). build.js:42 uses 'find . -type f', which omits symlinks. zip stores a symlink as a non-directory entry, so 'unzip -Z1' lists it. A symlink in extension/ therefore lands in 'zipped' but not in 'actual' and fails the build with 'unexpected in zip: link.js'. Verified: 'ln -s real.js link.js' in extension/ reproduces it. That is a FALSE failure — the file is legitimately in the zip.

NEWLINE IN A FILENAME (theoretical). 'unzip -Z1' escapes a newline as '^J' while find emits it raw, so the split('\n') at build.js:46 shreds one path into two entries and the build fails falsely. Only reachable if someone puts a newline in an extension/ filename, which for a hand-curated source dir is not a real risk.

DONE WHEN: the symlink case no longer fails the build falsely — either by widening find's predicate to match what zip actually stores, or by explicitly rejecting symlinks in extension/ with a clear error saying why (a symlink in a Chrome Web Store package is arguably wrong anyway, so refusing it is a legitimate fix). Prove it with a mutation: create a symlink in extension/, confirm the build behaves as designed, remove it. Handle the newline case only if it falls out for free; do not contort the code for it.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Closed in fbc3a12 on epic/oculist-67h-abk-296.9. Reviewer PASS, first pass.

RESOLUTION: reject any symlink in extension/ as a pre-flight, before zip -r runs, rather than teaching the set comparison to tolerate one. The bead allowed either that or widening find's predicate; rejection was chosen because it handles the file and directory cases uniformly and does not bless out-of-tree smuggling.

THE FIX IS LOAD-BEARING, and the reviewer proved it rather than assuming. On an isolated copy with extension/linkdir pointing at a sibling ../outside containing inner.js, the OLD build.js WROTE linkdir/inner.js into the zip on disk before failing. The new one exits at build.js:31 and no archive is written at all. It also confirmed the block holds for a chained symlink (extension/chain -> ../hop -> /abs/outside2) and an absolute one (extension/abs.js -> /etc/hosts), with no zip produced in either case.

WHY find -L WAS NOT THE FIX, restated here because it is the tempting one: it would make the guard follow symlinked directories too, which is precisely the smuggling path. That reasoning is now carried in the code comment so it survives the next person who notices find -type f 'misses' symlinks.

ONE FINDING FIXED BEFORE COMMIT, caught by the reviewer. The pre-flight originally ran a bare find . -type l with no exclusions, while the expected-set find carries -not -path './.*' -not -path './__MACOSX/*'. That meant a symlink under a top-level dot dir or __MACOSX, which zip -x would never store, still failed the build. That is the SAME anchoring-mismatch class oculist-1os had just fixed, reintroduced in the new check. Now mirrored on both sides and verified both directions: a symlink at extension/.hidden/x.js builds fine (11 files), a symlink at extension/link.js fails with the actionable message.

COMMENT ACCURACY, and it turned out better than expected. The oculist-1os block claims zip membership 'is a pure function of extension/ minus the excludes'. The reviewer found that sentence was ALREADY subtly false at HEAD, because a symlinked directory made membership not a function of extension/ at all. The pre-flight is what makes it true. So the existing comment was not left stale, it was repaired by the change.

NEWLINE CASE deliberately left unhandled, per the bead's own instruction to handle it only if free. A newline-named symlink reports two bogus paths but still fails the build loudly, matching the pre-existing behaviour of the set comparison. Not half-handled.

Pre-existing ordering quirk noted, not changed: build.js:14 unlinks a prior zip before this check runs, so a symlink now deletes the previous artifact and writes nothing. Harmless for a regenerated build output.

title: beacon_fade_persistent_overlays reduced-motion test is flaky at 5s under full-suite load
description:
Found by the oculist-296.5 reviewer on 2026-09-02 while re-running the gate.

SYMPTOM: test/beacon_fade_persistent_overlays.test.js:343, 'reduced motion: scroll fades the transient beacon...', timed out at 5000ms on a full npm test run (306 pass / 1 fail). An isolated re-run of that one file passed 2/2, and a second full run passed 307/0.

DIAGNOSIS SO FAR: puppeteer timeout under full-suite load, not a logic regression. It means the epic's '307 pass / 0 fail' gate is not reproducible on every run, which weakens every bead that cites it as evidence.

DONE WHEN: the cause is identified (raise the timeout for this case, await the right signal instead of racing a fixed deadline, or serialize the browser-backed tests) and the full suite passes 307/0 on three consecutive runs.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. scrollAndWaitForTransientGone()'s loop deadline moved from POLL_TIMEOUT (a single-poll budget) to LONG_TIMEOUT, the constant 22 other files use for multi-round-trip waits on this same assertion. Mutation-verified: with a slowed fade the test fails at 5247ms under POLL_TIMEOUT and passes under LONG_TIMEOUT; wiping the persistent overlay still fails in 150-300ms with a field-level assertion, so the test is not tautological. NOT a fix for the reported 5s flake: the loop measures 1 iteration and 77-117ms, so that stall was ~50x its cost and came from concurrent npm test runs, ruled out of scope under oculist-3sx. Investigation also disproved this bead's implied premise that reduced motion fades slower: fadeActiveBeacons() has no motion conditional. 308/0 on three consecutive solo runs.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THIS BEAD RECORDS. Evidence from the oculist-1os reviewer, 2026-09-02, which changes what 'done' should mean here.

It ran the full suite four times on a loaded machine and got 306 pass / 1 fail EVERY time, with a DIFFERENT test failing each run, and never the one this bead names:

  npm test                    306/1  instant_scroll_close_reopen_no_stale_draw.test.js:241
  npm test                    306/1  color_picker_persistence.test.js, slider drag
  npm test                    306/1  mount-restore (oculist-la4), 17.3s timeout
  --test-concurrency=2        306/1  'dim set holds exactly the inactive terms ranges', 30.1s timeout

All four are timeout-shaped and ALL FOUR PASS IN ISOLATION (it re-ran the first two individually: 1/1 and 3/3). Note the fourth failed even at concurrency 2, and at 30.1s, which is well beyond the 5000ms this bead describes.

WHAT THIS MEANS. beacon_fade_persistent_overlays:343 is not a special case, it is one sample from a suite-wide load sensitivity. So the done-criterion as written ('the full suite passes 307/0 on three consecutive runs') is measuring the MACHINE as much as the code, and fixing one test's timeout would not make that criterion reliably reachable. Whoever picks this up should treat the target as the contention family itself (see the test-suite-flake memory), not as one file.

Also note this reframes how much weight '307 pass / 0 fail' can carry as a gate. Several beads in the oculist-296 epic cite it as evidence. Those runs were real, but on a quiet machine; the same command on a loaded one produces a different failing test each time. That is worth knowing before anyone treats a single green run as proof.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
IMPORTANT CONFOUND, recorded 2026-09-02 before anyone spends effort on a fix.

The four-different-failures observation in my previous comment, and quite possibly this bead's original sighting, were both made WHILE OTHER AGENTS WERE RUNNING FULL SUITES ON THE SAME MACHINE. This session ran implementer and reviewer subagents back to back for hours, and several of them ran npm test concurrently with each other. node --test --test-concurrency=4 already saturates a machine; two or three of those at once is a load level no ordinary developer run produces.

So the evidence is CONFOUNDED. It is not clean evidence that the suite is broadly load-flaky in normal use, it is evidence that it degrades under self-inflicted parallel load. Note the counter-evidence from the same day: on quieter moments the same command returned 307 pass / 0 fail cleanly at least eight separate times across this session, including the run that closed oculist-296.7.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE FIX. Do not start by serializing the suite or scaling timeouts. Both carry a real, permanent cost (the test-suite-flake memory records concurrency 1 at 232-245s per run against roughly 67-95s at concurrency 4, so serializing is about a 3x slowdown on every run forever) and they would be paid to fix a load level that may never occur outside an orchestration session.

DO THIS FIRST: re-measure on a QUIET machine, nothing else running, several consecutive full runs at the default concurrency 4. If it is clean, this bead is about orchestration hygiene (do not run parallel full suites) rather than about the test suite, and it should be reframed or closed as such. If it still flakes when nothing else is running, the measurement is then trustworthy and the three options in the description are worth pricing.

THE CHOICE ITSELF IS AN OPERATOR DECISION, not an agent one, which is why this bead is being left open rather than guessed at. Raising timeouts weakens a real gate, per-test signal-awaiting is open-ended work across an unknown number of files, and serializing trades roughly 3x developer wait on every run for determinism. Those trade off against each other in a way the repo does not settle.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: One clean data point for the re-measurement above: immediately after the last subagent finished, with nothing else running on the machine, npm test returned 307 pass / 0 fail in 66.6s at the default concurrency 4. That is the fastest full run observed all session (contended runs were 78s, 84s, 93.7s). Consistent with the confound, though one run is not the several consecutive quiet runs the re-measurement calls for.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
MY 'not a defect' CONCLUSION WAS WRONG. Overturned 2026-09-02 by an independent re-measurement. Recording it properly so nobody re-derives the same mistake.

I ran five consecutive quiet-machine full suites, got 307/0 every time, and proposed closing this as orchestration hygiene. A reviewer then ran three more under the same quiet conditions and got:

  run 1  306 pass / 1 fail   86.3s   wizard_low_vision_palette_overlay.test.js:128, AssertionError, 1671ms
  run 2  305 pass / 0 fail / 2 CANCELLED  210.7s  beacon_fade_persistent_overlays.test.js:34, launchPersistentContext Timeout 180000ms exceeded
  run 3  307 pass / 0 fail   67.4s

Load averages before each run were 4.62, 15.22 and 4.54 on 10 cores, and pgrep found no leaked Chrome processes afterward.

WHY THIS BREAKS THE CONFOUND THEORY, on two independent counts:

1. Run 1's failure is an ASSERTION MISMATCH, not a timeout, on an idle machine. wizard_low_vision_palette_overlay.test.js runs 8 wizard cases against ONE SHARED chrome.storage.sync blob and never resets between cases. Its completion gate is (stored) => !!(stored && stored.setupWizardCompleted), and setupWizardCompleted goes true in case 1 and STAYS true, so for cases 2 through 8 the poll is VACUOUS and returns immediately with whatever is currently stored. The observed value, colorPalette 'amber-sky', is exactly the PRECEDING case's expected blob: the test asserted on the previous case's settings before its own write landed. The same file uses waitForTimeout(400) as its step-advance, which is precisely the 'racing a fixed deadline' anti-pattern this bead's own done-criteria names. Wrong by construction; it passes only when the write happens to land fast.

2. Run 2's 180s browser-launch timeout also happened with nothing else running. 51 of 58 test files call launchPersistentContext, at --test-concurrency=4. THE SUITE CONTENDS WITH ITSELF. So contention is real but INTRINSIC, and 'do not run subagents in parallel' does not remove it. My theory was not wrong that parallel orchestration made things worse; it was wrong that removing it makes the suite sound.

THE 30.1s FAILURE AT CONCURRENCY 2 IS EXPLAINED, and it exposes a gap. Nothing in dim_highlight.test.js has a 30s budget; every wait there uses POLL_TIMEOUT (5000ms). The 30s is PLAYWRIGHT'S DEFAULT ACTION TIMEOUT, applying to un-timeouted locator calls (page.locator(INPUT).fill(term) in addTerm, page.locator(CHIP_TERM).nth(i).click() in clickChip). So an element failed actionability for 30 straight seconds, which is a categorically deeper stall than a poll expiring. Critically, OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE does NOT scale it: the knob in test/helpers/wait.js only scales the 5s and 15s constants. The three observed budgets map cleanly onto 5s POLL_TIMEOUT, 17.3s vs 15s LONG_TIMEOUT, and 30.1s vs the Playwright default.

VARIANCE IS ITSELF THE FINDING. Quiet-machine runs spanned 67s to 210s, a 3x spread on an idle machine with a tail that reaches outright failure.

DONE-CRITERIA STATUS: BOTH HALVES FAIL. 'The measurement was confounded' explains why the earlier evidence was unreliable; it does not identify why any test fails, so the cause is not identified. And 307/0 on three consecutive runs was not achieved (307/0 once in three).

THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN. The orchestration-hygiene rule is true and worth recording, but it is a precondition for trustworthy MEASUREMENT, not a resolution. Do not close on it.

Two concrete items split out into their own beads rather than expanded here.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Left OPEN and now blocked on oculist-8ou, which covers the launchPersistentContext capacity problem that hit this very file (beacon_fade_persistent_overlays.test.js:34, 180s launch timeout on an idle machine). The separate wizard stale-read defect the investigation turned up is oculist-leu.

What remains specifically for THIS bead once 8ou lands: re-measure beacon_fade_persistent_overlays:343's original 5s timeout and decide whether it still reproduces once browser-launch contention is addressed. comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:

That fix CANNOT help this bead: it is a no-op at the default scale, and it applies to a context only after launchPersistentContext resolves.

The real blocker is oculist-3sx, the launch-capacity split from 8ou's finding 2. That is the failure mode that hit this very file (beacon_fade_persistent_overlays.test.js:34, launchPersistentContext Timeout 180000ms on an idle machine), so this bead now depends on it instead.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:

title: Stray v1.7.0 tag in the OUTER workspace repo predates the release
description:
Found by the oculist-296.5 reviewer on 2026-09-02, PRE-EXISTING, not created by this epic.

THE FACT: the OUTER workspace repo (/Users/ccho/Documents/Projects/oculist) carries an annotated tag v1.7.0 dated 2026-08-30 16:47, created before the epic branch was even checked out (2026-09-01 23:59). The CODE repo (repo/) correctly has only v1.5.0.

WHY IT MATTERS: oculist-296.6 asks the human to tag v1.7.0. If they run that in the wrong directory the tag already exists there, and if anyone reads the outer repo's tags as release history it says v1.7.0 shipped on 2026-08-30, which is false. Nothing shipped.

DECIDE, human call: delete the stray outer tag, or leave it and document what outer-repo tags mean. Agents never tag or delete tags, so this bead reports the proposed command and stops.

DONE WHEN: the outer tag is either deleted by the human or explicitly documented as intentional, and oculist-296.6's instructions name the correct repo for the real tag.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
DOCUMENTATION HALF DONE (2026-09-02). The outer v1.7.0 tag is now documented as intentional in the outer workspace's .agents/rules/vcs.md: kept deliberately because it is already published to the outer remote, explicitly NOT a release, not to be read as version history.

VERIFIED TODAY, all claims hold:
- Local tag object eb732fa == remote refs/tags/v1.7.0 (ya8282/oculist-workspace). It really is published; deleting it would rewrite a public ref.
- Peels to 8862e03, 'docs(store): correct the false claims the v1.5.0 doc was seeding', committed 2026-08-30 15:33 -0400. Tag object itself tagged 2026-08-30 16:47 -0400. Both dates land on 2026-08-30, so the '2026-08-30' in vcs.md is accurate for either reading.

REMAINING, unchanged: this bead's DONE WHEN also requires oculist-296.6's instructions to name repo/ as the repo for the real v1.7.0 tag. Leaving this bead open for that plus the human's explicit keep-or-delete call; vcs.md documents the keep, but no decision was ever recorded here, which is why the vcs.md citation 'decision 2026-09-02, see bead oculist-296.8' pointed at an empty bead until now.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Closed in 8cc3f39 on the OUTER repo's epic/oculist-bead-loop branch. Resolved by DOCUMENTING, per the human's decision on 2026-09-02: the tag stays.

Deciding factor beyond preference: the stray tag is already pushed to the outer remote (git ls-remote --tags origin shows refs/tags/v1.7.0 peeling to 8862e036), so deleting it would mean removing published history rather than dropping a local ref.

Written to .agents/rules/vcs.md, which the workspace CLAUDE.md already instructs agents to read before any git operation but which did not exist. Filling a documented gap rather than inventing a location.

REVIEWER FAILED THE FIRST DRAFT on a FALSE CLAIM, which is worth recording given this file's purpose. It said 'the extension is still unreleased'. The extension has been on the Chrome Web Store since v1.0.0: repo/README.md links the live listing, CHANGELOG.md:114 says 'Published to the Chrome Web Store', and the v1.5.0 tag message says the same. The true statement is that v1.7.0 has not shipped and the live listing still carries v1.0.0 copy. A rules file that is wrong is worse than no rules file, and that error pointed the wrong way for anyone working epic oculist-296, whose entire job is replacing a live listing.

TWO TRAPS FOUND WHILE VERIFYING, both now in the file:
1. Both repos can sit on identically-named branches simultaneously (they both were, on epic/oculist-bead-loop), so the branch name is not a cue for which repo you are in. Check the remote or the path.
2. repo/ has BRANCHES named v1.5.0 and v1.6.0 alongside the v1.5.0 TAG. So bare 'v1.5.0' is ambiguous and git warns. Verified resolution, having first gotten it wrong myself: bare v1.5.0 gives 2b10435, the annotated TAG OBJECT, not the branch and not the tag's target. refs/tags/v1.5.0^{} gives commit 2554612; refs/heads/v1.5.0 gives commit c5a00d7. Three different shas from one name. That is also why for-each-ref prints the tag's short name as 'tags/v1.5.0'.

The date in the file is the TAG's creation date (2026-08-30 16:47:17), stated as 'tagged 2026-08-30' to distinguish it from the pointed-at commit's own date of 15:33:51 the same day.

title: build.js asserts a hardcoded 11-file list, so a genuinely new extension file ships unverified
description:
Found by the oculist-296.2 reviewer on 2026-09-02, adjacent to that bead and not attributable to it.

THE SITE: build.js:22 defines

  const required = ['manifest.json', 'background.js', 'settings-migration.js', 'content.js',
                    'popup.html', 'popup.js', 'welcome.html', 'welcome.js',
                    'icon16.png', 'icon48.png', 'icon128.png'];

and then fails the build if any of those are missing from the zip.

THE GAP: that is a one-directional check. It proves the eleven KNOWN files are present. It cannot notice a TWELFTH file that extension/ gains later, because nothing compares the zip's file set against extension/'s actual contents. A new runtime file would be zipped (the zip step is a recursive 'zip -r .', so it would make it in) but it would ship with no assertion coverage at all, and the day the zip step or an exclude pattern goes wrong for that file, the build stays green.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN SHRUGGING AT: this is the same failure family that already shipped a real defect. build.js's own comment records it: an older explicit file list silently omitted welcome.js, which shipped a DEAD ONBOARDING WIZARD to users. The recursive zip was the fix for that, and the required list is the guard that was added on top. The guard just kept the old list's blind spot in a smaller form. oculist-rnr.17 exists because of a related staleness problem. Three incidents in this area is enough to treat the class as real.

Note the risk is currently latent, not live: at HEAD, extension/ holds exactly these 11 files and the reviewer verified the zip's set matches extension/ 1:1. Nothing is broken today. This bead is about the guard not being able to see the next change.

DONE WHEN: build.js verifies SET EQUALITY between the zip's entries and extension/'s actual contents, rather than checking a hardcoded list for presence. Both directions must fail the build: a file in extension/ missing from the zip, and a file in the zip that is not in extension/. Keep the existing exclude semantics (dotfiles and __MACOSX are deliberately excluded, so they must be excluded from both sides of the comparison, not counted as a mismatch).

The check must actually fail when it should. Verify with two mutations: add a throwaway file to extension/ and confirm the build fails if it is excluded from the zip, and inject an unexpected entry into the archive and confirm the build fails. Revert both. A guard nobody proved can fail is not a guard, which is the whole lesson of the three incidents above.

Not urgent. extension/ has been stable at 11 files and nothing is currently mis-shipped.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Closed in ddafdbb on epic/oculist-followups. Reviewer PASS on the second pass.

build.js now derives the expected file set with a single find run inside extension/ and compares it as a SET against the zip's entries, both directions, replacing the hardcoded 11-name presence list.

FIRST REVIEW FAILED on a real bug the first implementation introduced, and it is worth recording because it is subtle. The hand-rolled recursive walk skipped dotfiles at EVERY depth, while zip's -x '.*' anchors at the START of the member name and so only excludes TOP-LEVEL dot entries. The two sides disagreed, and the disagreement produced a FALSE BUILD FAILURE on a legitimate tree: a vendored subfolder carrying a .eslintrc, or any sub/.gitkeep, would break packaging. Reproduced through the real build path as 'unexpected in zip: subdir/.nestedhidden'.

The fix mirrors zip's anchoring BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by hand: find . -type f -not -path './.*' -not -path './__MACOSX/*'. The reviewer sandboxed both tools against the same tree and diffed the resulting sets: IDENTICAL across .topdot, .hiddendir/inside.js, __MACOSX/junk.js, subdir/.nestedhidden, subdir/__MACOSX/mac.js, subdir/nested.js, and a bare top-level FILE named __MACOSX. Positive cases now pass: clean tree 11 files, nested dotfile 12 files, nested plain file 13 files.

HONEST SCOPE OF THE GUARD, stated in the comment rather than oversold. 'missing from zip' is the live direction that catches a real packaging failure. 'unexpected in zip' CANNOT catch a stray file, because build.js:14 unlinks the zip and :18 regenerates it from extension/ every run, so membership is a pure function of extension/ minus the excludes and zip -r cannot invent a file. It is kept as a consistency assertion that the two exclude filters still agree, which is exactly the bug above.

SYMLINKS, deliberately left alone. find -type f matches neither a symlink nor anything under a symlinked directory without -L, while zip -r stores both, so a symlink in extension/ fails the build. The reviewer judged that CORRECT rather than a defect: zip -r follows a symlinked directory out of the tree (its sandbox pulled ../real/inner.js into the archive as linkdir/inner.js), so a store artifact silently absorbing out-of-tree files is a real problem and failing loudly is the right response. Note the obvious fix, find -L, would be actively WORSE: it would make the guard bless exactly that smuggling. Do not 'fix' this later without reading this note.

Size: net +3 lines. Logic shrank about 8 lines; the comment grew about 11, which was requested.

title: Verify the five store screenshots still match the shipped UI
description:

Confirm the commit list yourself rather than trusting the above:
  git log --oneline --since='2026-08-31 09:40' -- extension/welcome.html extension/welcome.js extension/popup.html extension/popup.js

STEPS:

2. For each of the five screenshots, identify which UI surface it shows and confirm that surface's markup and strings at HEAD still match what the image depicts. You cannot see the images, so work from the filenames and the captions in artifacts/outputs/store-submission-v1.7.0.md (around line 102), which state what each screenshot is supposed to demonstrate.
3. Pay particular attention to 05-vision-profiles.png and 04-settings.png. The functional-preset conversion (oculist-rnr.12, rnr.13) reworked welcome.html and popup.html substantially. Confirm those changes predate the 2026-08-31 09:40 capture, so the screenshots already show the converted UI rather than the old clinical-label UI. This is the one real risk in this task.
4. Confirm there are exactly five PNGs at top level and each is 1280x800 (the store caps the set at five). Use a tool that reads actual PNG dimensions, not the filename.

DONE WHEN:
• The commit list since capture is enumerated and each entry judged visual or non-visual, with reasoning.

title: trail_effect.test.js:657 can miss the flash entirely: waitForSelector on a self-cleaning element times out as a false contention signature

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Fixed in 7fcbe50 on epic/oculist-6j7. A MutationObserver is armed in the page's MAIN world before replay() runs (so before its internal cancelBeacons() and Enter press), latching appeared on the flash's add record and disappeared on its remove record. The two proofs are kept as two separate waits.

Reviewer PASS. Full suite 307 pass / 0 fail, trail_effect 9/9 across repeated runs, extension/content.js untouched. The reviewer verified the ordering guard EMPIRICALLY rather than by reading: it ran a Chromium MutationObserver harness against the exact callback shape and confirmed that add+remove in one synchronous task arrives as two separate records in one batch (so appeared latches first), and that a removal with no preceding add refuses to latch at all. Mutations: suppressing the appendChild fails at the first wait; suppressing flash.remove() fails at the second and ONLY in this test.

COVERAGE GAIN, not a narrowing. The old second wait was the broad .oc-beacon length === 0; the new one is flash-specific. The broad check still exists in its own test. Under the never-removed mutation the broad test PASSED while the new flash check FAILED, so the flash-specific wait catches something the old one did not.

JUDGMENT RECORDED, decided against and worth not relitigating: we considered wrapping the waits in a rethrow with a message saying a timeout here is a genuine regression rather than contention, since that misattribution is this bead's whole motivation. REJECTED. Contention can genuinely time out at these lines too (the flash chain is duration + flashDuration, and a loaded box can blow 5000ms), so such a message would assert something the test cannot determine. That would trade a triage annoyance for a fresh instance of this repo's worst recurring defect class, comments that describe something other than reality. What was shipped instead is free and honest: the two-wait split makes 'never rendered' and 'never removed' fail on DIFFERENT line numbers, which is the distinction a triager actually needs.

Also cleaned up while in here: the FLASH constant became unused once this test stopped using waitForSelector, so it was removed and the four historical d5c comments that named it now name '.oc-trail-flash' literally. Three comment inaccuracies in the new block were corrected before commit (a claim that flash.remove() was a DOM node, a wrong chronological-ordering justification for the within-record walk, and a claim that the render proof fails fast when it in fact times out at 5000ms).

title: full-suite flake list is out of date: trail_effect's WCAG absorption-flash guard fails under concurrency too
description:

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Intelligence from the oculist-1rf reviewer (epic/oculist-goal-7 run, 2026-09-01), gathered while reading trail_effect.test.js. Does NOT resolve this bead - narrows it.

MECHANISM 321bae6 PLAUSIBLY INTRODUCED: the new finally { scrollTo(0,0) } changed the scroll PRECONDITION for every case after :518. Fixture is a 4000px spacer with #target below it, viewport 800px. Pre-1rf the flash-geometry case left the page parked at desiredScrollY (match centred), so the next replay() found isFullyInViewport===true and drew on a flat 50ms timer. Post-1rf the match is ~4000px out of view, so the next replay() takes the out-of-viewport SMOOTH-SCROLL branch (content.js:5059-5135): triggerAutoScrollFlag(), smooth scrollIntoView, animate() deferred until scrollend / an 80ms debounce / a 600ms fallback timer. The fixture's own comment at :22-26 already names this hazard ('slow enough during smooth-scroll-into-view to make the beacon's own arrival flaky against a 5s timeout').

CONCRETE PATH TO THE :544 WCAG CASE: the 600ms fallback setTimeout(onScrollEnd,600) can fire and animate() while the smooth scroll is still in flight, so the preceding case at :522 can resolve its waitForSelector with the viewport still moving; :544's replay() then measures getBoundingClientRect() mid-scroll and can itself re-enter the smooth branch. Separately triggerAutoScrollFlag()'s window is 800ms; a residual scroll landing after it expires makes handleScroll -> fadeActiveBeacons() remove .oc-trail-flash on a 50ms timer, which would make :549's querySelector return null and :550's .getAnimations()[0] throw a TypeError inside page.evaluate.

DISCRIMINATOR THIS GIVES US: the FAILURE SHAPE tells us which. A 5s waitForFunction/waitForSelector TIMEOUT points at the smooth-scroll-arrival hazard; a TypeError inside page.evaluate points at the fade-removal race. Capture the shape, not just the name.

RULED OUT: fadeActiveBeacons() (content.js:5210-5242) captures a STATIC NodeList and its 50ms removal loop only touches captured elements, so a stale fade timer from an earlier case cannot remove a beacon drawn by a later case. That cross-test-removal theory is dead.

title: __ocDestroy() leaves activeScrollDebounceTimer set, so a close+reopen during a smooth scroll paints a stale border on the fresh overlay
description:
DEMONSTRATED by the oculist-rbx reviewer, with an instrumented build. Same class as oculist-rbx (commit 3ddc082), different teardown path.

__ocDestroy() at extension/content.js:986-998 clears activeScrollTimeout and both scroll listeners, but NOT activeScrollDebounceTimer - the exact omission rbx just fixed at the smooth-scroll branch entry.

It is reachable because window.__ocToggle (extension/content.js:7427-7434) calls __ocDestroy() and then buildUI() in the SAME module instance, so wrap becomes non-null again. The 'animate() early-returns on !wrap' argument does NOT hold - that reasoning was offered during rbx and falsified empirically.

Reviewer trace:
  {t:877 branch-entry} {t:877 armed}
  {t:932 destroy, adt:true}      // activeScrollDebounceTimer NOT cleared
  {t:935 toggle, wrap:false}     // rebuild -> wrap non-null
  {t:1004 via:'debounce-timer', already:false, wrap:true}
  => border drawn at top:6114.59px, scrollY 5726

Result: a stale border for the OLD match is painted on a freshly reopened, empty overlay. Trigger is a close+reopen within ~80ms of an in-flight smooth scroll - which is what the Ctrl+F command and the toggle/destroy messages invoke.

DONE WHEN: __ocDestroy() clears activeScrollDebounceTimer alongside activeScrollTimeout; a regression test drives close+reopen during an in-flight smooth scroll and asserts no stale border on the reopened overlay; it fails pre-fix and passes post-fix. See oculist-rbx's test for the probe shape.
close_reason: Closed

title: repositionActiveOverlays replays the accessibility overlays' entrance animations, so they blink on every settings change and every resize
description:
Found by the oculist-2c5 reviewer, which disproved 2c5's stated mechanism but found the user-facing harm is real.

repositionActiveOverlays() tears down and RE-CREATES the overlays. Every overlay constructor starts at opacity:0 and replays its entrance animation: drawActiveMatchBorder a 200ms fade, drawActiveMatchLabel a 250ms fade, drawActiveMatchMagnifier a 320ms zoom-lift including a 40px translate and a rescale.

DOM presence is continuous, so a MutationObserver sees nothing wrong - which is why oculist-2c5's first pass missed it. Measured per-element COMPUTED opacity instead:

  borderStyle thick->thin     border   opacity<0.95 for 15 frames, t=75..245ms (starts at 0)
                              magnifier                 20 frames, t=75..328ms (starts at 0, plus the lift)
  textLabels toggle           border 15 frames 68..247 | magnifier 21 frames 68..317
  motionSensitivity->reduced  border 13 frames 78..269 | magnifier 14 frames 78..278
  window resize 1200->1100    border 13 frames 223..398 | magnifier 18 frames 223..471

So the indicator blinks to invisible and ramps back over 13-21 painted frames, on every overlay-affecting vision-settings change and on every window resize (handleResize -> overlayResizeTimer -> repositionActiveOverlays, extension/content.js:5079).

WHY IT MATTERS: same reason 2c5 gave. Anyone adjusting a vision setting is by definition relying on these overlays, and the adjustment makes the match indicator blink. Resize hits everyone.

It also contradicts repositionActiveOverlays()'s own comment at content.js:3685-3690, which says it deliberately does not replay the beacon effect because that is noise for exactly these users. It does not replay the TRANSIENT effect, but it does replay the accessibility overlays' own entrances.

FIX DIRECTION: a settings change or resize does not move the match relative to the page, so the overlays need repositioning, not re-creation. Either update the existing elements' geometry and style in place, or suppress the entrance animation on a reposition-driven redraw (draw them at their final opacity). Prefer in-place update if the element set is unchanged; fall back to redraw-without-entrance when a setting actually adds or removes an overlay.
close_reason: Closed

title: changing a vision setting tears the active overlays down for ~400ms before the debounced rescan redraws them
description:
Found while debugging a flake in test/beacon_fade_persistent_overlays.test.js. Not a test artifact - measured against the real extension.

With a match active and its overlays drawn, changing a vision setting (measured with visionSettings.motionSensitivity) makes content.js:
  1. redraw the persistent overlays immediately, then
  2. remove them again about a frame later, then
  3. leave NOTHING drawn until a debounced rescan redraws everything ~400ms later.

MutationObserver trace on .oc-beacon, timestamps relative to the settings write:
  185 - transient
  188 - persistent, + persistent
  189 - persistent          <- nothing drawn from here
  581 + persistent, + transient
  618 - both, + both

So there is a ~390ms window with no border, no label, no shape and no magnifier on screen, followed by a second full teardown/redraw at 618.

WHY IT MATTERS: the whole point of the persistent overlays is that a low-vision user can keep track of where the match is. Anyone adjusting a vision setting is, by definition, in that group, and the adjustment itself makes the match indicator vanish and then flicker. The 618 cycle means it flashes twice.

WORTH CHECKING FIRST: whether step 2's removal is a bare cancelBeacons() that should have been followed by a redraw, or whether the redraw is simply deferred behind the rescan debounce and could reuse the existing overlays instead of tearing them down. A settings change does not move the match, so the overlays did not need to be removed at all.

REPRO: see the churn-observer in test/beacon_fade_persistent_overlays.test.js's fireAndTagBeacon (commit 4880dba) - it exists precisely to wait this window out.

title: the reduced-motion spotlight overlay is position:fixed and never tracks scroll
description:
Reviewer finding during oculist-9t5. Pre-existing. oculist-9t5 mitigates the symptom without fixing it.

extension/content.js's animateReducedMotion(), for displayPreset === 'reduced-motion', draws a dark spotlight overlay at around :3097-3104: position fixed, top/left/right/bottom 0, with a radial-gradient hole centred at 'cx px cy px' taken from the raw rect.left / rect.top - i.e. VIEWPORT coordinates, computed once and never recomputed.

Its siblings in the same function (the glow, the arrows) use rect.left + window.scrollX, i.e. document coordinates, and track scroll correctly. Only the spotlight is wrong.

Effect: on the first scroll the darkened mask stays fixed on screen while the actual match moves out from under it, so the hole points at whatever now happens to be at those coordinates. For a low-vision user relying on the spotlight to say 'the match is HERE', that is an overlay that lies.

oculist-9t5 now fades this beacon on scroll, which limits the exposure - but the mask still misrepresents the match for the ~50ms of the fade, and for any scroll that the fade does not cover.

FIX, pick one and say why:
- recompute cx/cy from the live range rect when the page scrolls, or
- render the overlay position:absolute sized to the document with the gradient centred at rect.left + scrollX / rect.top + scrollY, so it scrolls with the page like its siblings. This is the smaller change and matches what the rest of the function already does.

Note repositionActiveOverlays() (around :3618) exists for exactly this class of problem but currently runs on resize only and deliberately skips the beacon - see its comment before extending it, since re-running the beacon effect on every scroll is explicitly NOT wanted.

TEST: under displayPreset 'reduced-motion', run a search, scroll, and assert the gradient centre still corresponds to the match's current viewport position.

title: drawActiveMatchLabel and drawActiveMatchMagnifier remove overlays without cancelling their WAAPI animations
description:
Found during the oculist-qii audit of every .oc-beacon removal site. Same omission as oculist-qii, different call sites, and neither is one of the effects' own completion self-removals.

extension/content.js's drawActiveMatchLabel (around :3321) and drawActiveMatchMagnifier (around :3384) each replace a previous same-id overlay with a bare existing.remove(). The overlay being replaced may still have live entries in __waapiAnims - a 250ms label fade, a magnifier lift of up to about 470ms.

Why it matters: as cancelBeacons()'s own comment records, WAAPI animations do NOT stop when their target is detached. playState stays 'running' and currentTime keeps advancing unless .cancel() is called explicitly. So each replacement leaks a running Animation object on a detached element. Rapid next/previous navigation replaces these overlays repeatedly, so the leak accumulates for as long as the user keeps moving through matches.

Lower severity than oculist-qii: these are DOM/WAAPI overlays, not canvas rAF loops, so nothing reads a nulled hook and nothing can throw. It is wasted work and retained detached nodes, not a crash.

FIX: route both sites through the destroyBeacon(b) helper oculist-qii introduces (cancelAnimationFrame on __rafId, cancel every __waapiAnims entry, then remove), rather than adding a third copy of that teardown. If destroyBeacon's name reads wrong for a label or magnifier rather than a beacon, rename it to something neutral in the same change - one teardown, one name, every caller.

DEPENDS ON oculist-qii, which introduces the helper. Do not land this first.

TEST: mirror test/waapi_beacon_cancel.test.js. Navigate to a second match while the first match's label or magnifier animation is still running, and assert the replaced overlay's __waapiAnims entries reach 'idle' rather than staying 'running'.

title: content.js onChanged listener never refreshes the settings merge base
description:
Reviewer follow-up from oculist-xvh. That bead gave the page-side writers a three-way merge (OculistSettingsMigration.writeOcSettings) against a per-context base snapshot recorded by rememberOcSettings().

content.js's chrome.storage.onChanged listener (around extension/content.js:7222) updates the in-memory 'settings' object from a foreign write but never calls rememberOcSettings(), so 'base' stays at the boot snapshot until this tab's own next successful write.

Losing sequence, needs two foreign writes to the same key straddling a local save:
1. base.X = v1 at boot.
2. Foreign write sets X = v2. The listener adopts v2 into in-memory settings; base still says v1.
3. Foreign write sets X = v3. Suppose the listener has not yet applied it, or the tab saves first.
4. This tab calls saveSettings(). The merge sees local.X (v2) != base.X (v1), so it treats v2 as a local edit and it wins -> v3 is silently reverted to v2.

Narrow, but exactly the lost-update class oculist-xvh set out to close, so it should not be left standing.

FIX: call OculistSettingsMigration.rememberOcSettings() from the onChanged listener whenever it adopts a foreign change, so base tracks what the tab believes storage holds. Take care that base and the in-memory settings object are updated from the SAME payload and in the same pass - if base advances but the local object does not, a genuine local edit is lost instead, which is the worse direction.

Note content.js only merges SETTINGS_KEYS into its in-memory settings, while base should reflect the whole stored object. Decide deliberately whether rememberOcSettings() is handed the full new stored value or only the allowlisted subset, and write down which and why - the merge's deletion rule (a key in base but absent from local is treated as a deliberate deletion) makes this choice load-bearing. See the comment at extension/settings-migration.js:161-171.

Verify all line references against current files before acting.

title: PRIVACY.md says the reseed runs on every update, but it also runs on install
description:
Confirmed independently by two reviewers during oculist-3yi. A genuine scope understatement in a user-facing privacy disclosure, which is the unsafe direction.

PRIVACY.md (around lines 70-71) says the default disabled-sites reseed 'runs once on every update'. The code runs it on INSTALL too: seedDefaultBlocklist() is called at extension/background.js:198, directly in the onInstalled listener body and OUTSIDE the 'if (details.reason === 'install')' check at :199, so it is unconditional for every reason the event fires.

Why it matters rather than being a nit: a disclosure that understates when a step runs is narrower than the code, and narrower is the unsafe direction for a privacy policy. Everywhere else in these documents the wording is deliberately kept broader than the code.

Not purely theoretical on install: on a REINSTALL with Chrome Sync restoring a previous settings object, details.reason === 'install' and the seed runs against a non-empty object that may still carry a legacy key. It is only harmless on a genuinely fresh profile, where the object is empty and there is nothing to carry forward.

FIX: change 'runs once on every update' to cover install as well, e.g. 'runs once on every install and every update'. Note artifacts/outputs/store-submission-v1.7.0.md (OUTER repo) already documents this mismatch in its data-usage commentary and quotes PRIVACY.md verbatim, so all three files move together:
  repo/PRIVACY.md
  repo/docs/privacy.html   (KEEP IN SYNC pair)
  ../artifacts/outputs/store-submission-v1.7.0.md  (verbatim quote plus the note recording the mismatch, which can then be removed)

title: animateChronoTunnel and animateCyberVision share the stale-__ocTest-hook defect
description:
Sibling survey done during oculist-47e, confirmed independently by that bead's reviewer. The pattern holds in 3 of 3 effects that hang test state off __ocTest, so it is systemic to the idiom rather than isolated.

oculist-47e fixed animateSpeedLines: its early-return guard (rect.width===0 || rect.height===0) sat ahead of every __ocTest assignment, so a skipped run left all ten hooks holding the PREVIOUS run's values. A test polling speedLinesDone === true would resolve instantly off stale state and grade everything else against that stale run.

SAME DEFECT, NOT YET FIXED:
1. animateChronoTunnel (extension/content.js ~2638): the guard precedes lastChronoHueRun (~2721), lastChronoAnchor (~2726), chronoFrameCount (~2727) and chronoDone (~2728).
   This one is arguably WORSE than speed lines was: lastChronoHueRun.hueSamples.push(...) runs inside the frame loop, so a stale object keeps ACCUMULATING samples across runs rather than merely being read stale.
2. animateCyberVision (extension/content.js ~2827): the guard precedes cyberVisionBracketsSettled (~3000).

NOT AFFECTED, verified: animateTrail and animateDispersion contain no __ocTest references, and neither do the other nine animate* functions. There are 59 __ocTest lines in the file, none inside those functions and none after ~3002.

title: Page-side settings writers have no lost-update protection
description:
Reviewer follow-up from oculist-b65. That bead hardened only background.js; this is the larger half of the same race surface.

oculist-b65 gave extension/background.js's updateSettings() confirm-then-retry optimistic concurrency so a concurrent write landing in its get-to-set gap is detected and recovered. The page-side writers got no equivalent and each still does a bare read-modify-write or a bare set:
- extension/content.js:71 saveSettings() does a bare chrome.storage.sync.set
- extension/popup.js:195 and :395
- extension/welcome.js:833 saveProfileAndFinish()

Any two of these racing each other, or racing background.js, can still silently lose a write. Same permanence problem as b65: content.js:7217's onChanged handler guards per key with 'if (!(k in nv)) return;', so a key erased by a clobbering write produces no change entry and an open tab keeps its stale in-memory value indefinitely.

Realistic shape: the popup and an open page both writing settings, or the welcome wizard finishing while a content script persists something.

Likely fix: lift b65's confirm-then-retry into a shared helper both surfaces use. Note background.js is a service worker loading settings-migration.js via importScripts, while the page surfaces load it as a script tag, so the helper needs to work in both contexts the way settings-migration.js already does.

Verify line references against current files before acting.

title: Revisit PRIVACY.md's reseed wording now that background.js normalizes on every write
description:
Filed during oculist-rnr.23 (2026-08-31). Retitled and written up because the original title, 'overstates current risk', with an EMPTY description, reads cold as a mandate to narrow a privacy disclosure to match code. It is not. Read the whole of this before touching PRIVACY.md.

WHAT CHANGED IN THE CODE. Two beads landed after PRIVACY.md's reseed paragraph was written:
- oculist-9s9 routed both onInstalled write sites through one updateSettings() helper and sequenced the performanceMode write inside seedDefaultBlocklist()'s done callback.
- oculist-hzr added importScripts('settings-migration.js') to background.js, so normalizeOcSettings() now runs at that single choke point ahead of every mutate() and set().
Net effect, verified by two agents: on the NORMAL path neither write can persist an unmigrated legacy visionProfile, including the case that originally motivated the concern (seededDefaultBlocklist already true from a cross-profile sync, seed early-returns, performanceMode write still normalizes).

WHY THIS IS NOT A DEFECT. PRIVACY.md's disclosure ('can write the old key back once, the next read removes it') is still TRUE. background.js declares OculistSettingsMigration = null and only assigns it inside a try/catch, so if importScripts ever fails (packaging mistake, or a browser without it) normalization is skipped for both write sites and the originally-disclosed behaviour is exactly what happens. The disclosure now describes that guarded fallback rather than the common case.

BEING BROADER THAN THE CODE IS THE SAFE DIRECTION FOR A PRIVACY DISCLOSURE. Do NOT narrow this text merely because the common path improved. If it is ever revisited:
1. Re-verify the importScripts guard still exists and still fails closed. If that guard is ever removed and normalization becomes unconditional, only THEN does the fallback disappear.
2. PRIVACY.md and docs/privacy.html are a KEEP IN SYNC pair. Any change lands in both or they diverge.
3. test/privacy_invariants.test.js asserts across both files. Read it first.
4. artifacts/outputs/store-submission-v1.7.0.md (outer repo) carries the reasoning above in its Health/Data-usage commentary and would need to stay consistent.

The genuinely useful outcome here may simply be a sentence in PRIVACY.md noting the re-persist is now limited to a fallback path, leaving the conservative claim intact. Verify all line references against current files before editing.

title: animateSpeedLines early-return leaves all __ocTest hooks (not just lastSpeedLinesContainerRect) holding the previous run's stale values
description:
animateSpeedLines(rect) returns early at the top (rect.width===0 || rect.height===0) before ANY of its __ocTest hooks are touched: lastSpeedLinesStreakCount, speedLinesFrameCount, lastSpeedLinesLaneAlphaMax, lastSpeedLinesElseAlphaMax, speedLinesHighlightDrawCount, speedLinesDone, lastSpeedLinesAnchor, lastSpeedLinesHighlightY, and lastSpeedLinesContainerRect are all reset/set together, well after the guard. On a skipped run every one of these retains the PREVIOUS run's value -- not just the container rect. A test that polls e.g. speedLinesDone === true would resolve immediately off stale prior-run state, then grade every other hook (including the container rect) against that same stale run, without ever surfacing that the current run never actually fired.

Noted while working oculist-gor (container rect is viewport-relative, scroll-staleness). Fixing lastSpeedLinesContainerRect's staleness alone would not close this exposure since speedLinesDone shares the identical gap, so it was deliberately left alone there for consistency with the rest of the hooks.

Fix direction: reset the whole set of speed-lines __ocTest hooks together at the very top of animateSpeedLines (before the early-return check), or introduce a shared "run started" marker/counter the test suite can check to detect a skipped run, rather than fixing one hook in isolation. No test currently exercises the rect.width===0 path, so this is a latent exposure, not a live failure.

title: background.js can still resurrect a legacy settings key the popup deleted
description:
Split out of oculist-9s9, which closed on a narrower fix (serializing background.js's own two writes). This half was verified still-open by that bead's reviewer.

REPRODUCED against the CURRENT code, not theoretical:
  T0 initial:      {disabledSites: [], visionProfile: 'legacy-deuteranopia'}
  T1 popup wrote:  {disabledSites: [], colorProfile: 'deuteranopia'}
  FINAL:           {disabledSites: ['github.com'], visionProfile: 'legacy-deuteranopia', seededDefaultBlocklist: true}
  visionProfile resurrected: true. popup's colorProfile: lost.

MECHANISM: seedDefaultBlocklist()'s get() is the first thing in the onInstalled listener and is no fresher than before oculist-9s9. If the popup normalizes settings and writes between that get() and its set(), background writes back the stale object, resurrecting the legacy key the popup just deleted and dropping the popup's own write. oculist-9s9 only shortened the performanceMode write's window, not the seed's.

WHY BACKGROUND IS THE ONLY PATH THAT CAN DO THIS: background.js does not load settings-migration.js, so its write-back never passes through normalizeOcSettings(). Every other surface normalizes.

THE REAL FIX is loading settings-migration.js into the service worker, which was deliberately scoped OUT of oculist-9s9 because it needs a manifest change. background.js is a classic (non-module) service worker per manifest.json, so importScripts('settings-migration.js') is the likely mechanism. Confirm that against the manifest before assuming it.

NOTE the user-visible outcome is already disclosed in the privacy policy ('can write the old key back once, the next read removes it'), so nothing is misstated to users. This is about the code.

Related: oculist-9s9 (closed), oculist-ex1 (the other storage-robustness bead from this run).

title: speed_lines Lite Mode test passes only because of test ordering
description:
Found by the oculist-z4s reviewer while verifying that bead's fix. PRE-EXISTING and verified against unmodified HEAD, so NOT caused by the z4s change.

test/speed_lines.test.js 'Lite Mode still draws the centre-line highlight on every frame' passes in the full suite but FAILS when run alone:
  node --test --test-name-pattern='Lite Mode still draws' test/speed_lines.test.js
It fails on .oc-beacon already being torn down. The reviewer confirmed it fails identically on the unmodified HEAD version, so this is latent order-dependence, not a regression.

Mechanism: the test's speedLinesDone wait is satisfied by a STALE flag left by a prior effect's orphaned rAF loop. replay() removes the container from the DOM without cancelling that loop, so the flag from the earlier run is still set when this test checks it. That is also why the atomic read lands mid-flight rather than after completion.

Consequences:
1. The test does not actually wait for its own effect to finish, so 'draws on every frame' is only ever checked over an arbitrary partial prefix of the run.
2. A release-gate suite contains a test that depends on execution order, which will surface as a mystery failure the first time someone runs it in isolation or the file order changes.

Fix direction: cancel the rAF loop in replay() (or scope the done flag per run) so the wait gates on THIS run's completion, then re-check what the assertion is actually covering.

Related: oculist-z4s (closed), oculist-8s5, oculist-3z6.
close_reason: Closed

title: loadWorkList/saveWorkList silently drop writes and reads denied by storage.session access level
description:
Product bug found while root-causing the oculist-z4s test flake. NOT a test-harness artifact. Assessed by the z4s reviewer as P3 hardening, not a release blocker.

MECHANISM (verified in code by two agents):
background.js:8-18 calls chrome.storage.session.setAccessLevel('TRUSTED_AND_UNTRUSTED_CONTEXTS') as fire-and-forget service-worker top-level code with only a .catch logger. There is no ordering relationship between that grant and content-script boot.

content.js:163-183 saveWorkList() guards only on chrome.storage.session being UNDEFINED. In the racing case the API is defined-but-denied, so the guard does not fire, and the rejection is swallowed twice: 'void chrome.runtime.lastError;' in the callback and 'setResult.catch(function () {});'. No retry, no log, no signal. A write that loses the race is dropped permanently.

Measured: 2 of 15 cold launches had the content-script write land before the access grant, once by only 9ms, each producing an immediate (~2ms) chrome.runtime.lastError 'Access to storage is not allowed from this context.'

REACHABILITY (reviewer's assessment):
- Write side is close to unreachable in production. All four persistWorkList() callers (content.js:4286, 4310, 4410, 5450) require an already-open overlay, which only opens after background.js round-trips the command, plus seconds of human typing before any write.
- READ side is the reachable one. buildUI()'s loadWorkList() (content.js:5909) fires one message hop after SW start and, on lastError, silently returns defaultWorkList(). The user sees their carried-over list vanish, and the next chip mutation then persists over the stored list.
- Mitigating: the access level is a property of the session storage area and normally survives SW restarts, so the vulnerable window is before the first successful grant, when session storage is empty anyway and the default is the correct answer. NOT confirmed from code whether Chrome ever resets it on SW restart. That uncertainty is the residual risk and is the thing to establish first.

SUGGESTED FIX: on an access-denied chrome.runtime.lastError, retry once (or gate first storage use on a background ready-ping) in BOTH loadWorkList and saveWorkList, and log instead of unconditionally swallowing. The unconditional swallow currently makes any real storage failure undiagnosable, which also cuts against this repo's debug-logging guideline.

Verify all line references against the current file before editing.

title: Wizard reset has no working regression guard
description:
Reviewer follow-up from oculist-rnr.13. The BEHAVIOUR is fixed and verified; the TEST that should guard it does not.

Removing resetWizardState() from openWizard() (extension/welcome.js:110) leaves all 6 tests in test/wizard_no_clinical_persistence.test.js GREEN, even though a probe under that mutation shows run 2 inheriting run 1's amber-indigo + low-vision answers and persisting high-contrast/xl.

Why test 6 misses it: it re-clicks step 2's first option instead of clicking straight through with Next, so it never exercises inheritance; and it never leaves step 1 on the sample tab, so its tab-reset assertion is vacuous too.

Steps:
1. Rewrite the second-run portion of test 6 to complete run 1 with NON-default answers, then re-run and click straight through with Next only, asserting the persisted settings are the defaults rather than run 1's values.
2. Leave step 1 on the SAMPLE tab at the end of run 1, then assert the re-run reopens on the NAMED tab with the sample panel hidden by computed style.

title: Mapping tables duplicated in popup.js and welcome.js instead of importing the module's export
description:
Reviewer follow-up from oculist-rnr.12 (non-blocking, work already shipped correctly).

extension/settings-migration.js is the canonical home for the legacy-to-functional mapping, and it EXPORTS the tables. But two consumers keep their own verbatim copies rather than referencing the export:
- extension/popup.js:104-111 LEGACY_TO_FUNCTIONAL_PRESET, a verbatim duplicate of LEGACY_DISPLAY_PRESET_MAP.
- extension/welcome.js:35-41 WIZARD_PROFILE_TO_DISPLAY_PRESET, the same table minus 'custom'.

They are consistent today, so nothing is broken. The risk is drift: a future edit to the canonical table silently diverges from two copies, and the module docstring's claim that it is 'the one place it lives' is true of the normaliser but not of the tables.

Steps:
1. Have popup.js and welcome.js reference the exported tables from window.OculistSettingsMigration instead of declaring their own.
2. Preserve welcome.js's 'custom' exclusion explicitly at the point of use rather than by maintaining a trimmed copy of the table.
3. If a copy must remain for load-order reasons, prove it with a test that asserts the copies equal the canonical table, so drift fails the suite.
4. Correct the module docstring to match whatever ends up true.

ALSO, from the same review: no test seeds visionProfile AND displayPreset together, so the hasOwnProperty precedence branch in settings-migration.js:71-78 (new field wins, legacy deleted) is verified by inspection only. Add that test - it guards the exact behaviour that prevents user data loss.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Reproduced on branch epic/oculist-store-v1.7.0 during the unattended /goal run, 2026-08-30.

Contention-dependent, not deterministic:
- Full suite: FAILED once (241 tests, 240 pass, 1 fail) at test/speed_lines.test.js:347, assertion 7 !== 5. An immediately preceding full run of the same tree had passed.
- Isolated (node --test test/speed_lines.test.js): 3/3 runs GREEN, 8 pass / 0 fail each.

Not a regression from this run's work: no commit on this branch touches speed_lines.test.js (verified with git log main..HEAD --name-only). The four commits touch the store doc, the wizard test, settings-migration.js + display_preset_migration.test.js, and welcome.js/welcome.html.

Independently, the oculist-rnr.19 reviewer saw the same file flake in 1 of 4 full-suite runs, alongside stale_mount_guard.test.js and worklist_storage.test.js in a single degraded run.

Reads as the same load-dependent non-determinism tracked in oculist-z4s rather than a distinct defect in the Lite Mode draw count. Deciding whether these are one root cause or two needs a human.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Resolved by oculist-z4s (commit 1fa03f0), not by separate work. Closing as a duplicate of that root cause.

This bead's symptom — speed_lines.test.js Lite Mode draw count off, 'expected 5, got 7' — was diagnosed under z4s as a SPLIT-READ RACE, not a frame-counting problem. The test read frames, draws, highlightY and the independent anchor in four separate round trips (3 raw CDP plus one slower Playwright page.evaluate) off a LIVE, still-running rAF loop. The counters advanced between reads, so the two numbers came from different instants of the same animation.

Fix: all four reads collapsed into one atomic isolated-world CDP evaluation, mirroring the readFrameAndDrawCounts() pattern already in that file. This eliminates the race structurally rather than widening a tolerance. No assertion was changed: frames > 0, strictEqual(draws, frames), the independent-anchor check and the 2px highlightY check are all preserved verbatim.

Note this bead's own earlier recommendation was to convert the exact frame count to a range. That turned out to be unnecessary — the exact strictEqual is correct once both numbers come from the same sample.

Verification: two independent reviewers confirmed the assertions were not weakened, and mutation probes (breaking the draw-count increment, and offsetting highlightY by 40px/200px) went RED. Across this run the full suite passed 10/10 (implementer), 5/5 (first reviewer, before the worklist fix) and 5/5 (second reviewer) sequential runs at 249/249.

CAVEAT, filed separately as oculist-viv: this same Lite Mode test passes only because of test ordering. Run alone it fails on .oc-beacon already being torn down, identically on unmodified HEAD. Its speedLinesDone wait is satisfied by a stale flag from a prior effect's orphaned rAF loop, so 'draws on every frame' is only checked over a partial prefix of the run. The 7 != 5 symptom this bead tracked is gone; the test guarding it is weaker than it appears.

title: Intermittent full-suite failure: strictEqual 1 !== 0, test name uncaptured
description: Observed once during the epic/oculist-dvt-cleanup final verification on 2026-08-28, AFTER the oculist-li8 concurrency cap (=4) landed: one full-suite run at OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE=3 failed a single assertion with code ERR_ASSERTION, strictEqual, actual 1, expected 0 - NOT the old LONG_TIMEOUT contention signature. Three other full-suite runs immediately around it were 206/206 green, so roughly 1-in-4 that session. The failing test's name was not captured (only the stack tail was seen). Plausible candidates are the new zero-leak assertions added this epic (test/waapi_beacon_cancel.test.js asserts 0 running animations and 0 .oc-beacon elements after cancel; several effect tests assert no .oc-beacon leaks), but this is unattributed - do not assume. NEXT STEP: run the full suite in a loop capturing per-run logs until the failure reproduces, then read the failing test name from the log and diagnose from there.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: CAPTURED with a name during the oculist-5v9 review full-suite run (2026-08-28, concurrency=4, SCALE=3): the strictEqual 1 !== 0 failure is 'drawActiveMatchMagnifier: cancelBeacons() mid-flight...' in test/waapi_beacon_cancel.test.js - passed 32/32 when its file reran in isolation. Same run also had two other load flakes: 'removing the active first chip of several activates the new leftmost chip' (CDP Promise was collected) and 'an unscanned chip after a carry-over restore has no count in its accessible name' (timeout, chip_count_accessibility - also flaked once during the oculist-3ak implementation run). So the 0d2 signature is a load-contention race in the magnifier cancel subtest, not a product regression; the suite has grown ~10 Playwright files since the concurrency cap was tuned. Diagnosis should start at the magnifier subtest's post-cancel assertion (expected 0, got 1 - likely one animation still 'running' when sampled under CPU starvation, or a beacon element count).

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Root-caused and fixed as a test race, no product bug. Mechanism: setVisionSettings({magnifier:true}) is an OVERLAY_AFFECTING_KEYS change, so with an active match present the onChanged handler synchronously draws an incidental magnifier card; fireBeacon()'s waitForSelector resolved on that card while Enter's own redraw sat in a setTimeout(50); under load the assert slipped past t=50 and the deferred animate() resurrected the card after count===0 - hence strictEqual 1 !== 0, full-suite-only, ~1 in 4-8 runs. Fix: one cancelBeaconsMidFlight() between the settings change and fireBeacon(). Both implementer and reviewer reproduced the race deterministically (artificial post-cancel delay: fails 4/4 pre-fix, passes 4/4 post-fix at 150ms and 400ms); the fix also strengthens the subtest (snapshot now captures 25 running animations from the genuine Enter draw vs 2 stale ones before). Five full-suite runs green across both passes.

title: Lists panel has the same unbounded-height overflow as oculist-6cd
description: Found by the oculist-6cd reviewer: #oc-lists-panel (extension/content.js:6846-6862) has the same unbounded-height pattern the settings panel had - no max-height, host overflow hidden - so on short viewports the lists popover clips unreachably. Apply the same fix as oculist-6cd (max-height calc(100vh - bar chrome) + overflow-y auto) and cover it with a viewport-600 Playwright test at all four bar positions. Minor related notes from the same review, address while in there: the 44px barChromePx literal has ~3px slack and its comment credits the wrong tallest child (input.oc-input ~27px, not the 26px button); flex-shrink:0 on .oc-settings-header/.oc-settings-grid is currently inert, comments overstate it.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Premise correction discovered during implementation: the lists panel was not literally unbounded - it had a flat max-height:320px, which only clips unreachably on viewports shorter than ~360px (bar ~41px + 320px cap). At the bead's suggested vh=600 the old code never clipped. Fix replaces the flat cap with calc(100vh - barChromePx) matching oculist-6cd; regression test runs at vh=300 where old code demonstrably failed 4/4 positions (host bottom 361>300 top-anchored, host top -61 bottom-anchored). Also landed the 6cd review's comment corrections: barChromePx arithmetic now credits input.oc-input (~27px) as tallest bar child with 3px slack stated honestly, and the flex-shrink:0 comments no longer overstate an inert guard.

title: Nothing ties the effect enumerations to the registry
description:
Recommended by the oculist-dvt.6 re-reviewer, who noted this test would have caught that bead's own original miss.

Three prose sites now enumerate all 13 effects, plus one hardcoded count: extension/welcome.html:226 ('Choose from 13 effects - ...'), docs/index.html:497, docs/index.html:578. All four facts must be hand-synced against effectsRegistry (extension/content.js:685-699) and NOTHING in the suite ties them together. Adding a 14th effect silently makes four sites wrong, and a short stale list just looks like a list - only the numeric count reads as obviously wrong once it drifts.

This is exactly how the pre-existing Bloom/Trail omission survived unnoticed through two releases: both docs lists sat at 7 effects while the registry had 9.

FIX: one test that parses the i18n labels out of effectsRegistry in declaration order, then asserts each of the three prose sites contains all of them IN ORDER, and that the digit in 'N effects' equals the registry size. Model the label extraction on what the dvt.6 reviewer did. Keep it a static source scan like test/privacy_invariants.test.js - no browser needed.

DONE: adding a 14th registry entry without updating the three prose sites fails a test that names which site is stale.
close_reason: Closed

title: extension/welcome.html effect list is stale (missing Bloom, Trail, and 4 new effects)
description: extension/welcome.html line 226 (prose) and the effect <select> options (lines ~291-297) enumerate only 6 effects (Spotlight, Anime Laser, Warp Drive, Inferno Flame, Lightning, Electron Cloud, Pointing Arrows) and are missing Bloom, Trail, Speed Lines, Chrono Tunnel, Light Cycle, Cyber-Vision. Also note: the <option value="hud"> is labelled 'Spotlight' in welcome.html but content.js's effectsRegistry maps hud -> effectAnimeLaser (Anime Laser runs on hud); value="iris" is the actual Spotlight effect. Worth checking if welcome.html's option values are stale/mismatched too. Out of scope for oculist-dvt.6 because extension/ is explicitly DO NOT TOUCH in that bead's brief.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION and description fixes, from the oculist-dvt.6 review. 1. The PROSE enumeration at extension/welcome.html:226 has been REMOVED from this bead's scope - it is being fixed inside oculist-dvt.6 itself, because it is a plain

of onboarding copy and the dvt.6 done-criterion covers 'every place in the repo that enumerates effects'. What remains here is only the functional either uses the real registry keys and labels, or carries a comment stating explicitly that its vocabulary is deliberately separate and non-persisting.

title: Settings panel overflows a 600px viewport regardless of effect count
description:
Measured precisely by the oculist-dvt.5 reviewer on 2026-08-28 with real Chromium geometry. PRE-EXISTING and independent of the effect registry's size: at the pre-epic commit bfaaca8 with only 9 effects, the panel host measured 686.4px tall, already 86.4px over a 600px viewport. oculist-dvt.5's scroll cap brought the 13-effect panel DOWN to 674.4px - shorter than the old 9-effect panel - so that bead fixed the regression it introduced but did not and should not have fixed this.

The failure is unrecoverable, not merely ugly: content.js:6218-6222 sets ':host { position: fixed; overflow: hidden }' with no max-height and no scrollable ancestor, so clipped content cannot be reached by any page scroll. Measured hostTop -74.4px at vh=600 with the bar bottom-anchored (bl/br) - the panel header and first rows sit above the viewport. Top-anchored (tl/tr) loses the footer instead.

This bites real users on short windows, split-screen layouts, and laptops with browser chrome eating vertical space.

FIX: bound the PANEL, not just the effect list - a max-height on the panel tied to the available viewport height (with the bar's position taken into account, since bottom-anchored constrains upward) plus overflow-y auto, mirroring what dvt.5 did one level down. Check all four POS_DATA positions. DONE: at vh=600 every panel control is reachable at all four bar positions, with no clipped header or footer.
close_reason: Closed

title: Beacon geometry assumes host pages do not set box-sizing: border-box
description:
Found by the oculist-dvt.4 re-reviewer while deriving the bracket geometry. Cyber-Vision's targeting brackets (extension/content.js:2847-2857) are content-box elements: width/height 15px plus a 2px border, so the surviving border sits OUTSIDE the declared width and the far edges land at pad + 2px. That is correct on the test fixture.

But Oculist injects into arbitrary host pages, and a very large fraction of real sites ship 'html, body, *, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box }'. The extension's beacon elements are appended to document.documentElement, so a universal selector on the host page WILL match them. Under border-box the 2px border is drawn INSIDE the 15px, shifting every far edge in by 2px and making the brackets frame the match slightly differently than designed.

This is a PRODUCTION issue in content.js, not a test defect - the test correctly encodes what the code does today. Blast radius is cosmetic and small (2px, scaled by getBeaconScale, so 4.5px at xl), but it applies to any beacon element that relies on content-box sizing, not just Cyber-Vision's brackets - audit the others while here.

FIX: set an explicit 'box-sizing:content-box' (or border-box, chosen deliberately) in the cssText of beacon elements whose geometry depends on it, so host-page CSS cannot change their layout. The beacons already set position/pointer-events/z-index defensively for the same reason; box-sizing belongs in that set. DONE: bracket geometry is identical on a fixture that sets '* { box-sizing: border-box }' and one that does not.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Residual gap noted by the reviewer: the fix uses non-!important inline styles, so a host page shipping '* { box-sizing: border-box !important }' still overrides beacon geometry. The test fixture deliberately uses a realistic no-!important reset. Accepted scope for this bead.

title: Light Cycle applies getBeaconScale twice
description:
Found by the oculist-dvt.3 reviewer. animateLightCycle applies getBeaconScale() at BOTH levels: once as the container's transform scale(scale) (extension/content.js:2531) and again per child element - THICK = 3 * scale (:2536), headSize = 8 * scale (:2558), boxPad = 6 * scale (:2632, :2641). The established pattern in animateAnimeLaser (content.js:877) applies the container scale ONLY, with fixed child sizes.

Consequence: at beaconSize 'xl' (scale 2.25) the wall renders about 15px thick instead of the intended ~7px, i.e. scaled twice over. Nothing fails today because test/light_cycle.test.js never varies beaconSize - and note that 15px would also breach that test's own 'min(width,height) <= 10' right-angle threshold, so the bug is currently invisible only because the test runs at the default size.

FIX: drop the per-child scale multipliers and let the container transform do the work, matching animateAnimeLaser. Then extend the right-angle test to run at all four beacon sizes so the threshold is exercised where it actually bites. DONE: wall thickness at xl is proportionate, and the right-angle test passes at s/m/l/xl.

RELATED, same review, same file: midYVp = Math.min(vpCy + 96, window.innerHeight - 26) at content.js:2487 can land within a pixel of finalYVp (:2488) for a match low in the viewport, yielding a ~1px stub segment via Math.max(len, 1). Not reproduced on the test fixture, but a real geometry edge case worth guarding while in here.
close_reason: Closed

title: WAAPI animations leak on every effect except Light Cycle
description:
Confirmed empirically by the oculist-dvt.3 reviewer in a clean Chromium page: after el.remove() a Web Animations API animation still reports playState 'running' with currentTime advancing (192.4ms to 601.0ms observed). Only Animation.cancel() stops it (playState 'idle', currentTime null). So removing a beacon element does NOT stop its animations - they keep ticking until GC.

oculist-dvt.3 fixed this for Light Cycle only: animateLightCycle collects its animations into container.__waapiAnims (extension/content.js:2668) and cancelBeacons() (content.js:835-839) cancels them. That block is guarded and is a strict no-op for every other effect, because NO OTHER EFFECT SETS __waapiAnims.

So the fix is half-adopted. animateTrail, animateAnimeLaser, animateLightning, animateIris, animateWarpDrive, animateFlame, animatePointingArrows, animateDispersion and drawActiveMatchMagnifier all drive WAAPI animations and all still leak them on cancel. Impact is bounded - the animations are short and the elements are detached, so it is wasted work rather than a visible bug - but it is real, and it is exactly the class of thing that compounds on a page where the user searches repeatedly.

FIX: hang __waapiAnims off each WAAPI effect's container the way animateLightCycle does. Mechanical and low-risk; the cancelBeacons() side already exists. DONE: firing each effect and calling cancelBeacons() mid-flight leaves no animation in playState 'running'.
close_reason: Closed

title: speed_lines.test.js clear-lane test flakes under full-suite parallel load (elseMax starved of real animation frames)
close_reason: Closed

title: Document the four new effects
description:
Bring the user-facing docs up to date with the 13-effect registry. Dependency-gated on the two chain tails so it documents the shipped reality, not the plan.

SCOPE:
1. CHANGELOG.md - add an entry for the four new effects following the existing Keep a Changelog format. Read the file's conventions first: a dated heading means RELEASED (established by commit 26d10f6 and confirmed during the oculist-l6m.10 review), so do NOT date the heading unless the operator is cutting a release. Check with the orchestrator rather than guessing the version number.
2. docs/index.html - THE EFFECT LIST HERE IS ALREADY STALE, independent of this epic. Line 497 and line 578 both enumerate only 7 effects (Anime Laser, Spotlight, Warp Drive, Inferno Flame, Lightning, Electron Cloud, Pointing Arrows) - they are missing Bloom and Trail, which already shipped. Fix that pre-existing omission AND add the four new ones, so both lists name all 13. Line 566 describes the picker generally and may need no change.
3. README.md line 12 names a few effects as examples rather than enumerating them; check whether it still reads correctly at 13 and leave it alone if so.

Do NOT touch PRIVACY.md or docs/privacy.html - no storage or permission behaviour changes in this epic, and test/privacy_invariants.test.js pins the claim they make.

DONE: every place in the repo that enumerates effects names all 13, the pre-existing Bloom and Trail omission in docs/index.html is fixed, and the CHANGELOG entry is undated unless the orchestrator says otherwise. A grep for the old 7-effect list returns nothing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Settings panel at 13 effects: picker ergonomics
description:
The effect picker is makeRadioList (extension/content.js around 4062-4103), rendering one row per registry entry. This epic takes it from 9 rows to 13. Established behaviour: a row is marked active only on an exact item.value === currentVal match, and the panel is rebuilt via rebuildSettingsPanelPreservingFocus() on storage changes.

INPUT: all four new effects registered (this bead is dependency-gated on the two chain tails).

INVESTIGATE FIRST, then fix only what is actually broken. Do not restructure a panel that works:
1. Does the settings panel overflow the viewport at 13 rows, at each of the four beacon sizes and at the browser's larger default font sizes? The panel is inside the overlay's shadow root and is height-constrained by the find bar's position (top/bottom, left/right - see POS_DATA).
